docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
FunFlux is a Snakemake workflow for fungal isolate genome analysis. It accepts Illumina reads, Oxford Nanopore (ONT) or PacBio HiFi reads, short and long reads from the same isolate, or an existing assembly. The workflow combines assembly, contamination and mitochondrion screening, quality control, ITS-based taxonomy, repeat masking, gene prediction and functional annotation.

FunFlux was developed for the genomic characterisation of fungal isolates. Its results describe the assembled genome, its predicted genes and their functional annotation, including the secondary-metabolite gene clusters found by antiSMASH. They are predictions from the genome sequence, to be weighed with curation and experimental evidence.

An optional screen looks for point mutations known to confer resistance to antifungal drugs and fungicides. The configuration key mode selects the input mode. This site documents version v2.0.0.

FunFlux belongs to the BioFlux family of pipelines.

Terms used on this page

ONT Oxford Nanopore Technologies, a long-read sequencing platform HiFi PacBio's accurate long reads, each the consensus of several passes over one molecule (CCS) ITS internal transcribed spacer — the rDNA region used as the barcode of fungi BUSCO a set of single-copy genes expected in every genome of a lineage, used to estimate completeness soft-masking writing repeats in lower case, so that gene finders can treat them differently without losing the sequence AMR antimicrobial resistance; in FunFlux, point mutations studied for resistance against antifungal drugs and fungicides

docs.title: The workflow at a glance
docs.text:
Each coloured line is one mode: follow yours from its input to the report. The four lines take their own routes to contigs_final.fasta, the genome every mode delivers, and from there run on together through the analyses. In hybrid the purple line has two arms: the Illumina arm builds a guide assembly with SPAdes, screens it and keeps the Illumina pairs that map to it, and Polypolish uses those pairs to correct the long-read assembly. In contigs mode the solid gold line goes straight to contigs_final.fasta; the dashed gold path is the contamination and mitochondrion screen, which the configuration can switch on. Where the lines split into parallel tracks, the steps run side by side. Analysis groups after the final genome may run in parallel. The order along the line is a reading order, not the order in which the steps must run. An open ring marks a step the configuration switches on or off; the two Medaka steps apply to ONT samples only. Thin lines are extra inputs, and the dashed red line is the optional resistance-mutation screen. Select the map to open it larger; select it again to see it at full size, and close it with × or Esc.

The stages, their tools and when they run:

Stage Tools Runs Assembly depends on the mode (below) illumina, longread, hybrid; contigs mode starts from your assembly Contamination screen BLAST against NCBI core_nt, BlobTools always; in contigs mode only when the screen is switched on Mitochondrion screen BLAST, with the assembler's evidence in the long-read modes with the contamination screen Assembly QC QUAST, BUSCO always Contig summary tidk finds the telomeres; one table per sample gives every contig of the draft a verdict (Contig summary) always ITS taxonomy ITSx, SINTAX against UNITE always Repeat masking tantan, or RepeatModeler and RepeatMasker always Gene prediction funannotate with its own gene finders, Tiberius (on by default) and GeneMark-ES (with a licence) always Functional annotation InterProScan, eggNOG-mapper, antiSMASH, SignalP 6 always; SignalP 6 is optional Antifungal resistance mutations ChroQueTas against the FungAMR database only when switched on Report MultiQC, one report for all samples always

From the contamination screen on, every mode runs the same steps. Only polishing differs between the read-based modes.

docs.title: The four modes
docs.text:
illumina longread hybrid contigs Input Illumina paired-end reads, {sample}_R1.<ext> and {sample}_R2.<ext> ONT reads {sample}_ont.<ext> or PacBio HiFi reads {sample}_pacbio.<ext>; one batch may hold both Illumina pairs and ONT or PacBio HiFi reads for every sample one assembly per sample, {sample}.fasta, .fa or .fna Read QC PhiX removal (bowtie2), then fastp NanoPlot before and after Filtlong both of the above none Assembly SPAdes hifiasm (default) or Flye an Illumina guide assembly (SPAdes) to select the isolate's read pairs, then hifiasm or Flye on the long reads no assembler Contig filter ≥ 500 bp and ≥ 2× coverage, read off SPAdes' own headers none the same cut-offs, on the guide assembly only the same cut-offs when the headers are SPAdes-style; otherwise headers are cut at the first space or tab and nothing is removed Polishing none Medaka, ONT samples* Medaka (ONT samples*), then Polypolish with the Illumina pairs none Delivered genome the screened SPAdes contigs the screened long-read assembly, polished with Medaka for ONT samples the screened long-read assembly, corrected with the Illumina pairs the input contigs, screened only with parameters.contigs.screen: true

* Medaka is on by default for ONT samples, and medaka_model: false switches it off. PacBio HiFi samples are never polished with Medaka. <ext> is fastq, fq, fastq.gz or fq.gz, the same for all files of one kind in a batch, and _pacbio files must hold HiFi (CCS) reads. CLR reads are not supported.

hybrid requires more computation than either single-technology mode, because it assembles and screens the Illumina reads as well. In hybrid, Filtlong can also score the ONT reads against the selected Illumina pairs, but only when short_read_guidance is switched on. If you used FunFlux 1.x, Funnotator or FunFluxL, Coming from v1 lists what changed. See Modes and Choosing a mode.

docs.title: Delivered genome files
docs.text:
Every sample ends with up to three FASTA files in 02.assembly/{sample}/. Their content depends on two settings: whether the contamination and mitochondrion screen runs, and parameters.mitochondria.mode. The screen always runs in illumina, longread and hybrid, and in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true.

File Screen on, mitochondrion split off (separate_confirmed, the default) Screen on, parameters.mitochondria.mode set to off or report contigs mode without the screen contigs_all.fasta the assembly after the contamination screen and, in longread and hybrid, after polishing; mitochondrion included the same not written contigs_final.fasta the nuclear genome: contigs_all.fasta without the confirmed mitochondrial contigs every contig the input after the contig filter, including a mitochondrial genome if the input contains one contigs_mitochondrial.fasta the confirmed mitochondrial contigs; an empty file when none was confirmed an empty file not written

contigs_final.fasta is the genome that QC, ITS and annotation read

QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS extraction and funannotate run on contigs_final.fasta. It is the nuclear genome alone only when the screen runs with the default separate_confirmed. Otherwise nothing is split off.

The gene models refer to a renamed copy of that genome. funannotate clean and funannotate sort turn contigs_final.fasta into 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_sort.fasta, whose contigs are named scaffold_1, scaffold_2, ... from the longest down, and the gene models use these names. QUAST, BUSCO and the ITS files keep the names of contigs_final.fasta. contigs_removed_by_clean.txt, next to contigs_sort.fasta, lists the contigs funannotate clean removed.

docs.title: One command, one configuration, one report
docs.text:
All four modes are launched the same way, from the repository root:

snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

--sdm conda builds the conda environment of each rule on first use, so only Snakemake is installed by hand. --cores sets the CPU budget of a local run and is used without --jobs. See Running FunFlux.

Pass the configuration file explicitly with --configfile. FunFlux ships a template, config/config.yaml, but does not load it on its own: copy it, then set the mode, the input and output paths, the database locations and the annotation table. A wrong mode, a missing input directory, a bad sample name or a missing annotation row stops the dry run before any job starts. See Configuration and Quick start.

Results are written to numbered folders that are the same in every mode: 00.resources for material shared by the samples of a run, 01.reads (not in contigs mode), 02.assembly, 03.taxonomy, 04.annotation, 05.amr (only with the resistance-mutation screen on), 06.report and logs. The funannotate database stays in directories.funannotate_db, outside the output folder. Every run ends with a MultiQC report, 06.report/multiqc_report.html, which collects the QC of all samples. The annotation itself is in 04.annotation/{sample}/funannotate/annotate_results/. See Output files.

What has to be prepared in advance

FunFlux installs its own software, but three resources must be on disk before the first run: NCBI core_nt with its taxonomy files (not read in contigs mode without the screen), the eggNOG-mapper data, and an InterProScan installation. GeneMark-ES and SignalP 6 are optional and need a licence. Everything else is downloaded on first use, or can be pointed at a copy you already hold. See Reference databases and Licensed and external tools.

docs.title: Where the resistance-mutation screen fits
docs.text:
Stage 05.amr is disabled by default (parameters.amr.chroquetas: off). When enabled, ChroQueTas searches each genome for the point mutations that the FungAMR database lists with evidence for or against resistance to antifungal drugs and fungicides, and FunFlux summarises for each sample the known changes found and the drugs FungAMR links them to. A sample of a species that FungAMR does not cover is reported as not screened.

These calls describe known mutations in the genes and species that FungAMR covers. They do not establish a resistance phenotype, and the absence of a call is not evidence of susceptibility. Interpret them together with the evidence levels FungAMR gives each mutation. See Antifungal resistance mutations.
