docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
This page shows the path from your input to the annotated genome: the stages, the file each step hands to the next, and the settings that add or remove steps. Read it to trace a result back to the step and the file it came from. Output files describes every file, and Running FunFlux every command.

Terms used on this page

front end the steps that differ by mode, chosen by mode: read processing, assembly and contig filter before the screen, and polishing after it contig filter rule filter_contigs: on SPAdes-style headers it drops contigs under 500 bp or 2x coverage; other headers are only cut at their first space or tab the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true draft assembly (the draft) the assembly the screen examines, before any contig is removed: contigs_filt.fasta in illumina mode and in contigs mode with the screen, assembly.fasta in longread and hybrid nuclear genome the delivered genome without the confirmed mitochondrial contigs, contigs_final.fasta; it holds every contig when nothing is split off (parameters.mitochondria.mode off or report, or no screen) AMR screen (resistance-mutation screen) the optional step, off by default (parameters.amr.chroquetas), in which ChroQueTas looks in each genome for the changes FungAMR lists for the species; results in 05.amr/ scaffold_N the name funannotate sort gives each contig, scaffold_1 being the longest; nothing is joined, and the gene models refer to these names launcher environment the conda environment you create by hand for Snakemake itself

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
The diagram follows one sample through the workflow, from its input to the report. The numbered names in the boxes are the folders of the output directory.

---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    ILL[illumina<br/>PhiX removal, fastp,<br/>SPAdes, contig filter] --> DRAFT([draft assembly])
    LONG[longread<br/>Filtlong,<br/>hifiasm or Flye] --> DRAFT
    HYB[hybrid<br/>guide, selected pairs,<br/>Filtlong, hifiasm or Flye] --> DRAFT
    CON[contigs<br/>contig filter] -.->|screen on| DRAFT
    DRAFT --> SCREEN[contamination and<br/>mitochondrion screen<br/>BLAST, BlobTools, selector]
    SCREEN --> POLISH[polishing<br/>Medaka for ONT samples,<br/>Polypolish in hybrid]
    POLISH --> ALL([contigs_all.fasta])
    SCREEN -->|no polishing| ALL
    ALL --> SPLIT[mitochondrion split]
    SPLIT --> MITO([contigs_mitochondrial.fasta])
    SPLIT --> FINAL([contigs_final.fasta<br/>nuclear genome])
    CON -->|screen off| FINAL
    MITO -.-> AMR[AMR screen, if on<br/>ChroQueTas with FungAMR<br/>05.amr]
    FINAL -.-> AMR
    FINAL --> ITS[ITS extraction<br/>SINTAX against UNITE<br/>03.taxonomy]
    FINAL --> PRED[gene prediction<br/>clean, sort, repeat masking,<br/>Tiberius, funannotate predict]
    PRED --> FUNC[functional annotation<br/>InterProScan, eggNOG-mapper,<br/>antiSMASH, SignalP 6 if on]
    FUNC --> MERGE[funannotate annotate<br/>04.annotation]
    FINAL --> QC[assembly QC<br/>QUAST, BUSCO<br/>02.assembly]
    MERGE --> CS[contig summary of the draft<br/>tidk telomeres, verdicts<br/>02.assembly]
    QC --> CS
    ITS --> CS
    QC --> REP[MultiQC report<br/>06.report]
    CS --> REP
    AMR -.-> REP

From the screen on, every mode runs the same steps, except polishing

The mode key chooses the front end, the part of the run that differs between modes. Before the screen, it is read processing, assembly and the contig filter, whichever of these the mode runs. After the screen, it is polishing, in longread and hybrid only. Medaka polishes ONT samples unless medaka_model: false switches it off, and Polypolish corrects every hybrid sample. When the screen runs, the front end ends with contigs_all.fasta. The contamination and mitochondrion screen and the mitochondrion split are shared by all modes.

The MultiQC report holds QUAST, BUSCO and the contig summary in every mode. It adds the read and mapping QC of the read-based modes, and the AMR table when the AMR screen is on. See Report.

docs.title: From the draft to the nuclear genome
docs.text:
Between the draft and the genome files, each step works on the file the step before it wrote:

Order Step Writes, in 02.assembly/{sample}/ Runs 1 Draft assembly: the SPAdes contigs or your FASTA after the contig filter, or the hifiasm or Flye assembly contigs_filt.fasta (illumina; contigs with the screen) or assembly.fasta (longread, hybrid) whenever the screen runs 2 Assembler evidence (assembly_evidence): the read depth and circularity of each contig, from the assembler's own files (hifiasm/hifiasm.p_ctg.gfa or flye/assembly_info.txt) assembly_evidence.tsv longread, hybrid 3 Contamination screen: BLAST against NCBI core_nt and BlobTools give each contig a genus contaminants/ with the screen 4 Mitochondrion screen: finds the mitochondrial contigs from the BLAST hits and, in longread and hybrid, the table of row 2 mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv with the screen 5 Contig selector: keeps or removes contigs by genus, as parameters.decontamination says (the default, off, keeps all); with parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, the default, the confirmed mitochondrial contigs are kept whatever their genus contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta, contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv with the screen 6 Medaka polishing medaka/consensus.fasta ONT samples with Medaka (longread, hybrid) 7 Polypolish correction with the Illumina pairs polypolish/polished.fasta hybrid 8 End of the front end: a copy of the last file written above contigs_all.fasta with the screen 9 Mitochondrion split contigs_final.fasta, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta with the screen

logs/finalize_assembly_{sample}.log names the file that became contigs_all.fasta. In contigs mode without the screen, the contig filter writes contigs_final.fasta directly, and rows 2 to 9 do not run.

Three of these files are read by more than the next step:

File Also read by the draft (row 1; in contigs mode without the screen, contigs_final.fasta) the telomere search and the contig summary, which therefore describes every contig of the draft, also those the screen removed contigs_final.fasta QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS extraction, the annotation and the AMR screen contigs_mitochondrial.fasta the contig summary, in every run with the screen; the AMR screen, when it is on (Two runs)

Delivered genome files shows what contigs_all.fasta, contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta hold for each setting of the screen.

docs.title: ONT and PacBio HiFi samples
docs.text:
In longread and hybrid mode, the file-name suffix sets the technology of each sample, and one batch may hold both, as Mixing ONT and PacBio HiFi samples explains. Only one decision changes the steps: whether Medaka runs. Medaka is on by default for ONT samples (medaka_model: auto) and adds two jobs to an ONT sample and none to a PacBio HiFi sample:

ONT sample, with Medaka on (the default) PacBio HiFi sample Medaka jobs check_medaka_model, which reads the raw reads before the assembler starts, so a wrong model name stops the run within seconds; long_read_consensus none contigs_all.fasta in longread made from the Medaka consensus made from the decontaminated assembly contigs_all.fasta in hybrid the Medaka consensus, corrected by Polypolish with the Illumina pairs the decontaminated assembly, corrected by Polypolish with the Illumina pairs

With medaka_model: false, an ONT sample follows the PacBio HiFi column. In hybrid, Polypolish corrects both kinds of sample. _pacbio files must hold HiFi (CCS) reads, and CLR reads are not supported. Long reads and Hybrid describe the two front ends.

docs.title: Annotation steps
docs.text:
The annotation runs on contigs_final.fasta, one step after the other. The rule names are those Snakemake prints while it runs, and the log files in logs/ are named after them.

Order Step Rule Writes, in 04.annotation/{sample}/ 1 funannotate clean and sort: removes short and duplicated contigs, sorts the rest longest first and renames them scaffold_1, scaffold_2, ... funannotate_preprocess contigs_clean.fasta, contigs_sort.fasta, contigs_removed_by_clean.txt 2 Repeat masking: tantan (the default), or RepeatModeler and RepeatMasker (masking_method: repeatmodeler_repeatmasker) repeat_masking contigs_mask.fasta 3 Tiberius gene prediction (on by default) tiberius_prediction, tiberius_gff3 tiberius/tiberius.gtf, tiberius/tiberius.evm.gff3 4 Gene prediction: funannotate predict combines its own gene finders with the Tiberius genes funannotate_prediction funannotate/predict_results/: gene models, proteins, GenBank file 5 Functional annotation of the predicted proteins, four tools side by side iprscan_annotation, eggnog_annotation, antismash_annotation, signalp6_annotation (SignalP 6 on) iprscan/interproscan_out.xml, eggnog/, antismash/, signalp6/ 6 funannotate annotate merges the gene models and the functional annotation funannotate_annotation funannotate/annotate_results/: the final GenBank, GFF3, proteins and .annotations.txt, the functional annotation with one row per transcript 7 Removal of funannotate's scratch files cleanup .cleanup_complete.txt

The gene models therefore use the scaffold_N names of step 1, not those of contigs_final.fasta, and the annotated_as column of the contig summary links the two.

Gene prediction waits for two short checks. An expired GeneMark-ES licence key or a wrong AUGUSTUS model name therefore stops the run before gene prediction starts, instead of partway through it.

Check What it does Stops the run when Writes genemark_check (GeneMark-ES on) runs GeneMark-ES on a 200 kb slice of contigs_mask.fasta; takes about a minute the licence key has expired genemark_check.txt augustus_model_check runs as soon as the funannotate database is ready, within minutes of the start, even when the run downloads the database first column 4 of the annotation parameter table names an AUGUSTUS model that the database does not hold augustus_model.txt: whether a stored AUGUSTUS model is used or AUGUSTUS is trained (The AUGUSTUS model)

docs.title: Settings that add or remove steps
docs.text:
With the defaults, FunFlux runs the screen in every read-based mode, splits off the mitochondrion, masks with tantan and predicts genes with Tiberius. GeneMark-ES, SignalP 6 and the AMR screen are added only when you switch them on. Each setting below adds or removes steps:

Setting Default Effect Also needs mode none: required which front end runs the input folder of the mode parameters.contigs.screen (contigs mode) false true adds the contamination and mitochondrion screen, which the read-based modes always run directories.blast_db, in every run with the screen parameters.mitochondria.mode separate_confirmed report or off: nothing is split off, and contigs_final.fasta keeps the mitochondrial contigs parameters.<mode>.assembler (longread, hybrid) hifiasm flye assembles with Flye instead parameters.<mode>.medaka_model (longread, hybrid) auto false removes the Medaka model check and Medaka polishing of ONT samples parameters.masking_method tantan repeatmodeler_repeatmasker masks with RepeatModeler and RepeatMasker; it takes hours parameters.genemark.mode auto adds the GeneMark-ES licence check and GeneMark-ES to gene prediction, but only when directories.genemark_dir is set a licence key in ~/.gm_key parameters.tiberius.mode on off removes the Tiberius model download and the Tiberius gene prediction links.tiberius_model_link while on parameters.signalp6.mode off fast, slow or slow-sequential adds the SignalP 6 installation and the signal-peptide prediction files.signalp6_archive parameters.amr.chroquetas off on adds the ChroQueTas download, the AMR screen of every sample (05.amr/) and the AMR table of the report links.chroquetas_link directories.unite_db, directories.antismash_db empty a folder you set is linked into 00.resources/ instead of downloading UNITE or the antiSMASH databases

Every key is listed on Configuration.

docs.title: Which Python runs the helper scripts
docs.text:
Several steps run FunFlux's own small Python scripts, most of them kept in workflow/scripts/. Each runs with the Python pinned in its rule's conda environment, not with the system Python, so the scripts behave the same on every computer:

The rule The Python has a tool environment (the Medaka model check, the telomere search, the contig summary, the ITS steps, the check of the InterProScan result, the SignalP 6 installation, the AMR screen) the pinned Python of that environment has none of its own (the contig selector, the mitochondrion screen and split, the assembler's evidence table, the repair of the funannotate database paths, the AUGUSTUS model check) the python environment: Python 3.12.15 and nothing else

Snakemake's own Python, in the launcher environment, only reads the configuration and runs FunFlux's checks before any job starts. The commands that the workflow still takes from the computer are listed on Commands outside the conda environments.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page lists the messages that stop a FunFlux run or leave a result missing, with the cause of each and what to change. It follows a run from start to end: the checks of the configuration before any job starts, the failures of single steps while the workflow runs, and the stops particular to a cluster.

Terms used on this page

dry run a Snakemake run with -n: FunFlux checks the configuration and the inputs, and Snakemake lists the jobs it plans without running any rule one step of the workflow as Snakemake defines it, such as select_contigs; the console and the log files in logs/ use its name launch folder the folder Snakemake is started from, normally the FunFlux repository; relative paths are read from it, and .snakemake/ is created there lock the record, in .snakemake/, of the files a run in progress reads and writes; a killed run leaves it behind, and --unlock removes it the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true contig selector rule select_contigs, the last step of the screen: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says; the default, off, keeps every contig annotation parameter table the tab-separated file named by files.annotation_params, one row per sample: name, species, a protein FASTA of related fungi and, optionally, an AUGUSTUS model heavy step, long step, light step on a cluster, heavy steps ask the scheduler for ram_gb and runtime_hours, long steps for runtime_hours only, and light steps for neither

docs.title: Where to look
docs.text:
What you see, and when it appears, tells you where the cause is and which part of this page to read.

What you see Where the cause is A [FunFlux] ... line before Snakemake's Building DAG of jobs..., and the run ends A configuration check failed and nothing ran. The message names the key. See Stops before any job runs. A [FunFlux] <step>: ... line after jobs have started, for example [FunFlux] funannotate_db: ... That step failed or, if it is a report step such as QUAST, it warns and the run goes on. Look the step up under Failures while the workflow runs. Its log is logs/<step>.log or logs/<step>_{sample}.log. Error in rule <rule>: while the workflow runs The block names the job's log:, the file that holds the tool's own messages. See Failures while the workflow runs. Error: Directory cannot be locked. or The files below seem to be incomplete. A previous run was killed. Directory cannot be locked has a second cause: another run from the same launch folder would write the same files, or one of the two runs would write a file the other reads. Use --unlock only when no other Snakemake process runs from that folder. See Resuming after an interruption. A finished run with an empty or missing result Some messages go only to the logs and never stop the run. See Messages that do not stop the run. A message from Slurm, a job killed for memory or time, SSL certificate problem, or a step that works on one computer but not on the cluster See On a cluster.

Three kinds of log are kept:

Log of Where every per-sample rule <output_dir>/logs/<rule>_{sample}.log the rules that run once for all samples <output_dir>/logs/, without a sample name: funannotate_db.log, normalize_funannotate_db.log, unite_db.log, unite_identified.log, antismash_db.log or antismash_db_local.log, tiberius_model.log, telomere_db.log, busco_data.log (a named BUSCO lineage), download_phix.log, build_phix.log, install_signalp6.log, chroquetas_db.log, multiqc.log Snakemake itself .snakemake/log/ in the launch folder, one file per run, named after its start time

--show-failed-logs makes Snakemake print the log of every failed job at the end of the run.

docs.title: Stops before any job runs
docs.text:
FunFlux checks the whole configuration before any job starts, on every run and every dry run. A failed check prints one [FunFlux] line and exits with status 1. Only the first failed check is reported, so fix it and run -n again. Lines that start with [FunFlux] NOTE: do not stop the run.

Placeholders in the messages below are in angle brackets. An empty cell means that the message itself already says what is wrong or what to change.

docs.title: Configuration file and mode
docs.text:
These checks concern the configuration file itself and its mode key.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] No configuration supplied. Pass one explicitly, e.g.: No --configfile on the command line. FunFlux has no default configuration. Add --configfile config/config_custom.yaml. [FunFlux] mode: this configuration has no 'mode' key. ... A v1 configuration (FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL, FunFluxL+), or an empty mode:. Start from the v2 template. Coming from v1 lists what moved. [FunFlux] mode: must be one of illumina | longread | hybrid | contigs (got: '<value>') Another word in mode. Use one of the four.

docs.title: Keys and values
docs.text:
These messages name a key that is missing, unknown or in the wrong block, or whose value has the wrong form or is out of range.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] <block>: must be a block of 'key: value' lines. input, directories, files, links, resources, parameters or a block inside parameters holds a single value or a list. Indent the keys under the block name. [FunFlux] <section>.<key>: required, but it is missing or empty in the config. A required entry is empty: directories.output_dir, eggnog_db, funannotate_db, blast_db (when the screen runs), files.iprscan, files.annotation_params, links.funannotate_link, links.phix_link (in illumina and hybrid mode). The template leaves them empty on purpose. Fill it in. [FunFlux] <key>: expected true or false (got <value>). A yes/no key holds another word. parameters.contigs.screen is checked in every mode, although only contigs mode uses it. Write true or false. [FunFlux] <key>: expected a whole number (got <value>)., ... must be at least N (got M)., ... must be at most N (got M). The value is not an integer, or it is out of range. The allowed values are listed on Configuration. [FunFlux] <key>: expected a number (got <value>)., ... must be above 0 (got X)., ... must be at most N (got X). The same for decimal keys, for example min_direct_blast_qcov: 150. nan and inf, and YAML's .nan and .inf, count as not a number. As above. [FunFlux] parameters.<block>: unsupported key(s): <keys>. Supported keys: <list>. A misspelled key inside a block of parameters. Use a key from the list. [FunFlux] parameters.<key>: unknown setting (a typo?). Known settings: ... A misspelled key directly under parameters. Use a name from the list. [FunFlux] parameters.<key>: this setting moved into the block named after your mode: ... long_read_assembler, flye_input_mode, medaka_model, filtlong or hifiasm at the top of parameters, as in FunFluxL. Move it into parameters.longread or parameters.hybrid. long_read_assembler is now called assembler.

A misspelled optional key outside parameters is ignored without a message

Only parameters and its blocks are checked for unknown keys. A misspelled optional key in directories, files, links, input or resources is ignored, and the default applies. For example, antismash: instead of antismash_db: in directories means that the antiSMASH database is downloaded, and resources.thread: means 24 threads.

docs.title: Input files and sample names
docs.text:
These checks look for the input files of the active mode and take the sample names from the file names.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] mode=<mode> requires input.<key> to be set in the config. The key for the input folder of the active mode is missing or empty. Set input.contigs_dir, input.illumina_dir or input.longread_dir or, in hybrid mode, the last two. [FunFlux] input.<key>: '<value>' is not an existing directory. Wrong path. A relative path is read from the launch folder, not from output_dir. Use an absolute path. [FunFlux] input.<key>: no input files found. Expected names like <example>. No file follows the naming pattern. Name the files as the mode expects: {sample}.fasta (or .fa, .fna) for assemblies, {sample}_R1.fastq.gz and {sample}_R2.fastq.gz for Illumina pairs, and {sample}_ont.fastq.gz or {sample}_pacbio.fastq.gz for long reads. [FunFlux] input.<key>: more than one file extension in this folder (<a>, <b>). ... Mixed extensions, or other files in the folder. In contigs mode every file whose name contains a dot is taken as a sample, so a README.txt gives (fasta, txt). Use one extension for all files of one kind. In hybrid mode the Illumina files and the long-read files may have different ones. Keep other files elsewhere. [FunFlux] input.<key>: file extension '<ext>' is not recognised (expected one of: ...). An extension FunFlux does not recognise, for example .fas. Use fasta, fa or fna for assemblies, and fastq, fq, fastq.gz or fq.gz for reads. [FunFlux] sample name '<name>' contains characters that are not allowed (...). Rename the input files. The name holds a space or one of * # @ % ^ / ! ? & : ; | < >. A FASTA in a subfolder of contigs_dir becomes the sample subfolder/name and stops here. Rename the files. Underscores and dots are allowed. Keep the input folder flat. [FunFlux] input.illumina_dir: sample '<name>' has an R1 file but no R2 mate: <path> The R2 file is missing or named differently. Name the pair {sample}_R1.<ext> and {sample}_R2.<ext>. [FunFlux] sample '<name>' has both _ont and _pacbio files in <dir>. ... One sample has files of both long-read technologies. Keep one long-read file per sample. [FunFlux] hybrid mode needs Illumina and long reads for every sample. Some samples have reads of one kind only. The message goes on with No _ont or _pacbio file for:, No Illumina _R1 file for: or both, each followed by the sample names. Supply both kinds of reads, or run the sample in another batch.

docs.title: Annotation parameter table
docs.text:
These messages concern the annotation parameter table, its rows and its columns.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: '<path>' not found. Wrong path in files.annotation_params. [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: line N has K tab-separated columns; expected 3 or 4 (sample, species, proteins and, optionally, augustus_species). Spaces instead of tabs, or a missing or extra column. A species name with a space is still one column. Separate the columns with tabs. [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: sample '<name>' names the AUGUSTUS model '<model>', which is not a trained species of the funannotate database at '<db>'. Did you mean '<model>'? Leave column 4 empty, or write '-', to train AUGUSTUS on this genome instead. ... Column 4 names a model that the database does not hold, for example through a typo, or with capitals where the folder name has none. The message appears at start-up when the database is already on disk. Otherwise it comes from rule augustus_model_check, right after the database is unpacked, and is also written to logs/augustus_model_check_{sample}.log. Use one of the suggested names, which are the folder names in <db>/trained_species/, or leave column 4 empty to train AUGUSTUS on the genome. [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: sample '<name>' names the AUGUSTUS model '<model>', which is not a possible model name (letters, digits, '_', '-' and '.' only). ... Column 4 holds a path, a space or another character that no model name has. Write the model's folder name only, or leave column 4 empty. [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: sample '<name>' appears more than once (line N). A duplicate row. Keep one row per sample. [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: sample '<name>' has no row in '<path>'. Every sample of the batch needs a row. Rows for samples outside the batch are ignored. Add the row. [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: protein file '<path>' of sample '<name>' does not exist. (or ... is empty.) A relative path in the table is read from the launch folder. Give an absolute path to a non-empty protein FASTA.

A sample whose column 4 is empty can also stop later, during gene prediction, with Not enough gene models <N> to train Augustus; see Other stops in the shared stages.

docs.title: Databases and links
docs.text:
These messages concern the reference databases and the download links of the configuration.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] directories.antismash_db: '<path>' is not a directory. ... (or ... has no 'clusterblast'. ...) The key must name the antiSMASH databases folder itself, the one that holds clusterblast/, pfam/ and the rest. Point it there, or leave it empty to download the database. [FunFlux] directories.unite_db: '<path>' is not a directory. ... (or ... has no 'unite_its_sintax.fasta'. ...) The folder must hold the UNITE SINTAX reference as an uncompressed unite_its_sintax.fasta. Unpack or rename the file, or leave the key empty to download it. [FunFlux] links.unite_its_link: required, unless directories.unite_db names a local UNITE copy. Both are empty. Set one of them. [FunFlux] links.funannotate_link: expected a Zenodo URL of the form https://zenodo.org/records/<id>/files/<archive>, got: <url> FunFlux finds the checksum file in the same Zenodo record, so the link must be a Zenodo record URL. Use a Zenodo record URL, as the template does. [FunFlux] links.funannotate_link: cannot read a file name from the URL: <url> The URL ends without a file name. As above. [FunFlux] links.telomere_db_link: required, but it is missing or empty in the config. The link to tidk's telomere repeat database is required in every mode. A configuration written before the contig summary existed lacks it. Copy the line from config/config.yaml. [FunFlux] parameters.prediction.busco_db: '<name>' is not in the funannotate database at '<db>'. Add it with FunFlux's funannotate conda environment activated ('Other BUSCO sets for gene prediction' in the documentation shows how to find it): funannotate setup -i busco -b <name> -d <db> -w The funannotate database ships only dikarya. Run the command shown, in the activated environment (see Other BUSCO sets for gene prediction), or use dikarya. [FunFlux] parameters.prediction.busco_db: expected a plain dataset name such as dikarya (got: '<value>') The name holds characters other than letters, digits and underscores. MissingInputException in rule blob_json ... (from Snakemake) The screen runs, and nodes.dmp or names.dmp is missing from directories.blast_db. When the folder itself is missing, [FunFlux] NOTE: directories.blast_db '<path>' does not exist on this machine; ... comes first. Correct the path, or unpack the NCBI taxonomy dump into that folder (see Reference databases).

docs.title: Screen, masking and BUSCO settings
docs.text:
These messages concern the settings of the screen, of repeat masking, of BUSCO and of the contig summary.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.mode: must be one of off | include | exclude (got: <value>) Another word. Use one of the three. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.mode: 'auto' is not available in FunFlux. BLAST genus labels are unreliable for poorly sequenced fungi, so auto can remove most of the genome. Use off (the default), read contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, then exclude the contaminant genera or include the genera that BLAST assigned to the isolate's own contigs. mode: auto, which FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL and FunFluxL+ had, is removed, for the reasons given on Configuration. Use off. To filter, use exclude or include as the message says. [FunFlux] parameters.mitochondria.mode: must be one of off | report | separate_confirmed (got: <value>) Another word, or true or yes, which YAML reads as true. An unquoted off is accepted. Use one of the three. [FunFlux] parameters.masking_method: must be tantan | repeatmodeler_repeatmasker (got: <value>) Another word. Use one of the two. [FunFlux] parameters.busco.lineage: must be 'auto' or a BUSCO lineage name such as hypocreales_odb12 (got: <value>). ... A lineage name must end in _odb and a number. busco --list-datasets prints each name with its version after a dot, such as hypocreales_odb12.2, and the dot and the number after it are not part of the name. Write auto, or a name such as hypocreales_odb12. [FunFlux] parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif: must be auto (the unit is chosen from the data) or the telomere repeat unit of the species, 4 to 30 letters A, C, G and T, such as TTAGGG (got: <value>) A value that is neither auto nor a plain unit. It may hold a character other than A, C, G and T, for example an IUPAC code such as N, a bracket or a digit. It may also be shorter than 4 or longer than 30 letters. Write auto, or the unit in plain letters. The known units are listed on Contig summary. [FunFlux] parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256: must be the SHA-256 checksum of the telomere database file, 64 hexadecimal characters (got: <value>) A shortened or mistyped checksum. Copy the 64 characters from config/config.yaml or, for another version of the database, the ones sha256sum prints for that file (see Telomere repeat database). [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.sample_overrides: sample '<sample>' has mode 'auto' in '<path>'. Mode auto is not available in FunFlux. BLAST genus labels are unreliable ... (the rest as in the auto message above) auto in the mode column of the override table. Write off, include, exclude or nothing in that cell. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.sample_overrides: sample '<sample>' has mode '<mode>' in '<path>'; the mode column must be off, include, exclude or blank (blank keeps the run-wide mode). Another word in the mode column. Every row is checked, including the rows of samples outside the batch. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.sample_overrides: sample '<sample>' has discard_no_hit '<value>' in '<path>'; the discard_no_hit column must be true or false (also yes/no, on/off, 1/0) or blank (blank keeps the run-wide setting). Another word in the discard_no_hit column of a sample of the batch. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.<key>: '<path>' is not an existing file. include_genera_by_sample, exclude_genera_file or sample_overrides names a file that does not exist. A relative path is read from the launch folder. Correct the path, or use an absolute one. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.<key>: '<path>' is not UTF-8 text. Save it again as plain text with UTF-8 encoding. The file has another encoding, for example a table that a spreadsheet program saved as UTF-16. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination.<key>: '<path>' must start with a tab-separated header line that has the columns sample and genus (missing: <columns>). (sample and mode for sample_overrides) The first line lacks a column name, or the columns are separated by spaces. Start the table with the column names, separated by tabs. [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination: mode include keeps only the genera you name, but no genus is given for sample(s) <samples>. Name the genus in include_genera, in include_genera_by_sample (one row per sample) or in the include_genera column of sample_overrides. include is set, run-wide or in sample_overrides, for samples without a genus.

The two decontamination.mode messages can stop any run. The checks of the decontamination files and of include without a genus run only when the screen runs, after the checks of the input folder and of the annotation table.

docs.title: GeneMark-ES settings
docs.text:
These messages concern GeneMark-ES and its licence key.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] parameters.genemark.mode: must be auto | off (got: <value>) Another word. An empty value (mode: or mode: "") means auto. Write auto or off. [FunFlux] directories.genemark_dir: must be an absolute path when GeneMark is enabled. A relative path. Use an absolute path. [FunFlux] directories.genemark_dir: '<dir>' has no executable gmes_petap.pl. Wrong folder, or the script lacks execute permission. Point at the folder that holds gmes_petap.pl, or make it executable (chmod u+x). [FunFlux] GeneMark is enabled but there is no licence key at <home>/.gm_key. ... GeneMark-ES is on (directories.genemark_dir set, genemark.mode: auto), but the user running Snakemake has no ~/.gm_key. Install the key (see Licensed and external tools), or set parameters.genemark.mode: off.

docs.title: Tiberius settings
docs.text:
These messages concern Tiberius, which is on by default, and the download of its model.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] parameters.tiberius.mode: must be on | off (got: <value>) Another word. An empty value means on. Write on or off. [FunFlux] parameters.tiberius.model_sha256: expected the SHA-256 checksum of the model archive, 64 characters 0-9 and a-f (got: <value>) A shortened or mistyped checksum. Copy the 64 characters sha256sum prints, or leave the key out for the default. [FunFlux] links.tiberius_model_link: required, but it is missing or empty in the config. Tiberius is on (the default) and the link is not in the configuration, for example in a configuration written before Tiberius was added. Copy the line from config/config.yaml, or set parameters.tiberius.mode: off.

docs.title: SignalP 6 settings
docs.text:
These messages concern SignalP 6 and the DTU archive it is installed from.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] parameters.signalp6.mode: must be off | fast | slow | slow-sequential (got: <value>) Another word. Use one of the four. [FunFlux] files.signalp6_archive: required when parameters.signalp6.mode is not off. SignalP 6 is on without an archive. Name the DTU archive, or set mode: off. [FunFlux] files.signalp6_archive: must be an absolute path to the official DTU archive. A relative path. Use an absolute path. [FunFlux] files.signalp6_archive: '<path>' is not a readable file. Wrong path or permissions.

docs.title: AMR screen settings
docs.text:
These messages concern the AMR screen (the resistance-mutation screen), which runs ChroQueTas against the FungAMR database.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] parameters.amr.chroquetas: must be on | off (got: <value>) Another word. An empty value means off. Write on or off. [FunFlux] parameters.amr.mito_genetic_code: must be auto or the number of an NCBI genetic code: 1-6, 9-16 or 21-33 (got: <value>) Another word, or a number that is not an NCBI genetic code (7, 8 and 17-20 are none, and miniprot refuses them). An unquoted yes, no, on or off fails too, because YAML reads it as true or false. Write auto, or the number of the code (see Two runs). [FunFlux] parameters.amr.chroquetas_script_sha256: must be the SHA-256 checksum of ChroQueTas.sh, 64 hexadecimal characters (got: <value>) (or chroquetas_db_sha256: must be the SHA-256 checksum of the FungAMR database archive, ...) A shortened or mistyped checksum. Copy the 64 characters from config/config.yaml, or leave the key out for the default. [FunFlux] links.chroquetas_link: required, but it is missing or empty in the config. The AMR screen is on and the link is not in the configuration. Copy the line from config/config.yaml, or set parameters.amr.chroquetas: off.

docs.title: Read-based modes
docs.text:
These messages concern the read and assembly settings of the read-based modes. <mode> is longread or hybrid, and each of these blocks is checked only in its own mode. spades_kmers is checked in illumina and hybrid mode.

Message Cause Fix [FunFlux] parameters.spades_kmers: expected auto, or whole numbers separated by commas (got: <value>). A word other than auto, or a list with another separator. Write auto, or for example "21,33,55,77,99,127". [FunFlux] parameters.spades_kmers: every k must be odd and below 128, and the list ascending (got: <value>). An even k, a k below 1 or above 127, a k given twice, or a list out of order. [FunFlux] parameters.<mode>.assembler: must be hifiasm | flye (got: <value>) Another word. [FunFlux] parameters.<mode>.flye_input_mode: 'pacbio-hifi' is not a value any more. ... PacBio HiFi reads are recognised from the file name. Name the reads {sample}_pacbio.fastq.gz and set flye_input_mode: auto. [FunFlux] parameters.<mode>.flye_input_mode: must be auto | nano-raw | nano-hq (got: <value>) Another word. [FunFlux] parameters.<mode>.filtlong.target_bases: must be empty or a size such as 1500000000 or 1.5g (got: <value>) [FunFlux] parameters.<mode>.hifiasm.genome_size: must be empty or a size such as 40000000 or 40m (got: <value>) [FunFlux] parameters.<mode>.hifiasm.telomere_motif: must be empty or a DNA/IUPAC motif (got: <value>)

docs.title: Notes that announce a later failure
docs.text:
These NOTE lines do not stop the run. Each one warns of a problem that shows later, in a step or in the result.

Note What follows [FunFlux] NOTE: directories.eggnog_db '<path>' does not exist on this machine; ... eggnog_annotation fails. [FunFlux] NOTE: files.iprscan '<path>' does not exist on this machine; ... iprscan_annotation fails. [FunFlux] NOTE: GeneMark-ES is enabled and needs a valid, unexpired licence key at <home>/.gm_key. ... An expired key stops the run at genemark_check. [FunFlux] NOTE: sample name '<name>' is not a valid NCBI locus-tag prefix ... The run finishes, but the gene IDs cannot be submitted to GenBank as they are. A valid prefix is 3 to 12 letters or digits, starting with a letter.

directories.eggnog_db and files.iprscan are only tested for existence

An eggNOG folder without the data, or an InterProScan installation that does not start, passes these checks and fails when its rule runs.

docs.title: Failures while the workflow runs
docs.text: These messages come from single steps after the jobs have started. Each entry gives the message and its cause, and most also say what to do. The step's log holds the tool's own messages.

docs.title: GeneMark-ES licence
docs.text:
[FunFlux] GeneMark-ES refused to run because of its licence (key file <home>/.gm_key). The key has probably expired: request a new one from the GeneMark site, or set parameters.genemark.mode: off. See <log>.

Cause. Rule genemark_check ran GeneMark-ES on a slice of the masked genome, and the output mentioned the licence. The key in ~/.gm_key has most likely expired (see The licence check before gene prediction).

Fix. Download a new key from the GeneMark site and copy it to ~/.gm_key of the user who runs Snakemake. GeneMark's INSTALL file gives the two commands: gunzip gm_key.gz, then cp gm_key ~/.gm_key. Then run the same Snakemake command again.

To run without GeneMark-ES, set parameters.genemark.mode: off. Gene prediction, and every step after it, then runs again for the samples already predicted with GeneMark-ES.

[FunFlux] GeneMark-ES could not start from <dir>: the Perl named in the first line of gmes_petap.pl (GeneMark ships it as /usr/bin/perl, the computer's own) is missing or lacks a Perl module GeneMark needs. funannotate starts GeneMark the same way, so its gene prediction would fail too. Fix it once, in that folder: perl change_path_in_perl_scripts.pl '/usr/bin/env perl' (GeneMark's scripts then use the Perl of FunFlux's funannotate environment, which has the modules), or install the missing modules into that Perl, or set parameters.genemark.mode: off. See <log>.

Cause. The test output contained Can't locate, which means a missing Perl module, or bad interpreter, which means that the Perl named in the script's first line does not exist. The check starts gmes_petap.pl the way funannotate predict does, so the first line of the script chooses the Perl. GeneMark ships it as #!/usr/bin/perl, which often lacks GeneMark's modules. On a cluster, the compute nodes can have another /usr/bin/perl than the login node.

Fix. Run perl change_path_in_perl_scripts.pl "/usr/bin/env perl" once in the GeneMark folder. The scripts then use the Perl of the funannotate environment, which holds the modules.

[FunFlux] GeneMark-ES could not start from <dir> (a program or a file is missing). See <log>.

Cause. The test output contained command not found or No such file. logs/genemark_check_{sample}.log holds GeneMark's output and names what is missing.

Any other failure on the test slice, for example too little sequence to train on, is logged and the run continues.

docs.title: SignalP 6
docs.text:
[FunFlux] signalp6_annotation: SignalP 6 is not installed in the conda environment of this rule (the environment was probably rebuilt after SignalP 6 was installed). Delete the file <output_dir>/00.resources/signalp6/installation.json and run the workflow again, so that install_signalp6 installs SignalP 6 into the current environment.

Cause. SignalP 6 is installed into the signalp6 conda environment, and the record of that installation, installation.json, lives in the output folder. A run with another --conda-prefix, from another launch folder, or after .snakemake/conda/ was deleted gets a new environment without SignalP 6. The old record still keeps install_signalp6 from running again.

Fix. Delete 00.resources/signalp6/installation.json and run again. SignalP 6 and funannotate annotate then run again for every sample of the run.

When the installation itself fails, install_signalp6 stops with SignalP 6 installation failed: ... in logs/install_signalp6.log. The rest of the message names the cause:

The message continues with Cause and fix the supplied archive does not contain the '<mode>' model (...). Download the DTU archive for the selected mode. The archive holds the model of another mode. A fast archive such as signalp-6.0i.fast.tar.gz works only with mode: fast. Get the archive for the mode, or change the mode. configured archive_sha256 does not match the supplied archive (expected ..., observed ...) files.signalp6_archive names another file than the one the checksum was taken from. Check the path, or update parameters.signalp6.archive_sha256 with what sha256sum <archive> prints. archive_sha256 must be a 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest A typo in parameters.signalp6.archive_sha256. expected exactly one SignalP Python package ..., archive member has an unsafe path: ..., archive contains an unsupported link or special file: ... The file is not the archive as DTU distributes it. Use the downloaded file unchanged. the official archive did not install the signalp6 command The package installed without its command-line program. The pip output is above the message in the same log.

docs.title: InterProScan
docs.text:
A failed InterProScan job is started once more before the run stops, and logs/iprscan_annotation_{sample}.log keeps the last attempt only.

InterProScan is a Java program, and the memory it may use, its heap, is the -Xmx value on the java line at the end of interproscan.sh in your InterProScan installation. FunFlux does not change it, and resources.ram_gb does not reach it. If logs/iprscan_annotation_{sample}.log shows java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, raise -Xmx there. Keep it below the memory the machine can spare while eggNOG-mapper, antiSMASH and SignalP 6 run beside InterProScan.

After InterProScan ends, the rule checks that iprscan/interproscan_out.xml is complete and is an InterProScan result, and stops otherwise:

InterProScan XML validation failed for <path>: <reason>

Cause. InterProScan exited without an error but left a file that does not parse, or that is not an InterProScan result. Its own messages are above this line in the same log. A full disk is one cause to rule out, as the XML can be a few GB.

Fix. Run again. The rule deletes the old XML before it starts, so a stale file is never taken for a new result.

Could not find a *.proteins.fa file in <dir>/predict_results or update_results. means that funannotate predict wrote no protein file. Its messages are in logs/funannotate_prediction_{sample}.log.

docs.title: Tiberius
docs.text:
Rule tiberius_model downloads the Tiberius model, and tiberius_prediction runs Tiberius on each sample.

Message Log Cause and fix [FunFlux] tiberius_model: the file downloaded from <link> does not match parameters.tiberius.model_sha256, so it was NOT unpacked ... tiberius_model.log The download was cut short, or the authors replaced the model at the same address. Run again for a fresh download. If the checksum still differs, the model has changed, so check it and put its checksum into parameters.tiberius.model_sha256, or set parameters.tiberius.mode: off (see Tiberius model). curl: (6) Could not resolve host or another curl error tiberius_model.log No network access to bioinf.uni-greifswald.de (see Network access). the job ends with Killed, or Snakemake reports that tiberius_prediction was terminated without a Python error tiberius_prediction_{sample}.log The job ran out of memory, as Tiberius needs about 16 GB. Free memory, run fewer jobs at once, or set parameters.tiberius.mode: off.

docs.title: Telomere repeat database and tidk
docs.text:
Rule telomere_db downloads tidk's telomere repeat database, and telomere_units reads it when it chooses the telomere unit of each sample.

Message Log Cause and fix [FunFlux] telomere_db: the file downloaded from <link> does not match parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256, so it was NOT used ... telomere_db.log The download was cut short, or the link and the checksum do not belong together. The template address names one commit of the database repository, so the file behind it does not change. The download is kept as 00.resources/telomeres/telo_database_v2.tsv.failed. Run again for a fresh download. To accept a file you have looked at, put its checksum, which sha256sum <file> prints, into parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256. For another version of the database, set the link and its checksum together (see Telomere repeat database). curl: (6) Could not resolve host or another curl error telomere_db.log No network access to raw.githubusercontent.com (see Network access). [FunFlux] telomere_units: error: ... telomere_units_{sample}.log The script stopped on a missing input, a malformed database file or a tidk failure, and tidk's own message follows. A database file that does not parse means that the file at the link has changed. Delete 00.resources/telomeres/telo_database_v2.tsv and run again, and the checksum then says whether it is still the expected file.

docs.title: ChroQueTas (AMR screen)
docs.text:
With the AMR screen on, rule chroquetas_db downloads ChroQueTas and the FungAMR database, and amr_chroquetas runs for each sample.

Message Log Cause and fix [FunFlux] chroquetas_db: the file downloaded from <link> does not match parameters.amr.chroquetas_script_sha256, so it was NOT used ... (or ... parameters.amr.chroquetas_db_sha256, so it was NOT unpacked ...) chroquetas_db.log The download was cut short, or the link and the checksums do not belong together. The template address names one commit, so the files behind it do not change. The download is kept as 00.resources/chroquetas/ChroQueTas.sh.failed or db-v20250811.tgz.failed. Run again for a fresh download. For another version of ChroQueTas, set the link and both checksums together (see ChroQueTas and the FungAMR database). [FunFlux] chroquetas_db: the database archive from <link> holds no species folder ... chroquetas_db.log The link names a commit whose FungAMR_db/db-v20250811.tgz is not the database ChroQueTas expects. Use the template link. curl: (6) Could not resolve host or another curl error chroquetas_db.log No network access to raw.githubusercontent.com (see Network access). [FunFlux] amr_chroquetas: error: ... amr_chroquetas_{sample}.log The script stopped on a missing input file, a database folder without species folders, or a position list of the database (<target>.txt) that does not look like the one of ChroQueTas 1.0.1. It also stops on a path with a space, or when a ChroQueTas run left neither its summary file nor the message that no target could be extracted. The last 20 lines of ChroQueTas's log follow the message. A position list unlike that of ChroQueTas 1.0.1 means another version of the database, so use the template link and checksums. ChroQueTas cannot handle a path with a space, so move the output folder to a path without spaces. ChroQueTas also takes bash, grep -P and other shell commands from the machine, so check them as shown under Commands outside the conda environments.

docs.title: funannotate database
docs.text:
Rule funannotate_db downloads the funannotate database and unpacks it into directories.funannotate_db, and normalize_funannotate_db repairs the paths stored in it.

Message Log Cause and fix [FunFlux] funannotate_db: <archive> does not match its checksum file <sha256>, so it was NOT unpacked ... funannotate_db.log The download was cut short or damaged. Delete both files from directories.funannotate_db and run again. Both are then downloaded afresh. curl: (6) Could not resolve host or another curl error funannotate_db.log No network access to zenodo.org (see Network access). Download the funannotate database by hand on a machine with network access and unpack it into directories.funannotate_db, as described under Downloading it by hand. Then run again. A folder that holds funannotate-db-info.txt is not downloaded again. ERROR: Funannotate trained-species directory is missing: ..., ERROR: Funannotate database index is missing: ... normalize_funannotate_db.log directories.funannotate_db does not hold a complete, unpacked funannotate database. Point it at the folder that holds trained_species/ and funannotate-db-info.txt. If the path is right but the database is incomplete, delete funannotate-db-info.txt and run again, as in the next row. ERROR: Trained-species asset is missing after extraction: ..., ERROR: Database asset is missing after extraction for archived path: ... normalize_funannotate_db.log The unpacked database lacks files. Delete funannotate-db-info.txt from the database folder and run again. The archive kept there is then checked against its checksum and unpacked again, without a new download. ERROR: [Errno 13] Permission denied: ... normalize_funannotate_db.log The database folder is read-only and its stored paths still need repair. Make it writable for one run. Once the paths are right, this step only reads it.

Two runs repairing one funannotate database at once can damage it

Two runs repairing one database at the same time, or one database reached under two different paths, cause damage or repeated work. See Reference databases.

docs.title: BUSCO downloads
docs.text:
Where BUSCO's lineage data come from depends on parameters.busco.lineage. With auto, every BUSCO job needs network access, while a named lineage needs it once, on the computer that runs Snakemake (see BUSCO on compute nodes without internet).

Setting Download Without network access auto, the default every BUSCO job downloads the datasets for its sample into 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/busco_tmp/, which is deleted when the job ends, and samples do not share the download. A hypocrealean fungus fetches eukaryota_odb12 (29.1 MB), six placement files (8.3 MB) and hypocreales_odb12 (274.6 MB) the BUSCO job fails and the run stops, but --keep-going lets the other jobs finish. BUSCO's messages are in logs/completeness_{sample}.log a lineage, such as hypocreales_odb12 rule busco_data downloads it once per output folder into 00.resources/busco/, on the computer that runs Snakemake, and every BUSCO job reads it offline busco_data fails, and its messages are in logs/busco_data.log. The BUSCO jobs themselves need no network

With a named lineage, a failed download stops rule busco_data:

Message Log Cause and fix [FunFlux] busco_data: BUSCO did not download the lineage <lineage> (details in <log>). Check parameters.busco.lineage against the list that busco --list-datasets prints, or set it to auto. busco_data.log A name BUSCO's server does not know, or no network access to busco-data.ezlab.org.

When BUSCO publishes a newer dataset, a run with auto uses it, and its completeness figures can differ from an earlier run of the same genome. A named lineage stays at the release in 00.resources/busco/ for every later run into the same output folder.

docs.title: Medaka model
docs.text:
These messages apply to ONT samples in longread and hybrid mode. Rule check_medaka_model checks the Medaka model before the assembler starts. When the check fails, it prints its log, with the table of available models, to the console as well.

ERROR: Medaka could not infer a model from the reads: their FASTQ headers carry no basecaller tag, or one this Medaka version does not recognise. Set parameters.<mode>.medaka_model to one of the consensus models below (pick by your flowcell / device / accuracy), or to FALSE to skip Medaka.

ERROR: Configured medaka_model '<model>' is not available in this Medaka version.

Fix. Use one of these settings:

To Set name the model parameters.<mode>.medaka_model, for example parameters.longread.medaka_model: r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v4.3.0 skip Medaka parameters.<mode>.medaka_model: false fall back to the inferred model when a named one is not available parameters.<mode>.medaka_model_fallback_auto: true 
ERROR: Medaka model '<model>' exists, but its weights are not stored on this computer and could not be downloaded (Medaka downloads them from GitHub). ...

Cause. The check downloads the weights of a model Medaka does not ship, so that polishing needs no network, and it runs on the computer that runs Snakemake.

Fix. Start Snakemake on a computer with internet, which on a cluster is the login node. Otherwise name a model whose weights come with Medaka 2.2.2, r1041_e82_400bps_hac_v6.0.0 or r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v5.2.0, or set parameters.<mode>.medaka_model: false.

The Medaka model describes the other messages of the check, what auto needs in the read headers and how to look at them.

docs.title: Other stops in the shared stages
docs.text:
The steps below run in more than one mode, and each can stop the run. Where a row mentions the log, it is the log of the rule in the Rule column.

Message Rule Cause and fix [FunFlux] filter_contigs: no contig of <sample> is left (kept 0 of M records). ... filter_contigs In contigs mode, the FASTA is empty, or its headers are SPAdes-style and no contig reaches 500 bp and 2x coverage. The log says which filter ran. In illumina and hybrid mode, no SPAdes contig reached 500 bp and 2x coverage, so check spades/spades.log and the reads. [FunFlux] long_read_consensus: Medaka failed for sample <sample> with model '<model>' ... long_read_consensus Medaka itself failed, for example for lack of memory or on a damaged read file, after the model had passed check_medaka_model. Medaka's messages are in the same log. parameters.<mode>.medaka_model: false runs without polishing. the hifiasm rule stops after hifiasm finished, with no [FunFlux] line long_read_assembly hifiasm's primary graph holds no contig, so the step that turns it into assembly.fasta stopped the rule. hifiasm's own messages are in the log. No contigs were kept for sample '<sample>' with mode '<mode>'. ... select_contigs The decontamination policy removed every contig, for example include with a genus that BLAST never assigned. Snakemake deletes the outputs of the failed job, the decision table included. contaminants/bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt still shows the genus of every contig, and --keep-incomplete keeps the failed job's files. See Decontamination. Mode 'include' requires at least one genus. select_contigs decontamination.mode: include is set without a genus for the sample. The dry run stops on this first, with [FunFlux] parameters.decontamination: mode include keeps only the genera you name, ... (above), so the rule meets it only when a table was changed after the run started. ERROR: Mitochondrial split would leave an empty nuclear assembly. separate_mitochondria Every contig was confirmed mitochondrial, for example in a FASTA that holds only a mitogenome. Run it without the screen, or with mitochondria.mode: report. [FunFlux] its_windows: ITSx's fungal profile file .../ITSx_db/HMMs/F.hmm is missing or empty. Is the job running in its itsx conda environment (--sdm conda), with the pinned ITSx 1.1.3? its_windows The job did not run in the itsx environment, or that environment has no intact ITSx 1.1.3. Run with --sdm conda. If the run already does, delete that environment's folder, which --list-conda-envs shows, so that Snakemake builds it again from the pin file. [FunFlux] its_windows: no 5.8S profile found in .../ITSx_db/HMMs/F.hmm (no NAME line contains 58S). Does this ITSx version name its 5.8S profiles differently? its_windows The ITSx in the itsx environment is not the pinned 1.1.3. Delete that environment's folder, which --list-conda-envs shows, so that Snakemake builds it again from the pin file. RepeatModeler did not produce a usable repeat library. repeat_masking Neither {sample}_rm-families.fa nor consensi.fa.classified exists or holds sequence. RepeatModeler's messages are in the same log. masking_method: tantan does not use RepeatModeler. Not enough gene models <N> to train Augustus (200 required), exiting (in logs/funannotate_prediction_{sample}.log) funannotate_prediction Column 4 of the sample is empty, so funannotate trains AUGUSTUS, and BUSCO found fewer than 200 usable training genes. The assembly may be fragmented, or the fungus far from the BUSCO set (fungi has 290 genes). Name a stored AUGUSTUS model in column 4 (see The AUGUSTUS model), or use a BUSCO set closer to the fungus. Funannotate did not create annotations.secretome.txt from the supplied SignalP 6 results. funannotate_annotation funannotate annotate did not use the SignalP 6 table. Its messages are in the same log. any MultiQC error multiqc Unlike a failed QUAST report, a failed MultiQC report stops the run. See logs/multiqc.log.

docs.title: Messages that do not stop the run
docs.text:
After these messages the run goes on, so a finished run can still lack a result. The Log column says where each message is written.

Message Log Meaning [FunFlux] genome_assembly_evaluation: QUAST exited with an error for sample <sample>. ... genome_assembly_evaluation_{sample}.log QUAST is a report that no other step reads, so the run continues and the MultiQC page lacks the QUAST table for this sample. After fixing the cause, delete 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/ and run again. [FunFlux] map_evaluation: Qualimap exited with an error for sample <sample>. ... (in hybrid also map_guide_evaluation) map_evaluation_{sample}.log, map_guide_evaluation_{sample}.log Qualimap is a report, so the run continues and the MultiQC page lacks the mapping table for this sample. After fixing the cause, delete 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/qualimap/ (or guide/eval/qualimap/) and run again. [FunFlux] raw_long_read_qc: NanoPlot exited with an error for sample <sample>. ... (or filtered_long_read_qc) raw_long_read_qc_{sample}.log, filtered_long_read_qc_{sample}.log NanoPlot is a report, so the run continues and the MultiQC page lacks the read-QC row for this sample. After fixing the cause, delete 01.reads/{sample}/long/raw_qc/ (or filtered_qc/) and run again. [FunFlux] its_extraction: no 5.8S window was found in the genome of <sample> ... its_extraction_{sample}.log No 5.8S gene matched the 358 anchor profiles of ITSx. The ITS files are empty and {sample}_ITS_copies.txt holds only a comment line. A fungus whose 5.8S differs from all of them gives this result. No ITS1 sequence to classify for sample <sample> ... (or ITS2) its_classification_{sample}.log ITSx found none, or every record failed the length guard, which accepts ITS1 and ITS2 of 50-600 bp. {sample}_ITS_copies.txt lists the rejected records. [FunFlux] telomere_units <sample>: no telomere repeat identified (best candidate <UNIT>: <n> ends in the telomere orientation, <m> opposite) telomere_units_{sample}.log, and the console No unit reached 2 contig ends in the telomere orientation with more than twice as many as in the opposite one. telomere_unit.txt reads none, the telomere columns of the contig summary read 0, and chromosomes come out as nuclear_contig. This is usual in a fragmented assembly or in a yeast with irregular telomeres. Set parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif when the repeat is known (see Telomeres). [FunFlux] NOTE telomere_units <sample>: ... telomere_units_{sample}.log, and the console The chosen telomere unit is unknown to the literature and to the tidk database, or the unit set in parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif is not the unit the data favour. eval/telomere_candidates.tsv shows every unit with its score. [FunFlux] NOTE amr_chroquetas <sample>: ... amr_chroquetas_{sample}.log, and the console The species in column 2 of the annotation table matches no folder of the FungAMR database, so the sample is not screened. The NOTE names the folders of the same genus, if any. Correct the name when it is misspelt (see The species). 00.resources/chroquetas/species.txt lists the folders. Column 2 is also funannotate's species. A corrected name re-runs augustus_model_check, funannotate_prediction and everything after them, and it goes into the GenBank and GFF files and their names. Change it only when the new name is the right one for the annotation as well. WARNING: N genera each hold at least 5% of this assembly (...) select_contigs_{sample}.log A mixed culture, or one genome split across related genera by BLAST. Read contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv before trusting the assembly. WARNING: decontamination is discarding X% of the assembly (...) select_contigs_{sample}.log More than 20 % of the bases were removed. If the kept assembly looks incomplete but not contaminated, the contig selector most likely removed genome. GeneMark-ES stopped on the test slice (exit status N) but not because of its licence or installation; ... genemark_check_{sample}.log Gene prediction itself then decides whether GeneMark-ES suits the genome.

docs.title: On a cluster
docs.text:
Most stops on a cluster come from a value larger than a node or a partition allows, or from a compute node that cannot see a file or the internet. The step's log in logs/ and its Slurm log say which. How to run FunFlux on a cluster is described under On a cluster.

Message Cause Fix maximum number of parallel jobs/used nodes has to be specified for remote execution (use --jobs N with N being a number >= 1) --executor slurm without --jobs. Add --jobs N, the number of jobs Snakemake may keep queued at once. SLURM job submission failed. The error message was sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Requested node configuration is not available A job asks for more CPUs (resources.threads) or more memory (resources.ram_gb) than any node of the partition has. Lower the value to what sinfo -o "%n %c" shows for CPUs, or sinfo -o "%n %m" for memory in MB (see How the settings reach Slurm). sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Requested time limit is invalid (missing or exceeds some limit), or jobs that stay pending with the reason PartitionTimeLimit in squeue resources.runtime_hours is longer than the time limit of the partition. Lower it to what sinfo -o "%P %l" shows, or choose a partition with a longer limit through slurm_partition in --default-resources. SLURM-job '<id>' failed, SLURM status is: 'OUT_OF_MEMORY' The step used more memory than it asked for. The Error in rule <rule>: block names the step. For a heavy step, raise resources.ram_gb. The heavy steps are listed under How the settings reach Slurm. For a light step, raise mem_mb in --default-resources. SLURM-job '<id>' failed, SLURM status is: 'TIMEOUT' The step ran past its time limit. For a heavy or long step, raise resources.runtime_hours. For a light step, raise runtime in --default-resources. No wall time information given. ... and No job memory information ('mem_mb' or 'mem_mb_per_cpu') is given - submitting without. ... (warnings) The light steps ask for no time and no memory, so Slurm's defaults apply. Nothing, if those defaults are a few GB and an hour or more. Otherwise add --default-resources mem_mb=8000 runtime=240. MissingOutputException ... Missing files after 5 seconds. This might be due to filesystem latency. (or after 60 seconds) The shared storage shows a file on the login node a while after a compute node wrote it. Add --latency-wait 60, as in the Run A command. If it is already there, raise it, for example to 120. a dry run plans finished steps, or download_all -n plans downloads again, with the reason Software environment definition has changed since last execution The run uses another --conda-prefix than the one the steps ran with. Use the same --conda-prefix as before, from the same launch folder. BUSCO (completeness) fails on the compute nodes and logs/completeness_{sample}.log shows a failed download parameters.busco.lineage: auto needs internet in every BUSCO job. Name a lineage, and run download_all on the login node (see BUSCO on compute nodes without internet). [FunFlux] GeneMark is enabled but there is no licence key at <home>/.gm_key in a job's log The compute node does not see the key in the home folder. Copy ~/.gm_key to the home folder the compute nodes see (see The GeneMark-ES key). SSL certificate problem (curl) or CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED (BUSCO, antiSMASH) in a download log A network proxy re-signs HTTPS with an in-house certificate, and the conda environments trust only their own list. Export CURL_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE before starting Snakemake (see Behind a proxy that re-signs HTTPS).

docs.title: Citation and references
docs.text:
Use this page when you publish results from FunFlux. It gives the reference for FunFlux itself and for the v1 workflows. It then lists, stage by stage, the tools and databases a run can use, with their versions and the numbers of their references. The page ends with the acknowledgements, the full list of references and the works cited on Validation on public genomes.

Terms used on this page

concept DOI the Zenodo DOI shared by all versions of a record, which always leads to the newest; each version also has a DOI of its own contig filter rule filter_contigs: on SPAdes-style headers it drops contigs under 500 bp or 2x coverage; other headers are only cut at their first space or tab mitochondrion screen rule screen_mitochondria, part of the contamination and mitochondrion screen: it confirms mitochondrial contigs from BLAST hits to mitochondrial genomes and, in the long-read modes, the assembler's evidence contig selector rule select_contigs, the last step of the screen: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says; the default, off, keeps every contig ITS window the stretch cut around one 5.8S gene, 2,000 bp on each side by default, turned to read from SSU to LSU before ITSx runs contig summary the table 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv: one row per contig of the draft, with its evidence (telomeres, depth, rDNA units, genes) and a verdict AMR screen the optional resistance-mutation screen, off by default (parameters.amr.chroquetas), in which ChroQueTas looks in each genome for the changes FungAMR lists for the species funannotate database the frozen snapshot of funannotate's data, such as Swiss-Prot, Pfam, the BUSCO set and stored AUGUSTUS models, downloaded once from Zenodo into directories.funannotate_db

docs.title: Citing FunFlux
docs.text:
Antonielli, L., & Brader, G. (2026). FunFlux: Integrated workflow for fungal genome assembly and annotation (v2.0.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13612159

The DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13612159 is the concept DOI, which always resolves to the newest version. Each release also has a version DOI of its own on Zenodo. Cite the version DOI when the exact code matters.

The repository is https://github.com/iLivius/FunFlux, and the documentation is at https://iLivius.github.io/FunFlux/. FunFlux is released under the MIT License. See Licensing.

The contig filter, the mitochondrion screen, the contig selector and the ITS windows have no tool of their own to cite, so cite FunFlux for them. The contig filter of contigs mode, the contig selector and the layout of the workflow come from BacFlux, which is also released under the MIT License.

For the contig summary, tidk does the telomere search, so cite tidk with FunFlux. The papers behind FunFlux's table of telomere repeat units are listed in the Contig summary rows under Tools and databases.

The ChroQueTas authors ask to be cited through the FungAMR paper

The AMR screen runs ChroQueTas. As the ChroQueTas authors ask, cite FungAMR and ChroQueTas through the FungAMR paper (Bédard et al. 2025). Cite the tools ChroQueTas runs as well, which are listed in the AMR screen rows under Tools and databases.

docs.text:

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
FunFlux is released under the MIT License. The tools and databases it uses carry their own licences, and some of them restrict commercial use. This page lists those licences as they were read on the dates given, with the source of each.

The repository contains code and download addresses, and no third-party data. Every database is either one you downloaded yourself or one the workflow downloads on your machine, from an address in the links block of the configuration or with the tool's own download command.

Terms used on this page

AMR screen the optional resistance-mutation screen, off by default (parameters.amr.chroquetas), in which ChroQueTas looks in each genome for the changes FungAMR lists for the species FungAMR the database of amino-acid changes studied for resistance to antifungal drugs and fungicides, with evidence levels for and against member database one of the separate signature databases, such as Pfam, PROSITE and SMART, that InterProScan searches; each keeps its own licence terms CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 a Creative Commons licence: credit the authors, non-commercial use only, and no modified copies may be shared; ChroQueTas, FungAMR and PROSITE carry it share-alike a licence condition that copies you change or pass on keep the same licence; it does not apply to running the program the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the assembly: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true funannotate database the frozen snapshot of funannotate's data, such as Swiss-Prot, Pfam, the BUSCO set and stored AUGUSTUS models, downloaded once from Zenodo into directories.funannotate_db

For each component that restricts commercial use, the table below gives the restriction, when FunFlux uses the component and how to leave it out. GeneMark-ES, SignalP 6, Medaka and the AMR screen can each be left out with one setting, but PROSITE and SMART are searched in every run.

Component Restriction When FunFlux uses it How to leave it out GeneMark-ES royalty-free only for academic and non-profit institutions and US government agencies; the download goes through a registration form optional: only when directories.genemark_dir is set leave directories.genemark_dir empty, or set parameters.genemark.mode: off SignalP 6 downloaded by academic users only, through a registration form optional: only when parameters.signalp6.mode is not off parameters.signalp6.mode: off Medaka research purposes only polishes the assemblies of ONT samples in longread and hybrid mode medaka_model: false in parameters.longread or parameters.hybrid ChroQueTas and its FungAMR database CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use only, and no modified copies may be passed on the AMR screen, off by default; parameters.amr.chroquetas: on is your acceptance of the licence, and FunFlux then downloads both, unchanged, on your machine (Antifungal resistance mutations) keep the AMR screen off PROSITE and SMART, two of the member databases InterProScan searches commercial users of PROSITE pay a yearly licence fee; SMART is free for academic users only every InterProScan run: FunFlux starts InterProScan without -appl, so it runs every analysis the installation provides, these two included no configuration key leaves them out

Of the terms that could be checked, those in the table above are the only ones that limit who may use a component. No terms could be found for dbCAN, the eggNOG 5.0.2 data, the Tiberius fungi model and the tidk telomere repeat database, and MIBiG's licence comes only from a registry entry. The terms of the databases antiSMASH downloads, and of the member databases InterProScan searches other than Pfam, PROSITE and SMART, were not checked.

The next table gives the licences of the tools and databases FunFlux uses. The Conditions column lists restrictions on who may use a component and what its licence asks of you: registration, citation, share-alike. A dash means none of these.

Running FunFlux places no share-alike duty on you

Share-alike applies when you modify or redistribute a program, not when you run it. Under the AGPL and the Open Software License (OSL), it also applies when others use a modified copy over a network.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
This page explains why FunFlux is built as it is. One workflow takes four kinds of input, and only its front end depends on the mode. The page also explains why the mitochondrial genome is kept out of the nuclear genome. Read it to understand what the mode key changes and what it leaves the same.

Terms used on this page

front end the steps that differ by mode, chosen by mode: read processing, assembly and contig filter before the screen, and polishing after it the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true draft assembly (the draft) the assembly the screen examines, before any contig is removed: contigs_filt.fasta in illumina mode and in contigs mode with the screen, assembly.fasta in longread and hybrid guide assembly in hybrid mode, the SPAdes assembly of the Illumina reads; it is screened, and only the pairs that map to it go on coverage track the reads aligned back to the draft, contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, from which BlobTools takes each contig's coverage; in contigs mode, the contigs aligned to themselves genus filter the setting parameters.decontamination.mode: include or exclude, under which the contig selector keeps or removes contigs by the genus BlobTools gave them confirmed mitochondrial contig a contig the mitochondrion screen classes confirmed_mitochondrial; with the default separate_confirmed, it is kept whatever its genus and moved to contigs_mitochondrial.fasta nuclear genome the delivered genome without the confirmed mitochondrial contigs, contigs_final.fasta; it holds every contig when nothing is split off (no screen, or parameters.mitochondria.mode off or report)

docs.title: One workflow instead of four
docs.text: FunFlux 2.0.0 joins four earlier workflows into one, and the mode key chooses which kind of input it starts from. Coming from v1 lists what changed for a v1 user.

docs.title: What is shared and what depends on the mode
docs.text:
Only the front end differs between the modes:

Part Steps Front end: differs by mode read QC, read filtering, assembly and the contig filter before the screen, and polishing after it; in hybrid also the Illumina guide assembly, its own screen, and the selection of the Illumina read pairs for Polypolish and, only with short_read_guidance: true (off by default), for Filtlong on ONT samples Shared: the same in every mode the contamination and mitochondrion screen, the split into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, QUAST and BUSCO, the contig summary, the ITS extraction and classification, repeat masking, gene prediction, functional annotation, the AMR screen and the MultiQC report

From the screen on, every mode runs the same code, and only polishing differs between the read-based modes. The stage folders, 02.assembly to 06.report, have the same names in every mode. Where a shared step depends on the data, it follows what the run has. The coverage track of the screen, for example, comes from the reads the run has, or from the contigs themselves in contigs mode, as described on Decontamination.

The long-read technology is not a mode of its own. It is a property of each sample, read from the file name (_ont or _pacbio), so one longread or hybrid batch can hold both. See One technology per sample.

docs.title: Why the mitochondrion is kept out of the nuclear genome
docs.text:
In every mode the assembly stage ends with 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta, and QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS extraction and funannotate read that file. The mitochondrial genome has to stay out of these steps, because fungal mitochondria use a different genetic code. The mitochondria of most fungi use code 4, in which UGA codes for tryptophan instead of stop, and those of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and related yeasts use code 3. On a mitochondrial contig, the nuclear gene predictors would call false genes.

contigs_final.fasta is the nuclear genome alone when the screen runs with the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed. Otherwise it holds every contig, a mitochondrion included.

The steps that set the mitochondrion apart run in this order:

  1. The mitochondrion screen runs on the draft assembly.
  2. With the default separate_confirmed, the confirmed mitochondrial contigs are protected from the genus filter, because BLAST can assign a fungal mitochondrion to another genus.
  3. Polishing comes next, in the long-read modes only. In longread, Medaka polishes the screened assembly of ONT samples unless medaka_model: false switches it off, and PacBio HiFi samples are not polished. In hybrid, Polypolish runs for every sample, after Medaka for ONT samples with Medaka on.
  4. Only after that are the contigs split into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, so the mitochondrion is polished together with the rest wherever a sample is polished. contigs_all.fasta keeps the two together.

See Mitochondria for the mitochondrion screen.

docs.title: Validation on public genomes
docs.text:
This page shows what FunFlux 2.0.0 produced on two public genomes, and how to repeat the runs. Read it to see, on real data, what each read-based mode delivers and how much the gene-finder settings change the annotation.

Botrytis cinerea strain B05.10 was run from ONT and Illumina reads in the three read-based modes, illumina, longread and hybrid. Five comparison runs then annotated the genome of its hybrid run again in contigs mode. Cordyceps cateniannulata strain GXU-8616 was run from PacBio HiFi reads, alone and with MGISEQ short reads (PacBio HiFi reads).
