Flye has run in longread mode on both genomes but not in hybrid mode, where every run used hifiasm, the default assembler. The results are measurements on these two genomes, so read the limitations below before the numbers.

Terms used on this page

Tiberius a deep-learning gene finder with a fungi model its authors trained on many fungal genomes; on by default, it adds its gene models to funannotate's evidence annotation parameter table the tab-separated file named by files.annotation_params, one row per sample: name, species, a protein FASTA of related fungi and, optionally, an AUGUSTUS model protein evidence proteins aligned to the genome to support the gene models: the FASTA in column 3 of the annotation table, plus UniProt Swiss-Prot, always added stored AUGUSTUS model the AUGUSTUS parameters trained earlier for one species, kept in trained_species/ of the funannotate database; named in column 4, they are used as they are telomere array tandem copies of the telomere repeat unit at a contig end; by default 5 or more copies within 25,000 bp of the end make a telomere contig summary the table 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv: one row per contig of the draft, with its evidence (telomeres, depth, rDNA units, genes) and a verdict such as chromosome or rDNA_array concatemer a contig of two or more copies of the mitochondrial genome joined end to end; flagged (concatemer_flag Y) unless the assembler reports it circular, never trimmed MGISEQ a short-read sequencer from MGI Tech (DNBSEQ technology) that produces paired reads like Illumina's; FunFlux ran such reads as Illumina pairs

The numbers record what FunFlux does on a well-studied genome, not its accuracy on a new one

  • One genome for ONT and Illumina reads (n = 1). Nothing here shows how FunFlux does with ONT or Illumina reads of other fungi. The HiFi runs, on another genome, have their own limitations (below).
  • Tiberius has seen genes of this species. B. cinerea is one of the species the Tiberius fungi model was trained on (its training list). What Tiberius adds here may be more than it adds on a species it has not seen.
  • A stored AUGUSTUS model for B. cinerea, botrytis_cinerea, is in the funannotate database. Only one comparison run used it. Every other run trained AUGUSTUS on the genome's own BUSCO genes.
  • The protein evidence given to funannotate was the reference annotation's own 13,703 proteins, beside UniProt Swiss-Prot, which FunFlux always adds and which holds 194 reviewed B05.10 proteins. It pulls the gene models towards the reference. The agreement with the reference is therefore an upper bound, not what a new species gets with proteins of related fungi. Every run had the same evidence, so the runs stay comparable with each other.
  • The reference annotation is not a perfect answer key. NCBI lists it as submitted by Syngenta Biotechnology, Inc. and carried into RefSeq on 2018-04-17 by its annotation propagation pipeline. The RefSeq records are marked provisional (not yet given final NCBI review). The genome paper, whose authors include Syngenta staff, predicted the genes, used RNA-seq of more than 20 samples to check and improve them, and curated chromosome 1 by hand (van Kan et al. 2017). A FunFlux gene that differs from the reference is not necessarily wrong.
  • Run times come from one shared server, with other runs going on at the same time, so they are indicative only.

docs.title: What this page is
docs.text:
The page is a record of what FunFlux 2.0.0 produced in these runs, with their settings. It checks that each mode gives a sensible genome and gene set, and it measures how much two annotations of the same genome, with the same gene-finder settings, differ. It is not a benchmark, because it has one genome per read type and one replicate. Nor is it a comparison with other tools or pipelines, or a measure of accuracy on a species the gene finders have not seen.

B05.10 was chosen because it has a gapless genome, a gene set and public reads of the strain itself. The assembly, the genes, the mitochondrion and the β-tubulin change can therefore be set against published records:

  • A gapless reference genome, which its authors call near-finished: 18 chromosomes in 18 sequences without gaps, 42.6 Mb.
  • A reference annotation of 11,698 protein-coding genes.
  • Public reads of the strain: ONT reads from the reference's own sample record, and Illumina pairs of a lab stock.
  • Features to check: telomeres at both ends of 10 of the 18 reference chromosomes (van Kan et al. 2017), and the β-tubulin change E198A, which the reference protein carries too (AMR worked example).

docs.title: Data and settings
docs.text:
The B05.10 runs used the public reference of the strain and two public read sets. Depth is the number of bases divided by the reference length.

Data Accession Details Used by Reference genome and annotation GCF_000143535.2 (assembly ASM14353v4) 18 chromosomes, 42,630,066 bp, PacBio reads assembled in 2015; 11,698 protein-coding genes with 13,703 mRNAs and proteins (RefSeq, 2018) its proteins: column 3 of the annotation parameter table in every run; its genome and genes: the comparisons on this page ONT reads SRR40741277 PromethION, 315,306 reads, 5.79 Gb (about 136x); BioSample SAMN02953628, the reference's own longread 136x (hifiasm and Flye), hybrid ONT subsample the first 95,000 reads of SRR40741277 1.78 Gb (about 42x) longread 42x + Medaka Illumina reads SRR10692911 HiSeq 2000, 11,963,877 pairs, reads of up to 150 bp, 3.35 Gb (about 79x); BioSample SAMN13563037, a stock named B05.10-1 illumina, hybrid

The ONT reads come from the same sample record as the reference. The Illumina reads come from another lab's stock of the strain, so a few real differences between the two stocks are possible.

The public ONT file names no basecaller model, so Medaka cannot work its model out: with auto, it reads the model from the read headers (The Medaka model). The two 136x runs and the hybrid run therefore skip Medaka. The 42x run names a model, r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v5.2.0, which is a guess, because the flow cell and the basecaller are not known.

In the next table, the five mode runs are those in illumina, longread and hybrid mode, and the five comparison runs are the annotations in contigs mode. The table lists the settings that differ from the configuration template, apart from paths: the input and output folders, the databases, the annotation table, InterProScan and the SignalP 6 archive. Keys missing from the run configurations took their defaults.

Setting Template default The five mode runs The five comparison runs mode illumina longread (three times), illumina, hybrid contigs, on the hybrid run's contigs_final.fasta assembler (under longread or hybrid) hifiasm hifiasm; flye in one 136x run not used medaka_model (under longread or hybrid) auto false (the two 136x runs and hybrid); r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v5.2.0 (42x) not used short_read_guidance (under hybrid) false true in the hybrid run: Filtlong guided by the Illumina reads, with filtlong_split: 1000 not used resources.threads 24 16 to 32 (the run-time table below) 20 resources.ram_gb 128 256 256 directories.genemark_dir empty: no GeneMark-ES a GeneMark-ES installation, so GeneMark-ES on the same, but genemark.mode: off in two runs parameters.tiberius.mode on on on, but off in two runs parameters.signalp6.mode off fast fast parameters.amr.chroquetas off on off Annotation table, column 3 (proteins) proteins of related fungi the reference's own proteins the same Annotation table, column 4 (AUGUSTUS model) -: trained on the genome - -, but botrytis_cinerea in one run

One of these changes shapes every gene result of the B05.10 runs: column 3 of the annotation table gave the reference's own proteins as evidence (see the limitations above). The other changes concern the mode, the assembler, the Medaka model, the Filtlong guidance of the hybrid run, and the CPU and memory. Three optional tools were also switched on: GeneMark-ES, SignalP 6 and the AMR screen. The five comparison runs, in addition, each changed one gene-finder setting, or two (the run with neither GeneMark-ES nor Tiberius), or none (the replicate).

docs.title: Assembly per mode
docs.text:
The first table sets the genome of each mode run against the 18 chromosomes of the reference. Every run with long reads used hifiasm, the default assembler, except the one marked Flye, which ran Flye 2.9.6 with --nano-hq, as flye_input_mode: auto chose.

Run Contigs Total length (Mb) N50 (Mb) Chromosomes in one contig (of 18) Share of each chromosome covered (%) Contigs with telomeres at both ends Reference (GCF_000143535.2) 18 42.63 2.62 18 – 10 (van Kan et al. 2017) longread, ONT 136x 32 44.04 2.58 18 99.8 to 100 15 longread, ONT 136x, Flye 25 42.95 2.58 16 99.8 to 100 6 longread, ONT 42x + Medaka 18 42.97 2.63 18 99.8 to 100 14 illumina, Illumina 79x 409 42.23 0.31 0 96.0 to 99.8 0 hybrid, ONT 136x + Illumina 79x 33 44.05 2.63 18 99.8 to 100 14

On B05.10, the three hifiasm runs with long reads put each of the 18 chromosomes into one contig and cover almost all of each. Flye, on the same 136x reads, is as contiguous (N50 2.58 Mb), but puts 16 chromosomes into one contig and ends fewer contigs in a telomere array. The Illumina-only run gives 409 contigs, no chromosome in one piece, and leaves up to 4 % of a chromosome uncovered.

  • Contigs and length are those of contigs_final.fasta, the nuclear genome, from QUAST. The hifiasm 136x and hybrid assemblies are 1.4 Mb longer than the reference. Most of the extra length is in 13 contigs that the contig summary calls rDNA_array (0.98 Mb in the hifiasm 136x run, 0.78 Mb in the hybrid run), which are pieces of the rDNA array. The 42x and Flye runs have no such contigs.
  • The Flye run has chromosomes 1 and 13 in two pieces each (2.72 and 1.39 Mb; 1.95 and 0.31 Mb). Its genome is 0.32 Mb longer than the reference.
  • Telomeres come from FunFlux's contig summary: arrays of the repeat unit it chose, AACCCT, at both contig ends. AACCCT is tidk's canonical form of TTAGGG, the same repeat read on the other strand. The hifiasm long-read runs have 14 or 15 such contigs, and in each, 3 or 4 more chromosomes lack an array at one end. In the Flye run, 23 contig ends carry an array, against 32 to 34 in the hifiasm long-read runs. The reference's 10 comes from its paper, not from FunFlux's search, so it is not the same measure.
  • Filtlong guidance was on in the hybrid run. The unguided longread 136x run, on the same ONT reads, has 32 contigs against 33, and all 18 chromosomes in one contig in both. That is one reason the guidance is off by default (Filtlong guidance).

The second table gives the differences of each assembly from the reference, and the run time.

Run Substitutions per Mb Small indels per Mb Run time (h) Cores longread, ONT 136x 38.9 36.2 8.9 28 longread, ONT 136x, Flye 35.8 33.4 8.4 20 longread, ONT 42x + Medaka 37.9 30.9 9.2 16 illumina, Illumina 79x 14.8 12.2 7.9 24 hybrid, ONT 136x + Illumina 79x 32.0 23.5 11.5 32

Every assembly differs from the reference by 15 to 39 substitutions and 12 to 36 small indels per Mb. In the long-read assemblies most substitutions sit in a few regions, and in every run most small indels sit in runs of identical bases. Each run took 8 to 12 hours.

  • Substitutions are not spread out. In each long-read assembly more than 90 % of them fall in ten windows of 10 kb of the reference. They mark a few regions where the assembly and the reference disagree, not errors along the whole genome.
  • Small indels, of 1 to 10 bp, are spread out. In every run three quarters or more of them (77 to 86 %) sit in a run of at least 3 identical bases of the reference. The hybrid assembly, corrected with the Illumina reads by Polypolish, has about a third fewer than the hifiasm 136x assembly without Medaka. The 42x run with Medaka also differs from the hifiasm 136x run in depth, so it does not measure Medaka alone, while Medaka on the 42x run does. The Illumina contigs differ least, but they cover less of each chromosome.
  • Not an error rate. Some of these differences may be errors of the reference itself or real differences between lab stocks. The counts compare the runs with each other.
  • Run time is that of the main Snakemake run, from its log. In the four runs without Flye, the ITS classification, the contig summary and the AMR screen were run afterwards on the finished output. They took under a minute each, so the times above leave out at most a few minutes.

To count the chromosomes and the differences, each contigs_final.fasta was aligned to the reference with minimap2 2.31 (-x asm5 -c --cs). A contig is placed on the chromosome that most of its bases align to, and a chromosome counts as one contig when the largest contig placed on it is at least 97 % of its length. The share of each chromosome covered counts alignments with a mapping quality of at least 5. Differences are counted in the alignments with a mapping quality of at least 30, per Mb of aligned contig.

docs.title: Medaka on the 42x run
docs.text:
The 42x run keeps both the assembly that Medaka polished (contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta) and Medaka's result (medaka/consensus.fasta). Medaka can therefore be measured alone, on the same reads and the same assembly, before and after. QUAST 5.3.0 compared both with the reference, and BUSCO 6.0.0 scored both, and the reference, with ascomycota_odb12.

Before Medaka After Medaka Reference Indels 1,879 1,590 – of them up to 5 bp 1,717 1,458 – of them longer 162 132 – Mismatches 1,684 1,698 – Contigs, misassemblies, genome fraction 19, 30, 99.98 % the same – BUSCO complete (of 2,826) 99.2 % 99.2 % 99.3 % BUSCO genes with internal stop codons 483 479 482

Medaka removed 289 indels, 15 %, most of them 5 bp or shorter, and added 14 mismatches. The number of contigs and of misassemblies, the genome fraction and the BUSCO completeness did not change. The BUSCO genes with internal stop codons went from 483 to 479, but Medaka's gain is too small to show in the genes. The reference itself has as many such genes (482), so that count measures BUSCO's alignments, not the assembly. Medaka took 15 minutes on 12 threads.

  • The model, r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v5.2.0, is a guess, because the public reads carry no basecaller tag in their headers. The reads look like R10.4.1 reads called with a "sup" model (median identity to the reference 98.97 %, median read quality Q20.5, on 20,000 reads), so the guess is plausible.
  • These counts are QUAST's, over all aligned bases. The table of differences under Assembly per mode counts differently (minimap2, mapping quality of at least 30, indels of 1 to 10 bp), so the two tables cannot be compared number for number.

docs.title: Gene models per mode
docs.text:
The gene models of each mode run were set against the reference annotation, to see how much the assembly changes the genes.

Run Protein-coding genes BUSCO complete (of 1,312) Reference genes found FunFlux genes that match Matching genes Reference (RefSeq) 11,698 – – – – longread, ONT 136x 11,802 1,301 (99.2 %) 90.4 % 89.7 % 10,591 longread, ONT 136x, Flye 11,760 1,302 (99.2 %) 90.2 % 89.8 % 10,560 longread, ONT 42x + Medaka 11,778 1,301 (99.2 %) 90.1 % 89.6 % 10,554 illumina, Illumina 79x 11,704 1,302 (99.2 %) 90.4 % 90.5 % 10,590 hybrid, ONT 136x + Illumina 79x 11,830 1,301 (99.2 %) 90.7 % 89.8 % 10,623

On B05.10, the assembly mode and the assembler made little difference to the genes

The runs predict 11,704 to 11,830 protein-coding genes, and 10,554 to 10,623 of them match a reference gene: a spread of 69, under 1 % of the genes.

  • BUSCO complete is the number of BUSCO dikarya_odb9 genes found complete among the predicted proteins, as funannotate annotate reports it. The five runs differ by at most one BUSCO gene.
  • Reference genes found is the share of the reference's gene loci with a matching FunFlux gene (gffcompare's locus sensitivity). FunFlux genes that match is the share of FunFlux genes with a matching reference gene (locus precision). Both are about 90 % in every run.
  • A match means that the coding part of the FunFlux gene has the same introns as a reference transcript, while its start and stop may differ. A gene without introns matches when the two overlap almost completely.
  • tRNA genes, 211 in every run, are left out of all counts.

To compare the genes, Liftoff 1.6.3 carried the reference genes onto the genome FunFlux annotated: all 11,698 of them, but 11,697 onto the Illumina assembly. Then gffcompare 0.12.10 compared the coding parts of the two gene sets (Shumate & Salzberg 2021; Pertea & Pertea 2020). These tools were used for this page only and are not part of FunFlux.

docs.title: Repeated runs and the gene finders
docs.text:
To tell run-to-run noise from the effect of each gene finder, one genome was annotated six times: the hybrid run, and five contigs-mode runs on its contigs_final.fasta. The five ran at the same time, each with 20 CPU threads instead of the hybrid run's 32. All six annotated the same masked genome, byte for byte. The default run used Tiberius, GeneMark-ES and AUGUSTUS trained on the genome.

Run What changed, besides the mode and the threads Protein-coding genes Genes identical to the default run Matching genes Matching genes, difference from the default Default (the hybrid run) – 11,830 – 10,623 – Replicate nothing 11,825 11,718 10,619 −4 No GeneMark-ES genemark.mode: off 11,834 11,253 10,590 −33 No Tiberius tiberius.mode: off 11,729 10,494 10,257 −366 Neither both off; AUGUSTUS, SNAP and GlimmerHMM remain 11,503 9,528 9,630 −993 Stored AUGUSTUS model annotation table, column 4: botrytis_cinerea 11,934 11,277 10,694 +71

In these runs, two annotations of the same genome with the same gene-finder settings differ at about 1 % of the genes, but by only 4 matching genes. Differences of a few hundred genes are therefore unlikely to be noise. Tiberius matters most: without it about 3 % of the matching genes are lost, and about 9 % without both Tiberius and GeneMark-ES. GeneMark-ES on its own makes a small difference (33 genes), which one replicate cannot separate from noise. The stored B. cinerea AUGUSTUS model adds 71. Read these numbers with the head start described in the note below.

  • The replicate. 112 of the 11,830 genes of the default run differ in the replicate. The matches lost (38) and gained (34) almost cancel, hence the difference of 4.
  • Noise. One replicate is one measurement of the run-to-run noise, not its range, and it holds any effect of the thread count as well.
  • The stored AUGUSTUS model is AUGUSTUS's model for B. cinerea itself.
  • Identical means the same coding intervals: every exon, the start and the stop. Run-to-run differences explains which steps differ between runs with the same input and settings, and why.
  • Run time. Each comparison run took 7.6 to 9.5 h.

Tiberius and the stored AUGUSTUS model had a head start on this species

Tiberius was trained on B. cinerea among many other fungi, and the stored AUGUSTUS model is a B. cinerea model. Both may therefore add more here than on a species they have not seen. Every run also had the reference's own proteins as evidence, which brings all runs closer to the reference and may hide part of what the gene finders add. These runs are consistent with Tiberius being on by default and GeneMark-ES being optional (Gene prediction), but they do not measure what Tiberius adds on a new species.

docs.title: Other results
docs.text:
The ITS taxonomy and the AMR screen gave the same result in all five mode runs, so in these runs they depend neither on the mode nor on the assembler:

  • ITS taxonomy. The main ITS2 sequence gives the genus Botrytis (confidence 0.99) and the species B. caroliniana (0.83), not the strain's species. The main ITS1 sequence stops at the family Sclerotiniaceae (0.93). See ITS taxonomy.
  • AMR screen. It finds β-tubulin E198A, with the verdict resistance (carbendazim, iprodione). Bos1 and OS1 are wild type, and cytochrome b is not evaluated. See the worked example of the AMR page.

The mitochondrion was found in every run (Mitochondria). The next table gives it per run, with the verdicts of the contig summary (worked example).

Per run longread 136x longread 136x, Flye longread 42x + Medaka illumina hybrid Mitochondrial contigs, in contigs_mitochondrial.fasta (bp) 82,351, circular 82,338, circular 116,252: a full copy with 34 kb repeated at its ends 82,466, plus three pieces of 572 to 1,139 175,274: about two copies, flagged as a concatemer Contig summary: chromosome 15 6 14 0 14 chromosome_arm 3 11 4 10 4 rDNA_array 13 0 0 0 13 nuclear_contig 0 6 0 260 0 nuclear_fragment 0 0 0 31 0 repeat 0 0 0 73 0 low_depth 1 1 0 34 2 unclassified 0 1 0 1 0 mitochondrion 1 1 1 4 1 All contigs 33 26 19 413 34

Only the two 136x longread runs give the mitochondrion as one circular contig of about the published length: 82,351 and 82,338 bp, against the published 82,212 bp (KC832409). A later hybrid run on the same reads, with the guidance off (the default) and with Medaka, gave the same circular contig as the longread 136x run, 82,351 bp in the draft and 82,375 bp after polishing: without the guidance, Filtlong passed hifiasm the same ONT reads. The concatemer of the hybrid run in the table therefore came from the guided reads, not from hybrid mode.

In the contig summary, every hifiasm run with long reads has 18 contigs that are chromosome or chromosome_arm, one per chromosome. The Flye run has 17 such contigs, some of them small pieces, and six nuclear_contigs with no telomere array: five of 2.0 to 3.0 Mb and one of 7.6 kb. The Illumina contigs are mostly nuclear_contig, with no telomere at both ends.

The contig summary describes the draft assembly, before the mitochondrion is split off and before polishing. Each run therefore counts its mitochondrial contigs (one, or four in illumina) on top of the nuclear contigs of the assembly table. The contig summary also lists the 42x and hybrid mitochondria at their draft lengths, 116,228 and 174,832 bp.

docs.title: PacBio HiFi reads: Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616
docs.text:
Three runs used PacBio HiFi reads of one strain of an insect-pathogenic fungus (family Cordycipitaceae). Two ran in longread mode, one with hifiasm, the default assembler, and one with Flye. The third ran in hybrid mode, which adds MGISEQ short reads of the same strain. On this genome the runs show that the HiFi path works from reads to annotation, and how close its genome comes to a chromosome-scale reference.

The HiFi runs do not measure the accuracy of the genes

  • One genome (n = 1). Nothing here shows how FunFlux does on HiFi reads of other fungi.
  • The reference comes from the same sample. It was assembled from HiFi reads with hifiasm 0.19.8, polished with short reads and joined into 7 chromosomes with Hi-C data (Liu et al. 2026). The sample's only HiFi run in the archive is the one used here. The reference is chromosome-scale with the help of Hi-C, while reads alone may not give every chromosome in one piece. Agreement with it, above all for the hifiasm runs, is expected and is not an independent check.
  • No gene comparison. The reference's gene annotation (10,743 protein-coding genes at NCBI) was not compared with FunFlux's genes. The gene table gives counts and BUSCO only.
  • Tiberius has seen no genes of this genus, only genes of the same family. No Cordyceps species is among the training species of the Tiberius fungi model, but two species of the same family, Akanthomyces muscarius and Beauveria bassiana, are (its training list).
  • The protein evidence comes from another species, Cordyceps militaris CM01, as for a new genome. The B05.10 runs had the reference's own proteins, which pull the genes towards the reference.
  • Run times come from one shared server, with other runs going on at the same time, so they are indicative only.

docs.title: Data and settings
docs.text:
The reads and the reference come from one sample record. Depth is again the number of bases divided by the reference length.

Data Accession Details Used by Reference genome GCA_056505955.1 (assembly ASM5650595v1) 7 chromosomes, 32,707,717 bp, no gaps; BioSample SAMN48746374 the comparisons below PacBio HiFi reads SRR34289959 PacBio Revio, 147,159 reads, 2.77 Gb (about 85x), mean length 18.8 kb; the same BioSample all three runs MGISEQ short reads SRR34289958 MGISEQ-2000RS, 16,427,628 pairs of 2 x 150 bp, 4.93 Gb (about 151x); the same BioSample hybrid Protein evidence GCF_000225605.1 Cordyceps militaris CM01, 9,651 proteins (RefSeq) column 3 of the annotation table, all three runs

The MGISEQ short reads are DNBSEQ pairs, and hybrid mode reads them as it reads Illumina pairs. In every run Filtlong kept 124,832 HiFi reads, 2.49 Gb, which is 90 % of the bases (Read filter).

The next table gives the settings of the three HiFi runs.

Setting longread, hifiasm longread, Flye hybrid mode longread longread hybrid assembler (under longread or hybrid) hifiasm (the default) flye, which runs with --pacbio-hifi hifiasm (the default), then Polypolish with the short reads resources.threads 24 20 24 Annotation table, column 3 (proteins) the C. militaris proteins the same the same

Everything else is set as in the B05.10 mode runs (settings table): 256 GB of memory, GeneMark-ES and SignalP 6 fast on, the AMR screen on, and AUGUSTUS trained on the genome. HiFi reads get no Medaka.

docs.title: Assembly
docs.text:
The table sets each HiFi assembly against the 7 chromosomes of the reference, with the run time of each run.

Run Contigs Total length (Mb) N50 (Mb) Reference chromosomes in one contig (of 7) Contigs with telomeres at both ends Run time (h) Cores Reference (GCA_056505955.1) 7 32.71 4.79 7 7 – – longread, hifiasm 18 34.58 4.79 6 7 6.6 24 longread, Flye 12 34.01 4.79 6 6 7.3, in two attempts 20 hybrid, hifiasm + Polypolish 18 34.58 4.79 6 7 7.8 24

On this genome, both assemblers give six of the seven reference chromosomes as one contig each, with a telomere array at both ends, and cover all of every reference chromosome. The seventh breaks in two at its rDNA array. Both assemblies also hold about 1.3 Mb that the reference lacks.

  • Chromosome 7 (3.58 Mb) comes as a piece of 3.10 Mb and one of 0.52 Mb, or 3.07 and 0.51 Mb with Flye. Each piece ends in a telomere array. The break lies in the tandem copies of the rDNA unit, the repeat that holds the ITS.
  • The extra 1.3 Mb. hifiasm gives it as one contig of 1,329,053 bp with a telomere array at both ends, the seventh chromosome in the next table. Flye gives it as four contigs, 1.30 Mb together. Only 4 % of it aligns to the reference, in short pieces. Its read depth is close to that of the chromosomes (1.14 times the median), and FunFlux predicts 275 genes on it. The contamination and mitochondrion screen places it in Cordyceps from its BLAST hits. Whether it is a small chromosome that the reference lacks was not checked further.
  • Other contigs. hifiasm adds 7 small contigs of rDNA units (rDNA_array, 0.34 Mb together) and 2 contigs with almost no read depth (low_depth, 0.17 Mb) that do not align to the reference. Flye has neither, and its genome is 0.57 Mb smaller.
  • hybrid. Its draft assembly is the hifiasm run's, byte for byte, because both runs filter and assemble the same HiFi reads. Polypolish then changed 38 positions with the short reads.
  • Run time is that of the main Snakemake run, from its log. The Flye run stopped once in InterProScan, with an error that did not come back when the run was started again by hand. Its time is the sum of both attempts, 3.7 and 3.6 h. The run was made without the second attempt that FunFlux makes by itself after a failed InterProScan job (Running FunFlux).

The assemblies were checked as for B05.10, with minimap2 2.31 (-x asm5), and a chromosome counts as one contig when the largest contig placed on it is at least 97 % of its length. The reference's telomeres were counted with FunFlux's own telomere search, run on the reference, which found AACCCT arrays at both ends of all 7 chromosomes.

The next table gives the contig summary verdicts of each run and its mitochondrial contig.

Per run longread, hifiasm longread, Flye hybrid Contig summary: chromosome 7 6 7 chromosome_arm 2 2 2 rDNA_array 7 0 7 nuclear_contig 0 3 0 low_depth 2 0 2 unclassified 0 1 0 mitochondrion 1 1 1 All contigs 19 13 19 Mitochondrial contig, in contigs_mitochondrial.fasta (bp) 49,194, circular: about two copies of the genome end to end 24,597, circular: one copy as the hifiasm run

With hifiasm, all 14 ends of the reference chromosomes and both ends of the extra contig carry a telomere array. With Flye, the 14 reference ends do too, but the extra 1.3 Mb has an array at one end only and comes as three nuclear_contigs and one chromosome_arm. Flye's 0.51-Mb piece of chromosome 7 is unclassified, because its read depth, 1.74 times the median, is above the 1.5 limit.

A circular mitochondrial contig of two copies is not flagged as a concatemer

The mitochondrion published for this strain is 24,712 bp (Liu et al. 2026). Flye gives one copy. hifiasm marks its 49,194-bp contig as circular, so the concatemer flag stays N although the contig holds about two copies. FunFlux sets the flag to Y only when length_ratio is above 1.5 and the assembler did not record the contig as circular. length_ratio is the contig length divided by the length of the mitochondrial genome it best matches in BLAST (Concatemers).

docs.title: Genes
docs.text:
The table gives the gene count of each HiFi run and two BUSCO scores, one of the genome and one of the gene models.

Run Protein-coding genes BUSCO of the genome: complete, cordycipitaceae_odb12 (of 4,122) BUSCO of the gene models: complete, dikarya_odb9 (of 1,312) Reference (GCA_056505955.1) 10,743 – – longread, hifiasm 10,924 4,112 (99.8 %) 1,299 (99.0 %) longread, Flye 10,919 4,112 (99.8 %) 1,300 (99.1 %) hybrid 10,921 4,112 (99.8 %) 1,298 (98.9 %)

The three runs agree, differing by at most 5 genes and 2 BUSCO genes. In each run 273 to 275 genes lie on the 1.3 Mb that the reference lacks, so the counts cannot be set against the reference's 10,743 one to one.

  • BUSCO of the genome comes from the assembly QC on contigs_final.fasta. BUSCO chose cordycipitaceae_odb12 itself (busco.lineage: auto).
  • BUSCO of the gene models comes from funannotate annotate, with dikarya_odb9, as in the B05.10 gene table. The two columns use different gene sets and cannot be compared with each other.
  • hybrid and hifiasm annotated nearly the same genome, 38 positions apart, and differ by 3 genes. That is about as much as the B05.10 default run and its replicate, which differ by 5 genes (Repeated runs).
  • tRNA genes, 105 to 107 per run, are left out.

docs.title: AMR screen and ITS
docs.text:
The AMR screen and the ITS classification gave the same result in all three runs.

A species outside the AMR database is reported, not failed, and the run goes on

Cordyceps cateniannulata is not among the 57 species of the ChroQueTas database, so the three runs report it as not screened. amr_summary.tsv has one row with status not screened, and a NOTE in the log gives the reason. The database holds no Cordyceps, and its only species of the same family is Beauveria bassiana (The species).

The ITS taxonomy is the same in all three runs. The main ITS2 sequence (158 bp) gives the strain's own species, C. cateniannulata (confidence 0.96, and 0.97 for the genus Cordyceps). The main ITS1 sequence (182 bp) stops at the phylum Ascomycota (class 0.60, below the cutoff of 0.8). The main ITS sequences themselves are the same in all three runs. The hifiasm assemblies hold 43 copies of the main ITS1 and 44 of the main ITS2, the Flye assembly 4 of each. See ITS taxonomy.

docs.title: To repeat the HiFi runs
docs.text:
The HiFi runs can be repeated from public data. First download the reads, the protein evidence and the reference genome:

# the reads (ENA); ENA names the HiFi file _subreads, but it holds HiFi reads
wget ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR342/059/SRR34289959/SRR34289959_subreads.fastq.gz \
     ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR342/058/SRR34289958/SRR34289958_1.fastq.gz \
     ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR342/058/SRR34289958/SRR34289958_2.fastq.gz

# the protein evidence and the reference genome (NCBI Datasets)
curl -L -o GCF_000225605.1.zip \
  "https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/v2/genome/accession/GCF_000225605.1/download?include_annotation_type=PROT_FASTA"
curl -L -o GCA_056505955.1.zip \
  "https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/v2/genome/accession/GCA_056505955.1/download?include_annotation_type=GENOME_FASTA"
# unpack both into ncbi_dataset/data/<accession>/ (protein.faa; the genome FASTA);
# -o because both zip files hold files of the same name, such as README.md
unzip -o GCF_000225605.1.zip
unzip -o GCA_056505955.1.zip

Name the reads GXU8616_pacbio.fastq.gz, GXU8616_R1.fastq.gz and GXU8616_R2.fastq.gz. The sample name, GXU8616, is the strain name without the hyphen. The longread runs had a folder with the _pacbio file only. Write the annotation table with the C. militaris proteins in column 3:

#sample species proteins    augustus_species
GXU8616 Cordyceps cateniannulata    /path/to/ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000225605.1/protein.faa  -

Then use the settings above, and run as in How to reproduce, step 5.

docs.title: How to reproduce
docs.text:
The B05.10 runs can be repeated from public data in five steps.

  1. Download the data:

    # the reference: genome, annotation and proteins (NCBI Datasets)
curl -L -o GCF_000143535.2.zip \
  "https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/v2/genome/accession/GCF_000143535.2/download?include_annotation_type=GENOME_FASTA&include_annotation_type=GENOME_GFF&include_annotation_type=PROT_FASTA"
unzip GCF_000143535.2.zip   # ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000143535.2/: the genome FASTA, genomic.gff, protein.faa

# the ONT reads (sra-tools)
fasterq-dump SRR40741277 && gzip SRR40741277.fastq

# the Illumina pairs (ENA)
wget ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR106/011/SRR10692911/SRR10692911_1.fastq.gz \
     ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR106/011/SRR10692911/SRR10692911_2.fastq.gz

  2. Name the reads B0510_ont.fastq.gz, B0510_R1.fastq.gz and B0510_R2.fastq.gz, as the modes expect (Choosing a mode). Symbolic links are fine. For the 42x run, take the first 95,000 ONT reads, 4 lines each, as sample B0510m:

    zcat SRR40741277.fastq.gz | head -n 380000 | gzip > B0510m_ont.fastq.gz

  3. Write the annotation table, tab-separated, with the reference proteins in column 3. Add a line for B0510m for the 42x run, and write botrytis_cinerea in column 4 for the run with the stored AUGUSTUS model:

    #sample species proteins    augustus_species
B0510   Botrytis cinerea    /path/to/ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000143535.2/protein.faa  -

  4. Copy the configuration template and set the mode, the input folder, the databases and the settings in the settings table. For the comparison runs, use contigs mode with the hybrid run's 02.assembly/B0510/contigs_final.fasta, named B0510.fasta.

  5. Run each configuration, with --cores equal to its resources.threads (Running FunFlux):

    snakemake --sdm conda --cores 32 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

To compare a B05.10 run with the reference, Liftoff carries the reference genes onto the genome FunFlux annotated, 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_sort.fasta. Then gffcompare compares the coding parts of the lifted reference genes with FunFlux's protein-coding genes. The commands are in the box below.

The comparison commands are not part of FunFlux 
REF=ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000143535.2
# 1. carry the reference genes onto the annotated genome (its contigs are named scaffold_N)
liftoff -g $REF/genomic.gff -o lifted_reference.gff3 -u unmapped_reference_genes.txt -p 16 \
  -dir liftoff_tmp -polish 04.annotation/B0510/contigs_sort.fasta \
  $REF/GCF_000143535.2_ASM14353v4_genomic.fna
# 2. rebuild the lifted reference transcripts from their coding parts only (CDS lines become
#    exons), because FunFlux's genes have no untranslated regions
awk -F'\t' 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} /^#/ {print; next} $3=="exon" {next} $3=="CDS" {$3="exon"; print; next} {print}' \
  lifted_reference.gff3_polished | gffread -T -o lifted_reference_cds.gtf -
# 3. FunFlux's protein-coding genes (-C leaves out the tRNA genes, which have no CDS)
gffread -T -C -o funflux_coding.gtf \
  04.annotation/B0510/funannotate/annotate_results/Botrytis_cinerea_B0510.gff3
# 4. compare: gffcmp_cds.stats holds the sensitivity, the precision and the matching counts
gffcompare -r lifted_reference_cds.gtf -o gffcmp_cds funflux_coding.gtf

# the chromosome check: align the nuclear genome to the reference
minimap2 -x asm5 -c --cs -t 8 $REF/GCF_000143535.2_ASM14353v4_genomic.fna \
  02.assembly/B0510/contigs_final.fasta > contigs_vs_reference.paf

All of these tools come from bioconda: Liftoff 1.6.3 (its own alignments made with minimap2 2.24), gffread 0.12.9, gffcompare 0.12.10, and minimap2 2.31 for the chromosome check.

docs.title: Antifungal resistance mutations
docs.text:
FunFlux can screen every genome for point mutations studied for resistance to antifungal drugs and fungicides. The AMR screen (the resistance-mutation screen) runs ChroQueTas against the FungAMR database (Bédard et al. 2025), which lists such mutations with the evidence for or against resistance. For every sample it writes 05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary.tsv, with one row per target protein of the species and the changes found. Each change gets a verdict from the evidence FungAMR holds: whether it confers resistance, to which drugs, and how strong the evidence is (Evidence levels and verdicts). The table also appears in the MultiQC report.

---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    TAB([species<br/>column 2 of the<br/>annotation parameter table]) --> MATCH[match to a species folder<br/>of the database]
    DB([ChroQueTas and its database<br/>downloaded once<br/>per output folder]) --> MATCH
    MATCH --> NUC[nuclear run<br/>contigs_final.fasta<br/>nuclear genetic code]
    MATCH -.->|species with cytochrome b| MIT[mitochondrial run<br/>mitochondrial genetic code]
    NUC --> CALL[each target read from the run<br/>of its own compartment<br/>verdicts from evidence levels]
    MIT --> CALL
    CALL --> OUT([05.amr/sample/<br/>amr_summary.tsv<br/>amr_positions.tsv])
    OUT --> REP([MultiQC report<br/>summary of every sample])

The AMR screen is off by default. ChroQueTas and its database are licensed only for non-commercial use, and switching the screen on is your acceptance of that licence (Licence). To switch it on, set:

parameters:
  amr:
    chroquetas: on

Terms used on this page

AMR screen antimicrobial resistance screen: the optional step, off by default, in which ChroQueTas looks in each genome for the changes FungAMR lists for the species FungAMR the database of mutations studied for resistance to antifungal drugs and fungicides, with evidence levels for and against; ChroQueTas screens each genome against part of it target protein a protein whose FungAMR positions ChroQueTas checks, such as Beta-tubulin or Cyp51; amr_summary.tsv has one row per target of the species FungAMR mutation the ChroQueTas call for a change that FungAMR lists at that position, whatever its evidence; it does not by itself mean resistance evidence level the FungAMR score for a change and a drug, by kind of study: 1 (strongest) to 8 for resistance found, -1 to -8 for none found verdict the reading of FungAMR's evidence for a change or a target: resistance, conflicting, no resistance, unknown, wild type, or not compared for a position compartment nuclear or mitochondrial: the ChroQueTas run, each with its own genetic code, from which a target protein's result is read contamination and mitochondrion screen the screen of the draft assembly: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true

docs.title: What the screen looks for
docs.text:
Fungi become resistant through changes in their own genes. FungAMR records amino acid substitutions and other changes, such as more copies of a gene, and ChroQueTas screens the substitutions. Many of them sit in the protein the drug acts on, at a few known positions. The gene itself is present in every strain of the species, sensitive or resistant, so a search for resistance genes, as used for bacteria, does not fit. What tells a resistant strain from a sensitive one is the amino acid at those positions. The AMR screen therefore finds each target protein in the assembly and reads those positions.

The table lists the main targets in the database, with drugs named in their entries.

Target (database name) Protein Drugs, for example Species in the database with this target Cyp51 sterol 14α-demethylase of the ergosterol pathway azoles: fluconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole 27 Cytochrome_b cytochrome b of respiratory complex III, encoded in the mitochondrial genome QoI fungicides (strobilurins): azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, trifloxystrobin 15 Beta-tubulin β-tubulin of the microtubules benzimidazoles: carbendazim, benomyl, thiophanate-methyl; diethofencarb 12 Fks β-1,3-glucan synthase of the cell wall echinocandins: caspofungin, anidulafungin, micafungin 10 Sdh succinate dehydrogenase, respiratory complex II SDHI fungicides: boscalid, carboxin, pydiflumetofen 4 Bos1, OS1 one histidine kinase of the osmotic stress pathway, listed under two names with the same reference protein (UniProt Q8X1E7) dicarboximides (iprodione, procymidone), fludioxonil 1 (Botrytis cinerea)

The database has 210 target proteins in all, under 109 target names. The others include efflux pumps and their regulators (Cdr1, Pdr1, Tac1, Mrr1) and the enzymes that turn 5-fluorocytosine into its toxic form (Fcy1, Fur1).

In two species the database holds one protein under two names: Botrytis cinerea Bos1 and OS1, and Fusarium graminearum Myosin-1 and Myosin-5. Each name gets its own row in the tables, so a change at a position both names list is reported twice.

docs.title: FungAMR and ChroQueTas
docs.text:
FungAMR (Bédard et al. 2025) was curated by hand from 501 published studies. It holds 35,792 entries for 208 drugs, 246 genes and 95 fungal species. Each entry gives the gene, the mutation and the drug, with a confidence score for the evidence (Evidence levels and verdicts). FungAMR can be searched online in the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD).

ChroQueTas, from the same paper, screens a genome against the part of FungAMR prepared for it. FunFlux runs version 1.0.1, downloaded from one fixed commit of its GitHub repository, as described under Settings. ChroQueTas takes each target protein of the species through four steps:

Step Tool What happens 1 miniprot 0.14 aligns the reference protein to the genome, across introns, and translates the gene it finds with the genetic code of the run 2 BLASTP of BLAST+ 2.16.0 compares the extracted protein with the reference, and ChroQueTas keeps it at more than 90 % identity over more than 75 % of the reference 3 MAFFT 7.525 aligns the extracted protein with the reference 4 ChroQueTas reads the amino acid at every FungAMR position of the target and calls it

Every position gets one of the calls below. FunFlux writes ChroQueTas's FungAMR MUTATION as FungAMR mutation, its New mutation as new mutation, and so on.

Call Meaning FungAMR mutation the amino acid differs from the reference, and FungAMR lists this change at this position, whatever the evidence says: for resistance, against it, or both. ChroQueTas adds the drugs with their evidence levels, and the verdict says which way they point (Evidence levels and verdicts) new mutation the amino acid differs from the reference, but FungAMR does not list this change at this position. It is a possible new resistance mutation that needs its own investigation (ChroQueTas README) no mutation the reference amino acid no alignment the found protein has a gap at the position. The gap is a deletion, a part of the gene missing from the assembly (as at a contig end), or a premature stop codon, which MAFFT turns into a gap. A nonsense mutation that FungAMR lists (written X) therefore shows up here, not as a FungAMR mutation. The copy's protein, <name>_<target>.<fragment>.faa, tells which, because a stop is written * there position not found the position lies outside the alignment, or it is not a number, or its codon could not be read (found amino acid X)

The last two calls are not comparisons. They do not count as positions checked, and the summary's note names them. A target with no compared position at all is not evaluated (Statuses).

Three database rows have no position number. ChroQueTas reports the insertion (Cryptococcus deuterogattii Uxs1, 1182ins(fs)) as position not found, and skips the duplication (Nakaseomyces glabratus Pdr1, c.3308dupT) without a word. It reads the translocation (Candidozyma auris Ncp1) as position 1, and FunFlux reports that row as position not found too.

ChroQueTas calls a position a FungAMR mutation when the letter it found is one of those the database lists there, and a new mutation when it is a letter other than the reference's. In three cases the letter is not a change, and FunFlux writes another call:

What ChroQueTas found ChroQueTas's call FunFlux's call X: miniprot's letter for a codon it cannot read, one with N bases (a gap in a scaffold). FungAMR writes a stop as X too, but miniprot writes a stop as * FungAMR MUTATION where FungAMR lists a stop, New mutation elsewhere position not found a gap where FungAMR lists a deletion (written -, 22 rows), beyond the part of the reference the found protein covers (BLASTP's sstart to send): the protein ends early, as for a gene cut at a contig end FungAMR MUTATION no alignment the reference amino acid, at the one row that lists the reference amino acid as the change: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Hap1 N832N (clotrimazole, level 4) FungAMR MUTATION no mutation

A gap inside the found protein, where FungAMR lists a deletion, stays a FungAMR mutation. As on every row, fungamr_drugs keeps ChroQueTas's drug text.

ChroQueTas does not screen the whole of FungAMR. The database of version 1.0.1 holds only single mutations, and only species with a reliable reference protein (ChroQueTas README):

FungAMR ChroQueTas database 1.0.1 entries 35,792 8,285 mutations: only single mutations, tested on their own rather than in combination with others species 95 57: only species for which an accurate reference protein exists; a species without one is left out, because a poor reference could give spurious calls

An entry can carry evidence for resistance, against it, or both (Evidence levels and verdicts).

Only single mutations in the target proteins are screened

The AMR screen does not detect gene duplication or loss, gene disruption, translocation, aneuploidy, combinations of mutations, or any change outside the protein, such as an insertion in a promoter that raises the expression of the target.

docs.title: Evidence levels and verdicts
docs.text:
The verdicts rest on the evidence levels of FungAMR. FungAMR gives each drug of a change two confidence scores, which ChroQueTas writes as Drug(positive/negative) (Bédard et al. 2025; ChroQueTas wiki, "Confidence score for antimicrobial resistance"):

Score Meaning positive, 1 to 8 evidence that the change causes resistance to that drug; 1 is the strongest, 8 the weakest negative, -1 to -8 evidence, from the same kinds of study, that it does not: the change was reported in susceptible strains; -1 is the strongest NA no report of that kind

When several studies report a change, each score is the strongest of its kind.

The level names the kind of study. FunFlux writes it in words after the number, and the same words serve both signs. After a positive level the study found resistance, and after a negative one it found none.

Level What the positive level means (ChroQueTas wiki) Words in the tables 1 the change was made in a susceptible strain of the same species, and its effect on resistance was measured the change made in the species and measured 2 the change was made in the same gene expressed in another species, possibly at another level of expression, and its effect measured the change made in the gene, expressed in another species 3 its effect was measured in a bulk competition assay, such as deep mutational scanning bulk competition assay 4 it arose in experimental evolution, often enough in independent replicates to suggest that it causes resistance experimental evolution 5 deleting the gene causes resistance gene deletion 6 overexpressing or duplicating the gene causes resistance gene overexpression or duplication 7 a significant association with resistance in a population: GWAS, QTL mapping or classical genetics population association study 8 found in a resistant natural strain, such as a clinical isolate, without further validation natural isolates, not validated further

A negative level is the same kind of study with the opposite result. -8, for example, records a natural isolate with the change that was not resistant, and -3 a deep mutational scan in which the change gave no resistance.

docs.title: A FungAMR mutation is not always a resistance mutation
docs.text:
ChroQueTas calls every change that FungAMR lists a FungAMR mutation, whatever its scores, and more than half of the changes in its database carry evidence against resistance only. In ChroQueTas 1.0.1 the evidence splits as follows:

Evidence Negative only Positive only Both No drug All rows of the database (changes), all drugs of the row together 4,655 2,943 686 1 8,285 drugs of those rows, one by one 19,397 8,868 108 28,373

Most of the negative-only rows, 4,596, belong to Candida albicans Cyp51 and Saccharomyces cerevisiae Fcy1, and all but five of those come from deep mutational scans (level -3). FunFlux therefore sorts the drugs of every FungAMR mutation by their evidence. Candida albicans Cyp51 A61V, for example, reads Clotrimazole(3/NA),Fluconazole(NA/-2),Isavuconazole(3/NA),Itraconazole(3/-2),Posaconazole(2/NA),Voriconazole(3/-2), and its drugs are sorted like this:

A drug with Goes to In A61V a positive level only resistance_to clotrimazole, isavuconazole, posaconazole a negative level only no_resistance_to fluconazole both both columns, each with its own level: a conflicting drug itraconazole, voriconazole

Each position then gets a verdict. For a FungAMR mutation, it is the first of its four rows below that applies:

Call Verdict When FungAMR mutation resistance at least one drug has a positive level only FungAMR mutation conflicting no drug has a positive level only, and at least one has both FungAMR mutation no resistance every drug named has a negative level only FungAMR mutation unknown no drug is named new mutation unknown a change FungAMR does not list, at a position where it lists others no mutation wild type the reference amino acid no alignment, position not found not compared the position could not be compared

A61V is resistance, although two of its drugs conflict. A change is conflicting only when no drug has resistance evidence alone, as for Aspergillus niger Cyp51 Q228R, Voriconazole(8/-8). FunFlux does not weigh one kind of evidence against the other, and both levels stay in the tables. The 8,285 rows of the database get these verdicts:

Verdict Rows resistance 3,610, of which 42 have a conflicting drug as well no resistance 4,655 conflicting 19 unknown 1: the Cryptococcus deuterogattii Uxs1 insertion, which names no drug; ChroQueTas does not compare it (FungAMR and ChroQueTas)

A target takes the first of these verdicts found among its compared positions, all copies together: resistance, conflicting, unknown, no resistance, wild type. A change of unknown effect ranks above no resistance and wild type, because it needs a look. A target that is not evaluated or not found, and a sample that is not screened, get -, and the status says why.

Botrytis cinerea β-tubulin E198V, for example, reads Benzimidazole(8/NA),Carbendazim(7/NA),Diethofencarb(8/NA),Iprodione(NA/-8) in the database. A genome with valine at position 198 gets these cells in amr_positions.tsv:

Column Cell verdict resistance resistance_to Benzimidazole (8: natural isolates, not validated further); Carbendazim (7: population association study); Diethofencarb (8: natural isolates, not validated further) no_resistance_to Iprodione (-8: natural isolates, not validated further)

That is evidence that E198V causes resistance to three drugs, and reports of natural isolates with E198V that were not resistant to iprodione.

docs.title: What a level does not say
docs.text:
A positive level says how good the evidence is that a change causes resistance, and a negative level how good the evidence is that it does not. Neither is a measurement of the isolate. Whether this strain is resistant, and how strongly, takes a susceptibility test. The FungAMR authors put it the same way: a confidence score is not a probability of treatment failure, but reflects the evidence that a change confers resistance under laboratory conditions (Bédard et al. 2025).

The verdict no resistance says only what the reports found

Evidence of no resistance is the harder kind to judge. A susceptible result can come from an assay that was not sensitive enough, and such assays rarely test a resistant control alongside. The FungAMR authors kept these reports in the database but left them out of their own analyses for that reason (Bédard et al. 2025). The verdict no resistance therefore means that the reports found no resistance to the drugs named. It does not show that the change never matters for resistance, and it says nothing about drugs that were not tested.

Levels 7 and 8 rest on association, not on a test of the change itself. The change was found in resistant isolates, or linked to resistance in a population. Field isolates are often resistant to several classes of fungicides at once. A drug at level 7 or 8 that acts on another target can therefore record a resistance found together with the change rather than caused by it. In Botrytis cinerea, for example, iprodione (level 8) is listed for β-tubulin E198A, and carbendazim (level 7) and boscalid (level 8) for cytochrome b G143A. Such a drug counts towards the verdict resistance like any other.

docs.title: The species
docs.text:
Each sample is screened against the database folder of its species. The species is column 2 of the annotation parameter table (files.annotation_params), the name funannotate uses as well. The database names its species folders Genus_species. FunFlux matches the name to a folder, ignoring case, and takes the first of three tries that succeeds:

  1. The whole name, with spaces turned into underscores and f. sp. (or f.sp.) removed: Blumeria graminis f. sp. hordei gives Blumeria_graminis_hordei.
  2. The first two words: Zymoseptoria tritici IPO323 gives Zymoseptoria_tritici.

  3. A short list of other names, older or newer, of species whose database folder carries a different name. Each pair is one taxon in NCBI Taxonomy:

    Name in the annotation table Database folder Candida glabrata Nakaseomyces_glabratus Candida auris Candidozyma_auris Parastagonospora nodorum Phaeosphaeria_nodorum Pseudocercospora fijiensis Mycosphaerella_fijiensis Fulvia fulva, Cladosporium fulvum Passalora_fulva Oculimacula yallundae Tapesia_yallundae Oculimacula acuformis Tapesia_acuformis Issatchenkia orientalis, Candida krusei Pichia_kudriavzevii Candida lusitaniae Clavispora_lusitaniae Lodderomyces metapsilosis Candida_metapsilosis Lodderomyces orthopsilosis Candida_orthopsilosis Pyricularia grisea Magnaporthe_grisea Blumeria hordei Blumeria_graminis_hordei

Only renamings of one species are listed. Pyricularia oryzae, the rice blast fungus, is not matched to Magnaporthe_grisea, because NCBI Taxonomy keeps them as two species (Magnaporthe grisea is Pyricularia grisea).

A name that matches no folder leaves the sample not screened, and the run goes on. amr_summary.tsv gets one row with status not screened, and a NOTE in the log and on the console names the database folders of the same genus, if there are any. 00.resources/chroquetas/species.txt lists the 57 folders.

A species outside the database is not screened against a relative

FunFlux never screens a sample against another species of its genus, because the positions of a resistance mutation are positions in the reference protein of one species. For a species outside the database, FungAMR itself may still list mutations of its targets. Search it in CARD (https://card.mcmaster.ca/fungamrhome, the address ChroQueTas gives) and compare the positions by hand with the predicted proteins in 04.annotation/{sample}/funannotate/annotate_results/.

docs.title: Two runs: the nuclear and the mitochondrial genome
docs.text:
ChroQueTas translates the genome with one genetic code per run. The nuclear and the mitochondrial genes of one fungus use different codes, so one run cannot translate both correctly. These are the codes that matter here (NCBI, The Genetic Codes):

NCBI table Used by Differs from the standard code in 1, the standard code the nuclear genes of most fungi 12 the nuclear genes of the yeasts of the CTG clade; ChroQueTas chooses 12 for its 8 species of that clade and 1 for the others CTG read as serine 4, the mold mitochondrial code fungal mitochondria TGA codes for tryptophan instead of a stop 3, the yeast mitochondrial code the mitochondria of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Candida glabrata TGA read as tryptophan too, ATA as methionine and CTN as threonine

Cytochrome b is the one target of the database encoded in the mitochondrial genome, and it is held for 15 species. Translated with the nuclear code, its gene gives a poorer protein, and the example below shows how much. Rule amr_chroquetas therefore runs ChroQueTas twice, each run in its own folder:

Run Input Genetic code Results read from it nuclear, chroquetas/nuclear/ 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta chosen by ChroQueTas for the species every target except Cytochrome_b mitochondrial, chroquetas/mitochondrial/ contigs_mitochondrial.fasta when the contamination and mitochondrion screen splits the mitochondrion off (parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, the default); otherwise contigs_final.fasta parameters.amr.mito_genetic_code; auto: 3 for the four Saccharomycetaceae of the database (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, S. paradoxus, Nakaseomyces glabratus, Kluyveromyces marxianus), 4 for every other species, as NCBI Taxonomy records them Cytochrome_b

A target is read only from the run of its own compartment, and a target the other run also extracts, translated with the wrong code, is ignored. The mitochondrial run reads the confirmed mitochondrion when the contamination and mitochondrion screen splits it off, and the whole assembly when nothing is split off. Whether the mitochondrial run happens, and what it reads, in each case:

Case Mitochondrial run Cytochrome_b the species' database folder does not hold Cytochrome_b none not a target of the species the contamination and mitochondrion screen splits the mitochondrion off and confirmed a contig on contigs_mitochondrial.fasta read from this run the contamination and mitochondrion screen splits the mitochondrion off but confirmed no contig none: contigs_mitochondrial.fasta is empty not evaluated (no mitochondrial contig) contigs mode without the contamination and mitochondrion screen, or any mode with parameters.mitochondria.mode off or report: nothing is split off on contigs_final.fasta, among whose contigs the mitochondrion lies if the assembly holds it read from this run

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
The status tells whether the positions of a target could be compared. Every target of the species gets one in amr_summary.tsv:

Status Meaning evaluated at least one copy of the protein passed step 2 and had at least one FungAMR position compared; amr_positions.tsv lists them not evaluated no position was compared: the protein was found but has insertions against the reference; or it was found, but every FungAMR position lies in a gap of the found protein, at a codon that could not be read, or outside the protein (no alignment, position not found); or ChroQueTas skipped it; or, for Cytochrome_b, there was no mitochondrial contig to search. The note says which not found no copy passed step 2: miniprot found no alignment of the reference protein in the genome (ChroQueTas's log says We could not extract <target> from the genome), or what it found does not pass the filter of step 2 (more than 90 % identity over more than 75 % of the reference). The gene is absent from the assembly, or too different from the reference not screened the species is not in the database (The species); one row for the sample, target -

For a copy whose positions it does not compare, ChroQueTas writes WARNING: genome contains insertions for <target> and thus AMR are not calculated instead of the positions. The line has two causes, which FunFlux reports differently:

  • Insertions. The extracted protein has residues the reference lacks. FunFlux counts the copy as found, with its positions not compared: not evaluated.
  • A copy below the thresholds of step 2. ChroQueTas then keeps no .blastp.txt file for it. FunFlux counts the copy as not found, and a target with no other copy is not found.

A common cause of insertions is an intron the protein aligner could not place, such as an intron of a mitochondrial cytochrome b gene (the example below).

ChroQueTas 1.0.1 also skips a target silently in one case. When a target is not found, it removes the name from its list of targets by a text replacement that also cuts that name out of longer names. Vma16 is therefore lost when Vma1 was not found. Such a target is not evaluated, with a note that says so.

ChroQueTas numbers the copies of a target it finds as fragment 1, 2, and so on. A second copy can be a gene duplication, a gene split across two contigs of a fragmented assembly, or aneuploidy (ChroQueTas README). Each copy is compared on its own, and the summary marks the changes of a later copy, for example E198A (copy 2) (resistance).

docs.title: The tables
docs.text:
amr_summary.tsv and amr_positions.tsv share a few conventions. In both tables - marks an empty cell. Drug names are FungAMR's, with underscores for spaces. A few contain a comma, such as Fludioxonil,_Iprodione (one entry, both drugs together), so the drugs of a FunFlux cell are separated by ;. Changes are written as reference amino acid, position and found amino acid, as in E198A.

05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary.tsv has one row per target of the species:

Column Content sample the sample name species the database folder the species was matched to, for example Botrytis_cinerea; for a sample that is not screened, column 2 of the annotation table as written there target the target protein as the database names it, for example Beta-tubulin; - for a sample that is not screened compartment nuclear or mitochondrial: the run the result comes from; - for a sample that is not screened status evaluated, not evaluated, not found or not screened (Statuses) positions_checked the FungAMR positions compared, over all compared copies; 0 when none verdict the first of resistance, conflicting, unknown, no resistance, wild type among the verdicts of the target's compared positions, all copies together (Verdicts); - for a target that is not evaluated or not found, and for a sample that is not screened fungamr_mutations the FungAMR mutations, each with its verdict, separated by ,: E198A (resistance); E198A (copy 2) (resistance) for a change in a second copy new_mutations the other changes at FungAMR positions, separated by ,: F200L, F200L (copy 2). Their verdict is unknown resistance_to the drugs with a positive level, from all FungAMR mutations of the target, each with the change and the level: Carbendazim (E198A, 7); Iprodione (E198A, 8). A drug named by two changes appears once for each; a change found on two copies names its drugs once no_resistance_to the drugs with a negative level, written the same way: Iprodione (E198V, -8) note for an evaluated target, the copies and positions that were not compared, and a target found more than once; otherwise why the target was not evaluated or not found, or why the sample was not screened

05.amr/{sample}/amr_positions.tsv has one row per FungAMR position of every copy that ChroQueTas read position by position, including the positions it could not compare (a copy with insertions has no rows):

Column Content sample, target, compartment as in the summary fragment the copy of the target: 1 for the first position the position in the reference protein reference_aa, found_aa the amino acid of the reference and of this genome call FungAMR mutation, new mutation, no mutation, no alignment or position not found verdict for a FungAMR mutation resistance, conflicting, no resistance or unknown; unknown for a new mutation; wild type for no mutation; not compared for the last two calls (Verdicts) resistance_to for a FungAMR mutation, the drugs with a positive level, each with the level and its words: Carbendazim (7: population association study); Iprodione (8: natural isolates, not validated further) no_resistance_to for a FungAMR mutation, the drugs with a negative level, the same way: Iprodione (-8: natural isolates, not validated further) known_resistance_changes for a compared position, the changes the database lists there with a positive level for at least one drug, in the order of the database file: E198A, E198G, E198K, E198V. On a wild type row, the changes that would matter there; on an unknown row, the changes known at that position fungamr_drugs ChroQueTas's text, unchanged: Carbendazim(7/NA),Iprodione(8/NA); - where it names no drug (NA, or Unknown for a new mutation). Its drugs are separated by commas, but a few names hold a comma (Fludioxonil,_Iprodione) or brackets (Azole(s)): split it at each comma that follows a closing bracket (),), not at every comma

05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary_mqc.tsv is the same summary with header lines for MultiQC. They hold the section name and a description that names FungAMR, says what the verdicts mean and how to read the evidence levels. The rows of the file are named {sample}: {target}, so the tables of all samples merge into one table in the section AMR mutations (ChroQueTas) of 06.report/multiqc_report.html (Report).

The log logs/amr_chroquetas_{sample}.log holds ChroQueTas's messages of both runs. It ends with one line, [FunFlux] amr_chroquetas <sample>: ..., which the rule copies to the Snakemake console. The line names the database folder used, the targets evaluated, not evaluated and not found, and the targets per verdict, as in verdicts: 1 resistance (Beta-tubulin), 2 wild type (Bos1, OS1). It then gives each FungAMR mutation found, with its verdict and the levels of its drugs, as in Beta-tubulin E198A (resistance: Carbendazim 7, Iprodione 8). A change with evidence against resistance only reads (no resistance: Iprodione -8). The NOTE of a sample that is not screened reaches the console the same way.

docs.title: ChroQueTas's own files
docs.text:
05.amr/{sample}/chroquetas/nuclear/ and mitochondrial/ hold ChroQueTas's output as it wrote it, the files to read when a call needs checking. FunFlux hands the genome to ChroQueTas as genome.fasta in the nuclear run and as mito.fasta in the mitochondrial run, and ChroQueTas names its files after it (<name> below):

File Content <name>.ChroQueTaS.AMR_summary.txt every FungAMR and new mutation of the run: Protein, Fragment, Position_reference, AA_reference, AA_query, Fungicide_resistance; or the single line No AMR mutations found in <name> <name>.ChroQueTaS.AMR_stats.txt per target, the number of FungAMR and new mutations; absent when there is none <name>.ChroQueTaS.<target>.<fragment>.tsv every FungAMR position of that copy: Position, Reference, Query, Result, Fungicides; or the single WARNING line of a protein whose positions were not compared <name>_<target>.<fragment>.faa the protein extracted from the genome <name>_<target>.<fragment>.paf miniprot's alignment of the reference protein to the genome; fields 6 to 9 give the contig and the coordinates <name>_<target>.<fragment>.blastp.txt the BLASTP comparison with the reference: identity, coverage, lengths, gaps; only for a protein that passed the thresholds tmp/ ChroQueTas's working files

A target miniprot could not extract has no file at all, and a run that was not made has no folder. mitochondrial/ exists only when the species has cytochrome b and its mitochondrial run was made (Two runs).

Files added to chroquetas/ are lost when amr_chroquetas runs again

Snakemake deletes the whole chroquetas/ folder before amr_chroquetas runs again, so each run starts clean, and files you add there are lost.

docs.title: How the step runs
docs.text:
Two rules make the tables. Both run only with parameters.amr.chroquetas: on.

Rule Runs Does Writes chroquetas_db once per output folder downloads bin/ChroQueTas.sh, FungAMR_db/db-v20250811.tgz and LICENSE from links.chroquetas_link, checks the script and the archive against their SHA-256, unpacks the archive (Reference databases); conda environment download for curl and tar, and sha256sum of the machine 00.resources/chroquetas/ amr_chroquetas once per sample, as soon as contigs_final.fasta exists (and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta where it is read) a FunFlux script matches the species to a database folder, runs ChroQueTas once or twice (Two runs) and writes the three tables; conda environment chroquetas; up to 4 threads; seconds 05.amr/{sample}/

The FunFlux script runs with the Python 3.12 of the chroquetas environment. That environment holds the tools ChroQueTas calls, at the versions its authors pin in their own conda package: BLAST+ 2.16.0, EMBOSS 6.6.0, MAFFT 7.525, miniprot 0.14 and SeqKit 2.1.0. ChroQueTas itself is a bash script and is not in the environment. The FunFlux script runs it as bash ChroQueTas.sh ... from 00.resources/chroquetas/. ChroQueTas takes bash, GNU grep (it uses grep -P), sed and basic commands such as cut, paste and tr from the machine (Commands outside the conda environments).

A failed ChroQueTas run stops the job with [FunFlux] amr_chroquetas: error: ... and the last 20 lines of ChroQueTas's log (Troubleshooting). A run in which no target could be extracted is not a failure, and every target is then not found.

The AMR screen reads only the assembly, so it runs early, beside the annotation, without waiting for it.

docs.title: Licence, and why the step is off
docs.text:
ChroQueTas and the FungAMR database that comes with it are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: use for non-commercial purposes only, with credit to the authors, and no distribution of modified copies. ChroQueTas is not packaged on bioconda or conda-forge, and its authors publish it on their own conda channel. FunFlux therefore handles both as follows.

  • It ships neither the script nor the database, and never changes them.
  • It downloads both at run time, unchanged, from one pinned commit of the authors' GitHub repository, and checks them against SHA-256 checksums before anything runs them.
  • It runs the script with the tools it needs from a pinned environment of bioconda and conda-forge packages.
  • It keeps the step off by default.

Switching the AMR screen on accepts a non-commercial licence

Setting parameters.amr.chroquetas: on is your acceptance of that licence, as naming a SignalP 6 archive is for DTU's. For commercial use, ask the authors.

Every dry run prints whether the AMR screen is on: AMR screen: ChroQueTas on (licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use). or AMR screen: off. 00.resources/chroquetas/ holds the script, the database and their licence text. The licence allows passing them on unchanged, for non-commercial purposes and with credit (Licensing).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
These are the settings of the AMR screen, with their defaults:

parameters:
  amr:
    chroquetas: off
    mito_genetic_code: auto
    chroquetas_script_sha256: d8961a0d311be57d4a9939bd9e4d90dbc796589b3298dd1835359ed776abfce3
    chroquetas_db_sha256: 6f89ecb3117110aad85b8b6ca7b8a3d3715cb5984b6cb75450a6cda5633d16e7
links:
  chroquetas_link: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nmquijada/ChroQueTas/1aad051d6ad48f5e403636699d19095e655764f7
Key Default Allowed values What it does chroquetas off off (also empty, false, no, 0, none, null), on (also true, yes, 1) on: every sample is screened, the report gets the AMR table, and links.chroquetas_link is required. off: none of this, and the link is not read. mito_genetic_code auto auto (any case; an empty value too), or the number of an NCBI genetic code: 1-6, 9-16 or 21-33 The genetic code of the mitochondrial run (Two runs). A number is used for every sample of the run. chroquetas_script_sha256 the checksum of bin/ChroQueTas.sh at the template address 64 hexadecimal characters The SHA-256 the downloaded script must have. chroquetas_db_sha256 the checksum of FungAMR_db/db-v20250811.tgz at the template address 64 hexadecimal characters The SHA-256 the downloaded database archive must have, checked before it is unpacked. links.chroquetas_link template URL the raw-file address of one commit of the ChroQueTas repository, without a trailing file name Where chroquetas_db downloads the three files. Required when chroquetas is on.

The address names one commit, so the files behind it do not change. To move to a newer version of ChroQueTas, change the link and both checksums together (Reference databases). FunFlux reads the files ChroQueTas 1.0.1 writes, and the position lists of its database (<target>.txt, for the known resistance changes). A version that writes them differently stops amr_chroquetas with an error, and needs a newer FunFlux. The keys are checked before any job starts, and a value outside the list stops the run with a [FunFlux] parameters.amr.<key>: ... message (Troubleshooting).

The table lists what each change runs again.

Change Runs again mito_genetic_code amr_chroquetas of every sample, and the report column 2 of the annotation table, the species amr_chroquetas of that sample; the species is also funannotate's, so augustus_model_check, funannotate_prediction and everything after them for that sample too links.chroquetas_link or a checksum chroquetas_db, then amr_chroquetas of every sample a new contigs_final.fasta or contigs_mitochondrial.fasta amr_chroquetas of that sample chroquetas: on adds the two rules chroquetas: off the report, without the AMR table; 05.amr/ stays on disk

A change to an AMR screen setting runs only the AMR screen and the report again. Snakemake's reasons for running a step again are listed under What makes Snakemake re-run a rule.

A change of species also runs the annotation of that sample again

The species in column 2 of the annotation table is funannotate's as well, so changing it runs the gene prediction and the annotation of that sample again, not only its AMR screen.

docs.title: A worked example: Botrytis cinerea B05.10
docs.text:
The public benchmark genome, Botrytis cinerea B05.10, was run in hybrid mode. Public ONT reads of the strain were assembled with hifiasm, and Polypolish corrected the assembly with the strain's public Illumina pairs. contigs_final.fasta holds 33 contigs, and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta the one mitochondrial contig. Column 2 of the annotation table reads Botrytis cinerea, which matches the folder Botrytis_cinerea at the first try. The folder holds three proteins under four target names. Beta-tubulin, and Bos1 and OS1, two entries of one histidine kinase, are in the nucleus, and Cytochrome_b is in the mitochondrion.

The nuclear run, with the standard code ChroQueTas chose, took 4.0 s and 0.58 GB of memory. The mitochondrial run, with code 4 (auto for this species), took 1.0 s. amr_summary.tsv reads, in part:

target compartment status positions_checked verdict fungamr_mutations resistance_to no_resistance_to Beta-tubulin nuclear evaluated 3 resistance E198A (resistance) Carbendazim (E198A, 7); Iprodione (E198A, 8) - Bos1 nuclear evaluated 11 wild type - - - Cytochrome_b mitochondrial not evaluated 0 - - - - OS1 nuclear evaluated 2 wild type - - -

The β-tubulin rows of amr_positions.tsv read, in part:

position reference_aa found_aa call verdict resistance_to known_resistance_changes 198 E A FungAMR mutation resistance Carbendazim (7: population association study); Iprodione (8: natural isolates, not validated further) E198A, E198G, E198K, E198V 200 F F no mutation wild type - F200Y 351 T T no mutation wild type - T351I

B05.10 carries β-tubulin E198A, verdict resistance. Its histidine kinase (Bos1, OS1) is wild type, and cytochrome b is not evaluated, the expected outcome for this strain, as explained below.

  • β-tubulin E198A. The extracted protein matches the FungAMR reference (UniProt P53373) at 99.8 % identity over its whole length, and position 198 is alanine where the reference has glutamate. FungAMR holds evidence that E198A causes resistance to carbendazim at level 7 (a population-level association) and to iprodione at level 8, and none against it, so the verdict is resistance. The protein of the B05.10 reference annotation, BctubA (RefSeq XP_024546500.1), also has alanine at 198, so the call is the genotype of the strain, not an error of the assembly. The iprodione entry is of the kind described under What a level does not say: iprodione acts on the osmotic stress pathway, not on tubulin.
  • The known resistance changes. E198A is one of four changes at position 198 with evidence of resistance. Positions 200 and 351 carry the wild type, and their rows name the change that would matter there: F200Y (carbendazim, level 7, and diethofencarb, level 8) and T351I (zoxamide, level 8).
  • Bos1 and OS1, two entries of the same protein with 11 and 2 positions (12 distinct, as 373 is in both), were found at 99.9 % identity. They have the reference amino acid at every FungAMR position, so their verdict is wild type. The nuclear run did not extract cytochrome b, as expected, because the mitochondrion is not in contigs_final.fasta.
  • Cytochrome b. The mitochondrial run extracted a protein of 398 amino acids against the reference's 391, at 96.2 % identity. The protein has 7 residues the reference lacks, so ChroQueTas compared no position. The status is not evaluated, and the verdict -. The same run with the standard code (table 1) did worse, with 91.2 % identity, 17 gaps, and five tryptophans, encoded by TGA, read as stops. That is why the mitochondrial run gets its own code.

Cytochrome b has insertions because of its introns. In B05.10 the gene has four introns, and two of them enclose a short exon of 12 codons, codons 132 to 143. One intron, of 1,366 bp, ends just before codon 132, and the other, of 1,205 bp, starts right after codon 143. Codon 142 is TGA, tryptophan in code 4, and codon 143 is GGT, glycine, the wild type. The next exon starts with codon 144.

Neither intron starts with GT and ends with AG, as most introns do: the first reads TA...TG, the second TT...TG. Because miniprot penalises intron ends other than GT-AG (Li 2023), it ended both introns too early and translated their last nucleotides as protein. That gave 3 extra residues around codon 131, and 4 at codons 142 and 143, where the protein it built reads MMINAL instead of WG. Together they make the 7 residues the reference lacks.
