The intron matters beyond the alignment. Banno et al. (2009) found two forms of the B. cinerea cytochrome b gene among field isolates: one with three introns, and one with an additional intron between codons 143 and 144, the form B05.10 carries. All 88 isolates with that intron were sensitive to the QoI fungicide azoxystrobin. The authors suggested that G143A, the change known to make plant pathogens resistant to QoI fungicides, would keep the intron from splicing itself out. Grasso et al. (2006) found an intron at the same place in the rusts and in Alternaria solani, in which G143A has never been reported. For a strain like B05.10, a not evaluated cytochrome b is therefore the expected outcome, and G143A is not expected.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Species. 57 species have a database folder. Any other species is not screened, and FunFlux does not fall back to a related species. The species says where to look instead.
  • Single mutations only. A combination of mutations that causes resistance only together, gene duplication or loss, aneuploidy and changes outside the protein are not detected (FungAMR and ChroQueTas).
  • Introns that miniprot cannot place. A gene with an intron whose ends are not GT...AG, as in the mitochondrial cytochrome b of B05.10, can come out with extra residues and stay not evaluated. The .faa then holds wrong residues around the misplaced junction (in B05.10, MMINAL where codons 142 and 143 should read WG), so do not read the position from it. Align the reference protein to the contig with the right genetic code instead, and read the position from the hit that covers it, since the hits follow the exons. BLAST+ is in the chroquetas environment: tblastn -query 00.resources/chroquetas/FungAMR_db/<species>/Cytochrome_b.faa -subject 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_mitochondrial.fasta -db_gencode 4 -outfmt '6 qstart qend sstart send pident qseq sseq'. In B05.10 the hit for codons 132 to 143 reads YVLPYGQMSLWG, glycine at 143. The .paf (fields 6 to 9) shows which contig and region miniprot used.
  • Nonsense mutations. A premature stop codon at a FungAMR position comes out as no alignment, not as a FungAMR mutation, even where FungAMR lists the stop. FungAMR lists such a stop, written X, in 242 rows, most of them in Saccharomyces cerevisiae Fcy1 and Fur1, for 5-fluorocytosine. The .faa of the copy shows the stop as *.
  • An unconfirmed mitochondrion. When the contamination and mitochondrion screen splits the mitochondrion off but confirms no contig, cytochrome b is not evaluated, even if the mitochondrion sits unconfirmed among the contigs of contigs_final.fasta. mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv says why no contig was confirmed (Mitochondria).
  • The genetic code is one per run. mito_genetic_code sets one code for the mitochondrial run of every sample, so a batch of species with different mitochondrial codes needs auto.
  • The assembly. A target split across two contigs, or with a sequencing error at a FungAMR position, gives a second copy, a lower identity or a false call. Read the .paf and .blastp.txt files of a surprising call. A copy cut at a contig end can still pass the filter of step 2 while it lacks up to a quarter of the protein. The positions it lacks are no alignment, also where FungAMR lists a deletion, and a codon with N bases is position not found (FungAMR and ChroQueTas). Neither is a finding about the strain.
  • Paths without spaces. ChroQueTas uses its file paths without quotes, so a space in the path of the output folder or of the database breaks it. The job then stops with [FunFlux] amr_chroquetas: error: ... before ChroQueTas starts.
  • Evidence, not phenotype. A verdict sums up what FungAMR records about a change (Verdicts). It is not a susceptibility test, and does not replace one for a decision on a treatment or a spray programme. ChroQueTas itself ends each completed run with the reminder that its mutations must be weighed by their confidence scores.

docs.title: How to cite
docs.text: Cite FungAMR and ChroQueTas through Bédard et al. (2025), as the ChroQueTas authors ask, together with the ChroQueTas repository and version (Quijada et al., 1.0.1). Also cite the tools ChroQueTas runs: miniprot (Li 2023), BLAST+ (Camacho et al. 2009), MAFFT (Katoh and Standley 2013), SeqKit (Shen et al. 2016) and EMBOSS (Rice et al. 2000). The full references are on Citation and references.

docs.title: Assembly QC
docs.text:
Three tools check the quality of each sample's assembly. QUAST measures its size and contiguity, and BUSCO its completeness. In the read-based modes, Qualimap also shows how the sample's reads map back to the draft. Read this page to interpret their results, to choose the BUSCO lineage of a batch and to find their files.

QUAST and BUSCO run on 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta, the nuclear genome that ITS extraction and funannotate also read. When the contamination and mitochondrion screen runs with the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, the mitochondrion has been split off before this point, as described in Mitochondria. If it were left in, its genetic code, gene content and copy number would distort both the contig statistics and the BUSCO counts of a genome that is annotated as nuclear. In contigs mode without the screen, contigs_final.fasta is the input FASTA after the contig filter.

Tool Version Measures Rule Output, in 02.assembly/{sample}/ If the tool fails QUAST 5.3.0 size and contiguity genome_assembly_evaluation eval/quast/ a line in the log; the run continues BUSCO 6.0.0 completeness of conserved single-copy genes completeness eval/busco/ the job fails and the run stops (--keep-going lets the other jobs finish) Qualimap 2.3 reads mapped back to the draft (read-based modes) map_evaluation eval/qualimap/ a line in the log; the run continues

Only MultiQC and the contig summary read these results. The contig summary counts the complete BUSCO markers on each contig and is written after the annotation (Contig summary).

Terms used on this page

nuclear genome the delivered genome without the confirmed mitochondrial contigs, contigs_final.fasta; it holds every contig when nothing is split off (parameters.mitochondria.mode off or report, or no screen) the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true draft assembly (the draft) the assembly the screen examines, before any contig is removed: contigs_filt.fasta in illumina mode and in contigs mode with the screen, assembly.fasta in longread and hybrid guide assembly in hybrid mode, the SPAdes assembly of the Illumina reads; it is screened, and only the pairs that map to it go on read-based modes (read modes) the modes illumina, longread and hybrid, which start from reads, as against contigs coverage track the reads aligned back to the draft, contaminants/{sample}_map.bam; BlobTools takes each contig's coverage from it and Qualimap its report; in contigs mode, the contigs aligned to themselves lineage dataset the BUSCO gene set of one taxonomic group, such as hypocreales_odb12, for the completeness check; with lineage: auto, BUSCO chooses one by placing the genome contig summary the table 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv: one row per contig of the draft, with its evidence (telomeres, depth, rDNA units, genes) and a verdict

docs.title: QUAST
docs.text:
QUAST measures the size and contiguity of the genome. Rule genome_assembly_evaluation runs it:

quast contigs_final.fasta -o eval/quast --labels {sample} --no-icarus -t <threads>
# hybrid: the screened guide assembly first, then the final genome, two labels
quast guide/contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta contigs_final.fasta -o eval/quast \
  --labels {sample}_guide,{sample} --no-icarus -t <threads>

QUAST uses min(resources.threads, 24) threads. It runs without a reference genome, so it reports size and contiguity only, with no misassemblies, no genome fraction and no NG50. Contigs shorter than 500 bp, QUAST's default minimum, are left out of every statistic except the rows marked (>= 0 bp). --labels names the assembly after the sample, so QUAST and MultiQC show the sample name. --no-icarus leaves out QUAST's interactive contig viewer.

When QUAST fails, its log ends with [FunFlux] genome_assembly_evaluation: QUAST exited with an error for sample S. ..., eval/quast/ stays in place, and the MultiQC page has no QUAST row for that sample.

In hybrid mode, one QUAST call compares the screened Illumina guide assembly with the final genome, labelled {sample}_guide and {sample} in that order. The guide is the short-read view of the same isolate, so the two rows show what the long reads added.

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text:
QUAST writes its report as eval/quast/report.tsv, also as .txt, .html, .pdf and .tex, and transposed as transposed_report.*. These are some of its rows:

Row Meaning # contigs (>= 0 bp) all contigs # contigs (>= 1000 bp) to (>= 50000 bp) contigs of at least 1, 5, 10, 25 and 50 kb Total length (>= 0 bp) sum of all contig lengths (bp) Total length (>= 50000 bp) bases in contigs of 50 kb or more # contigs contigs of 500 bp or more Largest contig length of the longest contig (bp) Total length bases in contigs of 500 bp or more GC (%) GC content N50 contigs of this length or longer hold half of the total length N90 the same for 90 % of the total length auN sum of the squared contig lengths divided by the total length: the mean length of the contig that a random base lies in L50 the number of contigs, longest first, that hold half of the total length L90 the same for 90 % # N's per 100 kbp gap characters

A higher N50 and auN and a lower L50 mean fewer and longer contigs.

docs.title: BUSCO
docs.text:
BUSCO searches the genome for genes that nearly every member of a lineage carries exactly once (single-copy orthologs) and reports how many it finds whole, duplicated, in pieces or not at all.

busco --mode genome -i contigs_final.fasta --out {sample} --out_path eval/busco \
  --download_path eval/busco/busco_tmp --auto-lineage-euk --opt-out-run-stats --cpu <threads>

Rule completeness uses min(resources.threads, 24) threads, as QUAST does. With a fixed lineage, -l <lineage> replaces --auto-lineage-euk, and --offline --download_path 00.resources/busco replaces the download folder of the sample. In a eukaryote genome, BUSCO 6.0.0 finds the genes with miniprot unless another predictor is requested. FunFlux requests none, and the summary says BUSCO was run in mode: euk_genome_min.

docs.title: Automatic or fixed lineage
docs.text:
The key parameters.busco.lineage names the dataset BUSCO uses, or leaves the choice to BUSCO:

parameters:
  busco:
    lineage: auto        # or a dataset name such as hypocreales_odb12
Setting What BUSCO runs Summaries in eval/busco/ MultiQC rows per sample auto (default) eukaryota_odb12, then the most specific lineage it reaches by placing the genome in the eukaryote tree short_summary.generic.eukaryota_odb12.{sample}.txt and short_summary.specific.<lineage>.{sample}.txt 2 a dataset name that dataset only short_summary.specific.<lineage>.{sample}.txt 1

For a batch, a fixed lineage keeps the BUSCO numbers comparable

Each sample is placed on its own, so auto can choose different lineages for the samples of one batch, and their numbers are then not comparable. A fixed lineage gives every sample the same dataset, skips the eukaryota run and the placement, and leaves a smaller result folder.

Each summary also exists as .json. The log names the lineage that the placement chose, in the line Lineage <lineage> is selected, supported by <n> markers out of <m>. A dataset name must match [a-z0-9_]+_odb[0-9]+ after lower-casing, or the dry run stops. busco --list-datasets prints the available names, each with its version after a dot, as in hypocreales_odb12.2. Leave out the dot and the number after it.

docs.title: Reading the summary
docs.text:
Each summary has one result line of this form:

C:<C>%[S:<S>%,D:<D>%],F:<F>%,M:<M>%,n:<n>,E:<E>%

C is the completeness of the genome, and D, F, M and E say what lies behind it:

Letter Meaning What an unusual value can mean C complete: found over its full length, S + D a lower C after a decontamination policy removed contigs points to removed genome rather than removed contamination (Decontamination) S complete, one copy D complete, two or more copies a high D can come from a recent whole-genome duplication, from haplotypes assembled separately, or from a mixed culture of two fungi of the same lineage, in which each gene is present twice F fragmented: found in part the gene is only partly present, or no full-length gene model was built although the gene may be there M missing the gene is absent, or the search found no significant match n genes in the dataset E complete genes whose miniprot prediction contains an internal stop codon caution before using BUSCO's predicted sequences downstream; those genes still count as complete

The readings of D (genome duplication, haplotypes), F, M and E are those of the BUSCO user guide.

The header of each summary names the dataset and its creation date, for example hypocreales_odb12 (Creation date: 2026-05-22, number of genomes: 76, number of BUSCOs: 4349). With auto, BUSCO downloads the current dataset at every run, and a newer dataset can change the numbers. Compare samples only across runs with the same dataset date. A fixed lineage is downloaded once per output folder, so every later run into that folder uses the same release.

docs.title: Downloads, disk and network
docs.text:
The lineage setting also decides where the datasets come from, and when BUSCO needs the network:

Setting Where the datasets come from Network auto every BUSCO job downloads its datasets into eval/busco/busco_tmp/, which is deleted when the job ends. Each sample downloads its own copy, because two BUSCO jobs downloading into one folder can corrupt it. The job downloads eukaryota_odb12, the placement files and the chosen lineage in every BUSCO job, on the computer that runs it a fixed lineage rule busco_data downloads it once per output folder into 00.resources/busco/lineages/<lineage>/, on the computer that runs Snakemake (logs/busco_data.log). Every BUSCO job reads it with --offline and writes nothing there, so the samples share one copy once; the BUSCO jobs need none

With auto, the computer that runs BUSCO needs internet in every job

A fixed lineage needs internet once, on the computer that runs Snakemake, and the BUSCO jobs need none. This is how BUSCO runs on cluster nodes without internet (Network access).

With a fixed lineage, the JSON summary records offline: True and the path of the shared lineage folder, 00.resources/busco/lineages/<lineage>/. The .txt summary and full_table.tsv are the same as with a download per job.

The odb12 datasets of 2026-05-22 have these archive sizes:

Dataset Archive size (MB) eukaryota 29.1 fungi 125.8 ascomycota 310.5 sordariomycetes 311.7 hypocreales 274.6 basidiomycota 151.2 agaricomycetes 196.7 mucoromycota 132.1

With auto, a job therefore downloads tens to hundreds of MB, every time. This is what stays on disk afterwards:

In eval/busco/ After the run the summaries kept run_<lineage>/: full_table.tsv (one line per gene with its status and location), missing_busco_list.tsv, miniprot_output/, BUSCO's own copy of the summary kept auto_lineage/, logs/, tmp/ kept every hmmer_output/ and busco_sequences/ folder deleted

The folder keeps hundreds of MB per sample.

FunFlux passes --opt-out-run-stats, so BUSCO 6.0.0 sends no usage statistics to busco-data.ezlab.org and makes no ipinfo.io lookup. Without the flag, BUSCO would send run details, results, a checksum of the input FASTA and the country of the machine's IP address. The flag changes no result.

docs.title: Qualimap (read modes)
docs.text:
Qualimap shows how the sample's reads map back to the draft. Rule map_evaluation runs it in illumina, longread and hybrid mode:

unset DISPLAY
JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-Djava.awt.headless=true" \
qualimap bamqc -bam contaminants/{sample}_map.bam --java-mem-size=<min(ram_gb, 64)>G \
  -nt <min(threads, 24)> -outdir eval/qualimap -outformat html

The BAM is the coverage track of the screen, the sample's reads aligned to the draft before decontamination (Decontamination). Every read-based mode gets a report on the reads that built the draft, hybrid a second one for the Illumina guide, and contigs mode none:

Mode Rule Reads in the BAM Report in 02.assembly/{sample}/ illumina map_evaluation the trimmed Illumina pairs (bowtie2) eval/qualimap/ longread map_evaluation the filtered long reads (minimap2) eval/qualimap/ hybrid map_evaluation the filtered long reads (minimap2) eval/qualimap/ hybrid map_guide_evaluation, the same command the Illumina pairs mapped to the guide assembly (guide/contaminants/{sample}_map.bam) guide/eval/qualimap/ contigs none its only BAM is the contigs aligned to themselves

The Java heap is the smaller of resources.ram_gb and 64 GB, and a changed ram_gb does not re-run the report (CPU cores and threads). The two settings in front of the command let Qualimap draw its plots on a server without a display. The Java runtime notes them with one Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS line in the log, which is expected.

When Qualimap fails, the log ends with [FunFlux] map_evaluation: Qualimap exited with an error for sample S. ..., eval/qualimap/ stays in place, empty, and the MultiQC page has no mapping table for the sample.

The report gives the share of mapped reads, insert sizes of read pairs, mapping quality, GC content, error rate, the depth along the draft and, in genome_results.txt, the mean depth of every contig. The mitochondrion stands out by its depth, because a cell holds many copies of it. A contaminant often has a depth different from that of the isolate.

docs.title: In the MultiQC report
docs.text:
MultiQC reads eval/quast/report.tsv, the BUSCO summaries and, in the read-based modes, eval/qualimap/ of every sample into 06.report/multiqc_report.html. In hybrid it also reads guide/eval/qualimap/. Each tool has one row per sample, with a second QUAST and Qualimap row for the guide in hybrid and a second BUSCO row with the automatic lineage:

Mode QUAST rows BUSCO rows Qualimap rows contigs 1 2 with the automatic lineage, 1 with a fixed one none illumina, longread 1 as above 1: mapping QC | <sample> hybrid 2 as above 2: mapping QC | <sample> and mapping Illumina QC | <sample>

The report also holds the contig summary table of every sample, with one row per contig of the draft assembly (Contig summary). Report describes the row names, the General Statistics table and the BUSCO folders that MultiQC skips.

docs.title: Re-runs
docs.text:
Snakemake deletes eval/quast/, eval/busco/ and eval/qualimap/ before it runs the step again, so files you add to these folders are lost. These changes re-run the following steps:

Change Re-runs contigs_final.fasta, for example after a new decontamination policy or mitochondrion threshold QUAST and BUSCO the BAM, that is, a new draft or new reads Qualimap busco.lineage BUSCO, the contig summary and MultiQC only, after busco_data has downloaded a newly named lineage

A new BUSCO lineage therefore re-runs only BUSCO and the two steps that read it, not the assembly or the annotation.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Everything these steps write is kept, except BUSCO's download folder, busco_tmp/, and the hmmer_output/ and busco_sequences/ folders inside eval/busco/.

Path Kept Read by 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/ yes MultiQC (report.tsv) 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/ yes MultiQC (the short_summary.*.txt files) 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/busco_tmp/ (auto only) no BUSCO (downloaded datasets) 00.resources/busco/lineages/<lineage>/, 00.resources/busco/file_versions.tsv (fixed lineage only) yes BUSCO, in every later run into the output folder 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/qualimap/ yes (read-based modes) MultiQC 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/eval/qualimap/ yes (hybrid) MultiQC 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/telomere_candidates.tsv, telomere_unit.txt, telomere_ends.tsv yes the contig summary; you. The telomere repeat unit of the assembly, from tidk (Contig summary) 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv, contig_summary_mqc.tsv yes you; MultiQC (contig_summary_mqc.tsv). Written after the annotation (Contig summary) 06.report/multiqc_report.html, 06.report/multiqc_data/, 06.report/multiqc_config.yaml yes you logs/genome_assembly_evaluation_{sample}.log, logs/completeness_{sample}.log, logs/busco_data.log (fixed lineage), logs/map_evaluation_{sample}.log, logs/map_guide_evaluation_{sample}.log, logs/telomere_units_{sample}.log, logs/contig_summary_{sample}.log, logs/multiqc.log yes you

The full output tree is on Output files.

docs.title: Contig summary
docs.text:
A fungal assembly is a list of contigs, and the list alone does not say what each contig is. For every sample, FunFlux writes one table that does: 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv. It has one row per contig of the draft assembly, with the evidence the run produced about that contig and a verdict with its reasons. The table also appears in the MultiQC report. Read this page to interpret the verdicts, to see how the telomere repeat unit is chosen, and to set the unit yourself when the data cannot choose it.

Terms used on this page

draft assembly (the draft) the assembly before the screen removes any contig, such as contigs_filt.fasta or assembly.fasta; the contig summary describes it the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true verdict the label the contig summary gives each draft contig, one of ten such as chromosome, chromosome_arm, rDNA_array or mitochondrion, with its reasons telomere repeat unit (telomere unit) the short sequence repeated in tandem at chromosome ends, TTAGGG in most filamentous fungi; FunFlux chooses it from each assembly unless parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif names one telomere array tandem copies of the telomere repeat unit at a contig end; by default a telomere needs 5 or more copies within 25,000 bp of the end canonical form the spelling tidk gives a repeat unit: the alphabetically first of its rotations and those of its reverse complement, so TTAGGG is written AACCCT rDNA unit one copy of the repeat SSU-ITS1-5.8S-ITS2-LSU; FunFlux counts one per 5.8S gene found, that is, one per ITS window BUSCO marker a BUSCO gene found complete on a contig (Complete or Duplicated); the contig summary counts them per contig as evidence of nuclear sequence

docs.title: What the contigs of a fungal assembly are
docs.text:
A long-read assembly of a filamentous fungus holds a few kinds of contig side by side, and a short-read assembly adds two more kinds, by the hundred. Each kind has its own signature in the evidence FunFlux already produces, as the table below shows. Telomeres, the first piece of evidence, are tandem arrays of a short repeat unit that cap every chromosome end. The unit is TTAGGG in most filamentous fungi. The left end of a chromosome reads CCCTAA on the forward strand, and the right end reads TTAGGG.

Kind of contig Telomere arrays Read depth Genes and BUSCO markers Other signs whole chromosome, telomere to telomere at both ends the depth of the bulk of the genome along its whole length size says nothing: an accessory chromosome or a minichromosome of 200 to 300 kb is a chromosome like a 4-Mb one chromosome arm at one end only; the other end is where the assembler stopped, usually at a repeat it could not resolve: the rDNA array, a centromere as a chromosome as a chromosome mitochondrion, a small genome (82 kb in Botrytis cinerea B05.10, the worked example) present in many copies per cell several times the nuclear depth a long-read assembler usually closes it into a circle and flags it as circular piece of the rDNA array can carry one at one end, when the array sits at a chromosome end says little: the reads of all the copies are shared out over however many pieces the assembler made of the array no BUSCO marker; few or no protein-coding genes several 5.8S genes in a row (the ITS windows of the taxonomy step, one per rDNA unit) alternative copy of a region, or noise: a second haplotype assembled on its own, a stretch assembled twice, or a leftover of the assembly graph well below the genome's, because the reads of the region were split between two copies, or were few contaminant: a contig from another organism its own, not the genome's its own GC content; the screen labelled it with a genus from its BLAST hits and removed it collapsed repeat (short-read assemblies) well above the genome's: the reads of all the copies pile up on it no BUSCO marker, at most a gene call or two (predictors call open reading frames inside transposons) several genome copies of a transposon, a satellite or another repeat family, assembled into one contig because short reads cannot tell the copies apart short piece of the nuclear genome (short-read assemblies) the depth of the genome none, because it is too short to carry a gene hundreds to a few thousand bases; nuclear sequence all the same, left over where the assembly broke

An empty cell means that the evidence is not part of that kind's signature. Taken together, the columns sort the contigs. Telomeres tell a chromosome from an arm. Depth sets the mitochondrion, collapsed repeats and alternative copies apart from the nuclear genome. Genes and BUSCO markers tell nuclear sequence from rDNA and debris. A few points the table cannot hold:

  • With the default settings, the mitochondrion screen confirms the mitochondrion from a BLAST hit to a mitochondrial genome that covers at least 35 % of the contig. In contigs and illumina mode, and on the Illumina guide assembly of hybrid mode, that hit is enough. On the long-read assembly of longread and hybrid mode, the hit must also be backed by the assembler's evidence, unless it covers 70 % or more. That support is an assembler depth of at least 3 times the median of all contigs, or a clean circle: a contig recorded as circular, not a repeat and in no alternative group. By default, the confirmed mitochondrion is then split off before the annotation. See Mitochondria.
  • The ribosomal RNA genes sit in tens to hundreds of tandem copies of one unit, SSU-ITS1-5.8S-ITS2-LSU, that no assembler resolves whole.
  • A long-read assembler resolves most repeats in place, so a long-read assembly has few collapsed repeats.

The contig summary gathers the evidence behind these signatures into one row per contig, and says for each contig how it was weighed. The telomere arrays are found with tidk, in the sequence itself. The other evidence is the read depth, the assembler's depth and circularity flag, the rDNA units, the BUSCO markers, the predicted genes, and the calls of the contamination and mitochondrion screen.

docs.title: The table
docs.text:
02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv has one row per contig of the draft assembly. Its verdict and reason columns give the answer, annotated_as gives the contig's name in the annotation, and the other columns hold the evidence:

Column Content NA when contig the name in the draft assembly: the first word of the FASTA header, as the screen tables use it never length bp never gc GC fraction, 3 decimals never depth read depth from the BlobTools table (bam0), 2 decimals contigs mode; a contig without a row in the table depth_x_median depth divided by the median depth of the nuclear genome, 2 decimals (the median) depth is NA assembler_depth the assembler's own depth, 1 decimal illumina and contigs mode; an empty cell in assembly_evidence.tsv circular Y or N, the assembler's flag illumina and contigs mode telomere_start, telomere_end copies of the telomere unit in the array at that end: the array length tidk measured, divided by the unit length and rounded; only an array that points the way a telomere points counts (Telomeres) never (0 when none) telomere_end_offset_start, telomere_end_offset_end distance (bp) from the contig end to the array no telomere array at that end telomere_unit the telomere repeat unit of the assembly in tidk's canonical form (AACCCT for TTAGGG), the same on every row of a sample; none when no unit was found never rdna_units ITS windows on the contig, that is, 5.8S genes found never (0 when none) busco_markers complete BUSCO markers on the contig (status Complete or Duplicated; a duplicated marker counts where each copy lies) never (0 when none) genes mRNA features of the annotation on the scaffold the contig became the contig has no scaffold in contigs_sort.fasta: dropped by funannotate clean, split off as the mitochondrion, or removed by the screen genus assigned_genus of contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv no screen screen kept (<reason>), removed (<reason>) or mitochondrion (<reason>), with the reason of the contig selector or, for a mitochondrion, of the mitochondrion screen; a mitochondrial_candidate, circular_unclassified or high_coverage_unclassified class of the mitochondrion screen is appended after ; no screen annotated_as scaffold_N, the name of the contig in every annotation file; or dropped by funannotate clean, not annotated (mitochondrion), not annotated (removed by the screen) never verdict one of the ten verdicts (The verdict): mitochondrion, contaminant, rDNA_array, chromosome, chromosome_arm, low_depth, repeat, nuclear_contig, nuclear_fragment, unclassified never reason the evidence behind the verdict, in words, for example telomere repeats at both ends (17 and 19 copies); depth 1.00x the median; 543 genes, 131 BUSCO markers never

The table describes the draft assembly, which is contigs_final.fasta only in contigs mode without the screen. Which file is the draft depends on the mode:

Mode The draft illumina; contigs with the screen contigs_filt.fasta longread, hybrid assembly.fasta contigs without the screen contigs_final.fasta

The contigs the screen removed and the mitochondrion have a row too

Because the table describes the draft, the contigs the screen removed and the mitochondrion get a row too, and nothing disappears silently. Evidence a mode cannot produce is NA, and the verdict rests on the rest.

docs.title: The verdict
docs.text:
Ten verdict rules give each contig its verdict. They are tried in the order of the table below, and the first that applies decides. Evidence a mode cannot produce is unknown (NA in the table) and is not tested, so "depth within 0.5 to 1.5 times the median when known" passes when the depth is unknown. A telomere is a contig end where tidk found an array of the telomere unit of at least min_telomere_copies copies, pointing the way a telomere points.

Rule Verdict The contig has What it is 1 mitochondrion the class confirmed_mitochondrial from the mitochondrion screen, or a place in contigs_mitochondrial.fasta the mitochondrial genome 2 contaminant the action remove from the screen; the reason names the genus a contig of another organism 3 rDNA_array at least parameters.contig_summary.min_rdna_units rDNA units (3 by default), and fewer predicted genes than rDNA units, or no gene count a piece of the rDNA array 4 chromosome telomere repeats at both ends; depth within 0.5 to 1.5 times the median when known; at least one gene when known a whole chromosome; size plays no part, so a small accessory chromosome qualifies 5 chromosome_arm telomere repeats at one end; the rest as in rule 4 a chromosome arm 6 low_depth depth below 0.5 times the median an alternative copy of a region (a second haplotype, a stretch assembled twice) or noise 7 repeat no BUSCO marker; at most two predicted genes; depth above 1.5 times the median (when the depth is unknown this rule does not fire) a collapsed repeat: several genome copies of a transposon, a satellite or another repeat family assembled into one contig, so the reads of all the copies pile up on it 8 nuclear_contig at least one gene or BUSCO marker; depth within 0.5 to 1.5 times the median when known; no telomere repeat a fragment of a chromosome 9 nuclear_fragment no gene and no BUSCO marker; no telomere repeat; depth within 0.5 to 1.5 times the median, or unknown a piece of the nuclear genome too short to carry a gene; a short-read assembly ends in many of them 10 unclassified anything else the reason says what was and was not seen

The screen decides first, then the rDNA count, then the telomeres, and depth and genes sort out the rest. Two verdict rules allow a gene call where none is expected. In verdict rule 3, a pure rDNA array holds no protein-coding gene, but the gene predictor now and then calls a gene inside an rDNA unit. A contig with more rDNA units than genes is still mostly rDNA. In verdict rule 7, a gene call or two is allowed because gene predictors call open reading frames inside transposons.

"No BUSCO marker" (verdict rule 7) and "no gene and no BUSCO marker" (verdict rule 9) apply only when at least one of the two counts is known, and then every known count they name must be 0. In a run both are always counted, because BUSCO and funannotate run in every mode. Only a contig without a scaffold in contigs_sort.fasta lacks its gene count.

The reason column spells out the evidence each verdict rule used, with the numbers, so a verdict can be checked against the columns.

docs.title: The median depth
docs.text: The median depth is what depth_x_median and the verdict rules compare each contig with. It is weighted by length, so a 4-Mb chromosome counts a hundred times as much as a 40-kb piece. It is taken over the contigs of at least 100 kb, or over all contigs when none is that long, and it leaves out the mitochondrion and the contigs the screen removed. Short debris, the deep mitochondrion and a contaminant genome at its own depth therefore cannot pull the median away from the depth of the bulk of the genome.

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text:
Three steps make the table, in every mode. The telomere unit is chosen as soon as the draft exists, and the table itself waits for the annotation:

Step Runs Does Writes telomere_db once per output folder downloads the tidk telomere repeat database and checks its SHA-256 (Reference databases) 00.resources/telomeres/telo_database_v2.tsv, PROVENANCE.txt telomere_units once per sample, as soon as the draft exists runs tidk on the draft and chooses the telomere repeat unit of the assembly (Telomeres); its own conda environment (tidk 0.3.0 with Python 3.12); seconds to a minute eval/telomere_candidates.tsv, telomere_unit.txt, telomere_ends.tsv contig_summary once per sample, after the annotation; one of the last jobs of a sample gathers the evidence into the table eval/contig_summary.tsv, contig_summary_mqc.tsv

The MultiQC report reads the _mqc copy of the table, and no other step reads it.

docs.title: Where the evidence comes from
docs.text:
Telomeres, rDNA units, BUSCO markers and genes are known in every mode. The read depth is known only in the read-based modes, the assembler's depth and circularity only in the long-read modes, and the calls of the screen only where the screen runs. Each piece of evidence is read from these files:

Evidence What it says Taken from Modes telomere arrays at the contig ends at both ends: a whole chromosome; at one end: a chromosome arm eval/telomere_unit.txt and eval/telomere_ends.tsv: tidk on the draft sequence itself (Telomeres) all read depth the nuclear contigs share one depth; the mitochondrion is several times deeper; an alternative copy of a region, or noise, is much shallower contaminants/bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt, column bam0: the sample's reads on the draft (Coverage track) illumina, longread, hybrid assembler depth and circularity a circular contig at a high depth is the usual shape of a mitochondrion assembly_evidence.tsv, columns coverage and circular longread, hybrid rDNA units a contig made of rDNA units is a piece of the rDNA array, not a chromosome 03.taxonomy/{sample}/its_windows.tsv, one row per 5.8S gene found (ITS taxonomy) all BUSCO markers genuine nuclear sequence, as against rDNA and debris eval/busco/run_<lineage>/full_table.tsv of the specific lineage, the markers with status Complete or Duplicated (BUSCO) all predicted genes the same the mRNA features of 04.annotation/{sample}/funannotate/annotate_results/<Genus_species>_{sample}.gff3, joined to the draft contig through 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_sort.fasta (the join) all the screen removed as a contaminant, with its genus; confirmed mitochondrial contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta screen

Paths without a stage prefix are under 02.assembly/{sample}/. In hybrid mode the screen files are those of the long-read draft, not of the Illumina guide.

In contigs mode the screen maps the contigs to themselves, so the depth in the BlobTools table reflects contig length and nothing else (Coverage track). The contig summary therefore does not read it there, and the depth columns are NA in contigs mode, with or without the screen.

docs.title: Telomeres
docs.text:
The telomere repeat unit differs between fungal groups (the table below), so FunFlux does not assume one. It chooses the unit from the assembly itself and says whether the unit it found is a known telomere repeat. Rule telomere_units runs tidk (Brown et al. 2025) on the draft assembly, and tidk does the heavy work. FunFlux uses two of its commands:

tidk command What it does Used for tidk explore lists every tandem repeat unit of a sequence set with its copy number collecting the candidate units (step 2 below) tidk ends takes one unit and reports, for both ends of every contig, whether an array of that unit sits there, how long it is, how far from the contig end, and which way it points scoring each candidate (step 4) and the telomere columns of the table

tidk measures the arrays, and FunFlux chooses the unit

Neither command chooses the telomere unit of a genome. Most units tidk explore lists are microsatellites, and tidk ends needs the unit as input. The choice is FunFlux's, made from how each candidate unit behaves at the contig ends, and checked against the telomere repeat database that comes with tidk and against the literature.

tidk writes every unit in a canonical form, the alphabetically smallest of all rotations of the unit and of its reverse complement, so TTAGGG, GGGTTA and CCCTAA are all AACCCT. The telomere_unit column, the three telomere files and the log use that form, and the table of database units under Which fungi carry which repeat gives the published spelling next to it.

docs.title: How the unit is chosen
docs.text:
1. The contig ends. FunFlux writes a FASTA of terminal windows. Of every contig longer than two windows (parameters.contig_summary.telomere_window, 25,000 bp by default), it takes the first and the last window, as <contig>__start and <contig>__end. A contig of at most two windows goes in whole. The window is wide because the array is not always the last thing in a contig. When the assembler ran past the telomere, the array sits some kilobases inside the contig end, and a window that stops short of it misses the telomere altogether.

  2. The units found there. tidk explore lists every unit of 5 to 30 bp that forms a tandem run of at least min_telomere_copies copies in the windows, with its copy number (copies_at_ends). It runs once more on the whole draft (copies_genome_wide). A telomere unit has nearly all its copies at the ends, while a satellite has most of them inside the contigs. Both numbers go into the candidates table, but neither enters the score, because a microsatellite can have nearly as many copies at the contig ends as the telomere unit. The copy number also does not say which way its arrays point.

  3. The candidates. They are the units found at the ends, every unit the database lists with strong or weak support, every unit of the literature table and, when parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif names one, that unit. All are written in canonical form and merged. Three filters drop what cannot be a telomere repeat, and the configured unit is exempt from them:

    Filter Drops, for example Why 5 to 30 bp long ACAT, AAAT no telomere repeat shorter than 5 bp is known, and 4-bp units are low-complexity sequence that forms arrays everywhere: AAAT alone gives 192 "telomere" ends on the Illumina (SPAdes) assembly of Botrytis cinerea B05.10 not a repeat of a shorter unit ACACAC (AC three times), TTAGGGTTAGGG the same array would be counted twice under two names the two strands differ: the unit holds more G than C, or more C than G AAAT, AGAGCC every telomerase-made repeat has a G-rich strand, and the orientation test of step 4 needs the two strands to be told apart

  4. The score. For every candidate, tidk ends runs on the whole draft. It searches the window at each contig end and accepts an array no further from the end than the window (-w and --max-offset, both telomere_window). An array must be at least min_telomere_copies copies long (--min-length, that is 30 bp for a 6-bp unit), and tidk's default mode tolerates sequencing errors inside the array. Each contig end gets a status:

    Status Meaning present an array pointing the way a telomere points: the C-rich strand at a contig start, the G-rich strand at a contig end wrong_strand an array pointing the other way not_terminal an array further from the end than the window absent no array other_end FunFlux's addition: on a contig shorter than two windows, one array is seen from both ends, once as present at its own end and once as wrong_strand from the other end; when the two rows describe the same stretch of the contig (their coordinates overlap), the row with the larger offset is relabelled and does not count

    Per unit, telomere_ends is the number of present rows, opposite_ends the number of wrong_strand rows, score their difference, and t2t_contigs the contigs with present at both ends. The reasoning is that a telomere repeat points one way at every chromosome end, with its G-rich strand towards the end. A satellite that happens to sit at contig ends points either way with equal chance, so however often it occurs, its score stays near zero.

  5. The choice. A unit is eligible with at least 2 telomere ends and more than twice as many telomere ends as opposite ends. The eligible units are ranked by score, then known units (literature or database) before unknown ones, then the shorter unit, then alphabetically. The first is the telomere unit of the assembly. When none is eligible, the unit is none, every telomere column reads 0, and a chromosome comes out as nuclear_contig. The log then names the best candidate and its counts.

docs.title: Which fungi carry which repeat
docs.text:
TTAGGG, the vertebrate telomere repeat, is the unit of most filamentous Ascomycota (the Pezizomycotina), of most Basidiomycota and of the Mucoromycota. The departures are single species or small groups, and the budding yeasts, the fission yeasts and the Microstromatales have no single unit. The full references are on Citation and references. The table lists the known departures and the groups that no single unit describes:

Fungi Telomere repeat Source most Pezizomycotina (filamentous Ascomycota), most Basidiomycota, Mucoromycota; among them Botrytis cinerea and Aspergillus fumigatus TTAGGG Lue 2021; Sun et al. 2023; Levis et al. 1997; Bowyer et al. 2022 the Aspergillus flavus group TTAGGGTCAACA Sun et al. 2023 Peltaster fructicola TAGGG Sun et al. 2023 Drechmeria coniospora CCGTTGCTGTTG Sun et al. 2023 Penicillium polonicum TTTAGGG Sun et al. 2023 a few Basidiomycota: Malassezia, Hericium TTAGGA (Malassezia furfur), TTAGTG (Malassezia restricta, M. globosa), TTGGA (Hericium erinaceus) Sun et al. 2023 Cryptococcus neoformans TTA(G)4-6: TTA followed by four to six G, a unit of varying length Edman 1992 budding yeasts (Saccharomycotina): Candida albicans (23 bp), Kluyveromyces lactis (25 bp) and most others long and often irregular units of 8 to 25 bp; no single unit McEachern and Blackburn 1994; Červenák et al. 2021; Lue 2021 Yarrowia lipolytica TTAGTCAGGG, a regular unit among the budding yeasts Lue 2021; Červenák et al. 2021 fission yeasts (Schizosaccharomyces) degenerate GGTTAC-type repeats; no single unit Sepsiova et al. 2016 Microstromatales yeasts no telomerase; a different tandem array at every chromosome end Brejová et al. 2026

Every exact unit of this table is a candidate in every run. When the data choose one of them, the candidates table marks it in_literature. The telomere repeat database of tidk (Reference databases) adds the units reported with strong or weak support in its 2,990 rows of all kingdoms, 256 distinct units. A unit the data choose is marked in_database, with the number of species per kingdom that carry it. The 126 fungal rows of the database name these units with strong or weak support:

Unit, canonical form Fungal species in the database AACCCT (TTAGGG) 20 AAACCCT (TTTAGGG) 18 AACCT (TTAGG) 9 AACCTAACT 3 AAAAAACCCT 2 AAAACCCT, AACCCCT, AACACT, AACCC, AACCCTAT, AAAT 1 each

TTAGGG and TTTAGGG account for most fungal species in the database. AAAT is 4 bp long and has no G-rich strand, so it fails two of the three filters and is never scored. For a species in none of these lists, TeloBase (Lyčka et al. 2024) and the Telomerase Database (Podlevsky et al. 2008) list the known telomere repeats.

docs.title: Setting the unit
docs.text:
parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif sets the telomere unit by hand. A configured unit is always used, and the data's own choice is still reported next to it.

parameters:
  contig_summary:
    telomere_motif: auto             # or a unit, such as TTAGGGTCAACA for the Aspergillus flavus group
telomere_motif Unit used The three filters Marked chosen in the candidates table auto (default) the unit chosen from the data, as described above applied the data's choice a unit: letters A, C, G and T only, 4 to 30 long, upper or lower case the unit as given, whatever its score: it is written to telomere_unit.txt and used for the telomere columns skipped the given unit

Either strand and any rotation work, because tidk ends gives the same result for TTAGGG, CCCTAA and GGGTTA. The ranking still runs, and a NOTE says when the data favour another unit or give the configured one no support (the NOTE). Set a unit when the data cannot decide, for example in a fragmented assembly with few chromosome ends. A changed value of this key re-runs telomere_units, contig_summary and MultiQC.

Setting one telomere_motif key does not set the other

hifiasm has a key of the same name, which is separate:

Key Read by The unit is written parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif the contig summary on either strand, in any rotation parameters.longread.hifiasm.telomere_motif or parameters.hybrid.hifiasm.telomere_motif (--telo-m) the assembler, hifiasm as it reads at the 5' end of a chromosome: CCCTAA for TTAGGG

docs.title: The three telomere files
docs.text:
Rule telomere_units writes three files to 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/. They hold the numbers behind the choice of the unit, and the arrays of that unit at every contig end.

telomere_candidates.tsv has one row per unit that was found at the contig ends or formed at least one array when it was scored. A known unit that formed none is counted in the log only. The rows are sorted by score, then telomere_ends, both descending, then unit:

Column Content unit the unit in canonical form unit_length bp copies_at_ends copies tidk explore counted in the terminal windows; 0 for a known unit that was not found there copies_genome_wide copies tidk explore counted on the whole draft telomere_ends contig ends with an array pointing the way a telomere points (present) opposite_ends contig ends with an array pointing the other way (wrong_strand) score telomere_ends minus opposite_ends t2t_contigs contigs with a present array at both ends in_literature the fungal groups or species of the literature table that carry the unit, with the published spelling and the references; - when none in_database species per kingdom with strong or weak support in the tidk database, for example Fungi 20; Metazoa 420; Viridiplantae 11; (no kingdom) 2 (the few rows without a kingdom are counted as (no kingdom)); - when none chosen yes for the telomere unit of the assembly, no otherwise

telomere_unit.txt holds one line, the unit in canonical form or none.

telomere_ends.tsv is the per-end table of the chosen unit after the same-array rule, the relabelling to other_end in step 4. It has tidk's ten columns and values, and holds the header line alone when the unit is none:

Column Content id the contig sequence_length its length in bp side start or end status present, wrong_strand, not_terminal, absent or other_end (step 4) telomere_start, telomere_end the array's coordinates on the contig, 0-based; NA when absent telomere_length the array's length in bp offset distance from the contig end to the array, bp strand C-rich or G-rich; a telomere is C-rich at a contig start and G-rich at a contig end window_limited tidk's flag: true when the array reaches the edge of the window tidk searched, so it may continue beyond it

The contig summary reads the rows of this table by their status, and only present rows are telomeres:

status In the contig summary present a telomere: the copies in telomere_start and telomere_end are telomere_length divided by the unit length, rounded, and the two offset columns are tidk's offset. An array more than 1,000 bp inside the contig is also named in the reason column, for example (the start array is 2814 bp from the end); the verdict does not change wrong_strand not a telomere; the reason names it (array in the opposite orientation at the end) other_end, not_terminal nothing

An array more than 1,000 bp inside is named because a telomere is the very end of a chromosome, so sequence beyond the array is a misjoin or an interstitial telomeric repeat.

An array further inside than the window is not seen at all

A wider telomere_window finds it, and the worked example shows an array that a narrow window would miss.

docs.title: The log line and the NOTE
docs.text:
The log logs/telomere_units_{sample}.log holds one line that sums up the choice, followed by the NOTE when there is one, and the rule copies that line to the Snakemake console:

[FunFlux] telomere_units <sample>: telomere repeat unit AACCCT (TTAGGG read on the other strand): 34 contig ends, 15 contigs with a telomere at both ends; known from the literature (filamentous Ascomycota, most Basidiomycota, Mucoromycota; Botrytis cinerea) and from 20 fungal species in the database
Text Appears when the part in parentheses after the unit the published spelling differs from the canonical form; for a configured unit it says set by telomere_motif the same line, reading ... no telomere repeat identified (best candidate <UNIT>: <n> ends in the telomere orientation, <m> opposite) no candidate is eligible a second line, [FunFlux] NOTE telomere_units <sample>: ..., also copied to the console the chosen unit is unknown to both the literature table and the database, so it may be a telomere repeat nobody has reported or a satellite that happens to point one way; or a configured parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif is not the data's first choice, because another unit scores higher or the configured one has no support

A NOTE is a reason to open the candidates table, which shows the numbers behind either case.

docs.title: Genes: the join to the scaffold names
docs.text:
genes is the one column that cannot be joined to the draft by name, because funannotate sort renames the contigs scaffold_1, scaffold_2, ... longest first (funannotate sort). The script therefore joins the GFF3 to the draft by sequence:

Draft contig Matched to its scaffold by unchanged since the draft the identical sequence: a draft contig and a scaffold with the identical sequence are the same contig polished after the draft (Medaka for ONT samples, Polypolish in hybrid mode), so it differs from its scaffold by a base here and there five 300-bp probes taken from inside the contig, searched in the scaffolds whose length is within 5 % of its own

The annotated_as column gives the result of this join. It links the two sets of contig names, which none of the other result files does.

docs.title: A worked example: Botrytis cinerea B05.10
docs.text:
The public benchmark genome, Botrytis cinerea B05.10 (RefSeq assembly GCF_000143535.2), shows how the table reads on a real assembly. It has 18 chromosomes: 16 core chromosomes of 2.0 to 4.1 Mb and two minichromosomes of 247 and 209 kb. Its mitochondrial genome is 82 kb, and the reference assembly carries telomere repeats at 27 of its 36 chromosome ends.

A longread run of public ONT reads of the strain (about 136x), assembled with hifiasm, gave 33 contigs: 32 in the nuclear genome and the mitochondrion. Validation on public genomes describes the runs. The telomere unit chosen from the data is AACCCT, that is TTAGGG, with arrays of 102 to 126 bp (17 to 21 copies) at 34 of the 66 contig ends. Every one of these arrays points the way a telomere points, with the C-rich strand at every contig start and the G-rich strand at every contig end, so there is no opposite end. Of the 33 contigs, 15 have an array at both ends. With the default settings and a median depth of 24.5, the table calls the 33 contigs:

Verdict Contigs What they are chromosome 15 13 of the 16 core chromosomes, and the two minichromosomes chromosome_arm 3 the other 3 core chromosomes, each with one end without a telomere array rDNA_array 13 pieces of the rDNA array mitochondrion 1 the mitochondrial genome low_depth 1 an alternative copy of a region, or noise

The 18 chromosomes of the reference come out as 18 contigs, 15 of them with telomere arrays at both ends. The other 15 contigs are rDNA pieces, the mitochondrion and one low-depth contig. A few rows, with the columns that decided:

contig length depth_x_median telomere_start telomere_end rdna_units busco_markers genes annotated_as verdict ptg000005l 4,109,401 1.00 18 17 0 287 1,127 scaffold_1 chromosome ptg000007l 3,044,302 1.00 18 0 0 193 869 scaffold_4 chromosome_arm ptg000014l 2,512,653 0.99 18 0 6 184 701 scaffold_9 chromosome_arm ptg000022l 208,977 0.79 18 17 0 0 21 scaffold_18 chromosome ptg000004l 282,192 0.77 17 17 0 0 22 scaffold_17 chromosome ptg000030l 175,720 1.15 18 0 20 0 1 scaffold_19 rDNA_array ptg000011l 58,954 0.16 0 0 6 0 0 scaffold_25 rDNA_array ptg000015l 61,330 0.27 0 0 6 0 NA dropped by funannotate clean rDNA_array ptg000028c 82,351 7.37 0 0 0 0 NA not annotated (mitochondrion) mitochondrion ptg000029l 42,998 0.07 0 0 0 1 5 scaffold_27 low_depth

What the rows show:

  • The core chromosomes. The 16 contigs of 2.0 to 4.1 Mb are the 16 core chromosomes. Of these, 13 are chromosome and 3 are chromosome_arm, each with one end without a telomere array. ptg000014l carries 6 rDNA units and 701 genes, so verdict rule 3 does not apply and it stays a chromosome arm. The start array of ptg000007l begins 2,814 bp inside the contig, and its reason says so: telomere repeats at the start only (18 copies) (the start array is 2814 bp from the end). Three chromosomes have one array more than 1,000 bp inside the contig end, named in their reasons the same way: 1,134 bp in ptg000002l, 3,660 bp in ptg000009l and 12,300 bp in ptg000017l.
  • The minichromosomes. The two contigs of 200 to 300 kb are the two minichromosomes, chromosome whatever their size. ptg000022l (209 kb) has its arrays right at the contig ends and 21 genes. ptg000004l (282 kb) has arrays of 17 copies that lie 19,746 and 15,234 bp inside the contig ends. The contig therefore carries about 35 kb beyond its telomeres, and the reference chromosome is 247 kb. Its reason names both offsets: telomere repeats at both ends (17 and 17 copies) (the start array is 19746 bp from the end; the end array is 15234 bp from the end); depth 0.77x the median; 22 genes, 0 BUSCO markers. With a window of 3,000 bp, neither array would be seen and the contig would read nuclear_contig, which is why the default window is 25 kb. The depths of the two minichromosomes, 0.79 and 0.77 times the median, are within the normal range.
  • The rDNA pieces. ptg000030l is a 176-kb rDNA array with a telomere at its start (18 copies), 20 rDNA units and one predicted gene, a gene call inside an rDNA unit. With fewer genes than rDNA units, it is an rDNA_array by verdict rule 3, with the telomere named in the reason. The 13 rDNA_array contigs are 36 to 176 kb of rDNA units at 0.16 to 1.15 times the median: the array is assembled in pieces and partly collapsed. Two of them, ptg000015l and ptg000024l, were dropped by funannotate clean as duplicates, so their genes cell is NA and annotated_as says so. The genus cell of the rDNA pieces names another genus than Botrytis, because a BLAST genus label is only as good as the closest sequence in the database (Decontamination). The rDNA unit holds lone copies of TTAGGG and CCCTAA, but a telomere call needs an array of at least 5 copies, so none of the other rDNA pieces gets a telomere.
  • The mitochondrion. ptg000028c is confirmed by the mitochondrion screen. It is circular, at 7.4 times the median depth, and not annotated.
  • The low-depth contig. ptg000029l, 43 kb at 0.07 times the median with 5 genes, is low_depth, an alternative copy of a region or noise.

The candidates table shows how the unit was chosen. telomere_candidates.tsv has 20 rows, and these are the three units with the most copies at the contig ends:

Unit Copies at the contig ends Ends in the telomere orientation Opposite ends Score AACCCT 657 34 0 34 ACCTCC 164 0 3 -3 AGATGG 152 0 4 -4

Only the telomere unit has arrays that point the telomere way. The two microsatellites that follow it have three and four arrays at contig ends, all pointing the wrong way for a telomere. AACCCT has 657 copies at the contig ends and 661 in the whole assembly, so nearly every copy sits at an end, while AGATGG has 405 in the whole assembly. Seven units have a single end in the telomere orientation and are not eligible. The table marks AACCCT known from the literature and from 20 fungal species in the database. The log of telomere_units ends with the summary line quoted above and has no NOTE.

A short-read assembly of the same strain chooses the same unit from thinner evidence. It was made with SPAdes from public Illumina reads and has 413 contigs, 4 of them mitochondrial:

Unit Copies at the contig ends Ends in the telomere orientation Opposite ends Score Outcome AACCCT 227 13 1 12 chosen; no contig with an array at both ends AAGAG 33 13 5 8 eligible, ranks second AGAGGG 115 12 6 6 not eligible: 12 is not more than twice 6 AAAGAG 179 5 5 0 arrays point either way AAGGAG 171 6 7 -1 arrays point either way

Here the copy number cannot choose the unit, but the orientation still can. The microsatellites AAAGAG and AAGGAG have nearly as many copies at the contig ends as AACCCT, but their arrays point either way, so they score 0 and -1. tidk ends first reports 7 opposite ends for AACCCT. Six of them are the same array seen from the other end of a short contig of 1.4 to 12 kb, which the same-array rule relabels other_end. The seventh is a 30-bp run 12.4 kb inside a long contig.

The gene count is FunFlux's own prediction. Where a published annotation exists, as here, its gene count is an independent check of the run as a whole. The table itself reads no reference.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The contig summary has five settings in parameters.contig_summary, and the address of the telomere database in links:

parameters:
  contig_summary:
    telomere_motif: auto
    telomere_db_sha256: 1d4f5c8c2cce6a76aaa8de01602317a8e0b8d0401711b96f3c7a826c385da699
    telomere_window: 25000
    min_telomere_copies: 5
    min_rdna_units: 3
links:
  telomere_db_link: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tolkit/a-telomeric-repeat-database/73c635c7b80e5ab369b4c7ec67d23db32dcaa1b8/data/telo_database_v2.tsv
Key Default Allowed values What it does telomere_motif auto auto (any case), or letters A, C, G and T, 4 to 30 long; lower case is upper-cased auto: the unit is chosen from the data. A unit: used as given, the data's choice reported next to it (Setting the unit). telomere_db_sha256 the checksum of the database file at the template address 64 hexadecimal characters The SHA-256 the downloaded database must have. Change it together with links.telomere_db_link. telomere_window 25000 an integer from 500 to 100000 The terminal window: the bases at each contig end in which the candidate units are collected, and how far from the end tidk ends accepts an array. The array can sit some kb inside a contig end when the assembler ran past the telomere, so the window must cover that; the offset columns show where each array lies. min_telomere_copies 5 an integer ≥ 2 Copies of the unit an array needs: tidk ends requires this many unit lengths (30 bp for a 6-bp unit), and tidk explore lists a unit only when it forms a tandem run of this many copies. min_rdna_units 3 an integer ≥ 1 rDNA units (ITS windows) from which a contig can be an rDNA_array.

The five values are checked before any job starts, like the other blocks (Configuration). A value outside the range stops the run with a [FunFlux] parameters.contig_summary.<key>: ... message. Every dry run prints the settings in one line: Contig summary: telomere motif auto (the repeat unit is chosen from the data), a telomere from 5 tandem copies within 25000 bp of a contig end, an rDNA array from 3 rDNA unit(s). A changed value re-runs the steps that use it (Re-runs).

docs.title: In the MultiQC report
docs.text:
For the report, 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary_mqc.tsv holds the same table prepared for MultiQC, with the rows named {sample}: {contig} and a description that names the telomere unit of the sample. MultiQC shows the tables of all samples of the run as one table in the section Contig summary of 06.report/multiqc_report.html. It writes the numbers to 06.report/multiqc_data/multiqc_contig_summary.txt. The table has all 20 columns, telomere_unit among them, so samples of different species keep their units apart. The column settings of the table show or hide columns.

Above 500 rows, MultiQC shows a violin plot instead of the table

MultiQC shows a table with more than 500 rows (its max_table_rows setting) as a violin plot instead, so for a batch of fragmented assemblies read contig_summary.tsv itself.

docs.title: Re-runs
docs.text:
Each change in the left column re-runs the contig summary steps on the right:

Change Re-runs a new draft telomere_units and contig_summary a new database file telomere_units parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif, telomere_window or min_telomere_copies telomere_units and contig_summary links.telomere_db_link or telomere_db_sha256 telomere_db, then telomere_units of every sample and the steps after it a new telomere unit or ends table contig_summary min_rdna_units contig_summary a new screen result, a new busco.lineage (the BUSCO markers are counted per contig), new ITS windows or a new annotation contig_summary

A re-run of these steps costs seconds to a minute and never touches the annotation. MultiQC follows each of them.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Some genomes, assemblies and settings leave a piece of evidence missing or unreliable. The table lists these situations and what the contig summary does in each:

Situation What the table does telomeres that vary from copy to copy: Saccharomyces, Schizosaccharomyces, Cryptococcus only exact units are found, and no tandem run of one unit exists: tidk explore lists no unit, tidk ends finds no array, and the unit comes out as none even when the irregular repeat is written into parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif telomere repeats that differ between chromosome ends: the Microstromatales yeasts no single unit covers more than a few of them a unit that no paper and no database names it is still found when it forms an array of at least min_telomere_copies copies within the window at the contig ends, because every tandem unit of the contig ends is a candidate; the NOTE then says that the unit is unknown a genuine telomere unit that fails one of the three filters it would be missed; none is known, and parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif bypasses the filters an assembly with few chromosome ends, such as a fragmented short-read assembly few votes: a unit needs at least 2 telomere ends and more than twice as many telomere ends as opposite ends; when it falls short no unit is chosen, so set parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif when the repeat is known an array further inside a contig than telomere_window it is not seen; the worked example shows the trade-off of a wider window an array of the chosen unit pointing the other way at a contig end (wrong_strand) not a telomere call; the reason names it, and the verdict rests on the rest a contig that ends at a centromere centromeres are not detected: it is a chromosome_arm like any other contigs mode, where depth is unknown (it is known only in the read-based modes) verdict rules 6 and 7 never apply; a mitochondrion that the screen did not confirm, or a contig at twice the depth of the genome, is judged on the other evidence alone: a gene-less contig at twice the depth is then a nuclear_fragment, not a repeat parameters.mitochondria.mode: off, read-based modes the screen confirms nothing, and the mitochondrion is judged on the rest of its evidence: its depth, several times the median, keeps it out of every verdict but repeat (when no gene was predicted on it) or unclassified parameters.mitochondria.mode: off, contigs mode without a depth, the mitochondrion is a nuclear_contig when genes were predicted on it parameters.mitochondria.mode: report the confirmed contig stays in the nuclear genome and is annotated; the table still calls it mitochondrion (verdict rule 1, from the screen's class), and its annotated_as cell names the scaffold_N under which funannotate annotated it, with its genes cell filled (Mitochondria) a fungus whose 5.8S matches none of ITSx's profiles rdna_units counts the 5.8S genes that nhmmer found with ITSx's profiles (Why the genome is cut into windows), so it is 0 on every contig, and the rDNA pieces are judged on depth and genes alone: low_depth, repeat, nuclear_fragment, nuclear_contig or unclassified the gene count it is the run's own gene prediction, counted per scaffold: evidence that a contig is nuclear sequence, not a measure of annotation quality a polished contig (Medaka in longread and hybrid mode, Polypolish in hybrid mode) its join to its scaffold_N rests on five 300-bp probes and a length within 5 %; dropped by funannotate clean on a contig that is in contigs_sort.fasta means the join failed, and the genes cell of that contig is then NA

Where evidence is missing or unreliable, the verdict rests on the evidence that remains

For the fungi of the first two rows, the table still gives the depth, rDNA, BUSCO and gene evidence, and the verdicts chromosome and chromosome_arm do not occur. The annotated_as column shows whether each contig found its scaffold.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Every file is kept, and contig_summary.tsv is the one to read:

Path Content 00.resources/telomeres/telo_database_v2.tsv the telomere repeat database of tidk, downloaded once per output folder 00.resources/telomeres/PROVENANCE.txt source URL, download date, checksum and row count of the database 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/telomere_candidates.tsv every candidate telomere unit with its counts (The three telomere files) 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/telomere_unit.txt the telomere unit of the assembly, or none 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/telomere_ends.tsv the arrays of that unit at every contig end 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv the table, one row per contig of the draft 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary_mqc.tsv the same table for MultiQC logs/telomere_db.log the database download logs/telomere_units_{sample}.log the count line of the script, the one-line summary and the NOTE when there is one; tidk's own messages only when tidk fails logs/contig_summary_{sample}.log the one-line summary

Each step writes its files only when every input was read without error. The job stops on a missing file, a malformed database, a tidk failure, a table without an expected column, a depth that is not a number or a FASTA with two records of the same name. It reports the cause as one line in the log, [FunFlux] telomere_units: error: ... or contig_summary.py: error: ..., which for a tidk failure includes tidk's own message.

The full output tree is on Output files.

docs.title: Decontamination
docs.text:
The contamination and mitochondrion screen, called the screen on this page, examines the draft assembly. This page covers its contamination part, which gives every contig of the draft a genus and keeps or removes contigs by genus. The screen runs before QC and annotation. A contaminant contig left in the assembly changes the QUAST, BUSCO and ITS results, and the fungal gene predictor calls false genes on it.

The genus comes from a megablast search against NCBI core_nt. BlobTools turns the hits into one genus per contig, and the contig selector applies parameters.decontamination, which decides what is kept. The default, mode: off, removes nothing and still records a genus and a decision for every contig, so you can read them before you choose a filter. The mitochondrion screen reads the same BLAST results.

Terms used on this page

the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector draft assembly (the draft) the assembly the screen examines, before any contig is removed: contigs_filt.fasta in illumina mode and in contigs mode with the screen, assembly.fasta in longread and hybrid read-based modes the modes illumina, longread and hybrid, which start from reads, as against contigs coverage track the reads aligned back to the draft, contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, from which BlobTools takes each contig's coverage; in contigs mode, the contigs aligned to themselves contig selector rule select_contigs: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says; the default, off, keeps every contig genus filter the setting parameters.decontamination.mode: include or exclude, under which the contig selector keeps or removes contigs by the genus BlobTools gave them confirmed mitochondrial contig a contig the mitochondrion screen classes confirmed_mitochondrial; with the default separate_confirmed, it is kept whatever its genus and moved to contigs_mitochondrial.fasta --forcerun a Snakemake option that runs the named rule again for every sample, with every step after it, even when Snakemake sees no change

docs.title: When the screen runs
docs.text:
The screen always runs in the read-based modes, and in contigs mode only on request. It works the same in every mode, except for the coverage track (below).

Mode Screen Screened draft, in 02.assembly/{sample}/ Kept contigs then go through contigs with parameters.contigs.screen: true contigs_filt.fasta: the input FASTA after the contig filter nothing more illumina always contigs_filt.fasta: the SPAdes contigs after the length and coverage filter nothing more longread always assembly.fasta: the hifiasm or Flye assembly Medaka (ONT samples) hybrid always assembly.fasta: the hifiasm or Flye assembly Medaka (ONT samples), then Polypolish
  • After the screen, the kept contigs, polished where the table says so, become contigs_all.fasta. In every mode that file is then split into the nuclear genome contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, as described in Mitochondria.
  • In hybrid, the Illumina guide assembly gets a screen of its own, with the same parameters.decontamination and parameters.mitochondria settings. Its steps carry guide in their names, from index_guide_contigs to select_guide_contigs, and its files are under 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/. The read pairs that map to its kept contigs, the selected pairs, go to Polypolish and, for ONT samples with short_read_guidance: true (off by default), to Filtlong (Hybrid). A contig removed from the guide therefore also loses its Illumina reads for those steps.
  • With the screen on, directories.blast_db must be set, and an empty value stops the run before any job starts. In contigs mode without the screen, the dry run prints a NOTE that the FASTA gets no contamination or mitochondrion screen (Pre-assembled contigs).

docs.title: Steps and files
docs.text:
Two steps gather the evidence, map_contigs and blast_contigs. Two BlobTools steps join it into one row per contig, and the contig selector, select_contigs, decides.

draft contigs
 ├── map_contigs ─────┐                                  coverage track (BAM)
 │                    ├── blob_json ── blob_table ──┐    one taxonomy row per contig
 ├── blast_contigs ───┘                             │
 │        └── screen_mitochondria ── confirmed IDs ─┤    see Mitochondria
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┴── select_contigs ── contigs_decontam.fasta
                                                                          + audit files
Step Tool Does Writes, in 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/ map_contigs contigs: minimap2 2.30, samtools 1.21; illumina: bowtie2 2.5.4 (index built by index_contigs), samtools 1.21; longread, hybrid: minimap2 2.30 with the sample's preset, samtools 1.21 aligns the reads to the draft: the coverage track {sample}_map.bam, {sample}_map.bam.bai blast_contigs BLAST+ 2.16.0 searches every contig in core_nt blastout blob_json BlobTools 1.1.1 joins the BLAST hits and the coverage blob.blobDB.json, blob.{sample}_map.bam.cov blob_table BlobTools 1.1.1 gives each contig one taxon per rank bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt select_contigs select_contigs_by_taxonomy.py (Python standard library), with the pinned Python 3.12 of the python conda environment keeps or removes each contig by its genus contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, {sample}_composition.txt, contigs.list, contigs_decontam.fasta

The step names are those Snakemake prints on the console, and each step writes logs/<step>_{sample}.log. BLAST uses at most 24 threads and the mapping resources.threads, while every other step uses one. Output files lists which files stay after the run.

docs.title: Choosing a policy
docs.text:
Start with off, read the decisions, then filter. off is the default and removes nothing, while exclude with a genus that core_nt gives to your own contigs removes genome. The table suggests a setting for each situation.

Situation Setting first run of any isolate mode: off; read contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv and the composition file (Audit files) a contaminant genus (a bacterium or yeast grown with the culture) has contigs of its own, and core_nt does not give that genus to your fungus mode: exclude with that genus contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv shows which genus labels your isolate's contigs carry, and every other label belongs to a contaminant mode: include with the labels of your isolate's contigs, which need not include its true genus one sample of a batch needs another policy a sample_overrides row for that sample only the contigs without any BLAST hit should go mode: exclude with no genus listed, and discard_no_hit: true

The screen can run alone, so that you see the decisions of a policy before QC and annotation start:

snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml --until select_contigs

docs.title: The keep/drop decision
docs.text:
The contig selector takes the genus of each contig from the BlobTools table (BlobTools) and applies parameters.decontamination:

parameters:
  decontamination:
    mode: off                  # off | include | exclude
    discard_no_hit: false
    include_genera:
    include_genera_by_sample:
    exclude_genera:
    exclude_genera_file:
    sample_overrides:

The dry run prints the policy in use, for example Decontamination mode: off (discard_no_hit=false).

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
parameters.decontamination.mode, written mode on this page, chooses one of three policies.

mode Keeps Removes off (default) every contig nothing include the contigs of the listed genera every other contig exclude every contig whose genus is not listed the contigs of the listed genera

For each contig the tests run in this order, and the first that applies decides.

  1. A confirmed mitochondrial contig is kept (Protected mitochondrial contigs).
  2. With mode: off, the contig is kept.
  3. With discard_no_hit: true, a contig whose genus is no-hit is removed. This applies in include and exclude alike.
  4. Otherwise the genus test of the mode decides.

include must list the genera that BLAST gave the isolate's own contigs, which for a poorly sequenced fungus need not be its true genus (Why there is no auto mode). When the screen runs, a sample left in include mode without any genus stops the run before any job starts:

[FunFlux] parameters.decontamination: mode include keeps only the genera you name, but no genus is given for sample(s) S. Name the genus in include_genera, in include_genera_by_sample (one row per sample) or in the include_genera column of sample_overrides.

discard_no_hit accepts true/false, yes/no, on/off or 1/0. It changes which contigs are kept only in exclude mode.

mode Effect of discard_no_hit: true off none include only the reason code of the no-hit contigs changes (discarded_no_hit); they go anyway because they are not on the list exclude the no-hit contigs are removed

docs.title: Genus lists and aliases
docs.text:
include_genera and exclude_genera take one genus, a YAML list, or one string with the names separated by ; or ,:

    include_genera: [Botrytis, Alternaria]
    exclude_genera: "Pseudomonas;Bacillus"

Genus names are compared without regard to case, and exclude uses no aliases. include also accepts two kinds of alias, which only ever keep more contigs.

  • A table of bacterial genus synonyms, under which Peribacillus and Priestia match Bacillus. It contains no fungal genus.
  • The prefix rule, which strips the prefixes brady, meso, neo, sino, aeri, caldi and geo when at least four letters remain. Neocosmospora and Cosmospora then match each other, and so do Geosmithia and Smithia.

For a fungus, only the prefix rule can apply.

docs.title: Per-sample settings
docs.text:
Three settings name files. The two genus files, include_genera_by_sample and exclude_genera_file, add to the run-wide lists, and a sample_overrides row has the last word. When the screen runs, the dry run checks the files before any job starts, as described below, and select_contigs reads them again when it runs. A relative path is resolved from the launch folder, the folder Snakemake is started from, so write absolute paths.
