self-training gene finder a gene finder that learns its parameters from the genome it annotates, with no stored model; GeneMark-ES works this way licence key the file ~/.gm_key that GeneMark-ES needs; it expires one year after download, and an expired key stops the run at genemark_check, before gene prediction secretome the predicted secreted proteins, which funannotate annotate lists from the SignalP 6 result in annotations.secretome.txt; none without SignalP 6 model weights the trained numbers that make up a model, such as a SignalP 6 model Sec/SPI signal peptides of the Sec pathway, cleaved by signal peptidase I; with --organism eukarya, SignalP 6 predicts only these pin file the file <name>.linux-64.pin.txt beside each environment file: the exact package builds FunFlux v2 was tested with, installed without solving dependencies --conda-prefix the Snakemake option naming the folder the conda environments are built in, instead of .snakemake/conda/ in the launch folder; several clones or users can share it lookup service the EBI online service that returns InterProScan matches already computed for known proteins; it receives checksums, not sequences, and saves run time

docs.title: GeneMark-ES
docs.text: GeneMark-ES is a self-training gene finder that funannotate predict adds to AUGUSTUS, SNAP and GlimmerHMM. It is optional, and FunFlux uses it only when you name an installation.

docs.title: Licence and installation
docs.text:
GeneMark-ES is free ("royalty free") for academic and non-profit institutions and US government agencies. Other users must contact the GeneMark team for a licence. Download the program and the licence key from https://genemark.bme.gatech.edu/license_download.cgi. In October 2026, the download for 64-bit Linux was GeneMark-ES/ET/EP+ 4.73.

The licence is valid for one year from the date of download, and the date of the key file does not tell when it expires. A key file dated January 2026 worked in July and had expired in October.

Unpack the program, for example into /path/to/gmes_linux_64_4, and follow its INSTALL file:

gunzip gm_key.gz
cp gm_key ~/.gm_key
cd /path/to/gmes_linux_64_4
perl change_path_in_perl_scripts.pl "/usr/bin/env perl"

The last command makes GeneMark's Perl scripts start the first perl on the PATH instead of /usr/bin/perl. This matters because funannotate predict starts gmes_petap.pl as a program, so the first line of the script chooses the Perl. Once the command has run, FunFlux runs GeneMark-ES with the Perl 5.32.1 of its funannotate environment. That environment contains the Perl modules the INSTALL file lists, so nothing has to be installed from CPAN. Without the command, GeneMark-ES runs with the computer's /usr/bin/perl, which often lacks those modules.

The key must be ~/.gm_key in the home folder of the account that runs Snakemake and its jobs. On a cluster, it must be in the home folder that the compute nodes see, as described in The GeneMark-ES key. Do not commit or share the key file.

directories:
  genemark_dir: /path/to/gmes_linux_64_4   # absolute path, holds gmes_petap.pl
parameters:
  genemark:
    mode: auto     # auto: use GeneMark-ES when genemark_dir is set; off: never

With GeneMark-ES enabled, the run stops before any job starts when genemark_dir is not an absolute path, when gmes_petap.pl is missing from it or not executable, or when ~/.gm_key does not exist. Whether the key has expired is checked later, before gene prediction starts, as the next section describes.

docs.title: The licence check before gene prediction
docs.text:
GeneMark-ES itself checks only that the key file exists. An expired key is found inside GeneMark's programs, partway through funannotate predict, which then fails with Your license period has ended. Rule genemark_check makes this failure show within a minute instead. It runs once per sample, after repeat masking. It starts GeneMark-ES the way funannotate does, with the options funannotate uses, on the first 200,000 bytes of the masked genome (04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_mask.fasta). funannotate predict waits for its result.

What FunFlux does next depends on what GeneMark-ES prints on this slice:

GeneMark-ES output on the slice FunFlux mentions "license" stops: [FunFlux] GeneMark-ES refused to run because of its licence (key file <home>/.gm_key). The key has probably expired: request a new one from the GeneMark site, or set parameters.genemark.mode: off. See <log>. contains "can't locate" or "bad interpreter" stops: [FunFlux] GeneMark-ES could not start from <genemark_dir>: the Perl named in the first line of gmes_petap.pl (GeneMark ships it as /usr/bin/perl, the computer's own) is missing or lacks a Perl module GeneMark needs. ...; the message names change_path_in_perl_scripts.pl as the fix contains "command not found" or "no such file" stops: [FunFlux] GeneMark-ES could not start from <genemark_dir> (a program or a file is missing). See <log>. another error continues, because the slice may be too short to train on; genemark_check.txt records the exit status no error continues; genemark_check.txt reads GeneMark-ES ran on the test slice.

The check therefore stops the run only for an expired key or for a GeneMark-ES that cannot start. genemark_check.txt is written to 04.annotation/{sample}/, and the GeneMark-ES output to logs/genemark_check_{sample}.log. After a stop, put the new key in ~/.gm_key and start the same command again. The check then runs again, because a failed check leaves no result.

docs.title: Without GeneMark-ES
docs.text: With genemark_dir empty or mode: off, there is no genemark_check job, and funannotate predict runs without GeneMark-ES. Rule funannotate_prediction clears GENEMARK_PATH and limits PATH to the funannotate environment plus /usr/bin and /bin, so a GeneMark-ES installed elsewhere is not picked up. FunFlux v2 was tested with GeneMark-ES on, and with mode: off on one public genome, as reported in Validation on public genomes.

docs.title: SignalP 6
docs.text: SignalP 6 finds signal peptides in the predicted proteins, and funannotate annotate turns its result into the secretome annotation, 04.annotation/{sample}/funannotate/annotate_misc/annotations.secretome.txt. SignalP 6 is optional and off by default.

docs.title: Licence and download
docs.text:
The SignalP 6 page of DTU, https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/services/SignalP-6.0/, states: "There is a download page for academic users; other users are requested to contact DTU Health Technology Software Package Manager". DTU offers version 6.0i as two packages, fast and slow_sequential. FunFlux never downloads SignalP and contains no DTU address. It installs the archive you name.

parameters.signalp6.mode chooses the model that SignalP 6 runs, and so the model that the archive must hold:

parameters.signalp6.mode Model the archive must hold Notes; speed and memory from the SignalP README off (default) none fast distilled_model_signalp6.pt a smaller model that approximates the full one; the DTU package fast holds only this model; the mode FunFlux v2 was tested with slow ensemble_model_signalp6.pt the full model, run in parallel; needs more than 14 GB of RAM slow-sequential sequential_models_signalp6 the full model, run sequentially: the memory of fast, 6 times slower

FunFlux looks for the model in models/ and in signalp/model_weights/ of the archive.

files:
  signalp6_archive: /path/to/signalp-6.0i.fast.tar.gz   # absolute path
parameters:
  signalp6:
    mode: fast
    archive_sha256:          # optional: the 64-character checksum, the first field sha256sum <archive> prints
    torch_num_threads: 8     # threads of each signalp6_annotation job, at most resources.threads
    batch_size: 10           # proteins per batch (--bsize)

With a mode other than off, the run stops before any job starts when signalp6_archive is empty, not an absolute path, or not a readable file.

docs.title: How FunFlux installs it
docs.text:
FunFlux installs SignalP 6 from your archive once per output folder, and then runs it once per sample. The two steps appear in the log under these names:

  1. install_signalp6 runs once per output folder, before the first SignalP job. It checks the archive against archive_sha256 when that is set, and refuses an archive with absolute paths, .. or links in it. It then checks that the model of the chosen mode is there. It installs SignalP 6 into the signalp6 conda environment (Python 3.10, PyTorch 1.13.1 for CPU), with nothing fetched from PyPI. It keeps the unpacked package, model weights included, in 00.resources/signalp6/package/ (1.6 GB with the fast model), and records what it installed in 00.resources/signalp6/installation.json.
  2. signalp6_annotation runs once per sample. It runs SignalP 6 on the predicted proteins with --organism eukarya, the chosen --mode, torch_num_threads and batch_size (--bsize), and writes the result to 04.annotation/{sample}/signalp6/prediction_results.txt. --organism eukarya limits the prediction to the Sec/SPI signal peptides of eukaryotes.

The installation log is logs/install_signalp6.log, and its errors start with SignalP 6 installation failed:. The package inside the 6.0i fast archive reports version 6.0h, and that is what installation.json records.

docs.title: When the conda environment is rebuilt
docs.text:
SignalP 6 is installed inside the signalp6 conda environment, and a new environment does not have it. Snakemake builds a new one when a FunFlux update changes signalp6.yaml or its pin file, when --conda-prefix points elsewhere, or when .snakemake/conda is deleted. The next SignalP job then stops with a message that names 00.resources/signalp6/installation.json. Delete that file and start the same command again, with the environment folder writable, and SignalP 6 is installed again. See Troubleshooting.

The SignalP 6 archive and its model weights must not be passed on

Both are licensed. Do not commit, upload or pass on the archive or the model weights. 00.resources/signalp6/package/ holds the weights, so remove it before you share an output folder. pip also keeps a built copy of the SignalP package in the pip cache (~/.cache/pip) of the account that ran the installation. pip cache remove signalp6 deletes that copy. With the fast archive, whose weights sit in models/, that copy holds no weights. With an archive whose weights sit in signalp/model_weights/, pip puts the weights into the pip cache and into the signalp6 conda environment as well, and so into a shared --conda-prefix.

docs.title: Without SignalP 6
docs.text: With mode: off, no SignalP job runs and funannotate annotate gets no SignalP result. The log of funannotate annotate then reads Skipping secretome: neither SignalP nor Phobius searches were run. Rule funannotate_annotation limits PATH to the funannotate environment plus /usr/bin and /bin, so a SignalP installed elsewhere is not picked up.

docs.title: InterProScan
docs.text:
InterProScan assigns protein families, domains and GO terms to every predicted protein, and funannotate annotate builds the domain and GO annotation from its XML. Every run needs it. InterProScan 5 is not on bioconda, so FunFlux runs the interproscan.sh of your installation inside its interproscan environment. That environment supplies Java (OpenJDK 11.0.30) and the Python 3 (3.11.15) that InterProScan runs for seven of its analyses: Gene3D, FunFam, HAMAP, MobiDB-lite, PANTHER, PIRSR and the PROSITE profiles.

FunFlux v2 runs InterProScan 5, not InterProScan 6

FunFlux v2 was tested with InterProScan 5.78-109.0, the final release of InterProScan 5. Later InterPro releases need InterProScan 6, a different program that FunFlux v2 does not use.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The InterProScan documentation gives these steps for 5.78-109.0, a 7.0 GB download that takes 50 GB once installed:

mkdir -p /path/to/software && cd /path/to/software
wget https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/software/unix/iprscan/5/5.78-109.0/interproscan-5.78-109.0-64-bit.tar.gz
wget https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/software/unix/iprscan/5/5.78-109.0/interproscan-5.78-109.0-64-bit.tar.gz.md5
md5sum -c interproscan-5.78-109.0-64-bit.tar.gz.md5
tar -pxvzf interproscan-5.78-109.0-64-bit.tar.gz
cd interproscan-5.78-109.0
python3 setup.py -f interproscan.properties

setup.py indexes the HMM databases, and -f re-indexes all of them. The InterProScan documentation also requires Perl 5 and Python 3.8 or newer on the machine. In a FunFlux run, both come from the interproscan environment (Python 3.11, Perl 5.32 with thread support), together with Java 11.

To test the installation by hand, use the environment FunFlux runs InterProScan in. It is built from the pinned package list in the FunFlux repository and holds the same Java, Python and Perl, so the test runs as it would in FunFlux on any Linux system. On a system without Python 3.8 or newer, run setup.py in this environment too:

conda create -n interproscan_test --file /path/to/FunFlux/workflow/envs/interproscan.linux-64.pin.txt
conda activate interproscan_test

The InterProScan documentation gives two test commands, run in the installation folder:

./interproscan.sh -i test_all_appl.fasta -f tsv -dp   # every analysis computed locally
./interproscan.sh -i test_all_appl.fasta -f tsv       # also contacts EBI's lookup service

Then point files.iprscan at the interproscan.sh of the installation:

files:
  iprscan: /path/to/software/interproscan-5.78-109.0/interproscan.sh

docs.title: What FunFlux runs
docs.text:
Rule iprscan_annotation runs InterProScan once per sample, on the protein FASTA of funannotate predict:

interproscan.sh -i <proteins> -f XML -goterms -pa -cpu <threads>
                -T 04.annotation/{sample}/iprscan/tmp
                -o 04.annotation/{sample}/iprscan/interproscan_out.xml
  • Threads and run time. InterProScan is capped at 10 threads (-cpu), because it gains little from more. Snakemake reserves the 10 threads for the whole job, and with --cores 24 eggNOG-mapper (12 threads) runs beside it. InterProScan takes 1 to 5 hours for a fungal proteome, depending on how many of its proteins EBI's lookup service already knows. The XML can be a few GB.
  • The XML check. FunFlux calls InterProScan directly, not through funannotate iprscan. Before funannotate annotate reads the XML, FunFlux checks that it parses and has the root element protein-matches. If it does not, the rule stops with InterProScan XML validation failed for ....
  • The lookup service. InterProScan asks EBI's lookup service for matches already computed for known proteins. The address of the service is set by precalculated.match.lookup.service.url in interproscan.properties. Without the service, InterProScan computes every match itself, which takes longer. See Functional annotation.
  • Licensed analyses. Phobius, SignalP and TMHMM are switched off in the InterProScan download because they contain licensed components. FunFlux does not switch them on, and SignalP 6 is its own optional step.

docs.title: Missing InterProScan
docs.text:
InterProScan cannot be switched off, because funannotate annotate needs its result. What happens without it depends on files.iprscan:

files.iprscan What happens empty the run stops before any job starts with [FunFlux] files.iprscan: required, but it is missing or empty in the config. a path that does not exist a NOTE before any job starts, [FunFlux] NOTE: files.iprscan '<path>' does not exist on this machine; the InterProScan step will fail without it.; then iprscan_annotation fails when it starts, after gene prediction

A files.iprscan path that does not exist only prints a NOTE, and the run fails after gene prediction

A NOTE does not stop the run, so a missing InterProScan shows only when iprscan_annotation starts. Read the NOTEs of the dry run.

docs.title: Coming from v1
docs.text:
This page explains how to move from FunFlux 1.x, Funnotator, FunFluxL or FunFluxL+ to FunFlux v2.0.0. Version 2.0.0 replaces these four workflows, and the mode key selects what used to be a separate workflow.

Terms used on this page

NOTE a line starting [FunFlux] NOTE that reports something to check without stopping the run; read them after every dry run launch folder the folder Snakemake is started from, normally the FunFlux repository; relative paths are read from it, and .snakemake/ is created there funannotate database the frozen snapshot of funannotate's data, such as Swiss-Prot, Pfam, the BUSCO set and stored AUGUSTUS models, downloaded once from Zenodo into directories.funannotate_db path repair rule normalize_funannotate_db, which rewrites the absolute paths stored in the funannotate database to your folder, in place and without a lock the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true confirmed mitochondrial contig a contig the mitochondrion screen classes confirmed_mitochondrial; with the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, it is kept whatever its genus guide assembly in hybrid mode, the SPAdes assembly of the Illumina reads; it is screened, and only the pairs that map to it go on Was Input Now FunFlux 1.x Illumina paired-end reads mode: illumina Funnotator, shipped inside FunFlux 1.x as workflow/Funnotator assembled genomes (FASTA) mode: contigs FunFluxL 0.1 ONT or PacBio HiFi reads mode: longread FunFluxL+, never published Illumina pairs plus ONT or PacBio HiFi reads mode: hybrid

The FunFlux repository continues as v2.0.0 under the same concept DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.13612159. Cite results produced with a v1 workflow by the version you ran, as described on Citation and references.

The v1 workflows are no longer in the main branch, but their releases stay available. FunFlux v1.1.0, with Funnotator inside it, is the tag v1.1.0 of this repository: git clone --branch v1.1.0 https://github.com/iLivius/FunFlux.git FunFlux-v1.1.0 puts it in a folder of its own. FunFluxL 0.1.0 is the tag v0.1.0 of the FunFluxL repository.

Neither a v1 configuration nor a v1 output folder can be reused as it is. Make these changes, in this order:

  1. Start from the v2 template, add mode and the input: block, and move the long-read settings into parameters.longread or parameters.hybrid (Why a v1 configuration stops).
  2. Name the configuration with --configfile, give --cores the value of resources.threads, and, on a single computer, drop --jobs (Command line).
  3. Give v2 a new, empty output_dir (Output folders).
  4. Point directories.funannotate_db at a new, empty folder, to get the newer snapshot of the funannotate database (Behaviour changes).
  5. Replace decontamination.mode: auto and parameters.genus, if you used them (Behaviour changes).
  6. Update scripts that read renamed files or columns (Output folders, Behaviour changes).

The "What to do" column of Behaviour changes lists the rest.

docs.title: Why a v1 configuration stops
docs.text:
A v1 configuration has no mode key, so FunFlux v2 stops before any job starts:

[FunFlux] mode: this configuration has no 'mode' key. FunFlux v2 needs one of illumina | longread | hybrid | contigs, and an 'input:' block that names the input directory for that mode. A configuration written for FunFlux, FunFluxL or FunFluxL+ v1 does not run unchanged: start from the config template shipped with FunFlux v2 (see 'Coming from v1' in the documentation).

Adding mode: is not enough. The input folder moved out of directories, and FunFluxL and FunFluxL+ kept their long-read settings at the top of parameters, where v2 stops on them:

[FunFlux] mode=illumina requires input.illumina_dir to be set in the config.
[FunFlux] parameters.flye_input_mode: this setting moved into the block named after your mode: parameters.longread.flye_input_mode or parameters.hybrid.flye_input_mode.

Start from the v2 template and copy your paths and settings into it:

cp config/config.yaml config/config_custom.yaml

The table lists the v1 keys that moved or were renamed, and some new keys. The other new keys are named under Behaviour changes.

v1 key v2 key Note none mode required: illumina, longread, hybrid or contigs directories.input_dir input.illumina_dir, input.longread_dir or input.contigs_dir hybrid reads two keys, which may name the same folder; v2 ignores directories.input_dir without a message none in FunFluxL 0.1, which assembled with Flye; parameters.long_read_assembler in FunFluxL+ parameters.<mode>.assembler hifiasm (the default) or flye parameters.flye_input_mode parameters.<mode>.flye_input_mode the value pacbio-hifi is gone: name the reads {sample}_pacbio.<ext> parameters.medaka_model parameters.<mode>.medaka_model none in FunFluxL 0.1, which ran Filtlong with --min_length 1000 --keep_percent 90 --target_bases 500000000; parameters.filtlong.* in FunFluxL+ parameters.<mode>.filtlong.* min_length 1000, keep_percent 90, length_weight 10, target_bases empty (no cap); see Behaviour changes parameters.filtlong.split (FunFluxL+) parameters.hybrid.filtlong_split a split key inside filtlong stops the run parameters.hifiasm.* (FunFluxL+) parameters.<mode>.hifiasm.* parameters.genus parameters.decontamination translated with a NOTE when there is no decontamination block: a genus becomes mode: include, an empty value mode: off (v1: mode: auto, which v2 does not have) none (FunFlux 1.x searched core_nt) parameters.nt_version now read in every mode none (FunFlux 1.x used 10 targets, 1 HSP) parameters.blast_max_target_seqs, parameters.blast_max_hsps defaults 50 and 5

On this page, <mode> is longread or hybrid. The long-read settings live in the block named after the mode, and only that block is read. All other v1 keys keep their names and meanings, apart from the exceptions listed under Behaviour changes, such as decontamination.mode: auto, which is gone. In addition, 'null' in quotes as medaka_model means off, as described on The Medaka model.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The table compares the v1 and v2 command lines. Relative paths and the conda environments now belong to the launch folder, not to output_dir.

v1 v2 Command snakemake --configfile config/config.yaml --sdm conda --cores 12 --jobs 2; Funnotator added --snakefile workflow/Funnotator snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml Configuration config/config.yaml was loaded by default must be named with --configfile; without it FunFlux stops with [FunFlux] No configuration supplied. CPUs most rules took their threads from resources.threads through resources: cpus, which --cores does not limit, so tools could run on more threads than --cores allowed every CPU-bound rule declares threads:, so --cores, equal to resources.threads, limits the whole run; no --jobs Working folder Snakemake moved into output_dir (workdir:): relative paths in the config were read from there, and the conda environments were built in <output_dir>/.snakemake/conda/ Snakemake stays in the launch folder: relative paths are read from there, and .snakemake/ with the conda environments is created there

docs.title: Output folders
docs.text:
FunFlux v2 does not upgrade a v1 output folder in place

Give v2 a new output_dir. Do not resume a v1 run with v2, and do not point v2 at a v1 output folder. The old layout is not converted, and some paths exist in both layouts (02.assembly/{sample}/, 04.annotation/{sample}/), so old and new files would mix.

The v2 layout is the same in every mode, and a mode that has nothing for a folder leaves it out:

<output_dir>/
├── 00.resources/    material shared by the run: UNITE, antiSMASH databases, telomere repeat database, SignalP 6, ChroQueTas, PhiX
├── 01.reads/        read QC, filtered and selected reads (not in contigs mode)
├── 02.assembly/     assembly, screen, mitochondrion split, QUAST, BUSCO, Qualimap
├── 03.taxonomy/     ITS extraction and classification
├── 04.annotation/   masking, gene prediction, functional annotation
├── 05.amr/          antifungal resistance mutations (new; only with the AMR screen on)
├── 06.report/       MultiQC
└── logs/            one log per rule and sample

FunFlux 1.x and FunFluxL

v1 v2 01.pre-processing/ (PhiX index, fastp reports, trimmed reads) 00.resources/phix/, 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/ 01.pre-processing/{sample}_long_filt.fastq, 01.pre-processing/read_qc/ (FunFluxL) 01.reads/{sample}/long/ 02.assembly/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/ 03.post-processing/contaminants/{sample}/, and the read-mapping BAM in 03.post-processing/{sample}/ (FunFlux 1.x) or 03.post-processing/contaminants/{sample}_map.bam (FunFluxL) 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/ 03.post-processing/consensus/{sample}/ (FunFluxL, Medaka) 02.assembly/{sample}/medaka/ 03.post-processing/assembly_evaluation/{sample}/ (FunFlux 1.x) 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/, now also in longread mode 03.post-processing/completeness_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/ 03.post-processing/mapping_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/qualimap/ 03.post-processing/ITS_extraction/{sample}/ 03.taxonomy/{sample}/ 03.post-processing/ITS_extraction/unite_its_sintax.fasta 00.resources/unite/ 04.annotation/{sample}/ 04.annotation/{sample}/ 04.annotation/antismash_db/ 00.resources/antismash/databases/ report/ 06.report/

FunFluxL+

FunFluxL+ v2 01.read_processing/illumina/, 01.read_processing/long/ 00.resources/phix/, 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/, 01.reads/{sample}/long/ 02.short-read_assembly/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/ 03.read_selection/contamination/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/contaminants/; the selected pairs in 01.reads/{sample}/selected/ 03.read_selection/mapping_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/eval/qualimap/ 03.read_selection/assembly_evaluation/{sample}/ and 07.genome_qc/assembly_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/, one report with the labels {sample}_guide and {sample} 04.long-read_assembly/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/ (hifiasm/ or flye/, assembly.fasta) 05.assembly_curation/contamination/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/ 05.assembly_curation/mapping_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/qualimap/ 06.polishing/medaka/{sample}/, 06.polishing/polypolish/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/medaka/, 02.assembly/{sample}/polypolish/ 07.genome_qc/completeness_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/ 07.genome_qc/ITS_extraction/{sample}/ 03.taxonomy/{sample}/ 07.genome_qc/ITS_extraction/unite_its_sintax.fasta 00.resources/unite/ 08.annotation/{sample}/, 08.annotation/antismash_db/ 04.annotation/{sample}/, 00.resources/antismash/databases/ 09.report/ 06.report/

Funnotator

Funnotator v2 01.pre-processing/pre_filtering/{sample}/contigs_filt.fasta 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta 01.pre-processing/assembly_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/ 01.pre-processing/completeness_evaluation/{sample}/ 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/ 01.pre-processing/ITS_extraction/{sample}/ 03.taxonomy/{sample}/ 01.pre-processing/ITS_extraction/unite_its_sintax.fasta 00.resources/unite/ 02.annotation/{sample}/, 02.annotation/antismash_db/ 04.annotation/{sample}/, 00.resources/antismash/databases/ report/ 06.report/

The delivered assembly files have new names, and the mitochondrion now has a file of its own:

v1 v2, in 02.assembly/{sample}/ contigs_sel.fasta (FunFlux 1.x), the Medaka consensus.fasta (FunFluxL), polished.fasta (FunFluxL+) contigs_all.fasta: the complete assembly after the screen and polishing, mitochondrion included none contigs_final.fasta: the nuclear genome, read by QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS steps and funannotate none contigs_mitochondrial.fasta: the confirmed mitochondrial contigs; an empty file when there are none

A new file, 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_removed_by_clean.txt, lists the contigs that funannotate clean removed before gene prediction.

docs.title: Behaviour changes
docs.text:
The tables below group the changes by part of the workflow. The "Affects" column names the v1 workflows that a change concerns, and the "What to do" column names the action. "Nothing" means that the change needs no action.

Running and configuration

Change Affects What to do One workflow with a mode key; the configuration must be named with --configfile all Start from the v2 template; add mode and the input block Every CPU-bound rule declares threads:, so --cores limits the whole run all Give --cores the value of resources.threads (24 in the template, as in v1); drop --jobs on a single computer FunFlux runs on a cluster with --executor slurm --jobs N. Every heavy step asks the scheduler for resources.ram_gb of memory and for the time limit of the new key resources.runtime_hours (default 48). Every download step runs where Snakemake runs, and snakemake download_all fetches all downloads in advance (On a cluster) all On a cluster, set the three resources keys from the limits of a node and a partition curl, tar and gzip come from a conda environment (download), and InterProScan's Perl from the interproscan environment; v1 took them from the computer all Nothing No workdir:: relative paths are read from the launch folder all Use absolute paths, or paths relative to the launch folder Thread caps: eggNOG-mapper 12 (FunFlux 1.x: 24), nhmmer and ITSx 8, SINTAX 1, SignalP 6 at most resources.threads (CPU cores and threads) all Nothing Conda environments built from pinned package lists of the tested tool versions (workflow/envs/*.linux-64.pin.txt), with the Python version pinned in every environment that contains Python all Nothing; the first v2 run builds new environments New optional keys whose defaults keep the v1 behaviour: spades_kmers, busco.lineage, prediction.busco_db, repeatmodeler_seed, directories.antismash_db, directories.unite_db, contigs.screen, medaka_model_fallback_auto all Nothing

Inputs

Change Affects What to do One input key per technology: input.illumina_dir, input.longread_dir, input.contigs_dir replace the v1 key directories.input_dir all Move the path The suffixes stay _ont and _pacbio, and flye_input_mode: pacbio-hifi is removed. Illumina plus PacBio HiFi is allowed in hybrid FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Name PacBio HiFi reads {sample}_pacbio.<ext> Underscores are allowed in sample names (v1 rejected them). FunFlux prints a NOTE when a name is not a valid locus-tag prefix all For GenBank submission, use 3 to 12 letters or digits starting with a letter

Assembly and screen

Change Affects What to do Long reads are assembled with hifiasm by default. FunFluxL 0.1 used Flye, which stays available FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Set parameters.<mode>.assembler: flye to keep Flye Filtlong keeps every read that passes its length and quality filters: target_bases is empty (no cap) by default, and length_weight: 10 favours longer reads. FunFluxL 0.1 kept at most 500 Mb (--target_bases 500000000) with Filtlong's default length weight of 1 FunFluxL To repeat FunFluxL 0.1's read selection, set parameters.longread.filtlong.target_bases: 500000000 and length_weight: 1 Before the assembly starts, a named Medaka model is checked against Medaka's list of models, and auto is worked out from the basecaller tag of the first 100 reads of the raw FASTQ. A wrong model therefore fails in seconds instead of after the assembly. auto needs network access once and exactly one basecaller tag in those reads. New key medaka_model_fallback_auto. The assembler waits for the check's file, so a changed medaka_model also re-runs the assembly of the ONT samples FunFluxL, FunFluxL+, ONT samples For public or re-headered ONT reads, name the model or set medaka_model: false (The Medaka model) The PhiX genome and its bowtie2 index are downloaded once per output folder and kept in 00.resources/phix/. In v1, they were kept with the processed reads and deleted after the run. The PhiX-free pairs are called {sample}_nophix_R1.fastq and _R2.fastq FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL+ Nothing SPAdes writes into 02.assembly/{sample}/spades/ (in hybrid, guide/spades/), so a re-run of SPAdes no longer deletes the screen's files of the sample. In FunFlux 1.x the whole sample folder was SPAdes' output. Flye likewise works in flye/, and its assembly is copied up one level FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Nothing Filtlong guidance by the Illumina reads is off by default. Switched on (short_read_guidance: true, filtlong_split: 1000), it applies to ONT samples only. FunFluxL+ always guided and cut every sample, PacBio included FunFluxL+ For FunFluxL+'s behaviour on ONT samples, set short_read_guidance: true; move filtlong.split to parameters.hybrid.filtlong_split (Filtlong guidance) Polypolish output headers are cut at the first space or tab (v1: >ptg000001l polypolish) FunFluxL+ Nothing assembly_linearized.fasta and assembly_single_line.fasta are no longer written FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Update scripts that read them The BLAST hit depth is 50 target sequences and 5 HSPs in every mode (FunFlux 1.x: 10 and 1), with a NOTE below 5 HSPs FunFlux 1.x Nothing; set 10 and 1 only to reproduce FunFlux 1.1.x numbers (BLAST hit depth) parameters.nt_version is read in illumina mode too FunFlux 1.x Set it if your BLAST database has another name than core_nt New: a mitochondrion screen and split in every mode with the screen. The screen classes each contig of the draft from its BLAST hits and, in longread and hybrid, from the assembler's read depth and circularity. With the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, the confirmed mitochondrial contigs are kept whatever their genus, on the hybrid guide assembly too. After polishing they are split off into contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, so that QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS steps and funannotate read only the nuclear genome, contigs_final.fasta. A confirmed mitochondrial contig missing from the BlobTools table is kept as no-taxonomy, and a confirmed ID missing from the FASTA stops the run (Mitochondria) all Read contigs_final.fasta as the genome; parameters.mitochondria.mode: report or off keeps the mitochondrial contigs in it decontamination.mode: auto is removed and stops the run before any job starts, also as a mode in sample_overrides when the screen runs. BLAST genus labels are unreliable for poorly sequenced fungi, so auto can remove most of the genome (Configuration) FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Use off (the default), read contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, then exclude the contaminant genera or include the genera BLAST assigned to the isolate's own contigs With the screen, the decontamination files (include_genera_by_sample, exclude_genera_file, sample_overrides) and an include mode without a genus are checked before any job starts (v1: when select_contigs ran, after BLAST) FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Nothing parameters.genus is translated with a NOTE, and an empty genus now means mode: off (v1: auto, the genus with the most contigs). The template sets discard_no_hit: false, where the v1 template had true (the v1 code default was already false) all Replace genus with parameters.decontamination; set discard_no_hit: true if you relied on the v1 template With SPAdes headers, the contigs mode filter keeps contigs of at least 500 bp and 2x coverage. Any other FASTA only has its headers cut at the first space or tab (Funnotator removed every contig of 500 bp or less). An empty result stops the run, and the screen is optional Funnotator Expect 500 bp contigs to be kept and no length filter on non-SPAdes FASTA Delivered files renamed (table above) all Update downstream scripts

QC and ITS

Change Affects What to do QUAST also runs in longread mode. In hybrid, one QUAST report holds the guide ({sample}_guide) and the final assembly ({sample}) FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Nothing BUSCO's result tree is now kept, except hmmer_output/ and busco_sequences/ (v1 deleted run_*/ and auto_lineage/). With the auto lineage, that is several hundred MB per sample. With auto, the lineage data is still downloaded per sample into a temporary folder, while a named lineage is downloaded once per output folder into 00.resources/busco/ and read offline. New key busco.lineage. With a named lineage, MultiQC shows one BUSCO row per sample instead of two all Allow several hundred MB per sample, or name a lineage, for example hypocreales_odb12, which keeps the result tree of that lineage only New: the contig summary, 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv. It has one row per contig of the draft assembly, with a verdict (chromosome, chromosome_arm, mitochondrion, rDNA_array, low_depth, repeat, nuclear_contig, nuclear_fragment, contaminant or unclassified) and the evidence behind it, and is also shown as a table in the MultiQC report. Its annotated_as column links each contig to its scaffold_N name in the annotation (Contig summary). The telomere repeat unit of each assembly is chosen from the data with tidk and checked against tidk's telomere repeat database, downloaded once per output folder. New keys parameters.contig_summary.*, new required link links.telomere_db_link all Copy the links.telomere_db_link line from the v2 template; the run stops without it ITS is cut out of contigs_final.fasta in one strand-oriented window per rDNA unit before ITSx runs (Funnotator ran ITSx on its raw input). New keys its.window_flank (2,000 bp on each side of the 5.8S gene) and its.max_full_length (1,500 bp). Identical ITS copies are collapsed and counted. ITS1 or ITS2 outside 50-600 bp is listed in {sample}_ITS_copies.txt and not classified, and a full ITS longer than its.max_full_length is marked rejected_too_long there (only ITS1 and ITS2 are classified, as in v1). Long-read assemblies, which could give empty or wrong ITS files in v1, now give the ITS all Update scripts that parse ITS record names: records are named after their window (contig:start-end_strand), classified copies {sample}_ITS1_1, {sample}_ITS2_1, ... (ITS on long-read contigs) SINTAX runs on one thread with --randseed 1, so the ITS confidences repeat from run to run. In v1, SINTAX used several threads and no fixed seed all Nothing SINTAX classifies against the UNITE records whose taxonomy names a genus (new rule unite_identified, new key its.unite_identified_only, default true). In v1, SINTAX used the whole release, in which about a third of the records stop above the genus, and one identical to the query can stop the result at d:Fungi all Nothing; its.unite_identified_only: false gives the v1 reference QC-only rules (QUAST, Qualimap, NanoPlot) no longer stop the run when the tool fails all Check the log and the MultiQC page for a missing table NanoPlot writes its plots as HTML pages only (--no_static). FunFluxL also wrote them as PNG, but the pinned NanoPlot 1.46.2 draws PNG only where a Chrome or Chromium browser is installed, so the output would differ between computers FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Open the HTML plots; MultiQC reads the NanoStats table as before Qualimap runs without a display, so it works on a server with no X session. Its Java heap is min(ram_gb, 64) GB, as in v1 FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL, FunFluxL+ Nothing BUSCO runs with --opt-out-run-stats, so it sends no usage statistics and makes no ipinfo.io lookup (v1 sent both). MultiQC no longer shortens sample names, so a sample named SAMPLE1.clean keeps its name all Nothing

Annotation and databases

Change Affects What to do The antiSMASH database stays in 00.resources/antismash/databases/ between runs on the same output folder (v1 deleted it and downloaded it again on every resume), or is linked from directories.antismash_db. The same holds for UNITE, with PROVENANCE.txt all Optionally point directories.antismash_db and directories.unite_db at copies you have The funannotate database archive is checked with sha256sum -c before it is unpacked (v1 downloaded the checksum file but did not check it). A mismatch stops the run all Delete the archive and its .sha256 file and run again The template links a newer snapshot of the funannotate database, funannotate_db_1.8.17_2026-10-08 (Zenodo record 23265189), with newer Swiss-Prot, Pfam, InterPro, Gene Ontology and gene2product releases. The v1 templates link the 2025-12-15 snapshot (record 18271295). What changed is listed under funannotate database snapshot all Point directories.funannotate_db at a new, empty folder, because a folder that holds the v1 snapshot keeps being used With GeneMark-ES on, the new rule genemark_check runs GeneMark-ES on a 200 kb slice of each masked genome before gene prediction (about a minute). An expired licence key therefore stops the run before funannotate predict starts instead of partway through it all, with GeneMark-ES Renew the key when the message asks for it The AUGUSTUS model (column 4 of the annotation parameter table, files.annotation_params) is optional. Empty or - makes funannotate train AUGUSTUS on the genome's BUSCO genes, which v1 never did, because v1 required a model. A named model must exist in the funannotate database, or the run stops with the closest names (v1 passed any name on, and funannotate silently trained AUGUSTUS under a misspelt one). The new rule augustus_model_check records the choice in 04.annotation/{sample}/augustus_model.txt and at the top of the gene prediction log. parameters.prediction.augustus_optimize adds the long training all Nothing for a v1 table with a valid model name: AUGUSTUS gets the same option as in v1 Tiberius, a gene finder with a model trained by its authors on many fungal genomes, runs by default before gene prediction, and funannotate predict adds its gene models to the evidence it combines (--other_gff, weight 1). It needs about 16 GB of memory and downloads its model (30 MB) once per output folder. New keys parameters.tiberius.mode and model_sha256, new link links.tiberius_model_link all Nothing; parameters.tiberius.mode: off gives gene prediction without it, as in v1 New key parameters.genemark.mode: auto, the default, uses GeneMark-ES when directories.genemark_dir is set, and off never uses it. An empty value (mode: or mode: "") means auto, as for the other mode keys all Nothing; leave directories.genemark_dir empty to run without GeneMark-ES New, off by default: SignalP 6, which predicts signal peptides for funannotate annotate. It needs the licensed archive from DTU (files.signalp6_archive) and a parameters.signalp6.mode other than off (Licensed and external tools) all Nothing New: rule normalize_funannotate_db, the path repair, rewrites the absolute paths stored inside the funannotate database to your folder. It runs in place and without a lock, so let one run pass it before others start on the same database (Reference databases) all Nothing New, off by default: the AMR screen. ChroQueTas screens each genome for the point mutations that the FungAMR database lists with evidence for or against resistance, and writes 05.amr/{sample}/. New keys parameters.amr.*, new link links.chroquetas_link (Antifungal resistance mutations) all Nothing; parameters.amr.chroquetas: on switches it on, and accepts the non-commercial licence of ChroQueTas

Logs

Change Affects What to do One log per rule and sample in logs/; InterProScan's scratch folder is 04.annotation/{sample}/iprscan/tmp/ (no top-level temp/) all Nothing

Kept as in v1

  • decontamination.mode: off as the default
  • BUSCO on the final genome only
  • the filtered long reads, the selected pairs and the read-mapping BAM of the read-based modes, kept after the run

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This page lists what FunFlux needs on the computer and how to install it before the first run. You install conda, Snakemake, InterProScan and one or two databases yourself. Snakemake installs every other tool, each in its own conda environment, and the workflow downloads the other databases.

The installation takes six steps, in this order:

Step What you do Where 1 Clone FunFlux Get FunFlux 2 Install conda, then Snakemake in the launcher environment The launcher environment 3 Check the commands FunFlux takes from the machine Commands outside the conda environments 4 Download the eggNOG-mapper data and, for the contamination and mitochondrion screen, NCBI core_nt Reference databases 5 Install InterProScan and, optionally, GeneMark-ES and SignalP 6 Licensed and external tools 6 Optionally, build the tool environments before the first run, and on a cluster also fetch the downloads Building the environments in advance, On a cluster

Terms used on this page

launcher environment the conda environment you create by hand for Snakemake itself; activate it before every run, and install no analysis tool into it launch folder the folder Snakemake is started from, normally the FunFlux repository; relative paths are read from it, and .snakemake/ is created there rule one step of the workflow as Snakemake defines it, such as select_contigs; the console and the log files in logs/ use its name job one run of a rule, for one sample or once for the whole run; the dry run lists the jobs it plans heavy step on a cluster, a step that asks the scheduler for both ram_gb and runtime_hours, such as the assemblers, BLAST and InterProScan pin file the file <name>.linux-64.pin.txt beside each environment file: the exact package builds FunFlux v2 was tested with, installed without solving dependencies the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true AMR screen the optional step, off by default (parameters.amr.chroquetas), in which ChroQueTas looks in each genome for the changes FungAMR lists for the species; results in 05.amr/

docs.title: System requirements
docs.text:
Check that the computer meets these requirements before you install FunFlux:

Item Requirement Operating system Linux on x86-64. The environment pin files are for linux-64, and GeneMark-ES and InterProScan are distributed as 64-bit Linux builds. conda 24.7.1 or newer. Snakemake 9.14.6 stops with an error on older versions. Snakemake 9.14.6 or a later 9.x release. FunFlux v2 was developed and tested with 9.14.6 and stops at start-up on an older version. Version 10 or later has not been tested. Commands bash and the GNU base commands (sha256sum, md5sum and the rest of coreutils, find, grep, sed, awk) on the machine's own PATH, outside conda. With the AMR screen on, also a grep that knows -P (GNU grep). No python, perl, curl, tar or gzip is needed. See Commands outside the conda environments. CPU the number in resources.threads (template: 24), given again as --cores Memory about 16 GB for Tiberius, on by default, and more than 14 GB for SignalP 6 in slow mode. See Memory. Disk about 380 GB of databases. The conda environments take 20 to 25 GB for a contigs run, 25 GB with the screen and SignalP 6, and the read-based modes add 4 to 9 environments, not measured. The output takes in the order of 10 GB per sample in contigs mode, plus the reads and assembly files of the read-based modes. See Disk. Network conda packages and several database downloads, on the computer that runs Snakemake; inside the jobs, only BUSCO with the automatic lineage. See Network access.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
With the default settings, plan for at least 16 GB of free memory, because of Tiberius. The table gives what is known of the memory each step needs.

Step Memory Tiberius, on by default about 16 GB for a fungal genome of about 40 Mb; switch it off (parameters.tiberius.mode: off) on a computer with less free memory SignalP 6 in slow mode more than 14 GB (SignalP 6) SPAdes (illumina, hybrid) resources.ram_gb (template: 128), given to SPAdes as its memory limit (-m) Qualimap (illumina, longread, hybrid) resources.ram_gb, capped at 64 GB, as its Java heap The other steps not measured

On a single computer, resources.ram_gb limits only SPAdes and Qualimap. Snakemake itself starts jobs by thread count alone and does not limit memory, unless --resources mem_gb=N is passed to cap how many SPAdes jobs run at once, or java_mem=N for Qualimap. See CPU cores and threads. On a cluster, ram_gb is also the memory every heavy step asks the scheduler for, as described under How the settings reach Slurm.

docs.title: Run time
docs.text: One fungal genome in contigs mode takes several hours, and InterProScan alone usually takes a few hours for a fungal proteome. Each rule declares its threads, and Snakemake runs jobs side by side as long as their threads fit into --cores. The steps that take longest are listed on Run time, and the threads each step asks for on CPU cores and threads.

docs.title: Disk
docs.text:
Disk space goes to three parts: the databases, the conda environments and the output of each sample. NCBI core_nt takes 264 GB of the about 380 GB of databases, and only the screen reads it.

What Size Where NCBI core_nt, build of 11 July 2026; its taxonomy files add 0.8 GB 264 GB directories.blast_db; only for the screen InterProScan 5.78-109.0, installed 50 GB files.iprscan eggNOG 5.0.2 data 48 GB directories.eggnog_db antiSMASH 8.0.4 databases 9.4 GB 00.resources/ of every output folder, or once in directories.antismash_db funannotate database, unpacked, archive included 8.1 GB directories.funannotate_db conda environments: the 18 of a contigs run with the screen, Tiberius and SignalP 6 about 25 GB; the download environment among them takes 120 MB .snakemake/conda/, or the folder given to --conda-prefix conda environments added by the read-based modes: 4 in illumina, 4 or 5 in longread, 8 or 9 in hybrid, listed under --sdm conda not measured the same folder conda environment of the AMR screen (chroquetas), when it is on about 2 GB the same folder output of one sample, contigs mode in the order of 10 GB directories.output_dir output of one sample, read-based modes: the kept reads (01.reads/), the assembler's working folder, the read-mapping BAM, the polishing files whole sample: 13 GB in illumina, 20 to 31 GB in longread and 39 GB in hybrid on the 42.6 Mb genome of Botrytis cinerea B05.10; 16 to 17 GB in longread and 29 GB in hybrid on the 32.7 Mb genome of Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616, with PacBio HiFi reads directories.output_dir

In the output of the read-based modes, the filtered long reads are kept uncompressed, and so are the selected Illumina pairs of hybrid.

Sizes are as du -h prints them, in powers of 1024. The environments were measured with the prefix on another file system than conda's package cache. On the same file system, conda hard-links files from its package cache, and the environments add less to the disk.

Each measured run is listed under Disk use per run, and Disk use shows where the space of the output folder goes.

docs.title: Network access
docs.text:
Most downloads happen on the computer that runs Snakemake. The download steps are local rules, so they run on that computer and never on a compute node of a cluster. Snakemake builds the conda environments there too. Only three things reach the network from inside a job: BUSCO with the automatic lineage, and two lookups that the results do not need.

Host What When Runs on conda.anaconda.org the packages listed in the pin files building an environment the computer that runs Snakemake zenodo.org the funannotate database and its checksum file while directories.funannotate_db does not hold it (funannotate_db) the computer that runs Snakemake s3.hpc.ut.ee UNITE first run in an output folder, unless directories.unite_db is set (unite_db) the computer that runs Snakemake dl.secondarymetabolites.org, ftp.ebi.ac.uk antiSMASH databases first run in an output folder, unless directories.antismash_db is set (antismash_db) the computer that runs Snakemake bioinf.uni-greifswald.de the Tiberius fungi model first run in an output folder, unless parameters.tiberius.mode is off (tiberius_model) the computer that runs Snakemake raw.githubusercontent.com the telomere repeat database of tidk; ChroQueTas and its FungAMR database first run in an output folder (telomere_db; with the AMR screen on also chroquetas_db) the computer that runs Snakemake ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov PhiX genome first run in an output folder, illumina and hybrid (download_phix) the computer that runs Snakemake chosen by Medaka (GitHub) model weights the model check of an ONT sample with Medaka, the first time a model is used (check_medaka_model), before the assembly the computer that runs Snakemake busco-data.ezlab.org BUSCO lineage datasets with a named lineage, once per output folder (busco_data) the computer that runs Snakemake busco-data.ezlab.org BUSCO lineage datasets with parameters.busco.lineage: auto, the default: every BUSCO job (completeness) the job www.ebi.ac.uk InterProScan's lookup service, a shortcut: without it, InterProScan computes every match itself (Functional annotation) every InterProScan job the job api.multiqc.info MultiQC's check for a newer version the report (multiqc) the job

FunFlux runs BUSCO 6.0.0 with --opt-out-run-stats. Without it, BUSCO ends each job by looking up the country of the machine's IP address online and sending usage statistics. See Assembly QC.

When the jobs have no internet, BUSCO, InterProScan and MultiQC behave as follows.

  • BUSCO, with lineage: auto, cannot download its lineage data, and the BUSCO job fails. Name a lineage instead, as described under BUSCO on compute nodes without internet.
  • InterProScan prints Pre-calculated match lookup service failed - analysis proceeding to run locally and computes every match itself. The matches are the same, and the run is longer (Functional annotation).
  • MultiQC gives up its version check after about 2 seconds, and the report is the same.

Compute nodes without internet need a named BUSCO lineage

On a single computer with internet, nothing needs preparing. On a cluster whose compute nodes have no internet, name a BUSCO lineage. The rest is fetched on the login node.

Snakemake itself may have to run on a computer without internet, for example when the whole run goes inside one batch job on a compute node. In that case, fetch everything first on a computer with internet, with snakemake download_all, as described under Preparation, on a computer with internet.

docs.title: Behind a proxy that re-signs HTTPS
docs.text:
FunFlux's downloads trust only the list of certificate authorities inside their conda environments, not the computer's own. Behind an institute proxy or mirror that re-signs HTTPS with an in-house certificate, they therefore fail with SSL certificate problem or CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.

curl, in the six download steps that use it, and Medaka read CURL_CA_BUNDLE, while BUSCO and antiSMASH read SSL_CERT_FILE. Point both variables at the computer's list before you start Snakemake:

System Commands Debian, Ubuntu export CURL_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt Red Hat Enterprise Linux and its rebuilds (Rocky, Alma) export CURL_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt

docs.title: Get FunFlux
docs.text:
The FunFlux repository holds the workflow, the configuration template and the environment files. Clone it:

git clone https://github.com/iLivius/FunFlux.git
cd FunFlux

The clone holds, among other files:

Path Content config/config.yaml the commented configuration template; copy it, for example to config/config_custom.yaml, which git ignores config/annotation_parameters.tsv an example annotation parameter table, the table files.annotation_params names workflow/envs/ <name>.yaml, one conda environment per tool, each with its pin file <name>.linux-64.pin.txt (see --sdm conda)

Start Snakemake from this folder, the launch folder. Snakemake finds workflow/Snakefile there and keeps its run records in .snakemake/, which git ignores. The conda environments go there too, unless --conda-prefix names another folder.

docs.title: The launcher environment
docs.text:
Snakemake runs in a conda environment of its own, the launcher environment. Create it and check the version:

conda create -c conda-forge -c bioconda -n snakemake "snakemake>=9.14.6,<10"
conda activate snakemake
snakemake --version

The launcher environment holds Snakemake and its Python, which reads the configuration and runs FunFlux's checks before any job starts. Activate it before every run. Install no analysis tool into it, because each tool runs in its own environment and every FunFlux script runs with the pinned Python of its rule's environment.

Snakemake prints a warning unless conda uses strict channel priority, set with conda config --set channel_priority strict. To let Snakemake send the steps to a Slurm cluster, add snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm to this environment, as described under Run A: Snakemake sends each step to Slurm.

FunFlux sets PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 for every job, so packages installed with pip install --user cannot be used instead of the packages of a rule environment.

docs.title: Commands outside the conda environments
docs.text:
A few commands come from the computer itself, not from a conda environment, and FunFlux does not install them. Two kinds of rule take commands from outside a tool environment:

  • Rules without a conda environment run standard shell commands only, and take them from the launcher environment and the machine. They are the contig filter (filter_contigs), finalize_assembly, the links to local databases (unite_db_local, antismash_db_local) and cleanup.
  • Rules with a conda environment take their commands from the environment, and from the machine for every command the environment lacks. Most environments lack the standard commands of the shell lines around the tool, such as awk, grep, sed, find, mkdir and rm. The download steps take sha256sum and md5sum from the machine.

Every command in the next table must be installed on the machine itself, outside conda

When Snakemake activates a rule's environment, conda, with its default settings, takes the launcher environment off the PATH. The rules that run in a conda environment therefore find these commands only on the machine's own PATH.

Command Used for bash every rule: Snakemake runs the shell lines of each rule with bash sha256sum, md5sum checking the downloads: the funannotate database, the Tiberius model, the telomere repeat database and ChroQueTas (sha256sum), UNITE (md5sum) awk, grep, sed, find, and basic commands such as head, cat, cp, ln, mkdir, rm the contig filter, copies, links to local databases, and the shell lines around the tool in most rules (awk and grep in its_windows and signalp6_annotation, grep in genemark_check, sed in eggnog_annotation, find in completeness and iprscan_annotation; in the read-based modes awk turns hifiasm's graph into FASTA and cuts the Polypolish headers, grep counts the SPAdes contigs the filter kept, cat reads the Medaka model file) grep with -P (GNU grep), sed, and basic commands such as cut, paste, tr ChroQueTas (rule amr_chroquetas, AMR screen on), a bash script that runs inside the chroquetas environment; the environment holds the tools it calls, not these commands

These commands come from conda instead, so the machine does not need them:

Command Comes from python the pinned Python of each rule's environment (Which Python runs the helper scripts) curl, tar, gzip the download environment of the six download steps that use them (download_phix, funannotate_db, unite_db, telomere_db, tiberius_model, chroquetas_db) perl the interproscan environment, for InterProScan's SUPERFAMILY analysis and PROSITE patterns; the funannotate environment for GeneMark-ES, once its scripts start the first perl on the PATH (GeneMark-ES)

Check the machine's commands with no conda environment active:

conda deactivate     # repeat until no environment is active, base included
command -v bash sha256sum md5sum awk grep sed find
command -v cut paste tr && echo ok | grep -P 'o\w'   # AMR screen on: the last line reads ok

Install a missing command with the system package manager. Installing it into the launcher environment does not reach the rules that run in a conda environment. FunFlux has been tested on x86-64 Linux only.

docs.title: --sdm conda: one pinned environment per tool
docs.text:
Every tool has its own environment file in workflow/envs/. With --sdm conda (short for --software-deployment-method conda), Snakemake builds the environments of the planned jobs before the first job starts and reuses them in later runs. A dry run lists the missing ones as Conda environment workflow/envs/<name>.yaml will be created.

Beside each <name>.yaml is its pin file, <name>.linux-64.pin.txt: the exact package builds of an environment FunFlux v2 was tested with, as written by conda list --explicit.

What Snakemake installs depends on whether it can use the pin file:

Situation What Snakemake installs The pin file exists that list, without solving dependencies; it logs Using pinnings from <path>/<name>.linux-64.pin.txt. Installing the pin file fails it prints a warning and solves <name>.yaml instead A platform other than linux-64 there is no pin file, and Snakemake always solves the yaml

Only the pin file reproduces the tested builds

The yaml fixes the versions of the main tools and of Python, but few of their dependencies. When Snakemake solves it, the versions and builds of everything else can differ from the pinned ones. That includes tools in the table below, such as AUGUSTUS, DIAMOND and HMMER, and the OpenJDK and PyTorch patch releases.

The table lists each environment, the tools in it and the runs that build it.
