  • The gene prediction without GeneMark-ES, and the effect of the number of threads on its own (the B05.10 runs above differ in the threads as well).
  • Tiberius on other genomes, and with a graphics card (FunFlux runs it on the CPU).
  • Genomes of other sizes and other fungi.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
The configuration key mode selects the front end, the steps that turn the input into an assembly. The launch command does not change with the mode. This page sets the four modes side by side and compares their steps, the contamination and mitochondrion screen as each mode runs it, and the files each mode writes. Read it when you choose a mode, or to look up what a mode does.

From the screen on, every mode runs the same steps, and only polishing differs between the read-based modes. Every mode produces 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta. This file is the nuclear genome alone when the screen runs with the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed. Otherwise nothing is split off, and any mitochondrial contig stays in it.

From that file on, all four modes run QUAST, BUSCO, ITS extraction and classification, repeat masking, gene prediction, functional annotation and the MultiQC report. Two of these steps take extra inputs in some modes. In hybrid mode QUAST also reports the Illumina guide assembly, and MultiQC adds the read-QC and mapping tables of the modes that have reads.

Terms used on this page

front end the steps that differ by mode, chosen by mode: read processing, assembly and contig filter before the shared screen, and polishing after it the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true draft assembly (the draft) the assembly the screen examines, before any contig is removed contig selector rule select_contigs, the last step of the screen: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says; the default, off, keeps every contig genus filter the setting parameters.decontamination.mode: include or exclude, under which the contig selector keeps or removes contigs by the genus BlobTools gave them guide assembly in hybrid mode, the SPAdes assembly of the Illumina reads; it is screened, and only the pairs that map to it go on assembler evidence what hifiasm or Flye report for each contig, above all read depth and circularity, written to assembly_evidence.tsv for the mitochondrion screen; longread and hybrid only

docs.title: The four modes side by side
docs.text:
Three modes build an assembly from reads, and contigs mode starts from one. The table compares the four modes step by step, and each column heading links to the page of its mode.

illumina longread hybrid contigs Status run on one public genome (Validation) run on ONT reads of one public genome and PacBio HiFi reads of another, with hifiasm and with Flye run on ONT and Illumina reads of one public genome and PacBio HiFi and short reads of another, with hifiasm; Flye in dry runs only run on the assembly of one public genome (Validation) Input Illumina paired-end reads ONT or PacBio HiFi reads, technology set per sample Illumina pairs plus ONT or PacBio HiFi reads of the same isolate an assembled genome (FASTA) Input folder and file names input.illumina_dir: {sample}_R1.<ext>, {sample}_R2.<ext> input.longread_dir: {sample}_ont.<ext> or {sample}_pacbio.<ext> both folders (may be the same one) and both sets of names input.contigs_dir: {sample}.fasta, .fa or .fna Other required keys directories.blast_db, links.phix_link directories.blast_db directories.blast_db, links.phix_link directories.blast_db, only with the screen Mode settings parameters.spades_kmers parameters.longread parameters.hybrid, parameters.spades_kmers parameters.contigs Read processing PhiX removal (bowtie2), fastp Filtlong; NanoPlot before and after PhiX removal, fastp; Filtlong (ONT reads scored against the Illumina pairs only if you switch it on); NanoPlot none Assembly SPAdes --isolate hifiasm (default) or Flye SPAdes guide assembly, then hifiasm or Flye none Contig filter at least 500 bp and 2x coverage none guide assembly only: at least 500 bp and 2x SPAdes headers: at least 500 bp and 2x; other headers: none Polishing none Medaka, ONT samples Medaka (ONT samples), then Polypolish with the Illumina pairs none Mapping QC Qualimap Qualimap Qualimap, guide and long-read assembly none contigs_all.fasta is the screened contigs the Medaka consensus (ONT) or the screened assembly (PacBio HiFi, or Medaka off) the Polypolish output the screened FASTA; written only with the screen Not run long-read steps PhiX removal, fastp, SPAdes, Polypolish; Medaka for PacBio HiFi Medaka and Filtlong guidance for PacBio HiFi read processing, assembly, polishing, mapping QC; the screen unless parameters.contigs.screen: true

contigs mode skips every read and assembly step and runs the screen only with parameters.contigs.screen: true. hybrid mode combines the other two read-based modes. Its Illumina steps build a guide assembly and select reads, its long-read steps build the genome that is delivered, and Polypolish corrects that genome with the Illumina pairs.

In longread and hybrid mode the read technology is taken from each file name, so one batch can hold ONT and PacBio HiFi samples. The flags that differ between the two technologies are listed on Long reads.

docs.title: The contamination and mitochondrion screen
docs.text:
The screen checks every contig of the draft assembly. BLAST compares each contig with NCBI core_nt, and BlobTools gives it a genus. The mitochondrion screen looks for the mitochondrial genome among the contigs, and the contig selector keeps or removes each contig and records the decision. With the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, the contig selector keeps a confirmed mitochondrial contig whatever the genus filter says. Polishing comes after the screen, on the contigs that were kept.

The screen is the same in every mode. Three things change with the mode: the draft it examines, the reads behind the BlobTools coverage and the evidence for the mitochondrion.

illumina longread hybrid contigs with the screen Draft screened contigs_filt.fasta assembly.fasta the guide's contigs_filt.fasta, then assembly.fasta contigs_filt.fasta Reads behind the BlobTools coverage trimmed Illumina pairs, bowtie2 filtered long reads, minimap2 guide: Illumina pairs, bowtie2; long-read assembly: filtered long reads, minimap2 none; the contigs are mapped to themselves and the coverage carries no information Evidence for the mitochondrion BLAST BLAST plus the assembler's read depth and circularity guide: BLAST; long-read assembly: BLAST plus assembler evidence BLAST

A long-read assembler adds read depth and circularity to BLAST when the mitochondrion is judged. hybrid mode runs the screen twice, on the guide as in illumina and on the long-read assembly as in longread. In contigs mode there are no reads, so the BlobTools coverage carries no information and BLAST alone decides.

With the default settings, the screen removes no contig

The screen is on in every read-based mode and off in contigs mode unless parameters.contigs.screen: true. With the default parameters.decontamination.mode: off, it removes no contig but records a decision for each one and splits off the confirmed mitochondrion. See Decontamination and Mitochondria.

docs.title: What 01.reads and 02.assembly contain
docs.text:
The table shows which folders and files each mode writes to 01.reads and 02.assembly. contigs_final.fasta, QUAST, BUSCO, the telomere files and the contig summary are there in every mode. The other rows depend on each mode's reads, assembler, screen and polisher. Rows without a stage prefix are under 02.assembly/{sample}/, and 01.reads/ is not created in contigs mode.

Path illumina longread hybrid contigs 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/: fastp reports (kept), PhiX-free and trimmed reads (temporary) yes yes 01.reads/{sample}/long/: {sample}_filtered.fastq, NanoPlot raw_qc/ and filtered_qc/ yes yes 01.reads/{sample}/selected/: Illumina pairs that map to the screened guide assembly yes 02.assembly/{sample}/spades/ yes 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/: the Illumina guide assembly, its screen and Qualimap report yes hifiasm/ or flye/, assembly.fasta, assembly_evidence.tsv, assembly_provenance.tsv yes yes contigs_filt.fasta yes with the screen {sample}_medaka_model.txt, medaka/consensus.fasta ONT samples with Medaka ONT samples with Medaka polypolish/polished.fasta yes contaminants/, mitochondria/ yes yes yes with the screen contigs_all.fasta, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta yes yes yes with the screen contigs_final.fasta yes yes yes yes eval/quast/, eval/busco/ yes yes yes yes eval/telomere_candidates.tsv, telomere_unit.txt, telomere_ends.tsv: the telomere repeat unit of the assembly and the arrays at the contig ends yes yes yes yes eval/contig_summary.tsv, _mqc.tsv: what each contig of the draft is yes yes yes yes eval/qualimap/ yes yes yes

Every file is described on Output files.

Choosing a mode explains which mode fits a dataset.

docs.title: Pre-assembled contigs
docs.text:
Use mode: contigs to annotate genome assemblies you already have. There is no read processing and no assembler. A contig filter prepares each FASTA, and the contamination and mitochondrion screen runs only when parameters.contigs.screen is true. The mode replaces Funnotator, which shipped inside FunFlux 1.x.

Terms used on this page

the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector; in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true SPAdes-style header a FASTA header of the form >NODE_<n>_length_<L>_cov_<C>; only with such headers does the contig filter remove contigs under 500 bp or 2x coverage contig selector rule select_contigs, the last step of the screen: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says; the default, off, keeps every contig confirmed mitochondrial contig a contig the mitochondrion screen classes confirmed_mitochondrial; with the default separate_confirmed, it is kept whatever its genus and moved to contigs_mitochondrial.fasta nuclear genome the delivered genome without the confirmed mitochondrial contigs, contigs_final.fasta; it holds every contig when nothing is split off (no screen, or parameters.mitochondria.mode off or report) self-mapping in contigs mode with the screen, the contigs aligned to themselves only because BlobTools needs a BAM file; the coverage then reflects contig length, not depth annotation parameter table the tab-separated file named by files.annotation_params, one row per sample: name, species, a protein FASTA of related fungi and, optionally, an AUGUSTUS model

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FunFlux takes one FASTA file per sample from one folder:

Folder input.contigs_dir File names {sample}.fasta, {sample}.fa or {sample}.fna, uncompressed, the same extension for every sample Sample name the file name up to the last dot: my.genome.fasta is sample my.genome

Every file in the folder whose name contains a dot is read as a sample, files in subfolders included. Keep the folder flat, with only uncompressed FASTA files that share one extension. Each of the following stops the run:

In the folder The run stops before any job starts with README.txt next to S1.fasta [FunFlux] input.contigs_dir: more than one file extension in this folder (fasta, txt). All files in it must use the same one. only gzipped FASTA files, such as S1.fasta.gz [FunFlux] input.contigs_dir: file extension 'gz' is not recognised (expected one of: fasta, fa, fna). sub/S2.fasta [FunFlux] sample name 'sub/S2' contains characters that are not allowed ('/'). Rename the input files.

Every sample needs a row in the annotation parameter table, the file named by files.annotation_params, as in the other modes. The configuration sets the mode, the input folder and the screen:

mode: contigs
input:
  contigs_dir: /path/to/assemblies
parameters:
  contigs:
    screen: false     # true: screen for contaminants and the mitochondrion (needs directories.blast_db)

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    IN([one FASTA file per sample]) --> CF[contig filter<br/>SPAdes: at least 500 bp and 2x<br/>other headers: cut to first word]
    CF -->|screen off,<br/>the default| FIN([contigs_final.fasta only])
    CF -.->|"parameters.contigs.screen: true"| FILT([contigs_filt.fasta])
    FILT -.-> MAP[self-mapping, minimap2<br/>coverage track for BlobTools]
    FILT -.-> BL[BLAST against core_nt]
    MAP -.-> BT[BlobTools<br/>one taxon per contig]
    BL -.-> BT
    BL -.-> MT[mitochondrion screen<br/>from BLAST alone]
    BT -.-> SEL[contig selector<br/>parameters.decontamination]
    MT -.-> SEL
    SEL -.-> OUT([contigs_all.fasta, then contigs_final.fasta<br/>and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta])

By default the contig filter writes contigs_final.fasta and no other genome file, and with parameters.contigs.screen: true it writes contigs_filt.fasta for the screen instead. In the screen, BLAST decides both the genus of each contig and whether it is mitochondrial, and the self-mapping only gives BlobTools the BAM file it needs. The contigs the selector keeps become contigs_all.fasta, which is then split into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta.

docs.title: The contig filter
docs.text:
Rule filter_contigs prepares every FASTA, with or without the screen. It looks at the first header of the FASTA and takes one of two branches:

First header Example What happens matches ^>NODE_[0-9]+_length_[0-9]+_cov_ (SPAdes) >NODE_12_length_45678_cov_23.4 keeps contigs of at least 500 bp with a coverage of at least 2.0, both read from the header; headers unchanged; each sequence written on one line anything else >contig_1, >ptg000001l polypolish, >scaffold_1 length_12345 each header cut at the first space or tab; nothing removed, line wrapping unchanged
  • The test requires the whole SPAdes pattern, so that numbers in other headers are never misread. >scaffold_1 length_12345 takes the second branch, and so does a SPAdes assembly whose contigs were renamed.
  • The coverage in a SPAdes header is SPAdes' k-mer coverage for its largest k, lower than the read depth. The 500 bp and 2x cut-offs are those of the illumina mode and are not configuration keys.
  • The other headers are cut at the first space or tab because BLAST, BlobTools and the mitochondrion screen read only the first word.

Short contigs in a FASTA without SPAdes-style headers are dropped later, by the first annotation step, as described under Short contigs and funannotate clean.

The log, logs/filter_contigs_{sample}.log, records the branch and the counts, for example:

SPAdes-style header detected for SAMPLE1: removing contigs shorter than 500 bp or below 2x coverage; headers kept unchanged.
Kept <kept> of <total> records.

Header of SAMPLE2 is not SPAdes-style: trimming headers to their first word; NO length or coverage filtering applied.
Kept <n> of <n> records.

When no contig is left, the rule stops instead of passing an empty genome to the annotation. This happens with an empty FASTA, or with a SPAdes FASTA in which every contig fails the cut-offs. The message reads:

[FunFlux] filter_contigs: no contig of S1 is left (kept 0 of 12 records). Check the input FASTA, and see /path/to/output/logs/filter_contigs_S1.log.

docs.title: Without the screen (default)
docs.text:
By default your FASTA gets no contamination or mitochondrion screen, and the dry run says so in a NOTE:

[FunFlux] NOTE: contigs mode without parameters.contigs.screen: your FASTA gets no contamination or mitochondrion screen. If its headers are SPAdes-style (>NODE_<n>_length_<L>_cov_<C>), rule filter_contigs drops contigs under 500 bp or under 2x coverage; otherwise it only cuts each header at its first space or tab. A mitochondrial genome in your FASTA, if present, will be annotated as nuclear. Set parameters.contigs.screen: true to find and split it off (needs directories.blast_db).

filter_contigs writes 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta directly, and QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS search and the annotation read that file. 02.assembly/{sample}/ then holds only contigs_final.fasta and eval/.

docs.title: With the screen
docs.text:
The screen changes what happens to a mitochondrial genome and to contaminants in your FASTA, and what the run costs:

Screen off (default) Screen on A mitochondrial genome in your FASTA goes through the nuclear gene predictor, although fungal mitochondria use a different genetic code (code 4 in most fungi, code 3 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and related yeasts) confirmed by BLAST and, with the default separate_confirmed, split off into contigs_mitochondrial.fasta Contaminants not looked for every contig gets a keep or remove decision; contigs are removed only when parameters.decontamination.mode is not off Jobs added per sample none 8 Time added none nearly all of it BLAST, which took 40 to 51 minutes on 24 threads for the 42.6 Mb genome of the validation runs; the self-mapping takes seconds directories.blast_db not needed required

An assembly made elsewhere usually still contains the mitochondrial genome

The screen, with the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, is what keeps the mitochondrial genome out of the nuclear annotation. The cost is the BLAST search, under an hour for a genome of about 40 Mb on 24 threads.

parameters.contigs.screen: true runs the screen of the read-based modes on the supplied FASTA. filter_contigs then writes contigs_filt.fasta instead of contigs_final.fasta, and eight jobs per sample are added:

Rule Does map_contigs maps the contigs to themselves with minimap2, because BlobTools needs a BAM file blast_contigs megablast against NCBI core_nt, up to 50 subjects and 5 alignments per subject blob_json, blob_table BlobTools: one taxon per contig from the BLAST hits screen_mitochondria a contig is confirmed mitochondrial when a BLAST hit to a mitochondrial genome in core_nt covers at least parameters.mitochondria.min_direct_blast_qcov percent of it (35); BLAST is the only evidence in this mode select_contigs applies parameters.decontamination (default off: every contig kept) and writes a decision for every contig; with the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, confirmed mitochondrial contigs are always kept finalize_assembly copies contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta to contigs_all.fasta separate_mitochondria splits contigs_all.fasta into contigs_final.fasta (nuclear) and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta

In this mode BLAST therefore decides both the genus of each contig and whether it is mitochondrial.

The screen needs directories.blast_db, one folder that holds the core_nt database, the BLAST taxonomy files taxdb.btd and taxdb.bti, and the NCBI taxonomy files nodes.dmp and names.dmp. If nodes.dmp or names.dmp is missing, the dry run already fails with Snakemake's MissingInputException in rule blob_json. See Reference databases.

The BlobTools coverage means nothing in this mode

Without reads, every contig maps once, to itself. BlobTools still reports a coverage, but it only reflects contig length, not read depth. Only the BLAST taxonomy carries information here, and the contig selector reads only that.

The alignments and the BlobTools database are temporary. The screen is explained in more detail on Decontamination, Mitochondria and BLAST hit depth.

docs.title: Short contigs and funannotate clean
docs.text:
On a FASTA without SPAdes headers filter_contigs removes nothing, so contigs_final.fasta can hold contigs shorter than 500 bp. The later steps treat them differently:

Step Contigs shorter than 500 bp Contig names BUSCO, the ITS search read the original names QUAST read, but left out of the main statistics (QUAST's default --min-contig 500) the original names Annotation dropped by funannotate clean, the first annotation step scaffold_1, scaffold_2, ..., given by funannotate sort

The annotated_as column of the contig summary links each original name to the name the annotation uses, as described on Contig summary.

funannotate clean drops three kinds of contig:

  • contigs shorter than 500 bp (it keeps 500 bp and longer),
  • contigs with characters that are not nucleotide codes, or with fewer than four different characters,
  • contigs shorter than the N50 that align to a contig of at least N50 length, or to a contig shorter than themselves, with more than 95 % identity over more than 95 % of their own length.

Duplicates of the last kind are typical of haplotigs (the second copy of a heterozygous region) in a provider's assembly. Of two such copies below the N50, the longer one is dropped.

The names of the dropped contigs go to 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_removed_by_clean.txt, and an empty file means nothing was dropped. funannotate sort then orders the remaining contigs longest first and renames them scaffold_1, scaffold_2, ... in contigs_sort.fasta, the genome the annotation refers to. The details of funannotate clean are on Repeat masking.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
What 02.assembly/{sample}/ holds depends on the screen, and an empty cell marks a file or folder that is not written:

Path under 02.assembly/{sample}/ Screen off Screen on contigs_filt.fasta the filtered input; the draft the screen examines contaminants/ blastout, bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt, contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, {sample}_composition.txt, contigs.list, contigs_decontam.fasta mitochondria/ mitochondrial_screen.tsv, confirmed_mitochondrial.ids contigs_all.fasta the screened genome, mitochondrion included contigs_final.fasta the filtered input the nuclear genome contigs_mitochondrial.fasta confirmed mitochondrial contigs; empty file when none eval/quast/, eval/busco/ yes yes eval/telomere_candidates.tsv, eval/telomere_unit.txt, eval/telomere_ends.tsv yes yes eval/contig_summary.tsv, eval/contig_summary_mqc.tsv yes; the depth and screen columns are NA yes; the depth columns are NA (the self-mapping gives no read depth), the screen columns are filled

01.reads/ is not created, and 03.taxonomy to 06.report are the same in every mode, as listed on Output files.

With the AMR screen on and parameters.contigs.screen: false, both ChroQueTas runs, the nuclear and the mitochondrial one, read contigs_final.fasta. A mitochondrial genome in your FASTA then stays among the contigs of that file, and the mitochondrial run looks for cytochrome b there (Two runs).

docs.title: Hybrid
docs.text:
Use mode: hybrid when Illumina paired-end reads and long reads, ONT or PacBio HiFi, are available for the same isolate. FunFlux assembles the Illumina reads into a guide assembly, screens it, and keeps the Illumina pairs that map back to it. It then assembles the long reads and corrects the long-read assembly with those pairs. This requires more computation than either single-technology mode.

The two read types provide complementary evidence: long reads span repeats, while accurate short reads correct residual base errors. The delivered genome is the corrected long-read assembly. The guide assembly is not delivered and serves only to tell the isolate's Illumina reads from those of a contaminant.

Terms used on this page

ONT Oxford Nanopore Technologies, a long-read sequencing platform HiFi PacBio's accurate long reads, each the consensus of several passes over one molecule (CCS) guide assembly the SPAdes assembly of the Illumina reads; it is screened, and only the pairs that map to it go on properly paired both reads of a pair map to the same contig, in the expected orientation and distance k-mer a short sequence of fixed length; Filtlong compares long reads with the Illumina reads through their k-mers

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Folders input.illumina_dir and input.longread_dir; they may be the same folder Illumina reads {sample}_R1.<ext> and {sample}_R2.<ext> Long reads {sample}_ont.<ext> or {sample}_pacbio.<ext>, one technology per sample <ext> fastq, fq, fastq.gz or fq.gz; one extension for all Illumina files and one for all long-read files

Every sample needs both kinds of reads. A sample found on one side only stops the run before any job starts, and the message lists the missing side:

[FunFlux] hybrid mode needs Illumina and long reads for every sample.
  No _ont or _pacbio file for: SAM3

Illumina pairs with PacBio HiFi reads are allowed. As in Long reads, _pacbio files must hold HiFi (CCS) reads.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    IR([Illumina R1 and R2]) --> TR[PhiX removal, fastp]
    TR --> GA[SPAdes guide assembly<br/>at least 500 bp and 2x]
    GA --> GS[guide screen<br/>BLAST, BlobTools, mitochondrion]
    GS --> SEL[bowtie2: pairs properly paired<br/>on the screened guide]
    TR --> SEL
    SEL --> PAIRS([selected pairs])
    LR([ONT or PacBio HiFi reads]) --> FL[Filtlong]
    PAIRS -.->|"ONT reads, only with short_read_guidance: true"| FL
    FL --> ASM[hifiasm or Flye]
    ASM --> LS[screen of assembly.fasta<br/>BLAST, BlobTools, mitochondrion with assembler evidence]
    LS --> MD[Medaka, ONT samples]
    MD --> PP[Polypolish]
    LS -->|PacBio HiFi, or Medaka off| PP
    PAIRS --> PP
    PP --> OUT([contigs_all.fasta, then contigs_final.fasta<br/>and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta])

The Illumina half builds and screens a guide assembly and selects reads from it. The long-read half filters, assembles and screens the long reads and, for ONT samples, polishes the assembly with Medaka. Polypolish then corrects the long-read assembly with the selected Illumina pairs.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Step Rule (as named in the console and in logs/) Tool Writes PhiX removal, trimming download_phix, build_phix, map_phix, trim_adapters bowtie2 2.5.4, fastp 1.0.1 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/ Guide assembly and filter illumina_assembly, filter_contigs SPAdes 4.2.0, awk guide/spades/, guide/contigs_filt.fasta Guide screen index_guide_contigs, map_guide_contigs, map_guide_evaluation, blast_guide_contigs, blob_guide_json, blob_guide_table, screen_guide_mitochondria, select_guide_contigs bowtie2 2.5.4, samtools 1.21, Qualimap 2.3, BLAST+ 2.16.0, BlobTools 1.1.1 guide/contaminants/, guide/mitochondria/, guide/eval/qualimap/ Read selection index_selected_contigs, map_sel_contigs bowtie2 2.5.4, samtools 1.21 01.reads/{sample}/selected/ Long-read filter filter_long_reads Filtlong 0.3.1 01.reads/{sample}/long/{sample}_filtered.fastq Long-read QC raw_long_read_qc, filtered_long_read_qc NanoPlot 1.46.2 01.reads/{sample}/long/raw_qc/, filtered_qc/ Model check (ONT with Medaka) check_medaka_model Medaka 2.2.2 {sample}_medaka_model.txt Long-read assembly long_read_assembly hifiasm 0.25.0 or Flye 2.9.6 hifiasm/ or flye/, assembly.fasta, assembly_provenance.tsv Assembler evidence assembly_evidence FunFlux script, Python 3.12 assembly_evidence.tsv Screen map_contigs, map_evaluation, blast_contigs, blob_json, blob_table, screen_mitochondria, select_contigs minimap2 2.30, Qualimap 2.3, BLAST+ 2.16.0, BlobTools 1.1.1 contaminants/, mitochondria/, eval/qualimap/ Long-read polishing (ONT with Medaka) long_read_consensus Medaka 2.2.2 medaka/consensus.fasta Short-read polishing short_read_correction Polypolish 0.6.1, bwa 0.7.19 polypolish/polished.fasta Genome files finalize_assembly, separate_mitochondria contigs_all.fasta, contigs_final.fasta, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta

Paths without a stage prefix are under 02.assembly/{sample}/. One sample plans 58 jobs, 60 for an ONT sample with Medaka, and the resistance-mutation screen adds 2 (Dry run). The threads of each step are listed on CPU cores and threads.

docs.title: The Illumina guide assembly
docs.text:
PhiX removal, fastp, SPAdes and the filter (at least 500 bp, at least 2x SPAdes coverage) run as in illumina mode. The reads and the fastp reports go to 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/, the SPAdes output and contigs_filt.fasta to 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/.

The guide is screened like an Illumina assembly:

  • the trimmed pairs are mapped to it with bowtie2, for the BlobTools coverage and for Qualimap (guide/eval/qualimap/); the BAM, guide/contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, is kept;
  • BLAST and BlobTools assign a taxon to each contig;
  • the mitochondrion screen confirms mitochondrial contigs from BLAST alone;
  • the contig selector applies parameters.decontamination and writes guide/contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta.

With the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, confirmed mitochondrial contigs are kept whatever the genus filter says. With a genus filter on, the Illumina reads of the mitochondrion therefore stay in the read selection, and so in Polypolish and, when it is on, in the Filtlong guidance.

The guide is not delivered as a genome. QUAST reports it next to the final genome, under the label {sample}_guide.

docs.title: Read selection
docs.text:
The trimmed pairs are mapped to the screened guide with bowtie2 --no-unal, and the properly paired reads are kept (samtools fastq -f 0x2). The selected pairs, 01.reads/{sample}/selected/{sample}_selected_R1.fastq and _R2.fastq, are kept after the run. Polypolish uses them, and so does Filtlong for ONT samples when the guidance is on.

parameters.decontamination.mode The selected pairs are those properly paired on off (default) every guide contig that passed the 500 bp / 2x filter a genus filter the guide contigs the filter kept; pairs on removed contigs drop out

With the default off, the selection drops only the pairs that are not properly paired on the filtered guide, among them the pairs of contigs under 500 bp or 2x coverage.

docs.title: Long-read filter
docs.text:
With the defaults, filter_long_reads gives every sample the plain filter of longread mode:

filtlong --min_length 1000 --keep_percent 90 --length_weight 10 [--target_bases <size>] <raw long reads>

With short_read_guidance: true, the ONT samples are also scored against the selected Illumina pairs:

filtlong -1 <selected R1> -2 <selected R2> --trim --split 1000 \
    --min_length 1000 --keep_percent 90 --length_weight 10 [--target_bases <size>] <raw ONT reads>

With -1 and -2, "read quality will be determined using these instead of from the Phred scores" (Filtlong 0.3.1 help): a stretch of a long read that has no k-mer match in the Illumina pairs scores low. --trim removes such bases from the read ends, and --split 1000 cuts a read wherever 1,000 or more consecutive bases have no match.

short_read_guidance filtlong_split ONT reads PacBio HiFi reads false (default) not used; a NOTE says so if it holds a number other than 1000 plain filter plain filter true 1000 (default) -1 -2 --trim --split 1000 plain filter true null -1 -2: scored, never cut plain filter

The plain filter is the one of longread mode: --min_length, --keep_percent, --length_weight and, if set, --target_bases. PacBio HiFi reads are never guided: they are already accurate, and cutting them where the Illumina reads leave a gap would discard the long, accurate reads that HiFi sequencing is used for. With Flye and very deep ONT reads, cap the reads with filtlong.target_bases (Flye).

Why the guidance is off by default

The Filtlong README: "I recommend against using short reads as an external reference unless you are very confident in the quality of your short-read set." Long reads that span regions the Illumina reads cover poorly, typically repeats, can be scored low and, with --split, cut there. In BacFlux's tests on five bacterial genomes this broke assemblies apart, and on B. cinerea B05.10 it gained nothing measurable: Filtlong guidance in hybrid mode.

The dry run prints the decision for each sample. With the guidance on, it reads:

[FunFlux] SAM1: ont reads -> Filtlong guided by the Illumina reads, hifiasm --ont, minimap2 map-ont, Medaka.
[FunFlux] SAM2: pacbio reads -> Filtlong not guided, hifiasm, minimap2 map-hifi, no Medaka.

docs.title: Long-read assembly, screen and Medaka
docs.text:
These steps are those of Long reads, with the settings of parameters.hybrid: NanoPlot on the raw and the filtered reads, the Medaka model check on the raw ONT reads, hifiasm (default) or Flye, the minimap2 coverage track and Qualimap, the screen of assembly.fasta with the assembler's evidence for the mitochondrion, and Medaka on contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta for ONT samples.

Medaka runs as in longread mode. parameters.hybrid.medaka_model takes the same values: auto (the default), a model name, or false to switch Medaka off. The model is checked on the raw ONT reads before the assembler starts, and PacBio HiFi samples are never polished with Medaka. See Medaka model, checked before assembly for how the model is chosen, and Coverage track, screen and polishing for the polishing step itself.

The guide and the long-read assembly are screened independently, with the same parameters.decontamination and parameters.mitochondria settings:

Guide screen Long-read screen Draft examined guide/contigs_filt.fasta assembly.fasta Decides which Illumina pairs are used which contigs are delivered Reads mapped for the BlobTools coverage and Qualimap trimmed Illumina pairs, bowtie2 filtered long reads, minimap2 Evidence for the mitochondrion BLAST only BLAST plus the assembler's evidence Qualimap rule and folder map_guide_evaluation, guide/eval/qualimap/ map_evaluation, eval/qualimap/ MultiQC row of the Qualimap report mapping Illumina QC | {sample} mapping QC | {sample}

The guide screen chooses the Illumina reads and the long-read screen the genome, so Qualimap reports twice per sample.

A mitochondrial genome joined to itself is not trimmed

The long-read assembler can join two copies of the mitochondrial genome end to end into one contig. FunFlux does not trim such a contig. It flags it in mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv (concatemer_flag Y), except when the assembler recorded the contig as circular, so check length_ratio as well: see Mitochondria.

docs.title: Polypolish
docs.text:
short_read_correction corrects the long-read assembly with the selected pairs. The draft is the Medaka consensus for ONT samples with Medaka, otherwise contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta. Polypolish runs for every sample.

cp <draft> polypolish/draft.fasta
bwa index polypolish/draft.fasta
bwa mem -t <threads> -a polypolish/draft.fasta <selected R1> > polypolish/align_1.sam
bwa mem -t <threads> -a polypolish/draft.fasta <selected R2> > polypolish/align_2.sam
polypolish filter --in1 align_1.sam --in2 align_2.sam --out1 filtered_align_1.sam --out2 filtered_align_2.sam
polypolish polish draft.fasta filtered_align_1.sam filtered_align_2.sam > polished_raw.fasta
awk <cut each header at its first blank> polished_raw.fasta | awk <one line per sequence> > polished.fasta

As the Polypolish documentation asks, the two read files are aligned separately, each read to all its possible locations (-a), so that repeats can be polished. polypolish filter then filters the alignments by insert size. Polypolish appends polypolish to every FASTA header, and FunFlux cuts the headers at the first space or tab, because the later steps identify a contig by the first word of its header. The result is polypolish/polished.fasta.

While the job runs, the two SAM files hold every alignment of every selected read as text, tens of GB each for a deep library. They are deleted with the other working files when the job ends. logs/short_read_correction_{sample}.log holds the messages of bwa and Polypolish, including how many alignments the filter kept and how many positions were changed.

contigs_all.fasta is then polished.fasta, and separate_mitochondria splits it into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta. One QUAST report holds the screened guide (guide/contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta, label {sample}_guide) and the final genome ({sample}).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
input:
  illumina_dir: /path/to/reads
  longread_dir: /path/to/reads       # may be the same folder
parameters:
  spades_kmers: "21,33,55,77,99,127" # guide assembly
  hybrid:
    assembler: hifiasm               # hifiasm | flye
    flye_input_mode: auto
    medaka_model: auto               # ONT samples: auto | a model name | false
    medaka_model_fallback_auto: false
    filtlong: {min_length: 1000, keep_percent: 90, length_weight: 10, target_bases: null}
    hifiasm: {genome_size: null, bloom_filter_bits: 0, purge_dups: auto, homozygous_coverage: auto, telomere_motif: null}
    short_read_guidance: false       # true: ONT reads scored against the selected Illumina pairs
    filtlong_split: 1000             # with guidance: --trim --split 1000; null: score, never cut

parameters.hybrid holds the keys of parameters.longread, explained on Long reads, plus short_read_guidance and filtlong_split; an unknown key in it stops the run. links.phix_link and directories.blast_db are required. Every key is listed on Configuration.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
<output_dir>/
├── 00.resources/phix/
├── 01.reads/{sample}/
│   ├── illumina/                         fastp HTML and JSON (kept); PhiX-free and trimmed reads (temporary)
│   ├── selected/                         {sample}_selected_R1.fastq, _R2.fastq (kept)
│   └── long/                             {sample}_filtered.fastq (kept), raw_qc/, filtered_qc/
└── 02.assembly/{sample}/
    ├── guide/                            spades/, contigs_filt.fasta, contaminants/ (BAM kept, indexes temporary), mitochondria/, eval/qualimap/
    ├── hifiasm/ or flye/                 the assembler's own files
    ├── assembly.fasta  assembly_evidence.tsv  assembly_provenance.tsv

In the MultiQC report a sample has the rows fastp read QC | {sample}, NanoPlot raw read QC | {sample}, NanoPlot filtered read QC | {sample}, mapping Illumina QC | {sample} (the guide), mapping QC | {sample} (the long-read draft), QUAST guide assembly QC | {sample}, QUAST assembly QC | {sample} and its BUSCO rows, and one row per contig of the long-read draft, {sample}: {contig}, in the contig summary table (Report). 03.taxonomy to 06.report are the same in every mode: see Output files.

docs.title: Tested so far
docs.text:
Reads Genome Assembler Details Illumina 79x plus ONT 136x Botrytis cinerea B05.10 hifiasm Validation on public genomes MGISEQ short reads 2 x 150 bp, 151x, plus PacBio HiFi 85x Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616 hifiasm PacBio HiFi reads

Both long-read technologies have run in this mode, each on one public genome and with hifiasm; hybrid with Flye has been checked in dry runs only. The short reads of GXU-8616 come from an MGISEQ-2000RS, a short-read sequencer from MGI Tech (DNBSEQ technology) that produces paired reads like Illumina's, here 2 x 150 bp. FunFlux ran them as Illumina pairs with the default settings, and the MultiQC row of the guide keeps its name, mapping Illumina QC.

docs.title: Illumina
docs.text:
Use mode: illumina for Illumina paired-end reads of a fungal isolate. FunFlux assembles the reads with SPAdes and runs the contamination and mitochondrion screen on the contigs before QC and annotation. This mode replaces FunFlux 1.x.

Terms used on this page

concordantly bowtie2's word for a pair whose reads align in the expected orientation and distance k-mer coverage the coverage in a SPAdes contig header, counted in k-mers of the largest k and so lower than the read depth the draft the assembly the screen examines, before the screen removes any contig: in this mode contigs_filt.fasta the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector contig selector rule select_contigs, the last step of the screen: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says genus filter the setting parameters.decontamination.mode: include or exclude, under which the contig selector keeps or removes contigs by the genus BlobTools gave them confirmed mitochondrial contig a contig the mitochondrion screen classes confirmed_mitochondrial; with the default separate_confirmed, it is kept whatever its genus and moved to contigs_mitochondrial.fasta nuclear genome the delivered genome without the confirmed mitochondrial contigs, contigs_final.fasta; it holds every contig when parameters.mitochondria.mode is off or report

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FunFlux finds the read pairs of a batch in one folder, by their file names:

Folder input.illumina_dir File names {sample}_R1.<ext> and {sample}_R2.<ext> <ext> fastq, fq, fastq.gz or fq.gz, the same for every sample of the batch

Samples are found from the R1 files, and a sample without its R2 file stops the run before any job starts:

[FunFlux] input.illumina_dir: sample 'S1' has an R1 file but no R2 mate: /path/to/reads/S1_R2.fastq.gz

Names as the sequencer writes them, such as S1_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz, are not found. Link such files under the expected names, in a folder of their own. For a sample sequenced on several lanes, join the files of the lanes first, R1 and R2 in the same order:

mkdir -p reads
ln -s /path/to/raw/S1_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz reads/S1_R1.fastq.gz     # one lane
ln -s /path/to/raw/S1_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz reads/S1_R2.fastq.gz
cat /path/to/raw/S2_*_R1_001.fastq.gz > reads/S2_R1.fastq.gz           # several lanes
cat /path/to/raw/S2_*_R2_001.fastq.gz > reads/S2_R2.fastq.gz

The rules for sample names are the same in every mode and are given under File names.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    IR([Illumina R1 and R2]) --> TR[PhiX removal, fastp]
    TR --> AS[SPAdes assembly]
    AS --> CF[contig filter<br/>at least 500 bp and 2x]
    CF --> SCR[screen of contigs_filt.fasta<br/>BLAST, BlobTools,<br/>mitochondrion by BLAST alone]
    TR --> COV[coverage track<br/>bowtie2: trimmed pairs<br/>on the filtered contigs]
    CF --> COV
    COV --> SCR
    SCR --> OUT([contigs_all.fasta, then contigs_final.fasta<br/>and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta])

After PhiX removal and fastp, SPAdes assembles the trimmed pairs, and the contig filter keeps the contigs of at least 500 bp and 2x. The screen checks these contigs with BLAST and BlobTools, which takes their coverage from the same pairs mapped back with bowtie2, and it confirms mitochondrial contigs from BLAST alone. With no polishing step in this mode, the screened contigs become contigs_all.fasta, which is then split into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
The reads lose PhiX and adapters, SPAdes assembles them, and the contigs are filtered and screened. The last step writes the nuclear genome, which QC, the ITS search and annotation read.

Step Rule (as named in the console and in logs/) Tool Writes PhiX reference download_phix, build_phix bowtie2 2.5.4 00.resources/phix/, once per output folder PhiX removal map_phix bowtie2 2.5.4 PhiX-free pairs (temporary) Trimming trim_adapters fastp 1.0.1 trimmed pairs (temporary), fastp HTML and JSON Assembly illumina_assembly SPAdes 4.2.0 spades/ Contig filter filter_contigs awk contigs_filt.fasta Coverage track index_contigs, map_contigs bowtie2 2.5.4, samtools 1.21 contaminants/{sample}_map.bam Mapping QC map_evaluation Qualimap 2.3 eval/qualimap/ Screen blast_contigs, blob_json, blob_table, screen_mitochondria, select_contigs BLAST+ 2.16.0, BlobTools 1.1.1 contaminants/, mitochondria/ Genome files finalize_assembly, separate_mitochondria contigs_all.fasta, contigs_final.fasta, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta

Paths without a stage prefix are under 02.assembly/{sample}/. One sample plans 43 jobs, 45 with the AMR screen on (Dry run). The threads of each step are listed on CPU cores and threads.

docs.title: PhiX removal
docs.text:
Illumina libraries are spiked with the genome of phage PhiX174, and three rules remove its reads:

  1. download_phix fetches the PhiX genome with curl from links.phix_link into 00.resources/phix/. The template points this key at NCBI assembly GCF_000819615.1.
  2. build_phix indexes it there. Both rules run once per output folder, and the genome and its index are kept.
  3. map_phix aligns every pair with bowtie2 --local, and the pairs that do not align concordantly to PhiX (--un-conc) go on to trimming.

The bowtie2 summary in logs/map_phix_{sample}.log gives the share of the library that was PhiX. links.phix_link is required in this mode, and an empty value stops the run before any job starts.

docs.title: Trimming
docs.text:
trim_adapters runs fastp, which finds the adapters itself, trims low-quality stretches from the start of a read and cuts the read at its first low-quality window. It keeps only reads of at least 75 bp.

Option Effect (fastp 1.0.1 help) --detect_adapter_for_pe adapter detection for paired-end data --cut_front sliding window from the 5' end; drops windows whose mean quality is below the threshold, stops at the first good one --cut_right sliding window from 5' to 3'; at the first window below the threshold, drops it and everything to its right --length_required 75 discards reads shorter than 75 bp (fastp default: 15)

The fastp HTML and JSON reports are kept in 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/ and appear in the MultiQC report. The trimmed reads are temporary and are deleted once SPAdes and the coverage mapping have read them.

docs.title: Assembly
docs.text:
illumina_assembly runs SPAdes once per sample into 02.assembly/{sample}/spades/, in isolate mode, on every thread and with resources.ram_gb as its memory limit:

Option Value --isolate SPAdes' mode for "high-coverage isolate and multi-cell data" (SPAdes help) -k parameters.spades_kmers, default 21,33,55,77,99,127, the list FunFlux 1.x hard-coded; or auto, SPAdes' own choice from the read length (21 to 77 for 150 bp reads) -t resources.threads -m resources.ram_gb (default 128): "RAM limit for SPAdes in Gb (terminates if exceeded)" (SPAdes help)

Of these options, only a changed k-mer list re-runs the assembly.

parameters.spades_kmers takes a string such as "21,33,55", a YAML list, or auto. Every value must be odd and below 128, and the list ascending, or the run stops before any job starts.

With thin coverage, try auto instead of the default k-mer list

On B. cinerea B05.10 (Illumina 79x, 150 bp reads), the default list gave 413 contigs and an N50 of 314 kb, and auto 592 contigs and an N50 of 217 kb. Both covered the same 98.8 % of the reference. With thin coverage, some 20-30x, the large k of the default may hold too few reads, so try auto there.

With several samples, snakemake --resources mem_gb=N starts only as many assemblies at once as fit into N GB, as described under CPU cores and threads.

spades/ holds the whole SPAdes working folder, the unfiltered contigs.fasta and the scaffolds included, but FunFlux reads the contigs and never the scaffolds.

docs.title: Contig filter
docs.text:
filter_contigs removes short and thinly covered contigs before the screen. It reads length and coverage from each SPAdes header, for example >NODE_12_length_45678_cov_23.4, and keeps contigs of at least 500 bp with a coverage of at least 2.0. Both cut-offs are fixed, not configuration keys. The header coverage is SPAdes' k-mer coverage for its largest k, which "is always lower than the read (per-base) coverage", as the SPAdes manual says.

The result, contigs_filt.fasta, is the draft the screen examines. logs/filter_contigs_{sample}.log records how many contigs were kept out of how many. When none is left, the run stops with [FunFlux] filter_contigs: no contig of <sample> is left ... instead of handing an empty draft to BLAST.

docs.title: Coverage track and mapping QC
docs.text:
One mapping serves both the screen and the mapping QC. The trimmed pairs are mapped back to contigs_filt.fasta with bowtie2, and the alignments, contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, are kept. BlobTools takes the read coverage of every contig from this BAM. Qualimap (map_evaluation) reads it for the mapping report in eval/qualimap/, with the share of mapped reads, the insert sizes and the depth per contig.

A Qualimap failure does not stop the run

When Qualimap fails, a [FunFlux] line in logs/map_evaluation_{sample}.log says so, and the run goes on. The MultiQC page then has no mapping table for the sample: see Assembly QC.

docs.title: Screen and genome files
docs.text:
The screen runs on contigs_filt.fasta, in four steps:

  1. blast_contigs runs megablast against NCBI core_nt (-evalue 1e-5) and saves up to 50 subjects and 5 alignments per subject, as set by parameters.blast_max_target_seqs and parameters.blast_max_hsps.
  2. screen_mitochondria decides from BLAST alone, because Illumina reads give no assembler evidence. A contig is confirmed mitochondrial when a hit to a mitochondrial genome covers at least parameters.mitochondria.min_direct_blast_qcov percent of it (default 35).
  3. blob_json and blob_table run BlobTools, which joins the BLAST hits, the coverage and the contigs and assigns a taxon to each contig.
  4. select_contigs, the contig selector, applies parameters.decontamination. Its default, off, keeps every contig and gives every contig a decision in contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv. With the default parameters.mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed, confirmed mitochondrial contigs are kept whatever the genus filter says.

contigs_all.fasta is then the screened assembly, as this mode has no polishing step. separate_mitochondria splits it into contigs_final.fasta, the nuclear genome, and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, an empty file when no contig was confirmed.

Decontamination and Mitochondria describe the screen in detail. BLAST hit depth explains why BLAST keeps 5 alignments per subject.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Of the keys below, input.illumina_dir and directories.blast_db have no default and must be set, while every other key here has one.

Key Default Effect input.illumina_dir none, required folder with the read pairs links.phix_link NCBI PhiX174 genome (GCF_000819615.1) PhiX reference; required parameters.spades_kmers "21,33,55,77,99,127" SPAdes -k resources.threads 24 SPAdes -t, bowtie2; upper limit for every other rule. Pass the same number to --cores resources.ram_gb 128 SPAdes -m; Qualimap Java heap min(ram_gb, 64) GB directories.blast_db none, required NCBI core_nt with its taxonomy files: Reference databases parameters.nt_version, blast_max_target_seqs, blast_max_hsps, decontamination.mode, mitochondria.mode core_nt, 50, 5, off, separate_confirmed the screen

Every key is listed on Configuration.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Up to 02.assembly, the output folder of this mode looks like this:

<output_dir>/
├── 00.resources/phix/                    PhiX genome and its bowtie2 index
├── 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/           fastp HTML and JSON (kept); PhiX-free and trimmed reads (temporary)
└── 02.assembly/{sample}/
    ├── spades/                           SPAdes output, including the unfiltered contigs.fasta
    ├── contigs_filt.fasta                after the 500 bp / 2x filter
    ├── contaminants/                     BAM, BLAST table, BlobTools table, decisions, contigs_decontam.fasta
    ├── mitochondria/                     mitochondrial_screen.tsv, confirmed_mitochondrial.ids
    ├── contigs_all.fasta                 screened assembly, mitochondrion included
    ├── contigs_final.fasta               nuclear genome: QUAST, BUSCO, ITS and annotation read this
    ├── contigs_mitochondrial.fasta       confirmed mitochondrial contigs
    └── eval/quast/  eval/busco/  eval/qualimap/  eval/telomere_*  eval/contig_summary*.tsv

In the MultiQC report a sample has the rows fastp read QC | {sample}, mapping QC | {sample}, QUAST assembly QC | {sample} and its BUSCO rows. It also has one row per contig, {sample}: {contig}, in the contig summary table (Report). 03.taxonomy to 06.report are the same in every mode: see Output files.

docs.title: Long reads (ONT and PacBio HiFi)
docs.text:
Use mode: longread for Oxford Nanopore (ONT) or PacBio HiFi reads. FunFlux assembles the reads with hifiasm (the default) or Flye, runs the contamination and mitochondrion screen on the assembly, and polishes ONT assemblies with Medaka. This mode replaces FunFluxL 0.1. Which assembler to choose is discussed under hifiasm or Flye.

Terms used on this page

HiFi PacBio's accurate long reads, each the consensus of several passes over one molecule (CCS) coverage track the filtered reads aligned back to assembly.fasta, kept as contaminants/{sample}_map.bam; BlobTools takes each contig's coverage from it and Qualimap its report assembler evidence what hifiasm or Flye report for each contig, above all read depth and circularity, written to assembly_evidence.tsv for the mitochondrion screen basecaller tag the basecall_model_version_id= field in ONT read headers, which names the basecaller model; with medaka_model: auto, Medaka reads it from the first 100 reads purge level how strongly hifiasm removes haplotigs from its primary contigs (-l, 0 to 3), set by hifiasm.purge_dups; auto passes nothing and keeps hifiasm's default rDNA array the tandem copies of the rDNA unit, SSU-ITS1-5.8S-ITS2-LSU; a contig with 3 or more units (by default) and fewer genes than units gets the verdict rDNA_array telomere array tandem copies of the telomere repeat unit at a contig end; by default 5 or more copies within 25,000 bp of the end make a telomere contig selector rule select_contigs, the last step of the screen: it keeps or removes each contig by genus, as parameters.decontamination says; the default, off, keeps every contig

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FunFlux finds the long reads of each sample by their file name, in one folder:

Folder input.longread_dir ONT reads {sample}_ont.<ext> PacBio HiFi (CCS) reads {sample}_pacbio.<ext> <ext> fastq, fq, fastq.gz or fq.gz, the same for every sample of the batch

FunFlux takes one file per sample. An ONT run usually delivers many files per barcode folder, so join them first. Gzip files can be joined with cat, for example cat fastq_pass/barcode01/*.fastq.gz > reads/SAM1_ont.fastq.gz.

One batch may mix ONT and PacBio HiFi samples. A sample with both an _ont and a _pacbio file stops the run before any job starts:

[FunFlux] sample 'SAM1' has both _ont and _pacbio files in /path/to/reads. Provide one long-read technology per sample.

PacBio reads must be HiFi, and nothing checks the read type

Every PacBio step assumes HiFi (CCS) reads, and no tool in the chain is set up for continuous long reads (CLR). Nothing checks the read type, so a _pacbio file of CLR reads is assembled as if it held HiFi reads. The dry run prints a NOTE naming the _pacbio samples.

docs.title: One technology per sample
docs.text:
The file-name suffix tells FunFlux the technology of each sample, in longread and in hybrid mode, and sets the following per sample. The assembler (parameters.<mode>.assembler) is one for the whole run, and everything else is the same for both technologies.

ONT (_ont) PacBio HiFi (_pacbio) hifiasm --ont no flag: hifiasm's HiFi mode Flye --nano-hq, or --nano-raw (see Flye) --pacbio-hifi minimap2 preset for the coverage track map-ont map-hifi Medaka yes, unless medaka_model: false never Filtlong guided by the Illumina pairs (hybrid only) only with short_read_guidance: true never

PacBio HiFi samples therefore get neither Medaka nor the Filtlong guidance. In hybrid mode, Polypolish corrects the assemblies of both technologies with the Illumina pairs, as described on Hybrid.

The dry run prints the decision for each sample. In hybrid mode the line also says Filtlong guided by the Illumina reads or Filtlong not guided. For a longread batch with one sample of each technology, the output reads:

Long-read assembler: hifiasm.
Sample SAM1 will be processed.
Sample SAM2 will be processed.
[FunFlux] SAM1: ont reads -> hifiasm --ont, minimap2 map-ont, Medaka.
[FunFlux] SAM2: pacbio reads -> hifiasm, minimap2 map-hifi, no Medaka.
[FunFlux] NOTE: samples with a _pacbio file are assumed to hold PacBio HiFi (CCS) reads: SAM2. Continuous long reads (CLR) are not supported by this workflow.
Medaka model will be worked out from the FASTQ headers (checked before assembly).

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    LR([ONT or PacBio HiFi reads]) --> FL[Filtlong]
    LR -->|ONT reads, Medaka on| MC[Medaka model check<br/>check_medaka_model]
    FL --> ASM[hifiasm or Flye]
    MC --> ASM
    ASM --> LS[screen of assembly.fasta<br/>BLAST, BlobTools, mitochondrion with assembler evidence]
    LS -->|PacBio HiFi, or Medaka off| OUT([contigs_all.fasta, then contigs_final.fasta<br/>and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta])
    LS --> MD[Medaka, ONT samples]
    MC -->|checked model| MD
    MD --> OUT

Filtlong filters the reads, hifiasm or Flye assembles them, and the screen examines assembly.fasta with BLAST, BlobTools and, for the mitochondrion, the assembler's evidence. For ONT samples, unless Medaka is off, check_medaka_model settles the model on the raw reads before the assembler starts, and Medaka polishes the screened assembly with that model. The polished assembly, or the screened one for PacBio HiFi samples or with Medaka off, becomes contigs_all.fasta, which is split into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
FunFlux filters the reads and reports on them, and checks the Medaka model of ONT samples before the assembler starts. It then screens the assembly and polishes ONT assemblies with Medaka before it writes the genome files.

Step Rule (as named in the console and in logs/) Tool Writes Read filter filter_long_reads Filtlong 0.3.1 01.reads/{sample}/long/{sample}_filtered.fastq Read QC raw_long_read_qc, filtered_long_read_qc NanoPlot 1.46.2 01.reads/{sample}/long/raw_qc/, filtered_qc/ Model check (ONT with Medaka) check_medaka_model Medaka 2.2.2 {sample}_medaka_model.txt Assembly long_read_assembly hifiasm 0.25.0 or Flye 2.9.6 hifiasm/ or flye/, assembly.fasta, assembly_provenance.tsv Assembler evidence assembly_evidence FunFlux script, Python 3.12 assembly_evidence.tsv Coverage track map_contigs minimap2 2.30, samtools 1.21 contaminants/{sample}_map.bam Mapping QC map_evaluation Qualimap 2.3 eval/qualimap/ Screen blast_contigs, blob_json, blob_table, screen_mitochondria, select_contigs BLAST+ 2.16.0, BlobTools 1.1.1 contaminants/, mitochondria/ Polishing (ONT with Medaka) long_read_consensus Medaka 2.2.2 medaka/consensus.fasta Genome files finalize_assembly, separate_mitochondria contigs_all.fasta, contigs_final.fasta, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta

Paths without a stage prefix are under 02.assembly/{sample}/. One sample plans 41 jobs, 43 for an ONT sample with Medaka, and the AMR screen adds 2 (Dry run). The threads of each step are listed on CPU cores and threads.

docs.title: Read filter
docs.text:
filter_long_reads runs Filtlong on the raw reads, without a reference. With the defaults, Filtlong drops reads under 1,000 bp and keeps the best reads up to 90 % of the bases, favouring long reads. The total is not capped unless target_bases is set.

Option Key in parameters.longread.filtlong Default Effect --min_length min_length 1000 discards reads shorter than this --keep_percent keep_percent 90 keeps the best reads up to this percentage of the bases --length_weight length_weight 10 weight of read length in Filtlong's score (Filtlong default: 1); a higher value favours longer reads --target_bases target_bases empty empty: no cap. A size such as 2.4g keeps the best reads up to that many bases, for a very deep run
  • Without a reference, Filtlong scores read quality from the Phred scores. --trim and --split need a reference and are not used in this mode. hybrid mode can score ONT reads against Illumina pairs instead, when you switch that on.
  • The defaults are sized for ONT reads. For PacBio HiFi reads they are provisional, because they have run on one public dataset only (PacBio HiFi reads).
  • The filtered reads are kept, uncompressed. Filtlong's report, which counts the reads and bases in and the reads and bases kept, is logs/filter_long_reads_{sample}.log.

docs.title: Read QC
docs.text: NanoPlot reports on the raw reads (raw_qc/) and on the filtered reads (filtered_qc/), with read lengths on a log scale, so that the two reports show what Filtlong removed. A NanoPlot failure leaves a [FunFlux] line in the log and does not stop the run. The MultiQC page then has no read-QC row for the sample.

docs.title: Medaka model, checked before assembly
docs.text:
Medaka polishes after the assembly and the screen, and its model has to match the basecaller that produced the reads. check_medaka_model settles the model on the raw ONT reads before the assembler starts, so a wrong model stops the run within seconds instead of hours later. PacBio HiFi samples are not checked.

Keep auto when the reads still carry their basecaller tag, name the model when they do not, and set false to skip Medaka.

parameters.longread.medaka_model Effect auto (default; also empty or an unquoted null, true, yes, on, 1) model worked out from the basecaller tag in the FASTQ headers a model name, e.g. r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v4.3.0 that model, after checking that this Medaka version has it false (also 0, no, off, none, and null in quotes) no Medaka; contigs_all.fasta is the screened assembly
  • auto asks Medaka for its generic consensus model for the basecaller named in the reads. It needs exactly one basecaller tag (basecall_model_version_id=) among the first 100 reads. Reads from public archives, or reads pooled from several basecalling runs, often lack tags or mix them, so name the model for those. zcat reads.fastq.gz | head -n 1 shows what a file carries.
  • Medaka downloads the weights of a model the first time it uses that model, so the first run needs network access. The download happens during the check, for a named model and with auto, on the computer that runs Snakemake, and polishing then needs no network. Medaka 2.2.2 ships the weights of four models, which need no download.
  • A named model that this Medaka version does not have stops the run with a table of the closest models, printed to the console as well as to logs/check_medaka_model_{sample}.log. medaka_model_fallback_auto: true makes it fall back to auto instead, with a warning.

Changing medaka_model re-runs the assembly of every ONT sample

The resolved model is written to 02.assembly/{sample}/{sample}_medaka_model.txt, and the assembler waits for this file. A changed medaka_model therefore re-runs the assembly of every ONT sample.

How the model is checked or worked out, and what can fail, is described on The Medaka model.

docs.title: Assembly
docs.text:
One assembler serves the whole run, parameters.longread.assembler: hifiasm (the default) or flye. Either way, the same three files end up next to the assembler's own folder, so the screen reads the same draft and the same evidence table whichever assembler ran:

File Content Written by assembly.fasta the assembly the screen examines long_read_assembly assembly_evidence.tsv per contig: contig, source, circular, coverage, repeat, alt_group; read by the mitochondrion screen assembly_evidence, a short step right after the assembly, from the assembler's own per-contig file assembly_provenance.tsv assembler, version, read type, input file and command line long_read_assembly

If assembly_evidence fails, the run stops there, but the assembly stays on disk. The next run makes the table again without assembling again.

docs.title: hifiasm
docs.text:
With hifiasm, long_read_assembly runs this command. The options in brackets come from the keys in the table that follows it, and --ont is added for ONT reads.

hifiasm -i --primary -f <bloom_filter_bits> [--hg-size ...] [-l ...] [--hom-cov ...] [--telo-m ...] [--ont] \
    -t <resources.threads> -o hifiasm/hifiasm <filtered reads>

assembly.fasta holds the primary contigs of hifiasm/hifiasm.p_ctg.gfa, and the rule stops when the graph holds no contig. The coverage in the evidence table is the rd:i read depth of each contig, and a contig whose name ends in c is recorded as circular. -i makes hifiasm ignore read corrections and overlaps saved by an earlier run.

Key in parameters.longread.hifiasm Default hifiasm option (hifiasm 0.25.0 help) genome_size empty --hg-size: estimated haploid genome size, used to infer read coverage, e.g. 40m. Empty: hifiasm infers it bloom_filter_bits 0 -f: bits of the bloom filter; 0 disables it (hifiasm default: 37) purge_dups auto -l: purge level, 0 none, 1 light, 2 or 3 aggressive. auto passes nothing homozygous_coverage auto --hom-cov: read depth of the homozygous peak. auto passes nothing telomere_motif empty --telo-m: "telomere motif at 5'-end; CCCTAA for human"

With the defaults, the only assembly options hifiasm gets are -i --primary -f 0, plus --ont for ONT reads. It infers the read coverage and the homozygous coverage itself, but not the purge level. With no -l, hifiasm uses its own default, -l 3 outside trio mode (hifiasm's mode for parental reads, which FunFlux does not use). No telomere motif is passed, because parameters.longread.hifiasm.telomere_motif is empty.

docs.title: Flye
docs.text:
With Flye, long_read_assembly runs:

flye <read flag> <filtered reads> --out-dir flye/ --threads <resources.threads> --iterations 5

--iterations 5 runs five rounds of Flye's own polishing (the Flye default is 1). Flye's assembly.fasta is copied from flye/ up one level. The evidence table comes from flye/assembly_info.txt, which gives the mean read depth, the circularity, and the repeat and alternative-group flags.

parameters.longread.flye_input_mode sets the ONT flag. It takes nano-hq, nano-raw or auto (the default), while the _pacbio suffix alone decides --pacbio-hifi.

Read flag Used for Flye 2.9.6 help --pacbio-hifi every PacBio sample PacBio HiFi reads (<1% error) --nano-hq ONT samples with flye_input_mode: nano-hq, or with auto (default) unless medaka_model names a model with fast in its name ONT R10 reads, aka Q20 (<3% error) --nano-raw ONT samples with flye_input_mode: nano-raw, or with auto when medaka_model names a model with fast in its name ONT reads with older chemistries, pre R9 Guppy5 (10-20% error)

With flye_input_mode: auto, naming a fast Medaka model also changes Flye's read mode

For ONT reads, flye_input_mode: auto follows the Medaka model. Naming a fast Medaka model then changes the assembler's read mode as well as the polisher. Set flye_input_mode explicitly to keep the two apart.

  • flye_input_mode: pacbio-hifi stops the run with a message, because the _pacbio suffix chooses --pacbio-hifi.
  • With hifiasm, flye_input_mode is ignored, and a NOTE says so when it is set to anything but auto.
  • Flye does not repeat its assembly byte for byte from run to run.
  • Very deep ONT data can leave Flye with no assembly. In BacFlux's runs on 300x to 1,000x reads of five bacteria, Flye reported Assembled 0 disjointigs, while the 136x reads of B05.10 assembled normally. For much deeper reads, cap them with filtlong.target_bases at about 100 times the genome size, for example 4g for a 40 Mb genome.

docs.title: hifiasm or Flye
docs.text:
Both assemblers have run on the same reads of two public genomes, with the same settings apart from the assembler and the number of cores. The runs are described on Validation on public genomes.

Reads Assembler Contigs Of them, rDNA pieces N50 (Mb) Contigs with telomeres at both ends Botrytis cinerea B05.10, ONT 136x hifiasm 32 13 2.58 15 Flye 25 0 2.58 6 Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616, PacBio HiFi 85x hifiasm 18 7 4.79 7 Flye 12 0 4.79 6

In these runs the N50 was the same with both assemblers, and hifiasm gave more contigs with telomeres at both ends, most clearly on the ONT reads (15 against 6).

  • Contigs are those of contigs_final.fasta, the nuclear genome, as QUAST counts them.
  • rDNA pieces are the contigs to which the contig summary gives the verdict rDNA_array. hifiasm's extra contigs are such pieces of the rDNA array, which Flye did not produce. Without them, hifiasm has fewer contigs than Flye: 19 against 25 on B05.10 and 11 against 12 on GXU-8616.
  • Telomeres come from the contig summary too: the last column counts the contigs with a telomere array at both ends. On the ONT reads, 11 Flye contigs carry a telomere array at one end only, against 4 with hifiasm.
  • Each assembler ran once on each genome. Whether a contig is a whole chromosome is checked against the reference on the validation page.

docs.title: Coverage track, screen and polishing
docs.text:
The filtered reads are mapped to assembly.fasta with minimap2 -ax map-ont or map-hifi. The alignments, contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, are kept. BlobTools reads them for the read coverage of each contig, and Qualimap (map_evaluation) reports on them in eval/qualimap/. A Qualimap failure does not stop the run (Assembly QC).

The screen runs on assembly.fasta with BLAST (50 subjects and 5 alignments per subject), BlobTools and the contig selector. The mitochondrion screen also reads assembly_evidence.tsv, and decides as follows whether a contig is confirmed:

A BLAST hit to a mitochondrial genome covers Plus, from the assembler Contig at least very_strong_qcov percent of it (70) nothing needed confirmed at least min_direct_blast_qcov percent of it (35) read depth at least min_assembler_coverage_ratio (3.0) times the median depth of the contigs confirmed at least min_direct_blast_qcov percent of it (35) a circle that is not a repeat or an alternative copy of another contig confirmed no hit circularity or depth never confirmed

A BLAST hit is always needed, and the assembler's evidence lets a partial hit count. See Mitochondria.

long_read_consensus polishes contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta, the contigs the contig selector kept, with the filtered reads:

medaka_consensus -i <filtered reads> -d contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta -x -t <up to 12> -m <model> -o medaka/
  • <model> is the line in {sample}_medaka_model.txt: the checked name, or the path of the model file auto found.
  • A Medaka failure stops the run with a [FunFlux] long_read_consensus: line that names the model and the log. Unlike the QC steps, polishing is never skipped on failure, because its output is the genome.
  • Medaka is distributed under the Oxford Nanopore Technologies Public License 1.0, which grants use for research purposes. See Licensing.

contigs_all.fasta is then the Medaka consensus for ONT samples with Medaka, and contigs_decontam.fasta for PacBio HiFi samples or with Medaka off. logs/finalize_assembly_{sample}.log names the file that was copied. separate_mitochondria splits contigs_all.fasta into contigs_final.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, and QUAST reports on contigs_final.fasta.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
parameters.longread is read only in longread mode, and hybrid mode reads the same keys from parameters.hybrid. An unknown key in the block stops the run. So do long_read_assembler, flye_input_mode, medaka_model, filtlong and hifiasm when they sit at the top of parameters, where FunFluxL kept its long-read settings, and the message then names their new place.

parameters:
  longread:
    assembler: hifiasm               # hifiasm | flye
    flye_input_mode: auto            # Flye, ONT samples: auto | nano-hq | nano-raw
    medaka_model: auto               # ONT samples: auto | a model name | false
    medaka_model_fallback_auto: false
    filtlong:
      min_length: 1000
      keep_percent: 90
      length_weight: 10
      target_bases:                  # empty: no cap
    hifiasm:
      genome_size:
      bloom_filter_bits: 0
      purge_dups: auto
      homozygous_coverage: auto
      telomere_motif:

directories.blast_db is required. Every key is listed on Configuration.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Each sample has its reads in 01.reads and its assembly in 02.assembly:

<output_dir>/
├── 01.reads/{sample}/long/
│   ├── {sample}_filtered.fastq           Filtlong output (kept, uncompressed)
│   └── raw_qc/  filtered_qc/             NanoPlot
└── 02.assembly/{sample}/
    ├── hifiasm/ or flye/                 the assembler's own files
    ├── assembly.fasta  assembly_evidence.tsv  assembly_provenance.tsv
    ├── {sample}_medaka_model.txt         ONT samples with Medaka
    ├── contaminants/                     BAM, BLAST table, BlobTools table, decisions, contigs_decontam.fasta
    ├── mitochondria/                     mitochondrial_screen.tsv, confirmed_mitochondrial.ids
    ├── medaka/consensus.fasta            ONT samples with Medaka
    ├── contigs_all.fasta  contigs_final.fasta  contigs_mitochondrial.fasta
    └── eval/quast/  eval/busco/  eval/qualimap/  eval/telomere_*  eval/contig_summary*.tsv

In the MultiQC report a sample has the rows NanoPlot raw read QC | {sample}, NanoPlot filtered read QC | {sample}, mapping QC | {sample}, QUAST assembly QC | {sample} and its BUSCO rows, and one row per contig, {sample}: {contig}, in the contig summary table (Report). 03.taxonomy to 06.report are the same in every mode, as described on Output files.

docs.title: Tested so far
docs.text:
Each read type has run on one public genome, and each assembler at least once on each:

Reads Genome Assemblers that have run Details ONT, 136x and a 42x subsample Botrytis cinerea B05.10 hifiasm (both depths), Flye (136x) Validation on public genomes PacBio HiFi, 85x Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616 hifiasm, Flye PacBio HiFi reads

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
One YAML file describes a FunFlux run: its mode, its input and output folders, the databases, the resources and the analysis settings. This page lists every key of that file, the modes that read it, its default and its allowed values. The template is config/config.yaml. Copy it, fill in the copy and pass it with --configfile:

cp config/config.yaml config/config_custom.yaml
snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

Without --configfile, the run stops at once with [FunFlux] No configuration supplied. Git ignores config/config_custom.yaml, so your filled-in copy is never committed.

Terms used on this page

YAML the text format of the configuration file, with keys indented under their block; unquoted yes, on, true read as true and no, off, false as false NOTE a line starting [FunFlux] NOTE that reports something to check without stopping the run; read them after every dry run launch folder the folder Snakemake is started from, normally the FunFlux repository; relative paths are read from it, and .snakemake/ is created there the screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen of the draft assembly: BLAST against core_nt, BlobTools, the mitochondrion screen and the contig selector batch the samples one run finds in its mode's input folder; each needs a row in the annotation parameter table funannotate database the frozen snapshot of funannotate's data, such as Swiss-Prot, Pfam, the BUSCO set and stored AUGUSTUS models, downloaded once from Zenodo into directories.funannotate_db checksum (SHA-256) a 64-character fingerprint of a file's content, printed by sha256sum; FunFlux checks several downloads against stored checksums and stops on a mismatch heavy step, long step on a cluster, heavy steps ask the scheduler for ram_gb and runtime_hours, and long steps for runtime_hours only

docs.title: How the file is read
docs.text:
FunFlux checks the configuration before any job starts, so a dry run (snakemake -n) finds configuration errors in seconds. The first failing check stops the run, so repeat the dry run until it passes. A line [FunFlux] NOTE: ... does not stop the run. Troubleshooting lists the messages.

FunFlux treats a wrong, empty, missing or unknown entry as follows.

In the file What FunFlux does a value outside the allowed values listed below stops the run with a message that starts [FunFlux] <key>: nan or inf (YAML .nan, .inf) where a number is expected refuses it, as above a missing optional key uses the default given in the tables below. The template ships the same value unless a table says otherwise a missing or empty required key stops the run a number key that is present but empty stops the run, unless its table lists empty as allowed. Delete the line to get the default an unknown or misplaced key under parameters stops the run with a message that lists the known keys or names the right place a misspelt optional key in the blocks input, directories, files, links or resources ignores it without a message, because these blocks are not checked for unknown keys. With antismash instead of antismash_db in directories, for example, the antiSMASH database is downloaded a misspelt top-level key ignores it without a message, because top-level keys are not checked either. With a misspelt parameter: block, every key under parameters takes its default

Outside parameters, a misspelt optional key is ignored without a message

A misspelt key or a refused value under parameters stops the run before any job starts. A misspelt optional key in another block is ignored, and its default is used. A misspelt parameters or resources block is ignored too, and all its keys take their defaults. Check those names yourself.

YAML reads unquoted off, no and false as false, and on, yes and true as true, before FunFlux sees them. What a key then does depends on the key:

Keys Unquoted off, no or false Empty (key: or key: "") mode of decontamination, mitochondria, genemark, tiberius and signalp6, and amr.chroquetas read as off, so decontamination.mode: off works without quotes the default of the key (off for amr.chroquetas) amr.mito_genetic_code refused, and so is true auto nt_version, masking_method, busco.lineage, prediction.busco_db, assembler, flye_input_mode read as empty, so the default applies: masking_method: off still masks with tantan the default

In a key that has an off value, off needs no quotes. The six keys of the last row have no such value, and an unquoted off gives their default. tiberius.mode and amr.chroquetas also read an unquoted on, yes or true as on.

A relative path is read from the launch folder, not from the folder of the configuration file and not from output_dir:

Keys A relative path output_dir, the directories.*_db paths, files.iprscan, files.annotation_params, the protein files of the annotation parameter table is made absolute as FunFlux reads it directories.genemark_dir, files.signalp6_archive stops the run when GeneMark or SignalP 6 is on, because these must already be absolute

Write absolute paths unless you know the launch folder in advance.

The Modes column of the tables below names the modes that read a key, and the other modes ignore it. "screen" stands for the contamination and mitochondrion screen, which runs in illumina, longread and hybrid mode, and in contigs mode with parameters.contigs.screen: true.

docs.title: What every run needs
docs.text:
These are the keys to fill in. The links come filled in, and every key under parameters has a default.
