Key Set it to mode illumina, longread, hybrid or contigs (Choosing a mode) input.illumina_dir, input.longread_dir or input.contigs_dir the input folder of the mode, and in hybrid mode the first two directories.output_dir the folder for results and logs directories.eggnog_db, directories.funannotate_db the eggNOG-mapper data, and the folder for the funannotate database (Reference databases) directories.blast_db the NCBI BLAST database folder, when the screen runs files.annotation_params the annotation parameter table files.iprscan the InterProScan launcher (Licensed and external tools) resources.threads the number you give to --cores

docs.title: mode
docs.text:
The top-level key mode selects the input mode of the run.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does mode required; illumina in the template illumina, longread, hybrid, contigs (case and surrounding spaces are ignored) all Selects the input type, how the reads are cleaned and assembled, and the input folder that is searched for samples. The contamination and mitochondrion screen and every later step except polishing are the same in all modes.

A configuration without mode is taken for a FunFlux 1.x, FunFluxL or FunFluxL+ configuration, and the run stops with a message that points to Coming from v1.

docs.title: input
docs.text:
The input block names the folders that FunFlux searches for samples. A run reads only the keys of its mode.

input:
  illumina_dir: ""             # illumina, hybrid
  longread_dir: ""             # longread, hybrid
  contigs_dir:  ""             # contigs
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does illumina_dir required in its modes an existing folder holding {sample}_R1.<ext> and {sample}_R2.<ext> illumina, hybrid Paired-end reads. Samples are found from the R1 files, and an R1 file without its R2 stops the run. longread_dir required in its modes an existing folder holding {sample}_ont.<ext> or {sample}_pacbio.<ext> longread, hybrid Long reads. The suffix sets the technology of each sample, _ont for Oxford Nanopore and _pacbio for PacBio HiFi (CCS). One batch may mix both, but a sample with both files stops the run. In hybrid mode it may be the same folder as illumina_dir. contigs_dir required in its mode an existing folder holding {sample}.fasta, {sample}.fa or {sample}.fna contigs One assembly per sample.
  • Read files end in fastq, fq, fastq.gz or fq.gz. All files of one kind in a batch (Illumina reads, long reads, assemblies) must share one extension, and two extensions stop the run.
  • A _pacbio file is taken to hold HiFi reads, and a NOTE says so. PacBio CLR reads are not supported.
  • In hybrid mode every sample needs Illumina and long reads. The run stops and lists the samples that lack either.
  • In contigs_dir every file whose name contains a dot is taken as a sample, and the last dot splits off the extension (my.genome.fasta is the sample my.genome). Keep nothing else there. A README.txt stops the run with the two-extensions error, and a FASTA in a subfolder becomes a sample name containing /, which is refused.

Sample names become file names, report labels and the locus-tag prefix of every gene (funannotate predict --name):

Sample name Result contains a space or one of * # @ % ^ / ! ? & : ; | < > stops the run contains underscores or dots allowed is not 3 to 12 letters or digits starting with a letter runs, with a NOTE that its gene IDs cannot be submitted to GenBank as they are

A name such as SAMPLE1, 3 to 12 letters or digits starting with a letter, gets neither the stop nor the NOTE.

docs.title: directories
docs.text:
The directories block names the output folder and the folders of the databases and of GeneMark-ES.

directories:
  output_dir:     ""
  blast_db:       ""
  eggnog_db:      ""
  funannotate_db: ""
  genemark_dir:   ""
  antismash_db:   ""
  unite_db:       ""
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does output_dir required any path all Root of every result and log, created by the first job. Later runs with the same output_dir reuse the databases and the SignalP 6 installation stored in 00.resources/. Two things are written elsewhere: the funannotate database, in directories.funannotate_db, and Snakemake's .snakemake/ folder, in the launch folder. The .snakemake/ folder holds Snakemake's records of the run, the run logs and, unless --conda-prefix is given, the conda environments. blast_db required with the screen a folder screen The NCBI nucleotide BLAST database. The folder holds the files named after parameters.nt_version (for core_nt, core_nt.nal and the core_nt.NN.* volumes), the BLAST taxonomy files taxdb.btd and taxdb.bti, and the NCBI taxonomy files nodes.dmp and names.dmp. FunFlux prints a NOTE when the folder does not exist. Without the two .dmp files the dry run stops with Snakemake's MissingInputException in rule blob_json, and without taxdb.* the organism names in the BLAST table read N/A. eggnog_db required a folder all The eggNOG-mapper data (eggnog.db, eggnog_proteins.dmnd), passed to emapper.py --data_dir. FunFlux prints a NOTE when the folder does not exist. funannotate_db required a folder, which may not exist yet all The funannotate database. When the folder holds no funannotate-db-info.txt, the archive named in links.funannotate_link is downloaded into it, checked against its .sha256 file and unpacked. The absolute paths stored inside the database are rewritten to this location once per output folder. genemark_dir empty: no GeneMark-ES absolute path of the folder holding an executable gmes_petap.pl all With parameters.genemark.mode: auto, funannotate predict runs GeneMark-ES from here. The licence key ~/.gm_key of the user who runs Snakemake must then exist, or the run stops. antismash_db empty: download a folder containing clusterblast/ all An antiSMASH database you already hold. It is linked into 00.resources/antismash/databases/ and never written to. When empty, download-antismash-databases fills that folder (about 9.4 GB for antiSMASH 8.0.4). unite_db empty: download a folder containing an uncompressed unite_its_sintax.fasta all A UNITE SINTAX reference you already hold. It is linked into 00.resources/unite/, and links.unite_its_link is not used (a NOTE says so).

antismash_db and unite_db are checked as soon as they are set. A missing folder, or a folder without clusterblast/ or unite_its_sintax.fasta, stops the run, dry runs included.

Start one run first when several runs share a funannotate database

Several runs can share one funannotate database, but nothing stops two of them from repairing its stored paths at the same time. Start one run, let it pass the step normalize_funannotate_db, then start the others, and reach the folder under the same path in every run (Reference databases).

docs.title: files
docs.text:
The files block names three single files: the annotation parameter table, the InterProScan launcher and the SignalP 6 archive.

files:
  annotation_params: ""
  iprscan:           ""
  signalp6_archive:  ""
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does annotation_params required path of a tab-separated table all The species name, protein evidence and AUGUSTUS model of each sample. See Annotation parameter table. iprscan required path of interproscan.sh all The InterProScan 5 launcher, installed by hand (FunFlux v2 was tested with 5.78-109.0). It runs on the Java 11 of the workflow's interproscan environment. FunFlux prints a NOTE when the file does not exist. signalp6_archive empty absolute path of a readable file all, when parameters.signalp6.mode is not off The SignalP 6 archive downloaded from DTU (for example signalp-6.0i.fast.tar.gz). It is installed once per output folder into 00.resources/signalp6/, and the workflow never downloads SignalP.

docs.title: links
docs.text:
The links block holds the download addresses of what the workflow fetches itself, and the template fills them in.

links:
  phix_link: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/819/615/GCF_000819615.1_ViralProj14015/GCF_000819615.1_ViralProj14015_genomic.fna.gz
  funannotate_link: https://zenodo.org/records/23265189/files/funannotate_db_1.8.17_2026-10-08.tar.gz?download=1
  unite_its_link: https://s3.hpc.ut.ee/plutof-public/original/338a1413-6039-4e00-b5cf-410346a1e366.gz
  tiberius_model_link: https://bioinf.uni-greifswald.de/bioinf/tiberius/models/fungi.tar.gz
  telomere_db_link: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tolkit/a-telomeric-repeat-database/73c635c7b80e5ab369b4c7ec67d23db32dcaa1b8/data/telo_database_v2.tsv
  chroquetas_link: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nmquijada/ChroQueTas/1aad051d6ad48f5e403636699d19095e655764f7

The workflow has no built-in links, so the run stops when a link that the mode needs is missing.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does phix_link template URL a URL illumina, hybrid (required there) The PhiX174 genome (RefSeq GCF_000819615.1) that Illumina libraries are spiked with. Reads that map to it are removed. funannotate_link template URL a Zenodo URL of the form https://zenodo.org/records/<id>/files/<archive> all, and required even when the database is already on disk The archive of the funannotate database (Zenodo record 23265189, 2.1 GB), downloaded only while directories.funannotate_db holds no database. To switch to another version of the database, change the link and point directories.funannotate_db at a new, empty folder, for the reasons given under Newer snapshots, and building your own. The checksum file, the archive name with .sha256 in place of .tar.gz, is taken from the same record and checked with sha256sum -c. A mismatch stops the run before anything is unpacked. unite_its_link template URL a URL of a gzip-compressed SINTAX FASTA all, and required unless directories.unite_db is set The UNITE reference for the ITS classification. The template points to UNITE's SINTAX release for eukaryotes of 19.02.2025 (266,589 sequences). It is downloaded once per output folder and unpacked on the fly into 00.resources/unite/unite_its_sintax.fasta, and PROVENANCE.txt beside it records the URL, date, md5 and size. No checksum is checked. tiberius_model_link template URL a URL of a .tar.gz archive holding one folder with the model files all, and required unless parameters.tiberius.mode is off The fungi model of the Tiberius gene finder, from its authors' server (about 30 MB). It is downloaded once per output folder, checked against parameters.tiberius.model_sha256 and unpacked into 00.resources/tiberius/model/. A mismatch stops the run before anything is unpacked. telomere_db_link template URL the URL of the tab-separated database file all, and required The telomere repeat database of tidk, telo_database_v2.tsv (0.6 MB), with the known telomere repeat units that the contig summary checks its candidates against. It is downloaded once per output folder into 00.resources/telomeres/ and checked against parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256, and a mismatch stops the run. The template address names one commit of the repository tolkit/a-telomeric-repeat-database, so the file behind it does not change (Reference databases). chroquetas_link template URL the raw-file address of one commit of the ChroQueTas repository on GitHub, without a file name all, required when parameters.amr.chroquetas is on and not read when it is off ChroQueTas 1.0.1 and its FungAMR database. Rule chroquetas_db downloads bin/ChroQueTas.sh, FungAMR_db/db-v20250811.tgz and LICENSE from this address once per output folder into 00.resources/chroquetas/. It checks the script and the archive against parameters.amr.chroquetas_script_sha256 and chroquetas_db_sha256, and a mismatch stops the run before anything runs or is unpacked (Reference databases).

docs.title: resources
docs.text:
The resources block holds three numbers: the threads, the memory in GB and, for a cluster, the time limit in hours.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does threads 24 an integer ≥ 1 all The most threads any rule asks for (see below). On a single computer, give the same number to --cores and do not add --jobs/-j. For a local run --jobs is another name for --cores, and giving both can let the jobs use more CPUs than the machine has. On a cluster each job asks the scheduler for its rule's threads, so use at most the CPUs of one compute node (Slurm: sinfo -o "%n %c"). ram_gb 128 an integer ≥ 1 all On a single computer, the memory limit SPAdes is given (-m, step illumina_assembly) and, capped at 64 GB, the Java heap of Qualimap (map_evaluation, and in hybrid also map_guide_evaluation). Snakemake reserves no memory for these steps unless --resources sets a limit, mem_gb for SPAdes and java_mem for Qualimap (Running FunFlux). On a cluster, it is also the memory every heavy step asks the scheduler for, in every mode, and Qualimap asks for its heap plus 4 GB, never more than ram_gb. Use at most the memory the scheduler offers one compute node, or no node can take those steps (Slurm: sinfo -o "%n %m", in MB). See How the settings reach Slurm. A change re-runs nothing. runtime_hours 48 an integer ≥ 1 all On a cluster, the time limit that every heavy and every long step asks the scheduler for. These are the steps that can run for more than an hour, such as the assemblers, BLAST, gene prediction and InterProScan, and a step still running at the limit is stopped. Use at most the time limit of the partition, or the scheduler refuses those steps or never starts them (Slurm: sinfo -o "%P %l"). A single computer ignores it. A change re-runs nothing.

The rules ask for threads in four ways:

Rules Threads they ask for funannotate_prediction, tiberius_prediction, the assemblers (illumina_assembly, long_read_assembly), the read mappings (map_phix, map_contigs, map_guide_contigs, map_sel_contigs) threads the other CPU-bound rules threads, up to a fixed cap between 2 and 24 SignalP 6 (signalp6_annotation) parameters.signalp6.torch_num_threads, lowered to threads when it is larger every other rule 1

threads is the most any one job takes, so it is the number to give --cores. When --cores is lower than a rule's number, Snakemake runs the job with --cores threads. The cap of every rule, with the reasons, is listed on CPU cores and threads. On a cluster the three keys must each fit one compute node and one partition (On a cluster).

docs.title: parameters
docs.text: The parameters block holds the analysis settings. FunFlux checks every key under parameters in every mode, so a wrong value stops the run even in a mode that does not use the key. There are three exceptions: spades_kmers is read only in illumina and hybrid mode, the longread and hybrid blocks only in their own mode, and the files that the decontamination keys name only when the screen runs. After a change of most settings, the next run re-runs the step that uses it and every step after it.

docs.title: BLAST database and hit depth
docs.text:
These keys choose the BLAST database of the screen and how many hits BLAST keeps for each contig.

parameters:
  nt_version: core_nt
  blast_max_target_seqs: 50
  blast_max_hsps: 5
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does nt_version core_nt the name of the BLAST database in directories.blast_db, usually core_nt or nt, not checked screen The database BLAST searches, as blastn -db <blast_db>/<nt_version>. blast_max_target_seqs 50 an integer ≥ 1, with a NOTE below 5 screen -max_target_seqs, the number of database sequences kept per contig. BLAST applies it during the search, not as a final best-N filter, so a small value can lose better matches. blast_max_hsps 5 an integer ≥ 1, with a NOTE below 5 while the mitochondrion screen is on screen -max_hsps, the number of alignments kept per database sequence. The mitochondrion screen reads qcovs, the share of the contig covered by one database sequence, which BLAST computes from the kept alignments only.

One BLAST table feeds both BlobTools (the genus of each contig) and the mitochondrion screen. With blast_max_hsps: 1 BLAST keeps only the single best local alignment per database sequence, so a complete mitochondrial genome that aligns to its closest reference in several blocks can look only half covered. Setting blast_max_target_seqs: 10 and blast_max_hsps: 1 gives the BLAST settings of FunFlux 1.1.x. These values also change the hits whose bit scores BlobTools adds up, and so can change the genus it gives a contig. See BLAST hit depth.

docs.title: spades_kmers
docs.text:
spades_kmers lists the k-mer sizes that SPAdes assembles the Illumina reads with.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does spades_kmers "21,33,55,77,99,127" auto, or comma-separated text or a YAML list, with every k odd, from 1 to 127, and strictly ascending illumina, hybrid The SPAdes -k list. auto lets SPAdes choose from the read length (Illumina mode).

docs.title: decontamination
docs.text:
These keys tell the contig selector which contigs to keep or remove by genus.

parameters:
  decontamination:
    mode: off                  # off | include | exclude
    discard_no_hit: false
    include_genera:
    include_genera_by_sample:
    exclude_genera:
    exclude_genera_file:
    sample_overrides:

The contig selector, rule select_contigs, takes the genus BlobTools assigned to each contig (the taxon with the highest summed BLAST bit score) and keeps or removes the contig. With every policy, off included, it writes contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, one line per contig with its genus, keep or remove, and the reason. With mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed (the default), the contig selector always keeps the contigs that the mitochondrion screen confirmed (reason protected_confirmed_mitochondrial). With report or off, nothing is protected.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does mode off off, include, exclude, while auto stops the run (see the warning box below) screen off keeps every contig. include keeps only the listed genera. Name the genera that contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv gives the isolate's own contigs, which for a poorly sequenced fungus are often not its true genus. When the screen runs, a sample in include mode without a genus stops the run before any job starts. exclude removes the listed genera. discard_no_hit false true, false (also yes/no, on/off, 1/0) screen With exclude, also removes the contigs without a BLAST hit (reason discarded_no_hit). include removes them anyway, because no-hit is not on its list, and the setting changes only the reason. No effect with off. include_genera empty a genus, a YAML list, or names separated by ; or , screen Genera that include keeps. include_genera_by_sample empty path of a tab-separated table with the header columns sample and genus, in which a sample may have several rows screen Adds the sample's genera to include_genera. exclude_genera empty as include_genera screen Genera that exclude removes. exclude_genera_file empty path of a text file with one genus per line, in which lines starting with # are skipped screen Adds its genera to exclude_genera. sample_overrides empty path of a tab-separated table with the columns sample and mode, and optionally include_genera, exclude_genera, discard_no_hit screen Replaces the named settings for single samples, and an empty cell keeps the run-wide value. A mode cell holds off, include, exclude or nothing, and a discard_no_hit cell a yes/no word or nothing.

Genus names are compared without regard to case. include also accepts a few aliases, from a table of bacterial genus splits and from the prefixes brady, meso, neo, sino, aeri, caldi and geo. Neocosmospora and Cosmospora, for example, match each other. An alias can only keep more contigs. exclude compares exact names.

When the screen runs, the three files are checked before any job starts. Each must exist and be UTF-8 text:

File Must also hold include_genera_by_sample a header line with the columns sample and genus exclude_genera_file no further check sample_overrides a header line with the columns sample and mode. Every mode cell holds off, include, exclude or nothing, and the discard_no_hit cell of each sample of the batch a yes/no word or nothing

Every sample of the batch that ends up in include mode needs at least one genus. The log logs/select_contigs_{sample}.log warns when more than 20 % of the bases are removed, and when two or more genera each hold at least 5 % of the bases.

The v1 key parameters.genus is still read when the decontamination block is missing or empty, and a NOTE reports the translation:

decontamination block v1 key parameters.genus Becomes missing or empty a genus mode: include with that genus missing or empty empty mode: off, so every contig is kept not empty any value nothing, and genus is ignored without a message

Move the genus into the decontamination block, because once that block holds anything, genus has no effect.

There is no auto mode, because BLAST genus labels are unreliable for poorly sequenced fungi

The v1 workflows had a mode: auto that kept the genus BlobTools gave the most contigs. FunFlux v2 refuses it before any job starts and, when the screen runs, also in the mode column of sample_overrides.

Why auto fails What happens it counts contigs, not bases when the contigs without a BLAST hit outnumber those of any genus, it keeps them and removes the rest of the genome the isolate's genus is poorly represented in core_nt BLAST labels much of the isolate's own DNA with related genera, so auto keeps a wrong genus, and even include with the true genus can remove most of the genome

auto can therefore remove most of the genome. Run with off (the default), read contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv and {sample}_composition.txt, then exclude the contaminant genera or include the genera BLAST gave the isolate's own contigs (Why there is no auto mode).

docs.title: mitochondria
docs.text:
These keys set how the mitochondrion screen recognises the mitochondrial genome, and what happens to it.

parameters:
  mitochondria:
    mode: separate_confirmed   # off | report | separate_confirmed
    min_direct_blast_qcov: 35
    min_assembler_coverage_ratio: 3.0
    very_strong_qcov: 70

A direct hit is a BLAST hit whose title names a mitochondrial genome, and qcovs is the percentage of the contig that its best direct hit covers.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does mode separate_confirmed off, report, separate_confirmed screen separate_confirmed writes mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv, protects the confirmed contigs from the contig selector, and writes them to contigs_mitochondrial.fasta instead of contigs_final.fasta, the nuclear genome that QC, ITS and gene prediction read. report writes the table only, so nothing is protected or split off. off classifies nothing. min_direct_blast_qcov 35 a number above 0 and at most 100 screen Without assembler evidence (illumina and contigs mode, and the hybrid guide), a direct hit with qcovs at or above this value confirms the contig, and a weaker one makes it a mitochondrial_candidate. With assembler evidence, it is the minimum that depth or circularity must back up. min_assembler_coverage_ratio 3.0 a number above 0 longread, hybrid Contig depth divided by the median contig depth, as reported by the assembler (Flye depth, hifiasm rd:i). A direct hit at or above min_direct_blast_qcov, plus a ratio at or above this value or a clean circle (circular, not a repeat, not an alternative copy), confirms the contig. very_strong_qcov 70 a number above 0 and at most 100 longread, hybrid A direct hit at or above this value confirms the contig without depth or circularity.

The assembler evidence comes from the hifiasm or Flye assembly of longread and hybrid mode. illumina and contigs mode, and the guide screen of hybrid, give the screen none, so the last two keys change nothing there. Neither circularity nor high depth confirms a contig without a direct hit. See Mitochondria.

docs.title: busco
docs.text:
The busco block chooses the lineage dataset of the BUSCO completeness check.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does lineage auto auto, or a BUSCO dataset name ending in _odb and a number, such as hypocreales_odb12 (case is ignored) all auto runs busco --auto-lineage-euk. BUSCO then reports a generic (eukaryota) and a specific lineage, and MultiQC shows two BUSCO rows per sample. A name runs busco -l <name>, which gives one row and the same dataset for every sample.

Where the lineage data come from depends on the setting:

Setting Where the lineage data come from Internet needed auto downloaded again for every sample in every run, into a temporary folder of that sample in every BUSCO job a name downloaded once per output folder by rule busco_data into 00.resources/busco/, and read by every BUSCO job with --offline. Later runs into the same folder reuse it once, on the computer that runs Snakemake

A named lineage is the one choice for compute nodes without internet

A named lineage is downloaded once, on the computer that runs Snakemake, while auto needs internet in every BUSCO job.

The dry run checks only the form of the name. A name BUSCO does not offer stops busco_data with a [FunFlux] busco_data: message. A dataset archive takes tens to hundreds of MB (274.6 MB for hypocreales_odb12), and with auto the BUSCO folder of one sample holds several hundred MB. See Assembly QC.

docs.title: contig_summary
docs.text:
These keys steer the contig summary, and above all how it finds the telomeres.

parameters:
  contig_summary:
    telomere_motif: auto
    telomere_db_sha256: 1d4f5c8c2cce6a76aaa8de01602317a8e0b8d0401711b96f3c7a826c385da699
    telomere_window: 25000
    min_telomere_copies: 5
    min_rdna_units: 3

After the annotation, rule contig_summary writes 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv. It has one row per contig of the draft assembly, with the evidence the run produced about it and a verdict. The evidence consists of the telomere arrays at the contig ends, read depth, the assembler's depth and circularity flag, rDNA units, BUSCO markers, predicted genes and the calls of the contamination and mitochondrion screen. The verdict is one of chromosome, chromosome_arm, mitochondrion, rDNA_array, low_depth, repeat, nuclear_contig, nuclear_fragment, contaminant or unclassified.

The telomere arrays are the one piece of evidence worked out from the sequence itself. Their repeat unit differs between fungal groups, so rule telomere_units chooses it from the assembly with tidk. It checks the unit against tidk's telomere repeat database, which rule telomere_db downloads once per output folder (Telomeres). The first four keys steer that choice.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does telomere_motif auto auto (any case), or letters A, C, G and T only, 4 to 30 long, with lower case upper-cased all With auto, the telomere repeat unit is chosen from the data. Every tandem repeat unit found at the contig ends, every unit of the tidk database and every unit of the literature is scored by how it behaves at the contig ends. The best-supported one is the unit of the assembly. A unit you set is used as given, whatever the data say, and the data's own choice is reported next to it, with a NOTE when it differs. The known fungal units are listed under Which fungi carry which repeat. Either strand and any rotation work, so CCCTAA gives the same result as TTAGGG. telomere_db_sha256 the checksum of the database file at the template address 64 hexadecimal characters (capitals are accepted) all The SHA-256 that the file downloaded from links.telomere_db_link must have, checked by rule telomere_db before it is used. A mismatch stops the run. The template address names one commit of the database repository, so the file behind it does not change. To use another version, change the link and this checksum together (sha256sum <file> prints it). telomere_window 25000 an integer from 500 to 100000 all The terminal window, in bp. It is the stretch at each contig end in which the candidate units are collected, and how far from the end tidk ends accepts an array. The telomere array can sit some kb inside a contig end when the assembler ran past the telomere, so the window must cover that. The two offset columns of the table show where each array lies. min_telomere_copies 5 an integer ≥ 2 all The copies of the unit an array needs to count as a telomere. tidk ends requires this many unit lengths (30 bp for a 6-bp unit), and a unit is collected at the contig ends only when it forms a tandem run of this many copies. min_rdna_units 3 an integer ≥ 1 all The number of rDNA units (the ITS windows of its_windows) from which a contig can be an rDNA_array.

A parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif that is neither auto nor a plain unit stops the run with [FunFlux] parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif: must be auto (the unit is chosen from the data) or the telomere repeat unit of the species, 4 to 30 letters A, C, G and T, such as TTAGGG (got: <value>). A malformed checksum stops it with [FunFlux] parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256: must be the SHA-256 checksum of the telomere database file, 64 hexadecimal characters (got: <value>). The three numbers are checked as whole numbers against the limits above.

Every dry run prints the settings in one line: Contig summary: telomere motif auto (the repeat unit is chosen from the data), a telomere from 5 tandem copies within 25000 bp of a contig end, an rDNA array from 3 rDNA unit(s). With a unit set, the line reads telomere motif TTAGGG (used as given; the data's own choice is reported next to it).

A change of these settings re-runs the following steps:

Change Re-runs telomere_motif, telomere_window, min_telomere_copies telomere_units and contig_summary, then MultiQC min_rdna_units contig_summary only links.telomere_db_link or telomere_db_sha256 telomere_db, then telomere_units of every sample

These keys re-run only the telomere and contig-summary steps, never the assembly or the annotation. hifiasm has a separate key of its own, parameters.longread.hifiasm.telomere_motif or parameters.hybrid.hifiasm.telomere_motif. It takes the unit as it reads at the 5' end of a chromosome (CCCTAA for TTAGGG). See Contig summary.

docs.title: its and its_taxonomy_cutoff
docs.text:
These keys steer how the ITS is extracted from the genome and classified against UNITE.

parameters:
  its:
    window_flank: 2000
    max_full_length: 1500
    unite_identified_only: true
  its_taxonomy_cutoff: 0.8

nhmmer finds every 5.8S gene in contigs_final.fasta with ITSx's own profiles. A window is cut around each, and windows on the minus strand are reverse-complemented. ITSx extracts ITS1, 5.8S and ITS2 from the windows, and SINTAX classifies ITS1 and ITS2 against UNITE.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does its.window_flank 2000 an integer ≥ 200 all The bases kept on each side of the middle of each 5.8S site. 2,000 bp hold the end of the SSU, ITS1, ITS2 and the start of the LSU, which ITSx needs to recognise the unit. its.max_full_length 1500 an integer ≥ 400 all The longest ITS1-5.8S-ITS2 record listed as ok in {sample}_ITS_copies.txt. A longer one is listed as rejected_too_long (1,500 bp is ITSx's own "suspiciously long" limit). Only ITS1 and ITS2 are classified, so this key changes that table only. its.unite_identified_only true true or false all With true, rule unite_identified keeps the UNITE records whose taxonomy names a genus (g: followed by a name) in 00.resources/unite/unite_its_sintax.identified.fasta, and SINTAX classifies against that file. About a third of the records of the default release stop above the genus, and one that is identical to the query can hold the result at d:Fungi. With false, SINTAX classifies against the whole release, and rule unite_identified does not run. See The UNITE reference filter. its_taxonomy_cutoff 0.8 a number above 0 and at most 1 all Passed as vsearch --sintax_cutoff. {sample}_ITS1_taxonomy.txt and {sample}_ITS2_taxonomy.txt hold every rank with its bootstrap confidence in column 2, and in column 4 only the ranks whose confidence reaches the cutoff.

ITS1 and ITS2 sequences outside 50 to 600 bp are listed in {sample}_ITS_copies.txt and not classified. That range is fixed. See ITS taxonomy and ITS on long-read contigs.

docs.title: Repeat masking
docs.text:
Before gene prediction, the genome is soft-masked by tantan, or by RepeatModeler and RepeatMasker.

parameters:
  masking_method: tantan       # tantan | repeatmodeler_repeatmasker
  repeatmodeler_quick: true
  repeatmodeler_ltrstruct: false
  repeatmodeler_seed:
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does masking_method tantan tantan, repeatmodeler_repeatmasker all How contigs_sort.fasta is soft-masked (repeats in lower case) before gene prediction. tantan masks tandem repeats and low-complexity sequence. repeatmodeler_repeatmasker builds a repeat library from this genome with RepeatModeler and masks with RepeatMasker, which also finds interspersed repeats such as transposons. This method takes hours. repeatmodeler_quick true true, false all (RepeatModeler only) RepeatModeler -quick, a shorter run that finds fewer repeat families. repeatmodeler_ltrstruct false true, false all (RepeatModeler only) RepeatModeler -LTRStruct, which adds the LTR retrotransposon structural module. repeatmodeler_seed empty empty, or an integer ≥ 0 all (RepeatModeler only) RepeatModeler -srand <seed>. When empty, RepeatModeler seeds itself from the clock, and two runs on the same genome build slightly different libraries.

RepeatMasker needs no Dfam or RepBase library here, because it masks with the library RepeatModeler built. See Repeat masking.

docs.title: prediction
docs.text:
The prediction keys pass two settings to funannotate predict.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does busco_db dikarya letters, digits and _, and once the database is on disk, a folder of that name must exist in it all funannotate predict --busco_db, the conserved-gene set that SNAP and GlimmerHMM are trained on, and AUGUSTUS too for the samples without a model in column 4 of the annotation table. The funannotate database as downloaded holds only dikarya (BUSCO dikarya_odb9, 1,312 genes). For a fungus outside the Dikarya, add a set such as fungi (Other BUSCO sets for gene prediction) and set busco_db: fungi. augustus_optimize false true, false all funannotate predict --optimize_augustus, for the samples whose column 4 of the annotation table is empty. After the quick training, optimize_augustus.pl tunes AUGUSTUS's meta-parameters, the settings the quick training keeps fixed, by 8-fold cross-validation: each eighth of the BUSCO test genes is predicted by a model trained without it. AUGUSTUS is then trained again (see The AUGUSTUS model). It adds about a quarter of an hour for a 40 Mb genome and uses at most 8 CPUs. It does not apply to samples that name a stored AUGUSTUS model, and a NOTE names them. Switching it re-runs gene prediction only for the samples whose column 4 is empty.

docs.title: genemark
docs.text:
The genemark block decides whether funannotate predict uses GeneMark-ES.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does mode auto auto, off (also false, no, 0, none, and null in quotes). An empty value (mode:, mode: "" or an unquoted null) means auto, as for the other mode keys all With auto, funannotate predict uses GeneMark-ES when directories.genemark_dir is set. With off it never does, and funannotate runs without GeneMark.

With GeneMark on, the run stops before any job starts when genemark_dir is not absolute, holds no executable gmes_petap.pl, or ~/.gm_key is missing. The step genemark_check also tests the licence key before gene prediction (The licence check before gene prediction). FunFlux v2 was tested with GeneMark-ES on, and with mode: off on one public genome (Validation on public genomes).

docs.title: tiberius
docs.text:
The tiberius block switches the Tiberius gene finder on or off and pins its model.

parameters:
  tiberius:
    mode: on                   # on | off
    model_sha256: 4a309a630574f395d82d747dcf64716704dab056db534e427ae0cec1b7410e20
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does mode on on (also true, yes, 1, and an empty value), off (also false, no, 0, none, and null in quotes) all With on, Tiberius predicts genes (step tiberius_prediction) before funannotate predict, which adds them to its evidence (--other_gff <file>:1). With off, Tiberius does not run, its model is not downloaded, and links.tiberius_model_link is not read. Tiberius is independent of GeneMark-ES, and both can be on. model_sha256 the checksum of the fungi model of 8 February 2026 64 hexadecimal characters (capitals are accepted) Tiberius on The SHA-256 that the file at links.tiberius_model_link must have, checked before it is unpacked. The address carries no version number. When its authors replace the model, the run stops until you accept the new file by putting its checksum (sha256sum <archive>) here.

Tiberius needs about 16 GB of memory, so switch it off on a computer with less free memory. What it does, and how its genes are combined with the others, is described under Tiberius.

docs.title: signalp6
docs.text:
The signalp6 block sets whether and how SignalP 6 runs.

parameters:
  signalp6:
    mode: off                  # off | fast | slow | slow-sequential
    archive_sha256:
    torch_num_threads: 8
    batch_size: 10
Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does mode off off, fast, slow, slow-sequential (off also as empty, false, no, 0, none or null) all Any value but off installs SignalP 6 from files.signalp6_archive once per output folder, predicts the signal peptides of the predicted proteins, and passes them to funannotate annotate --signalp. The archive must hold the model of the mode (table below). archive_sha256 empty 64 hexadecimal characters SignalP on Compared with the SHA-256 of the archive before installing, by the step that installs SignalP 6 (install_signalp6) and not by the dry run. sha256sum <archive> prints it. torch_num_threads 8, or resources.threads when that is smaller an integer ≥ 1. A value above resources.threads is lowered to it, with a NOTE SignalP on The threads of signalp6_annotation, passed as --torch_num_threads. batch_size 10 an integer ≥ 1 SignalP on --bsize, the number of proteins that SignalP 6 processes together. Raise it only after checking memory use.

Each mode needs its own model in the archive:

mode The archive must hold fast distilled_model_signalp6.pt slow ensemble_model_signalp6.pt slow-sequential sequential_models_signalp6

Choose the mode that matches the archive you downloaded, because a fast archive works only with fast. The speed and memory of the three modes, from the SignalP 6 README, are given under SignalP 6. FunFlux v2 was tested with fast. See Functional annotation.

docs.title: amr
docs.text:
The amr block switches the AMR screen (the resistance-mutation screen) on or off, and sets the genetic code of its mitochondrial run and the checksums of its downloads.

parameters:
  amr:
    chroquetas: off            # off | on
    mito_genetic_code: auto
    chroquetas_script_sha256: d8961a0d311be57d4a9939bd9e4d90dbc796589b3298dd1835359ed776abfce3
    chroquetas_db_sha256: 6f89ecb3117110aad85b8b6ca7b8a3d3715cb5984b6cb75450a6cda5633d16e7

In the AMR screen, rule amr_chroquetas runs ChroQueTas on every genome. For each sample it writes 05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary.tsv, with one row per target protein of the species, each with the mutations of the FungAMR database found in it and a verdict on resistance. It also writes amr_positions.tsv, every position compared. The species is column 2 of the annotation table.

Switching the AMR screen on accepts a non-commercial licence

ChroQueTas and its database are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, non-commercial use only. FunFlux downloads them at run time and does not ship them, and on is your acceptance of that licence (Antifungal resistance mutations).

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does chroquetas off off (also empty, false, no, 0, none, null), on (also true, yes, 1) all With on, ChroQueTas and its database are downloaded once per output folder (step chroquetas_db), every sample is screened (step amr_chroquetas) and gets 05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary.tsv, and MultiQC shows the AMR table. links.chroquetas_link is then required. With off, neither step runs, and the link is not read. mito_genetic_code auto auto (any case, or an empty value), or the number of an NCBI genetic code, 1-6, 9-16 or 21-33 (7, 8 and 17-20 are not NCBI codes, and miniprot refuses them) AMR on The genetic code of the second ChroQueTas run, on the mitochondrial genome, where cytochrome b is encoded. That run is made only for the 15 species whose database entry includes cytochrome b. With auto, the code is chosen per sample: code 3 (yeast mitochondrial) for the four Saccharomycetaceae of the database (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, S. paradoxus, Nakaseomyces glabratus, Kluyveromyces marxianus), and code 4 (mold mitochondrial) for every other species. A number sets that code for every sample. The nuclear run always uses the code ChroQueTas chooses for the species (Two runs). chroquetas_script_sha256 the checksum of bin/ChroQueTas.sh at the template address 64 hexadecimal characters (capitals are accepted) AMR on The SHA-256 that the downloaded script must have, checked before anything runs it. chroquetas_db_sha256 the checksum of FungAMR_db/db-v20250811.tgz at the template address 64 hexadecimal characters (capitals are accepted) AMR on The SHA-256 that the downloaded database archive must have, checked before it is unpacked.

The template address names one commit, so the files behind it do not change. To use another version, change the link and both checksums together (sha256sum <file> prints them). A wrong value stops the run with [FunFlux] parameters.amr.<key>: ..., for example [FunFlux] parameters.amr.mito_genetic_code: must be auto or the number of an NCBI genetic code: 1-6, 9-16 or 21-33 (got: <value>). Every dry run prints one line, AMR screen: ChroQueTas on (licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use). or AMR screen: off.

A change re-runs the following steps:

Change Re-runs mito_genetic_code amr_chroquetas and MultiQC links.chroquetas_link, chroquetas_script_sha256 or chroquetas_db_sha256 chroquetas_db, then amr_chroquetas of every sample the species, column 2 of the annotation table also the gene prediction and everything after it, because funannotate reads the species too

The amr keys and the link re-run only the AMR steps and the report, while a new species re-runs the whole annotation.

docs.title: longread and hybrid
docs.text:
These two blocks hold the long-read settings: the assembler, Filtlong, Medaka and hifiasm, and in hybrid mode also the Filtlong guidance.

parameters:
  longread:
    assembler: hifiasm         # hifiasm | flye
    flye_input_mode: auto      # auto | nano-raw | nano-hq
    medaka_model: auto
    medaka_model_fallback_auto: false
    filtlong:
      min_length: 1000
      keep_percent: 90
      length_weight: 10
      target_bases:
    hifiasm:
      genome_size:
      bloom_filter_bits: 0
      purge_dups: auto
      homozygous_coverage: auto
      telomere_motif:
  hybrid:
    # the same keys as longread, plus:
    short_read_guidance: false
    filtlong_split: 1000

The long-read settings sit in the block named after the mode, parameters.longread in longread mode and parameters.hybrid in hybrid mode. Each block is read only in its own mode. The same keys at the top of parameters, where FunFluxL and FunFluxL+ kept their long-read settings, stop the run in every mode.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does assembler hifiasm hifiasm, flye longread, hybrid One assembler for the whole run. Flye does not repeat its assembly byte for byte from run to run. flye_input_mode auto auto, nano-raw, nano-hq, while pacbio-hifi stops the run longread, hybrid The Flye read mode of ONT samples. auto gives --nano-hq, or --nano-raw when medaka_model names a model containing fast. PacBio samples always get --pacbio-hifi. Ignored with hifiasm, with a NOTE when it is set. medaka_model auto auto (also empty or an unquoted null, true, yes, on, 1), false for no Medaka (also no, off, 0, none, null in quotes), or any other text, taken as a model name longread, hybrid Medaka polishing of ONT samples. PacBio samples never use Medaka. auto takes the model from the basecaller tag in the first 100 reads of the raw FASTQ (exactly one tag must be present) and needs network access once. The model is checked before the assembler starts. medaka_model_fallback_auto false true, false longread, hybrid When a named model is not valid, try auto instead of stopping. filtlong.min_length 1000 an integer ≥ 1 longread, hybrid Filtlong --min_length, in bp. filtlong.keep_percent 90 a number above 0 and at most 100 longread, hybrid --keep_percent, the share of the bases kept, best reads first. filtlong.length_weight 10 a number above 0 longread, hybrid --length_weight. Higher values favour longer reads. filtlong.target_bases empty empty or 0 for no cap, or a size such as 1500000000 or 1.5g longread, hybrid --target_bases, a cap on the bases kept, for very deep runs. With Flye and very deep ONT reads, set it to about 100 times the genome size (Flye). hifiasm.genome_size empty empty or 0, or a size such as 40000000 or 40m longread, hybrid --hg-size, the haploid genome size. When it is empty, hifiasm infers the depth itself. hifiasm.bloom_filter_bits 0 an integer from 0 to 63 longread, hybrid -f, where 0 suits small fungal genomes. hifiasm.purge_dups auto auto (also empty), or 0 to 3 longread, hybrid -l, how strongly duplicated haplotigs are purged. auto keeps hifiasm's own choice. hifiasm.homozygous_coverage auto auto (also empty), or an integer ≥ 1 longread, hybrid --hom-cov, the read depth of the homozygous peak. hifiasm.telomere_motif empty DNA or IUPAC letters, such as CCCTAA longread, hybrid --telo-m. Set it only when the organism's telomere repeat is known. short_read_guidance false true, false hybrid With true, Filtlong scores each long read of an ONT sample against the selected pairs, the Illumina pairs properly paired on the screened guide assembly (-1, -2). With false, every sample gets the plain filter of longread mode. PacBio samples are never guided. filtlong_split 1000 when the key is missing an integer ≥ 1, or empty or null to score but never cut hybrid With guidance, adds --trim --split <N>, so that a read is cut where the Illumina reads stop supporting it for N bp. Not used when short_read_guidance is false, and a number other than 1000 then gets a NOTE.

PacBio samples are not guided, because cutting accurate HiFi reads where the Illumina coverage has a gap would throw away their length. Filtlong's README advises against a short-read reference unless you are confident in the quality of the short reads, since long reads that span a region the short reads miss can score low. That is why the guidance is off by default. short_read_guidance: true turns it on, and filtlong_split: null then keeps the scoring without cutting.

The Filtlong defaults are sized for ONT reads and provisional for PacBio HiFi. hifiasm always runs with --primary. Every dry run prints the decisions for each sample, and One technology per sample lists what differs between ONT and PacBio HiFi samples.

See Long reads, Hybrid, The Medaka model and Filtlong guidance in hybrid mode.

docs.title: contigs
docs.text:
The contigs block has one key, which switches the screen on for supplied assemblies.

Key Default Allowed values Modes What it does screen false true, false contigs (checked in every mode) With true, the contamination and mitochondrion screen runs on the supplied FASTA. It needs directories.blast_db, and adds contigs_filt.fasta, the contaminants/ and mitochondria/ folders, contigs_all.fasta and contigs_mitochondrial.fasta to the outputs. With false there is no screen, and contigs_final.fasta is the FASTA after the contig filter. With SPAdes-style headers the filter keeps the contigs of at least 500 bp and 2x coverage, and other headers are only cut at the first space or tab. With false, a NOTE also warns that a mitochondrial genome in contigs_final.fasta would be annotated as nuclear.

Assemblies from a sequencing provider usually still contain the mitochondrial genome. See Pre-assembled contigs.

docs.title: Annotation parameter table
docs.text:
The annotation parameter table gives FunFlux the species, the protein evidence and the AUGUSTUS model of each sample. It is a tab-separated text file, named by files.annotation_params, with three or four columns (the fourth is optional) and one row per sample.

Column Content Used as 1 sample the sample name, as found in the input folder the link between the row and the sample 2 species the species name, such as Fusarium graminearum funannotate predict -s, the organism of the GenBank files and of the .sqn submission file. With spaces turned into _ and _{sample} appended, it is the stem of funannotate's file names (Fusarium_graminearum_SAMPLE1.gbk). With the AMR screen on, it is also the species looked up in the FungAMR database (The species). 3 proteins path of a protein FASTA of related fungi, such as the RefSeq proteome of a species of the same genus (how to download one) gene evidence, as funannotate predict --protein_evidence <file> <funannotate_db>/uniprot_sprot.fasta 4 augustus_species optional: the name of a stored AUGUSTUS model, or empty, or - a name gives funannotate predict --augustus_species <name>, and AUGUSTUS uses that model as it is, without training on this genome. Empty or -, or no fourth column at all, means that AUGUSTUS is trained on the genome's BUSCO genes, the long way with prediction.augustus_optimize 
#sample species proteins    augustus_species
SAMPLE1 Fusarium graminearum    /path/to/fusarium_proteins.faa  -
ARSEF3097   Beauveria bassiana  /path/to/beauveria_bassiana_proteins.faa    fusarium_graminearum

The first row trains AUGUSTUS on the genome (the default), and the second uses the stored fusarium_graminearum model as it is.

FunFlux checks the table before any job starts:

  • Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped, and spaces around each field are removed. Column names are not read, so the position decides. The shipped example config/annotation_parameters.tsv, for instance, calls the fourth column model.
  • Every data line, including a line for a sample outside the batch, has three or four tab-separated fields, and no sample name appears twice. Columns separated by spaces give, for example, [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: line 2 has 1 tab-separated columns; expected 3 or 4 (sample, species, proteins and, optionally, augustus_species).
  • Every sample of the batch has a row, and its protein file exists and is not empty. A relative path is read from the launch folder. The protein files of samples outside the batch are not checked, so one table can serve several batches.

A named AUGUSTUS model must be one of the stored models, the folder names in <funannotate_db>/trained_species/. The default funannotate database holds 166 of them, including fusarium_graminearum, aspergillus_nidulans, botrytis_cinerea and neurospora_crassa. With FUNANNOTATE_DB set, funannotate species lists them. Capitals count. When the name is checked depends on whether the database is on disk yet, and every dry run prints the choice for each sample:

The funannotate database The name is checked The dry-run line, for example is on disk before any job starts AUGUSTUS: SAMPLE1 uses the stored model fusarium_graminearum. is not downloaded yet by rule augustus_model_check, right after the database is unpacked, with its log in logs/augustus_model_check_{sample}.log SAMPLE1 names the stored model fusarium_graminearum (checked once the database is unpacked), and a sample with an empty column 4 gets the same (checked once the database is unpacked)

A name that is not in the database stops the run, at the latest right after the database is unpacked. The message gives the closest names, for example [FunFlux] files.annotation_params: sample 'SAMPLE1' names the AUGUSTUS model 'fusarium_graminaerum', which is not a trained species of the funannotate database at '<db>'. Did you mean 'fusarium_graminearum'? ....

With column 4 empty, AUGUSTUS is trained on the genome and needs at least 200 BUSCO models for it (The AUGUSTUS model). If the database holds a model stored earlier under the sample's own name, funannotate uses that instead, and a NOTE says so. Which of the two to choose is discussed on Gene prediction. A changed row re-runs gene prediction and every annotation step of that sample.

docs.title: Coming from a v1 configuration
docs.text: A v1 configuration stops at once, because it has no mode. Start from the v2 template and carry your values over. Coming from v1 lists every key that was renamed, moved or removed, and every v1 value that now stops the run.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
This page lists the files and folders a FunFlux run writes, and whether each one is still there when the run has finished. Every path on this page is relative to directories.output_dir, and a relative value of that key is read from the launch folder, the folder Snakemake is started from. The numbered folders are the same in every mode, and a mode with nothing to put into a folder does not create it.

Most tables name the rule that writes each file, as the console and logs/ name it. They also give the file's status, which says whether it stays, and the modes or settings under which it is written. The terms below define the labels of the Status and Modes columns.

Terms used on this page

deliverable a result to read, keep or pass on; a later step may read it too intermediate a working file that one step hands to the next; kept after the run temporary deleted by Snakemake once the last step that reads it has finished; absent from a finished run scratch deleted by the step that wrote it, when that step ends; a download whose checksum did not match is kept instead, for you to inspect cleanup deleted by cleanup, the last step of each sample screen the contamination and mitochondrion screen, always run in illumina, longread and hybrid mode, and in contigs mode only with parameters.contigs.screen: true SignalP, GeneMark, Tiberius for SignalP, parameters.signalp6.mode is not off; for GeneMark, GeneMark-ES is enabled (directories.genemark_dir set, parameters.genemark.mode: auto); for Tiberius, parameters.tiberius.mode is on, the default AMR antimicrobial resistance; as a label, the AMR screen is switched on: parameters.amr.chroquetas is on (off by default)

docs.title: Files to read first
docs.text:
These are the files that hold the results of a run, with the question each one answers and the modes that write it.

File What it answers Modes 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta The nuclear genome. QUAST, BUSCO, the ITS search and funannotate read this file and no other version of the assembly. all 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_mitochondrial.fasta The confirmed mitochondrial contig(s); an empty file when none was confirmed. screen 02.assembly/{sample}/mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv Why each contig was or was not called mitochondrial. screen 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv Genus, keep or remove, and the reason, for every contig. screen 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/short_summary.specific.<lineage>.{sample}.txt Completeness of the genome. all 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/report.tsv Contig count, total length, N50, GC content. all 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv What each contig of the draft assembly is (chromosome, chromosome arm, mitochondrion, rDNA array, low-depth piece, collapsed repeat, nuclear contig or fragment, contaminant, unclassified), with the evidence; it also links each contig to its scaffold_N name in the annotation. all 03.taxonomy/{sample}/{sample}_ITS1_taxonomy.txt, {sample}_ITS2_taxonomy.txt UNITE classification of the ITS barcode. all 03.taxonomy/{sample}/{sample}_ITS_copies.txt How many rDNA units were found, and which records the length guard rejected. all 04.annotation/{sample}/funannotate/annotate_results/ The annotated genome: GenBank, GFF3, proteins, transcripts, and .annotations.txt, the functional annotation with one row per transcript. all 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_sort.fasta The genome as annotated. all 05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary.tsv The FungAMR mutations found in the genome, one row per target protein of the species, with a verdict on resistance and the drugs with evidence for and against it. AMR 06.report/multiqc_report.html QUAST and BUSCO of every sample of the run on one page; in the read-based modes also the read QC (fastp, NanoPlot) and the mapping QC (Qualimap). all

The annotation and the assembly use different contig names

funannotate sort renames the contigs scaffold_1, scaffold_2, ..., longest first, before repeat masking, so the masked genome and every annotation file use these names. The screen, QUAST, BUSCO and the ITS files use the names of contigs_final.fasta. The annotated_as column of 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/contig_summary.tsv links the two, as described on Contig summary, and 04.annotation/{sample}/contigs_clean.fasta holds the same sequences under their original names.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
The tree shows the folders of an output folder and the main files in them. A label in square brackets names the modes that write a line, or the setting it needs. On the eval/ line, the label covers only qualimap/. A line without a label is written in every mode, although what 00.resources/ holds depends on the mode and the settings, as its table shows.

<output_dir>/
├── 00.resources/                        run-level material: databases, Tiberius model, SignalP 6 installation, ChroQueTas, a named BUSCO lineage
├── 01.reads/{sample}/                   [illumina, longread, hybrid]
├── 02.assembly/{sample}/
│   ├── contigs_final.fasta              nuclear genome
│   ├── contigs_all.fasta                screened genome, mitochondrion included   [screen]
│   ├── contigs_mitochondrial.fasta                                                [screen]
│   ├── contigs_filt.fasta               the draft the screen examines   [contigs + screen, illumina]
│   ├── contaminants/                    BLAST, BlobTools, keep/remove decisions   [screen]
│   ├── mitochondria/                    mitochondrion screen                      [screen]
│   ├── spades/                                                                    [illumina]
│   ├── hifiasm/ or flye/, assembly.fasta, assembly_evidence.tsv, assembly_provenance.tsv   [longread, hybrid]
│   ├── {sample}_medaka_model.txt, medaka/            [longread, hybrid: ONT samples with Medaka]
│   ├── polypolish/, guide/                                                        [hybrid]
│   └── eval/                            quast/, busco/, telomere_*, contig_summary*.tsv; qualimap/ [illumina, longread, hybrid]
├── 03.taxonomy/{sample}/                ITS windows, ITS sequences, UNITE classification
├── 04.annotation/{sample}/              masking, gene prediction, functional annotation
├── 05.amr/{sample}/                     antifungal resistance mutations (ChroQueTas)   [AMR]
├── 06.report/                           MultiQC
└── logs/                                one log per rule and sample

docs.title: Disk use
docs.text:
One sample in contigs mode takes in the order of 10 GB. The table shows where the space goes.

Folder What takes the space Size 01.reads/{sample}/, 02.assembly/{sample}/ (read-based modes only) the kept reads in 01.reads/ (the filtered long reads, uncompressed; in hybrid also the selected pairs of Illumina reads), the assembler's working folder (spades/, hifiasm/ or flye/), the read-mapping BAM (two in hybrid) and the polishing output 3.7 to 30 GB for the two folders together in the runs below 04.annotation/{sample}/ most of the rest: the InterProScan XML, there twice (iprscan/interproscan_out.xml and funannotate's copy funannotate/annotate_misc/iprscan.xml), and funannotate's working files in funannotate/predict_misc/ and annotate_misc/ the XML can be a few GB 02.assembly/{sample}/ the BUSCO result tree 0.65 to 1.8 GB with the automatic lineage in the runs below 00.resources/ the antiSMASH 8.0.4 database, unless directories.antismash_db is set 9.4 GB 00.resources/ the SignalP 6 package, with the fast model 1.6 GB 00.resources/ UNITE: the reference and, by default, its copy of the records that name a genus 354 MB (207 + 147 MB) 00.resources/ the Tiberius model 31 MB 00.resources/ the BUSCO lineage data, when parameters.busco.lineage names a lineage a few hundred MB 00.resources/ ChroQueTas with its FungAMR database (AMR screen on) 3 MB 00.resources/ the telomere repeat database 0.6 MB

In the long-read modes, the kept long reads are the largest single item. Apart from them, the annotation takes most of a sample's space, mainly because the InterProScan XML is kept twice. Of the material shared by the run, the antiSMASH database is the largest item. With directories.antismash_db set, 00.resources/ holds only links to your copy.

To free space once you have checked the results, run workflow/scripts/clean_funflux_output.sh <output folder>. The script lists the bulky working files that no result needs, and deletes them only with --run:

  • assembler caches and read mappings;
  • the working files and copies of Medaka, BUSCO and funannotate;
  • the antiSMASH and UNITE databases and the BUSCO lineage data FunFlux downloaded;
  • the licensed SignalP 6 package.

The reads kept in 01.reads/ go only with --include-reads. The results, the logs and tbl2asn's validation reports stay.

Cleaning is for a folder that FunFlux will not use again

The script refuses a folder in which a sample has not finished, but it cannot tell whether another FunFlux run is using the folder. Do not give a cleaned folder to FunFlux again: the deleted files would be made again and most of each sample repeated.

The conda environments are not counted here. They are in .snakemake/ of the launch folder, or in the --conda-prefix folder, as listed under Outside the output folder.

docs.title: Disk use per run
docs.text:
The sizes below were measured on two public genomes, with one sample per run, and are given as du -sh prints them. The runs are described on Validation on public genomes.

Genome Run 01.reads/ 02.assembly/ Whole output folder Botrytis cinerea B05.10, 42.6 Mb illumina, Illumina 79x 0.6 MB 3.7 GB 13 GB longread, ONT 42x, hifiasm, Medaka 3.1 GB 7.1 GB 20 GB longread, ONT 136x, hifiasm 9.8 GB 12 GB 31 GB longread, ONT 136x, Flye 9.8 GB 6.7 GB 26 GB hybrid, ONT 136x plus Illumina 79x, hifiasm 16 GB 14 GB 39 GB Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616, 32.7 Mb longread, PacBio HiFi 85x, hifiasm 4.7 GB 3.1 GB 17 GB longread, PacBio HiFi 85x, Flye 4.7 GB 2.3 GB 16 GB hybrid, PacBio HiFi 85x plus MGISEQ short reads 151x, hifiasm 14 GB 5.7 GB 29 GB

A whole sample took 13 to 39 GB in these runs, and the kept long reads were the largest single file of every run with long reads. Their size follows the bases sequenced: 9.8 GB from the 5.8 Gb of ONT reads of B05.10, 4.7 GB from the 2.8 Gb of HiFi reads of GXU-8616.

  • In hybrid, 01.reads/ also holds the selected pairs, uncompressed: 9.3 GB of the 14 GB for GXU-8616.
  • 02.assembly/ was smaller with Flye than with hifiasm on both genomes, because hifiasm keeps larger working files: hifiasm/ took 5.5 GB on B05.10 and 1.5 GB on GXU-8616, flye/ 858 MB and 570 MB.
  • The whole output folder of every run includes about 2 GB of 00.resources/, most of it the SignalP 6 package. It does not include the antiSMASH database, because these runs set directories.antismash_db.

docs.title: 00.resources
docs.text:
00.resources/ holds the material that belongs to the run, not to a sample. It is kept, so a later run on the same output folder downloads or installs none of it again unless the settings behind it change.

Path Content Written by Status Modes unite/unite_its_sintax.fasta UNITE reference for SINTAX, unpacked from links.unite_its_link (207 MB, 266,589 sequences with the default link); with directories.unite_db, a symbolic link to your copy unite_db or unite_db_local intermediate all unite/PROVENANCE.txt source URL (or source folder), UTC date, md5 and size in bytes of that FASTA same deliverable all unite/unite_its_sintax.identified.fasta the records of that FASTA whose taxonomy names a genus (147 MB, 180,343 sequences with the default link; 86,246 are dropped); what SINTAX classifies against while parameters.its.unite_identified_only is true unite_identified intermediate all unite/identified_filter.txt two lines: kept_with_genus: <n> and dropped_without_genus: <n>, the records the filter kept and dropped (180,343 and 86,246 with the default link) unite_identified deliverable all antismash/databases/ antiSMASH database from download-antismash-databases; with directories.antismash_db, one symbolic link per entry of your copy antismash_db or antismash_db_local intermediate all funannotate_db_paths.normalized.json marker that the paths inside the funannotate database were repaired, with the number of files checked and paths rewritten normalize_funannotate_db intermediate all signalp6/installation.json archive name and SHA-256, SignalP version, mode, model folder, and the conda environment SignalP 6 was installed into install_signalp6 intermediate SignalP signalp6/package/ the SignalP 6 package with the model weights of the DTU archive (1.6 GB, fast model) install_signalp6 intermediate SignalP signalp6/.matplotlib/ matplotlib cache install_signalp6 intermediate SignalP signalp6/.signalp6-install-*/ the unpacked archive during installation install_signalp6 scratch SignalP tiberius/model/ the Tiberius fungi model, unpacked from links.tiberius_model_link after its SHA-256 matched parameters.tiberius.model_sha256: model_config.json, model_layers.json, weights.h5 (31 MB) tiberius_model intermediate Tiberius tiberius/model.tar.gz the downloaded archive; deleted once unpacked, kept when its checksum does not match tiberius_model scratch Tiberius telomeres/telo_database_v2.tsv the telomere repeat database of tidk, downloaded from links.telomere_db_link after its SHA-256 matched parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256: 4,051 rows, one per examined species, with the telomere repeat unit and its support (0.6 MB) telomere_db intermediate all telomeres/PROVENANCE.txt source URL, download date, SHA-256 and row count of that file telomere_db deliverable all telomeres/telo_database_v2.tsv.failed the downloaded file when its checksum did not match; absent otherwise telomere_db scratch all chroquetas/ChroQueTas.sh the ChroQueTas script, version 1.0.1, downloaded unchanged from links.chroquetas_link after its SHA-256 matched parameters.amr.chroquetas_script_sha256 (29 kB) chroquetas_db intermediate AMR chroquetas/FungAMR_db/ the FungAMR database of ChroQueTas: one folder per species (57), each with a <target>.faa (the reference protein) and a <target>.txt (its resistance positions) per target; unpacked from db-v20250811.tgz after its SHA-256 matched parameters.amr.chroquetas_db_sha256 chroquetas_db intermediate AMR chroquetas/db-v20250811.tgz the downloaded database archive; deleted once unpacked chroquetas_db scratch AMR chroquetas/species.txt the database's species folders, one per line, sorted chroquetas_db intermediate AMR chroquetas/LICENSE the licence of ChroQueTas and its database, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 chroquetas_db deliverable AMR chroquetas/PROVENANCE.txt the three source addresses, the UTC date, the checksums, the species count and the licence chroquetas_db deliverable AMR chroquetas/ChroQueTas.sh.failed, chroquetas/db-v20250811.tgz.failed a download whose checksum did not match; absent otherwise chroquetas_db scratch AMR phix/ phix.fna.gz, the PhiX genome from links.phix_link, still compressed, and its six bowtie2 index files phix.*.bt2 download_phix, build_phix intermediate illumina, hybrid busco/lineages/<lineage>/ the BUSCO dataset named in parameters.busco.lineage, downloaded once and read by every BUSCO job with --offline (a few hundred MB); later runs into the folder use the same release busco_data intermediate all, with a named lineage busco/file_versions.tsv BUSCO's list of the dataset versions it downloaded busco_data deliverable all, with a named lineage

The folders named in directories.unite_db and directories.antismash_db are only read. signalp6/package/ is licensed DTU material, so remove it from any copy of the output folder you share, as explained on Licensing. chroquetas/ is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 material: it may be passed on unchanged, for non-commercial purposes and with credit.

docs.title: 01.reads
docs.text:
01.reads/ holds the processed reads and their QC reports, in one folder per sample and read type. It is not created in contigs mode.

Path Content Written by Status Modes {sample}/illumina/{sample}_nophix_R1.fastq, _R2.fastq the read pairs that did not align to the PhiX genome, uncompressed map_phix temporary illumina, hybrid {sample}/illumina/{sample}_trim_R1.fastq, _R2.fastq the PhiX-free pairs after fastp: adapters and low-quality ends cut, reads under 75 bp dropped trim_adapters temporary illumina, hybrid {sample}/illumina/{sample}_fastp.html, {sample}_fastp.json fastp's read-QC report as a page and as numbers; MultiQC reads the JSON trim_adapters deliverable illumina, hybrid {sample}/long/{sample}_filtered.fastq the long reads Filtlong kept, uncompressed; the assembler, the coverage mapping and Medaka read it filter_long_reads intermediate longread, hybrid {sample}/long/raw_qc/, filtered_qc/ NanoPlot on the raw and on the filtered reads: {sample}_NanoStats.txt (MultiQC reads it), an HTML report, the plots as HTML pages (no PNG, --no_static) raw_long_read_qc, filtered_long_read_qc deliverable longread, hybrid {sample}/selected/{sample}_selected_R1.fastq, _R2.fastq the trimmed Illumina pairs properly paired on the screened guide assembly; Polypolish reads them, and so does Filtlong for ONT samples with short_read_guidance: true map_sel_contigs intermediate hybrid

docs.title: 02.assembly
docs.text:
02.assembly/ holds one folder per sample with the genome files, the draft and the assembler's files, the results of the screen and the assembly QC. In contigs mode without the screen, the folder holds only contigs_final.fasta and eval/.

Path Content Written by Status Modes contigs_final.fasta the nuclear genome filter_contigs (no screen) or separate_mitochondria deliverable all contigs_all.fasta the screened genome, mitochondrion included finalize_assembly deliverable screen contigs_mitochondrial.fasta the confirmed mitochondrial contigs, headers unchanged; an empty file when none was confirmed or parameters.mitochondria.mode is off or report separate_mitochondria deliverable screen contigs_filt.fasta the draft the screen examines: your FASTA after the contig filter (contigs), or the SPAdes contigs of at least 500 bp and 2x coverage (illumina) filter_contigs intermediate contigs + screen, illumina spades/ SPAdes' working folder: the unfiltered contigs.fasta, scaffolds.fasta, the assembly graph, one K<k>/ folder per k-mer size, spades.log; emptied whenever SPAdes runs again illumina_assembly intermediate illumina hifiasm/ or flye/ the assembler's own files: hifiasm's graphs (hifiasm.p_ctg.gfa, the primary contigs; hifiasm.a_ctg.gfa) and .bin files, or Flye's assembly.fasta, assembly_info.txt, graph and working files; emptied whenever the assembler runs again long_read_assembly intermediate longread, hybrid assembly.fasta the long-read draft the screen examines, one line per contig (hifiasm: the primary contigs; Flye: a copy of flye/assembly.fasta) long_read_assembly intermediate longread, hybrid assembly_evidence.tsv per contig: contig, source, circular, coverage, repeat, alt_group, taken from hifiasm/hifiasm.p_ctg.gfa or flye/assembly_info.txt; the mitochondrion screen and the contig summary read it assembly_evidence deliverable longread, hybrid assembly_provenance.tsv field and value columns: assembler, version, read type, input file, command line long_read_assembly deliverable longread, hybrid {sample}_medaka_model.txt one line: the Medaka model name after the check, or the path of the model file auto found; the assembler waits for it, Medaka reads it check_medaka_model intermediate longread, hybrid: ONT samples with Medaka medaka/consensus.fasta the screened draft polished by Medaka; medaka/ also holds Medaka's working files and is emptied whenever Medaka runs again long_read_consensus intermediate longread, hybrid: ONT samples with Medaka polypolish/polished.fasta the draft after correction with the selected pairs, headers cut at the first blank, one line per sequence short_read_correction intermediate hybrid guide/ the Illumina guide assembly and its screen (below) hybrid

What the contig filter, rule filter_contigs, does depends on the mode and, in contigs mode, on the first FASTA header:

Mode and draft What filter_contigs does contigs, SPAdes-style headers (>NODE_12_length_45678_cov_23.4) the SPAdes filter: keeps contigs of at least 500 bp and 2x coverage contigs, any other header cuts each header at its first space or tab; removes nothing illumina, SPAdes' contigs.fasta the same SPAdes filter; an empty result stops the run

An assembly from another assembler therefore loses no contig at this step, only the text after the first space or tab of its headers. See Pre-assembled contigs.

docs.title: contaminants/
docs.text:
contaminants/ holds the contamination part of the screen: the BLAST hits, the BlobTools table, the decisions of the contig selector (select_contigs) and the coverage track.

Path Content Written by Status blastout megablast hits of every contig, 15 tab-separated columns blast_contigs intermediate bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt BlobTools table: per contig, length, GC, coverage and the best-sum taxon at every rank blob_table deliverable contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv contig, assigned_genus, action (keep, remove), reason select_contigs deliverable {sample}_composition.txt share of the DNA and of the contigs per genus, over every contig, kept or not select_contigs deliverable contigs.list IDs of the kept contigs select_contigs deliverable contigs_decontam.fasta the kept contigs select_contigs intermediate {sample}_map.bam, {sample}_map.bam.bai the coverage track: the trimmed Illumina pairs (illumina, bowtie2) or the filtered long reads (longread, hybrid, minimap2) aligned to the draft; in contigs mode the contigs mapped to themselves, only because BlobTools needs a BAM, and the coverage BlobTools derives from it means nothing map_contigs kept in the read-based modes (Qualimap reads it too); temporary in contigs mode contigs.*.bt2 (six files) the bowtie2 index of the draft index_contigs temporary (illumina) blob.blobDB.json, blob.{sample}_map.bam.cov BlobTools database and coverage file blob_json temporary

With the default decontamination.mode: off, every contig is kept and still gets a row in contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv. The decontamination policy and the meaning of each reason are explained on Decontamination.

docs.title: mitochondria/
docs.text:
mitochondria/ holds the result of the mitochondrion screen.

Path Content Written by Status mitochondrial_screen.tsv one row per contig: class, reason, best organelle hit and its query cover, the assembler columns, concatemer_flag screen_mitochondria deliverable confirmed_mitochondrial.ids the confirmed contig IDs, one per line; empty unless mitochondria.mode: separate_confirmed screen_mitochondria intermediate

The columns, classes and reasons are explained on Mitochondria.

docs.title: eval/
docs.text:
eval/ holds the assembly QC: QUAST, BUSCO and, in the read-based modes, Qualimap, together with the telomere search and the contig summary.

Path Content Written by Status Modes quast/ report.tsv, report.txt, report.html, report.pdf, report.tex, transposed_report.*, basic_stats/, quast.log genome_assembly_evaluation deliverable all busco/short_summary.specific.<lineage>.{sample}.txt, .json BUSCO result for the most specific lineage completeness deliverable all busco/short_summary.generic.<lineage>.{sample}.txt, .json BUSCO result for the broad lineage; only with busco.lineage: auto completeness deliverable all busco/run_<lineage>/ full_table.tsv (every expected gene: complete, duplicated, fragmented or missing, and where), missing_busco_list.tsv completeness deliverable all busco/auto_lineage/, busco/logs/, busco/tmp/ BUSCO's lineage-placement runs, its logs, its tmp/ folder completeness intermediate all busco/busco_tmp/ the lineage datasets downloaded for this sample; only with busco.lineage: auto completeness temporary all hmmer_output/, busco_sequences/ in the BUSCO tree per-gene search results and gene sequences completeness scratch all qualimap/ Qualimap on contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, the sample's reads on the draft: qualimapReport.html, genome_results.txt (mapping rate, mean depth per contig), raw_data_qualimapReport/; an empty folder when Qualimap failed map_evaluation deliverable illumina, longread, hybrid telomere_candidates.tsv every telomere repeat unit weighed for the assembly, the units found at the contig ends and those of the tidk database and of the literature: copies, contig ends in the telomere orientation and in the opposite one, score, whether the unit is known, and which one was chosen telomere_units deliverable all telomere_unit.txt one line: the telomere repeat unit of the assembly in canonical form, or none telomere_units intermediate; contig_summary reads it all telomere_ends.tsv per contig end, tidk's call for the chosen unit: status, the array's coordinates and length, its distance from the end, its strand telomere_units deliverable; contig_summary reads it all contig_summary.tsv one row per contig of the draft assembly: length, GC, read depth and depth relative to the median, the assembler's depth and circularity, the telomere array at each end (copies) and its distance from the end, the telomere unit, rDNA units, BUSCO markers, genes, genus, the screens' calls, the scaffold_N name, the verdict and its reason; written after the annotation contig_summary deliverable all contig_summary_mqc.tsv the same table behind MultiQC's header lines, rows named {sample}: {contig} contig_summary deliverable; MultiQC reads it all

The columns, the verdicts and how the telomere unit is chosen are explained on Contig summary.

docs.title: guide/ (hybrid)
docs.text:
In hybrid mode, guide/ holds the Illumina guide assembly and its own screen, laid out like the sample folder itself. The guide is not delivered. QUAST reports its screened version under the label {sample}_guide, and the Illumina pairs that map to it are the selected pairs in 01.reads/.
