Path Content Written by Status guide/spades/ SPAdes' working folder for the guide, as spades/ above illumina_assembly intermediate guide/contigs_filt.fasta the guide after the 500 bp / 2x filter filter_contigs intermediate guide/contaminants/{sample}_map.bam, .bai the trimmed Illumina pairs aligned to the guide; Qualimap reads it too map_guide_contigs intermediate guide/contaminants/filtered.*.bt2, selected.*.bt2 the bowtie2 indexes of the filtered and of the screened guide index_guide_contigs, index_selected_contigs temporary guide/contaminants/blastout, bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt, contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, {sample}_composition.txt, contigs.list the same files as in contaminants/ above, for the guide blast_guide_contigs, blob_guide_table, select_guide_contigs as in contaminants/ guide/contaminants/contigs_decontam.fasta the screened guide: QUAST reports it as {sample}_guide, and the read selection maps to it select_guide_contigs intermediate guide/contaminants/blob.blobDB.json, blob.{sample}_map.bam.cov, selected_map.sam BlobTools' working files; the alignments of the read selection blob_guide_json, map_sel_contigs temporary guide/mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv, confirmed_mitochondrial.ids the mitochondrion screen of the guide, from BLAST alone screen_guide_mitochondria deliverable, intermediate guide/eval/qualimap/ Qualimap on the Illumina pairs mapped to the guide (MultiQC row mapping Illumina QC) map_guide_evaluation deliverable

docs.title: 03.taxonomy
docs.text:
03.taxonomy/ holds the ITS taxonomy, in one folder per sample. The method is described on ITS taxonomy.

Path Content Written by Status its_windows.fasta one window per rDNA unit, its.window_flank bp (2,000) on each side of the 5.8S gene, turned to read SSU-ITS1-5.8S-ITS2-LSU; headers contig:start-end_strand its_windows intermediate its_windows.tsv window_id, contig, start, end, strand, anchor_hits, best_evalue, window_length its_windows deliverable {sample}.full.fasta, {sample}.ITS1.fasta, {sample}.ITS2.fasta ITSx output, one record per rDNA unit, named after its window its_extraction deliverable {sample}.summary.txt ITSx summary its_extraction deliverable {sample}_ITS_copies.txt one row per distinct sequence: region, sequence_id (- when rejected), length, copies, status (ok, rejected_too_short, rejected_too_long), windows its_classification deliverable {sample}_ITS1_taxonomy.txt, {sample}_ITS2_taxonomy.txt SINTAX result for the distinct sequences ({sample}_ITS1_1, ...); no header; record name, taxonomy with a confidence per rank, strand, taxonomy kept at its_taxonomy_cutoff its_classification deliverable {sample}.ITSx_tmp/ ITSx working folder its_extraction scratch

The full ITS region is listed in the copies table but not classified. A genome without a recognisable 5.8S gene gives an empty windows file, empty ITS and taxonomy files and a note in the logs, and the run continues.

docs.title: 04.annotation
docs.text:
04.annotation/ holds the annotation, in one folder per sample: the cleaned and renamed genome, the repeat masking, the gene prediction and the functional annotation. The methods are described on Repeat masking, Gene prediction and Functional annotation.

Path Content Written by Status Modes contigs_clean.fasta contigs_final.fasta after funannotate clean, which removes contigs under 500 bp and duplicated contigs shorter than the N50 (the rules); original names funannotate_preprocess deliverable all contigs_sort.fasta the same contigs sorted longest first and renamed scaffold_N: the genome that is annotated funannotate_preprocess deliverable all contigs_removed_by_clean.txt names of the contigs funannotate clean removed; an empty file when none funannotate_preprocess deliverable all contigs_mask.fasta contigs_sort.fasta with repeats in lowercase repeat_masking intermediate all repeatmasking/ RepeatModeler library and RepeatMasker reports; empty with masking_method: tantan; emptied whenever the rule starts repeat_masking intermediate all genemark_check.txt date and outcome of the GeneMark-ES test on a 200 kb slice of contigs_mask.fasta genemark_check intermediate GeneMark tiberius/tiberius.gtf Tiberius's gene models (GTF): one transcript per gene, with exons, CDS, start and stop codons tiberius_prediction intermediate Tiberius tiberius/tiberius.evm.gff3 the same models as GFF3 for EVidenceModeler, the file funannotate predict gets with --other_gff tiberius_gff3 intermediate Tiberius augustus_model.txt what AUGUSTUS does for the sample: the stored AUGUSTUS model it uses as it is, or training on the genome's BUSCO genes (optimised or not); copied to the top of logs/funannotate_prediction_{sample}.log augustus_model_check intermediate all funannotate/predict_results/ the gene prediction: <Genus_species>_{sample}.gbk, .gff3, .proteins.fa, .cds-transcripts.fa, .mrna-transcripts.fa, .discrepency.report.txt, .error.summary.txt, and <model>.parameters.json (the name of the stored AUGUSTUS model, or <genus>_<species>_<sample> in lower case for a model trained on the genome) funannotate_prediction intermediate all funannotate/predict_misc/, funannotate/logfiles/ funannotate's working files and logs funannotate_prediction intermediate all funannotate/annotate_results/ the final annotation: <Genus_species>_{sample}.gbk, .gff3, .tbl, .sqn, .agp, .contigs.fsa, .scaffolds.fa, .proteins.fa, .cds-transcripts.fa, .mrna-transcripts.fa, .annotations.txt, .clusters.txt, .stats.json, .discrepency.report.txt, and Gene2Products.must-fix.txt, Gene2Products.need-curating.txt, Gene2Products.new-names-passed.txt funannotate_annotation deliverable all funannotate/annotate_misc/ working files of funannotate annotate, among them annotations.secretome.txt (with SignalP), genome.fixedproducts and iprscan.xml, funannotate's copy of the InterProScan XML funannotate_annotation intermediate all iprscan/interproscan_out.xml InterProScan matches with GO terms and pathways (can be a few GB) iprscan_annotation deliverable all iprscan/tmp/ InterProScan's working folder, left in place; empty or nearly so after a finished run iprscan_annotation intermediate all eggnog/{sample}.emapper.annotations, .emapper.hits, .emapper.seed_orthologs eggNOG-mapper results eggnog_annotation deliverable all eggnog/eggnog_tmp/ eggNOG-mapper working folder eggnog_annotation temporary all antismash/ index.html (the cluster report), antismash.gbk (read by funannotate annotate), antismash.json, antismash.zip, regions.js, one <scaffold>.regionNNN.gbk per region antismash_annotation deliverable all signalp6/ prediction_results.txt (read by funannotate annotate), output.gff3, output.json, region_output.gff3, processed_entries.fasta, proteins.for_signalp.faa, .matplotlib/ signalp6_annotation deliverable SignalP .signalp6-{sample}.XXXXXX/ SignalP working folder; it replaces signalp6/ only after the result passed its checks signalp6_annotation scratch SignalP .annotation_complete.txt, .cleanup_complete.txt empty markers: funannotate annotate finished; the cleanup finished funannotate_annotation, cleanup intermediate all clean_*/, *.log, genome.fixedproducts directly in this folder funannotate scratch files, if any are left; listed in logs/cleanup_{sample}.log cleanup all

In the file names, <Genus_species> is the species column of the annotation parameter table with spaces turned into underscores, for example Fusarium_graminearum_SAMPLE1.gff3. The sample name is also the locus-tag prefix of every gene ID.

docs.title: 05.amr
docs.text:
05.amr/ is written only when the AMR screen is on, and holds its results in one folder per sample. The method, the target statuses and the columns are explained on Antifungal resistance mutations.

Path Content Written by Status amr_summary.tsv one row per target protein of the species: compartment, status (evaluated, not evaluated, not found, not screened), positions compared, the verdict (resistance, conflicting, unknown, no resistance, wild type), the FungAMR mutations with their verdicts and the new mutations found, the drugs with evidence of resistance and of no resistance with their levels, a note amr_chroquetas deliverable amr_positions.tsv one row per FungAMR position of every copy read position by position: target, compartment, copy, position, reference and found amino acid, call (FungAMR mutation, new mutation, no mutation; or no alignment or position not found where the position could not be compared), verdict, the drugs with evidence of resistance and of no resistance with their levels in words, the changes with evidence of resistance at that position, ChroQueTas's drug text amr_chroquetas deliverable amr_summary_mqc.tsv the summary behind MultiQC's header lines, rows named {sample}: {target} amr_chroquetas deliverable; MultiQC reads it chroquetas/nuclear/, chroquetas/mitochondrial/ ChroQueTas's own output of the two runs, unchanged: its summary and statistics, one table per target copy, the extracted proteins, miniprot's alignments, the BLASTP comparisons, tmp/. A run that was not made has no folder: mitochondrial/ exists only when the species has cytochrome b and its mitochondrial run was made amr_chroquetas deliverable

docs.title: 06.report
docs.text:
06.report/ holds the MultiQC report of the run and the files behind it.

Path Content Status multiqc_report.html QUAST and BUSCO results and the contig summary table of every sample of the run, and the AMR table with the AMR screen on; in the read-based modes also fastp (illumina, hybrid), NanoPlot (longread, hybrid) and Qualimap deliverable multiqc_data/ the tables behind the plots, for example multiqc_general_stats.txt, multiqc_busco.txt, multiqc_quast.txt, multiqc_contig_summary.txt deliverable multiqc_config.yaml the MultiQC configuration of the run, with the sample-name rules intermediate

Rows are named after the tool and the sample, for example QUAST assembly QC | <sample> and BUSCO completeness QC (<lineage>) | <sample>. A sample has two BUSCO rows with the automatic lineage and one with a named lineage. The rows of the contig summary table are named {sample}: {contig}, and those of the AMR table {sample}: {target}. The rows of each mode are listed under Report. The report covers the samples of the current run only and is rewritten when they change.

docs.title: logs
docs.text:
logs/ holds a log for every per-sample rule and sample, and the logs of the steps that run once for the whole run.

File Written by <rule>_{sample}.log every per-sample rule, for example funannotate_prediction_SAMPLE1.log funannotate_db.log, normalize_funannotate_db.log the funannotate database download and path repair unite_db.log unite_db or unite_db_local busco_data.log busco_data: the download of a named BUSCO lineage unite_identified.log unite_identified: the one-line summary of the filter and the two counts telomere_db.log telomere_db: the download of the telomere repeat database and its checksum chroquetas_db.log chroquetas_db: the download of ChroQueTas and its database, the two checksums, the unpacking (AMR screen on) tiberius_model.log tiberius_model: the download of the Tiberius fungi model, its checksum and the unpacking (Tiberius on) antismash_db.log or antismash_db_local.log the antiSMASH database rule of the run install_signalp6.log the SignalP 6 installation download_phix.log, build_phix.log the PhiX genome download and its bowtie2 index (illumina, hybrid) multiqc.log the report

Snakemake deletes the log of a job before it runs that job again, so each log holds the latest attempt only. Copy a log you want to keep before you run again. Some messages go only to the logs:

Only in the log Log the warnings of the contig selector select_contigs_{sample}.log a QUAST, Qualimap or NanoPlot failure genome_assembly_evaluation_{sample}.log, map_evaluation_{sample}.log, map_guide_evaluation_{sample}.log, raw_long_read_qc_{sample}.log, filtered_long_read_qc_{sample}.log a genome without 5.8S its_extraction_{sample}.log the share of PhiX in an Illumina library map_phix_{sample}.log fastp's and Filtlong's read totals trim_adapters_{sample}.log, filter_long_reads_{sample}.log how many SPAdes contigs the filter kept filter_contigs_{sample}.log which file became contigs_all.fasta finalize_assembly_{sample}.log tidk's messages and the candidate units behind the telomere unit (the [FunFlux] telomere_units summary line and its NOTE reach the console too) telomere_units_{sample}.log the one-line summary of the contig summary: contigs per verdict, contig ends with a telomere, median depth, BUSCO lineage contig_summary_{sample}.log ChroQueTas's messages of both runs, among them the targets it could not extract (the [FunFlux] amr_chroquetas summary line and its NOTE reach the console too) amr_chroquetas_{sample}.log

Snakemake writes its own log of each run to .snakemake/log/ in the launch folder. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Temporary files and folders a re-run replaces
docs.text:
The files and folders below are deleted during the run, either by Snakemake once no later step needs them or by the step that made them. A finished run has none of them, so they take space only while the run goes on.

Path Modes 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/{sample}_nophix_R1.fastq, _R2.fastq illumina, hybrid 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/{sample}_trim_R1.fastq, _R2.fastq illumina, hybrid 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/{sample}_map.bam and .bai contigs + screen (kept in the read-based modes) 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/contigs.*.bt2 illumina 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/blob.blobDB.json, blob.{sample}_map.bam.cov screen 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/contaminants/filtered.*.bt2, selected.*.bt2, blob.blobDB.json, blob.{sample}_map.bam.cov, selected_map.sam hybrid 02.assembly/{sample}/polypolish/draft.fasta, its bwa index files, align_1.sam, align_2.sam, filtered_align_1.sam, filtered_align_2.sam, polished_raw.fasta hybrid 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/busco_tmp/ (busco.lineage: auto), and BUSCO's hmmer_output/ and busco_sequences/ all 03.taxonomy/{sample}/{sample}.ITSx_tmp/ all 04.annotation/{sample}/eggnog/eggnog_tmp/ all 04.annotation/{sample}/.signalp6-{sample}.XXXXXX/, the SignalP working folder, and 00.resources/signalp6/.signalp6-install-*/ SignalP a folder in the system's temporary directory, for its_windows and its_classification all a folder in the system's temporary directory, for genemark_check GeneMark

The folders below are outputs that Snakemake deletes before it runs their rule again.

Folder Rule 01.reads/{sample}/long/raw_qc/, filtered_qc/ raw_long_read_qc, filtered_long_read_qc 02.assembly/{sample}/spades/, 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/spades/ illumina_assembly 02.assembly/{sample}/hifiasm/ or flye/ long_read_assembly 02.assembly/{sample}/medaka/ long_read_consensus 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/quast/ genome_assembly_evaluation 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/busco/ completeness 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/qualimap/, 02.assembly/{sample}/guide/eval/qualimap/ map_evaluation, map_guide_evaluation 04.annotation/{sample}/funannotate/ funannotate_prediction 04.annotation/{sample}/antismash/ antismash_annotation 04.annotation/{sample}/eggnog/ eggnog_annotation 05.amr/{sample}/chroquetas/ amr_chroquetas 00.resources/antismash/databases/ antismash_db or antismash_db_local 06.report/multiqc_data/ multiqc

Files you put into these folders are lost on a re-run

The same holds for repeatmasking/, which repeat_masking empties itself, and for signalp6/, which signalp6_annotation replaces as a whole. Because funannotate annotate writes into funannotate/, a re-run of funannotate_prediction also deletes annotate_results/, and the annotation runs again. With antismash_db_local, a re-run deletes only the links, never your database.

.snakemake_timestamp inside such a folder is Snakemake's time stamp for it, so leave it in place. What triggers a re-run is explained on Running FunFlux.

docs.title: Outside the output folder
docs.text:
A run also writes outside directories.output_dir, in the places below.

Where What directories.funannotate_db the funannotate database: archive (funannotate_db_1.8.17_2026-10-08.tar.gz by default, 2.1 GB) and its .sha256, both kept after unpacking; the unpacked database, whose stored paths normalize_funannotate_db rewrites in place; 8.1 GB in total .snakemake/ in the launch folder Snakemake's records of what was made and how, locks, markers of unfinished jobs, run logs, and the conda environments unless --conda-prefix names another folder the BlobTools conda environment nodesDB.txt, built by BlobTools from nodes.dmp and names.dmp on first use the Medaka conda environment, or ~/.medaka/data when it cannot be written the weights of each Medaka model, downloaded by the model check the first time a model is used the pip cache of the user the wheel pip builds while installing SignalP 6

The databases are described on Reference databases, and the environments and the launch folder on Running FunFlux.

docs.title: Running FunFlux
docs.text:
This page describes how to launch FunFlux and how to manage a run. It covers the dry run, CPU cores and memory, conda environments and run times. It also explains what to do when a run stops or a step must run again, how to run several batches or use a cluster, and what to remove before you share an output folder. Read it before the first run.

A run starts from the repository root, with a dry run first:

cd /path/to/FunFlux
cp config/config.yaml config/config_custom.yaml     # once; edit the copy

# check the configuration and list the jobs, without running anything
snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml -n

# run
snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

The configuration must be named with --configfile, and without it the run stops with [FunFlux] No configuration supplied. FunFlux has no default configuration, so nothing missing from your copy is filled in from the template. config/config_custom.yaml is ignored by git, so a git pull leaves it alone. Every key is described on Configuration.

Terms used on this page

launch folder the folder Snakemake is started from, normally the FunFlux repository; relative paths are read from it, and .snakemake/ is created there dry run a Snakemake run with -n: FunFlux checks the configuration and the inputs, and Snakemake lists the jobs it plans without running any rule one step of the workflow as Snakemake defines it, such as select_contigs; the console and the log files in logs/ use its name job one run of a rule, for one sample or once for the whole run lock the record, in .snakemake/, of the files a run in progress reads and writes; a killed run leaves it behind, and --unlock removes it batch the samples one run finds in its mode's input folder; files of one kind share one extension heavy step, long step, light step on a cluster, heavy steps ask the scheduler for ram_gb and runtime_hours, long steps for runtime_hours only, and light steps for neither login node, compute node on a cluster, the computer you log in to, which usually has internet, and the machines the scheduler runs the jobs on, which may have none

Launch from the repository root every time, because three things depend on the launch folder:

  • workflow/Snakefile is found there without --snakefile.
  • .snakemake/ is created there. It holds Snakemake's record of how each output was made, its locks, the markers of unfinished jobs, its run logs and, by default, the conda environments.
  • Relative paths in the configuration are read from there, by Snakemake and by every job.

FunFlux treats the paths in the configuration in three ways:

Paths A relative path is directories.output_dir, the database folders, files.iprscan, files.annotation_params, the protein paths in the annotation parameter table turned into an absolute path when FunFlux starts the input.*_dir folders, the decontamination tables used as given directories.genemark_dir, files.signalp6_archive not allowed: these must be absolute

With absolute paths throughout, a configuration works from any launch folder.

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text:
A dry run shows whether a configuration is ready, without running anything. -n (--dry-run) runs every FunFlux check, builds the job list and stops. FunFlux checks the configuration before Snakemake plans any job, so a dry run takes seconds:

Problem What the dry run does a wrong mode, a missing input folder, a bad sample name, a missing row in the annotation table, a mistyped key; when the contamination and mitochondrion screen runs, a decontamination table that is missing or malformed, or a sample in include mode without a genus the first failed check prints a [FunFlux] message and stops (Troubleshooting) a missing eggNOG or InterProScan path (these are only tested for existence) prints a [FunFlux] NOTE:; the run fails later, in that rule a missing directories.blast_db, with the screen on prints the same NOTE, then stops with MissingInputException in rule blob_json: the screen needs nodes.dmp and names.dmp from that folder

A missing eggNOG or InterProScan path does not stop the dry run

Most configuration mistakes stop the dry run. These two paths only get a NOTE, and the run fails when the rule that reads them starts.

A dry run first prints the FunFlux banner and the settings FunFlux read, with any [FunFlux] NOTE: lines among them:

Mode: contigs — Annotation of fungal genome assemblies you already have.
[FunFlux] NOTE: contigs mode without parameters.contigs.screen: your FASTA gets no contamination or mitochondrion screen. ...
Decontamination mode: off (discard_no_hit=false).
GeneMark-ES: off (funannotate runs its no-GeneMark branch).
Tiberius: on (its gene models join the others in EVidenceModeler, weight 1).
SignalP 6: off.
Contig summary: telomere motif auto (the repeat unit is chosen from the data), a telomere from 5 tandem copies within 25000 bp of a contig end, an rDNA array from 3 rDNA unit(s).
AMR screen: off.
Sample SAMPLE1 will be processed.
AUGUSTUS: SAMPLE1 is trained on its BUSCO genes (checked once the database is unpacked).

Then comes Snakemake's plan:

  • Conda environment workflow/envs/<name>.yaml will be created. for each environment not built yet
  • the Job stats table
  • one block per job, with its reason:
  • Would remove temporary output <path> for each temporary file
  • last, This was a dry-run (flag -n). The order of jobs does not reflect the order of execution.

When the output is redirected to a file, FunFlux's lines can land after Snakemake's.

Check the Job stats. With Tiberius on, and GeneMark-ES, SignalP 6 and the AMR screen (the resistance-mutation screen) off, the first run of one sample plans:

Mode Per sample Once per run First run, one sample illumina 32 11 43 longread 32, plus check_medaka_model and long_read_consensus for an ONT sample with Medaka 9 41 (PacBio HiFi) or 43 (ONT with Medaka) hybrid 47, plus the same two for an ONT sample with Medaka 11 58 (PacBio HiFi) or 60 (ONT with Medaka) contigs 19; the screen adds 8 9 28; 36 with the screen

illumina and hybrid add download_phix and build_phix to the jobs that run once per run. The other once-per-run jobs are normalize_funannotate_db, antismash_db or antismash_db_local, unite_db or unite_db_local, telomere_db, multiqc and all. Six more are added only when their condition holds. The counts in the table include the first three, which hold on a first run with the default settings; with the funannotate database already in place, funannotate_db drops out and every count is one lower:

  • funannotate_db, only while the database is missing
  • unite_identified, unless parameters.its.unite_identified_only is false
  • tiberius_model, with Tiberius on
  • install_signalp6, with SignalP 6 on
  • chroquetas_db, with the AMR screen on
  • busco_data, for a named BUSCO lineage

The optional steps change these counts in every mode:

Setting Jobs per sample Once per run Tiberius off 2 fewer (a contigs sample without the screen: 17 instead of 19) tiberius_model left out GeneMark-ES on 1 more SignalP 6 on 1 more install_signalp6 added AMR screen on 1 more (amr_chroquetas) chroquetas_db added parameters.its.unite_identified_only: false unite_identified left out parameters.busco.lineage names a lineage busco_data added parameters.contigs.screen: true (contigs mode only) 8 more

For example, the first run of one contigs sample without the screen plans 28 jobs, and 30 with the AMR screen on. The two-sample examples of config/config_test_examples.yaml plan 75 jobs in longread mode, with one ONT and one PacBio sample, and 107 in hybrid mode. With the AMR screen on, they plan 78 and 110. On a finished output folder, a dry run prints Nothing to be done (all requested files are present and up to date).

docs.title: CPU cores and threads
docs.text:
--cores N is the only CPU setting. Give it the same number as resources.threads.

Snakemake starts a job only when the threads it asks for fit into what is left of N, and keeps them reserved until the job ends. Each step asks for what its tool can use. The assemblers, the read mappings, Tiberius and funannotate predict take every thread, while the other multi-threaded tools are capped, so that several run side by side. In the table, "up to 12" means 12, or resources.threads when that is smaller:

Threads asked for Steps (rule names as in the console) resources.threads SPAdes (illumina_assembly), hifiasm or Flye (long_read_assembly), Tiberius (tiberius_prediction), funannotate predict (funannotate_prediction); the read mappings: PhiX removal (map_phix), the coverage track (map_contigs) and, in hybrid, the guide mapping and the read selection (map_guide_contigs, map_sel_contigs) up to 24 BLAST (blast_contigs, blast_guide_contigs), QUAST (genome_assembly_evaluation), BUSCO (completeness), Qualimap (map_evaluation, map_guide_evaluation), bwa mem before Polypolish (short_read_correction; Polypolish itself runs on one thread) up to 16 fastp (trim_adapters) up to 12 Medaka (long_read_consensus), RepeatModeler and RepeatMasker (repeat_masking), antiSMASH (antismash_annotation), eggNOG-mapper (eggnog_annotation), funannotate annotate (funannotate_annotation) up to 10 InterProScan (iprscan_annotation) up to 8 nhmmer (its_windows), ITSx (its_extraction), NanoPlot (raw_long_read_qc, filtered_long_read_qc) parameters.signalp6.torch_num_threads (default 8), at most resources.threads SignalP 6 (signalp6_annotation) up to 4 ChroQueTas, which hands them to miniprot and MAFFT (amr_chroquetas) up to 2 funannotate clean (funannotate_preprocess) 1 every other step, among them SINTAX (its_classification), Filtlong (filter_long_reads), the bowtie2 indexes (build_phix, index_contigs, index_guide_contigs, index_selected_contigs), the Medaka model check (check_medaka_model) and the GeneMark-ES licence test (genemark_check)
  • With --cores equal to resources.threads, a step that asks for every thread runs alone. InterProScan holds its 10 threads for hours, and eggNOG-mapper (12) and the ITS steps (8, 8, 1) are capped so that they can run beside it.
  • In hybrid, the guide BLAST and the long-read BLAST of a sample each ask for 24 threads, so with --cores 24 they run one after the other.
  • At the start, Snakemake prints Provided cores: N and Rules claiming more threads will be scaled down., which means that a step asking for more than N gets N.
  • Two steps use a little more than they ask for. RepeatMasker's -pa counts parallel batches, and each batch can run several RMBlast threads. funannotate clean runs 2 minimap2 searches at a time, and each starts 3 threads.
  • A parameters.signalp6.torch_num_threads above resources.threads is lowered to resources.threads, with a NOTE.

Do not add --jobs on a single computer

For a local run, Snakemake treats --jobs (-j) as another name for --cores. Passing both can let the rules use more CPUs than the machine has, so use --cores alone. On a cluster it is the other way round: --executor slurm needs --jobs (see On a cluster).

Snakemake does not limit memory on its own. resources.ram_gb reaches two steps:

Step Gets resources.ram_gb as To cap how many run at once SPAdes (illumina_assembly) its memory limit, -m --resources mem_gb=N Qualimap (map_evaluation; in hybrid also map_guide_evaluation) its Java heap: the smaller of ram_gb and 64 GB --resources java_mem=N

Snakemake passes the value on but limits nothing unless you ask it to. With --resources mem_gb=N, it starts only as many SPAdes jobs as fit into N GB at the same time. Changing ram_gb re-runs nothing. On a cluster, ram_gb is also the memory every heavy step asks the scheduler for, as described under How the settings reach Slurm. InterProScan's Java heap is set in its own interproscan.sh (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Conda environments
docs.text:
--sdm conda, short for --software-deployment-method conda, makes Snakemake build one conda environment per tool from workflow/envs/<name>.yaml the first time a rule needs it, and run the rule inside it. The exact package builds come from workflow/envs/<name>.linux-64.pin.txt next to each file, captured from tested environments. Besides Snakemake, only InterProScan and the licensed tools are installed by hand, as described on Installation and Licensed and external tools.

Building needs network access, once per environment. A contigs run builds 14 environments by default and a hybrid run up to 26. The full list is on Installation.

The environments are stored in .snakemake/conda/ of the launch folder. --conda-prefix stores them elsewhere, so that several clones or launch folders share one set:

snakemake --sdm conda --conda-prefix /path/to/funflux_envs --cores 24 \
    --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

The environments are built once and reused. The table lists two options that act on them, and what happens when they move or are deleted:

Option or event Effect --conda-create-envs-only builds the environments and exits (Building the environments in advance) --list-conda-envs (with --sdm conda --configfile ...) prints the folder of each environment, for example to run funannotate setup inside the funannotate one with conda activate <folder> another --conda-prefix, or the prefix moved, for runs from the same launch folder new environments, and the finished steps run again: Snakemake records where each step's environment was, and a step whose environment now sits elsewhere runs again (Software environment definition has changed since last execution), with every step after it a deleted .snakemake/conda/ or prefix folder new environments in the same place; finished steps are kept either of the two rows above, with SignalP 6 on SignalP 6 was installed into the old signalp6 environment and has to be installed again: delete 00.resources/signalp6/installation.json in the output folder (Troubleshooting)

Keep one --conda-prefix for an output folder

A new place for the environments means building them, and installing SignalP 6, again. From the same launch folder, it also re-runs every finished step.

Every job runs with PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, so packages installed with pip install --user cannot be used instead of those of an environment.

docs.title: Run time
docs.text:
One fungal genome in contigs mode takes several hours:

Step Time for one fungal genome InterProScan usually a few hours for a fungal proteome Tiberius about half an hour for a 40 Mb genome, with about 16 GB of memory GeneMark-ES licence test about one minute repeat masking with tantan seconds repeat masking with masking_method: repeatmodeler_repeatmasker far longer than with tantan (Repeat masking) most other steps minutes

Tiberius, gene prediction, InterProScan and funannotate annotate run one after the other, so these steps set the length of a run. Because eggNOG-mapper is capped at 12 threads, it can run beside InterProScan with --cores 22 or more. With fewer, one of the two waits for the other. The read-based modes add read processing and assembly before this chain, and polishing where it runs (hybrid, and ONT samples with Medaka in longread).

Whole runs from reads, one sample each, took 6.6 to 11.5 hours on 16 to 32 cores, on two public genomes (Validation on public genomes):

Genome Mode and reads Assembler Cores Run time (h) Botrytis cinerea B05.10, 42.6 Mb illumina, Illumina 79x SPAdes 24 7.9 longread, ONT 136x hifiasm 28 8.9 longread, ONT 136x Flye 20 8.4 longread, ONT 42x, with Medaka hifiasm 16 9.2 hybrid, ONT 136x plus Illumina 79x hifiasm 32 11.5 Cordyceps cateniannulata GXU-8616, 32.7 Mb longread, PacBio HiFi 85x hifiasm 24 6.6 longread, PacBio HiFi 85x Flye 20 7.3 hybrid, PacBio HiFi 85x plus MGISEQ short reads 2 x 150 bp, 151x hifiasm 24 7.8

The runs shared one server with other runs going on at the same time, so the times are indicative only.

  • Run time is that of the main Snakemake run, from the first to the last time stamp of its log.
  • The Flye run on GXU-8616 took two attempts, because InterProScan failed once and the run was started again by hand. Its run time, 7.3 h, is the sum of the two attempts, 3.7 and 3.6 h (Validation).

docs.title: Resuming after an interruption
docs.text:
Start the same command again from the same launch folder. Snakemake skips every job whose outputs exist and are up to date and runs the rest. The launch folder matters, because its .snakemake/ records which outputs were being written when the run stopped.

Snakemake prints What to do Error: Directory cannot be locked. ... A killed run (kill signal, power loss) left its lock. If no other Snakemake process runs from this folder, run the same command with --unlock, then the command again. The files below seem to be incomplete. ... Jobs were running when the run stopped; their outputs may be half-written. Add --rerun-incomplete (--ri): those jobs start again from the beginning. Exiting because a job execution failed. Look below for error messages A job failed and Snakemake deleted its outputs (Removing output files of failed job ...). The block Error in rule <rule>: names the log; fix the cause and run again (Troubleshooting).

Run the same command again, and add --unlock or --rerun-incomplete only when Snakemake prints the matching message:

snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml --unlock
snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml --rerun-incomplete
  • --unlock needs --configfile as well, because FunFlux reads the configuration before Snakemake removes the lock, and stops without one.
  • --keep-going (-k) lets the jobs that do not depend on a failed job carry on, so the other samples of a batch finish. It covers failures of running jobs, not [FunFlux] stops.
  • A resumed run does not download or install again what is already in 00.resources/. That covers the UNITE reference, the antiSMASH database, the telomere repeat database, the SignalP 6 installation, ChroQueTas and its database, the data of a named BUSCO lineage and the repaired funannotate database paths. The funannotate database is not downloaded again either: it is downloaded only while funannotate-db-info.txt is missing from directories.funannotate_db. With parameters.busco.lineage: auto, BUSCO downloads its lineage datasets again in every BUSCO job.
  • Snakemake deletes the log of a job when it starts that job again, so copy the log of a failed job before you resume if you need it.

docs.title: What makes Snakemake re-run a rule
docs.text:
A dry run lists every job Snakemake plans to run again, each with its reason. With its default --rerun-triggers code input mtime params software-env, Snakemake runs a job again when:

What happened The reason: a dry run prints an output is missing Missing output files an input file is newer than the output; for an input of at most 1,000,000 bytes only if its content changed as well, so touching a small file triggers nothing Updated input files a job before it runs again; a re-run spreads to every later step of that sample Input files updated by another job a value FunFlux passes to the rule changed Params have changed since last execution the rule's command changed, for example after updating FunFlux Code has changed since last execution its environment file changed, or its environment now sits in another folder (another --conda-prefix) Software environment definition has changed since last execution its list of input files changed, for example multiqc when the samples of the batch change Set of input files has changed since last execution

A changed setting re-runs the first rule that reads it, and every later step follows. The settings FunFlux passes to rules, and the first rule each one re-runs:

Changed in the configuration First rule that runs again directories.blast_db, parameters.nt_version, blast_max_target_seqs, blast_max_hsps blast_contigs parameters.decontamination.* select_contigs parameters.mitochondria.* screen_mitochondria parameters.busco.lineage busco_data when a named lineage is not in 00.resources/busco/ yet, then completeness parameters.contig_summary.telomere_motif, telomere_window, min_telomere_copies telomere_units, then contig_summary and multiqc; nothing else parameters.contig_summary.min_rdna_units contig_summary, then multiqc; nothing else links.telomere_db_link, parameters.contig_summary.telomere_db_sha256 telomere_db, then telomere_units of every sample, contig_summary and multiqc parameters.its.window_flank its_windows parameters.its.max_full_length, parameters.its_taxonomy_cutoff its_classification parameters.its.unite_identified_only its_classification (its UNITE input changes); switched on, unite_identified runs first if its files are missing directories.unite_db, links.unite_its_link unite_db_local or unite_db links.funannotate_link funannotate_db, if a run from this launch folder downloaded the database: the archive the new link names is downloaded unless present, checked and unpacked into directories.funannotate_db directories.funannotate_db normalize_funannotate_db directories.antismash_db antismash_db_local or antismash_db parameters.masking_method, repeatmodeler_quick, repeatmodeler_ltrstruct, repeatmodeler_seed repeat_masking directories.genemark_dir, parameters.genemark.mode genemark_check when GeneMark-ES is on after the change, otherwise funannotate_prediction parameters.prediction.busco_db, column 3 (proteins) of a sample's row in the annotation table funannotate_prediction column 2 (species) or 4 (AUGUSTUS model) of a sample's row in the annotation table augustus_model_check, then funannotate_prediction; for column 2 also amr_chroquetas (AMR screen on) parameters.prediction.augustus_optimize augustus_model_check of the samples whose column 4 is empty, then their funannotate_prediction parameters.tiberius.mode from off to on: tiberius_model (when the model is not there yet), then tiberius_prediction; from on to off: funannotate_prediction links.tiberius_model_link, parameters.tiberius.model_sha256 tiberius_model, then tiberius_prediction of every sample files.iprscan iprscan_annotation directories.eggnog_db eggnog_annotation parameters.signalp6.mode install_signalp6 when SignalP 6 is on after the change, otherwise funannotate_annotation parameters.signalp6.archive_sha256, files.signalp6_archive install_signalp6 parameters.signalp6.batch_size signalp6_annotation parameters.amr.chroquetas from off to on: chroquetas_db (when its files are not there yet), then amr_chroquetas of every sample and multiqc; from on to off: multiqc only, and 05.amr/ stays on disk parameters.amr.mito_genetic_code amr_chroquetas, then multiqc; nothing else links.chroquetas_link, parameters.amr.chroquetas_script_sha256, parameters.amr.chroquetas_db_sha256 chroquetas_db, then amr_chroquetas of every sample and multiqc links.phix_link download_phix, then build_phix and every map_phix parameters.spades_kmers illumina_assembly (in hybrid: the guide assembly) parameters.<mode>.filtlong.*, parameters.hybrid.short_read_guidance, parameters.hybrid.filtlong_split filter_long_reads parameters.<mode>.assembler, flye_input_mode, hifiasm.* long_read_assembly parameters.<mode>.medaka_model, medaka_model_fallback_auto check_medaka_model; long_read_assembly of every ONT sample waits for its file and runs again too. Switching Medaka off or on also changes which file finalize_assembly (longread) or short_read_correction (hybrid) copies or corrects

A new BUSCO lineage, for example, re-runs BUSCO, the contig summary and the report, and a new directories.funannotate_db re-runs the whole annotation of every sample.

Other changes re-run nothing, except where a changed file is itself an input of a step:

Changed Re-runs resources.threads, resources.ram_gb, resources.runtime_hours, --cores, parameters.signalp6.torch_num_threads nothing the content of the databases and of the protein evidence files (only their paths are passed) nothing, except for the files in the next row a newer copy of nodes.dmp or names.dmp in directories.blast_db, funannotate-db-info.txt, the SignalP 6 archive, the folder named in directories.antismash_db (its own modification time, which changes when an entry is added or removed), the unite_its_sintax.fasta that directories.unite_db points to (Snakemake follows the link) the steps that read it

Updating a database in place re-runs nothing, unless a file in the last row becomes newer

Only the paths of the databases and of the protein evidence files are passed to the rules. A change to their content therefore re-runs nothing, unless one of the files in the last row of the table becomes newer.

To redo a step anyway:

# this rule for every sample, and every step after it
snakemake --sdm conda --cores 24 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml \
    --forcerun iprscan_annotation

To redo a step for one sample only, delete that step's output, for example 04.annotation/{sample}/iprscan/interproscan_out.xml. A deleted final result is rebuilt on the next run, with every step after it. A deleted intermediate file that no pending job needs is not rebuilt. The final results are the files every run makes sure exist:

Mode Final results every mode eval/quast/, eval/busco/, eval/contig_summary.tsv, the seven ITS files, contigs_clean.fasta, contigs_sort.fasta, contigs_mask.fasta, funannotate/, iprscan/interproscan_out.xml, eggnog/, antismash/, signalp6/prediction_results.txt (SignalP 6 on) and .cleanup_complete.txt of every sample, 05.amr/{sample}/amr_summary.tsv (AMR screen on), plus 00.resources/funannotate_db_paths.normalized.json and 06.report/multiqc_report.html contigs also contigs_final.fasta; with the screen also contigs_mitochondrial.fasta and mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv illumina also the three genome files, always (contigs_final.fasta, contigs_mitochondrial.fasta, mitochondria/mitochondrial_screen.tsv); 01.reads/{sample}/illumina/{sample}_fastp.json and eval/qualimap/ longread also the three genome files; 01.reads/{sample}/long/{sample}_filtered.fastq, raw_qc/, filtered_qc/, assembly_provenance.tsv, eval/qualimap/ and, for ONT samples with Medaka, medaka/consensus.fasta hybrid also the three genome files; all of the longread files plus the fastp JSON, the two selected read files, polypolish/polished.fasta and guide/eval/qualimap/

--list-changes params (or code, input) lists the output files whose parameters, code or inputs changed since they were made.

docs.title: Running several batches
docs.text:
A run processes every sample in the input folder of its mode, and those samples form one batch. All files of one kind in a batch share one file extension, but in hybrid the Illumina files and the long-read files may have different ones. The annotation table may hold rows for samples of other batches, and FunFlux ignores the rows without a sample in the batch.

  • One output folder per batch gives each folder its own 00.resources/. The UNITE reference (207 MB), the antiSMASH database and a named BUSCO lineage are downloaded into each, and SignalP 6 is installed into each (1.6 GB). Point directories.unite_db and directories.antismash_db at shared copies to download them once, and give every run the same --conda-prefix.
  • Several batches can share one output folder when their sample names differ. 00.resources/ is reused, and 06.report/multiqc_report.html is rewritten with the samples of the latest run only. A sample name that comes back with another input file is processed again, and its earlier results are replaced.
  • Runs at the same time each count only their own --cores, and the sum must fit the machine. From one launch folder, Snakemake refuses a second run (Directory cannot be locked) only when both would write the same file, or one would write a file the other reads. Runs from different launch folders are not checked against each other.
  • Runs that name the same directories.funannotate_db: start one, let it pass normalize_funannotate_db, then start the others. Every run must reach the folder under the same real path (see Reference databases).

docs.title: On a cluster
docs.text:
FunFlux runs on a Slurm cluster in one of two ways. In run A, Snakemake spreads the samples and steps over many nodes and keeps every download on the login node. Run B is a single-computer run inside one batch job:

A. Snakemake sends each step to Slurm B. The whole run in one batch job Where Snakemake runs on the login node, or another node with internet, for the whole run inside one batch job, on one compute node Where the steps run each step is a Slurm job of its own, on any compute node; the download steps and augustus_model_check run where Snakemake runs all on that node Command --executor slurm --jobs N (Run A) --cores N, as on a single computer (Run B) Memory and time each heavy step asks Slurm for resources.ram_gb and resources.runtime_hours the batch job asks once, for the whole run Internet on the compute nodes not needed, except by BUSCO with parameters.busco.lineage: auto not needed once the preparation has run, except by BUSCO with lineage: auto Needs the Slurm executor plugin; a login node on which Snakemake may run for many hours one node with the cores, memory and time of the whole run Checked with Snakemake's generic cluster executor and a submit command that only records each job; not yet on a Slurm cluster as on a single computer

Both start with the same preparation, and both need the same shared storage.

docs.title: Preparation, on a computer with internet
docs.text:
The preparation builds the environments, fetches what FunFlux downloads itself and checks the result, from the folder and with the --conda-prefix of the real run. Run these commands from the FunFlux folder on a computer that has internet and sees the same storage as the compute nodes: the login node or a data-transfer node.

  1. Copy the template and fill it in. Put every path on shared storage, and set resources.threads, ram_gb and runtime_hours from the limits of the cluster (table below). When the compute nodes have no internet, also name a BUSCO lineage. The command that lists the lineage names runs in the busco environment, which step 2 builds, so you can name the lineage after step 2.

    conda activate snakemake
cd /path/to/FunFlux
cp config/config.yaml config/config_custom.yaml

  2. Build the conda environments of every step of the run. To build them, conda first downloads every package into its package cache, by default inside the conda installation. If that sits in a home folder with a small quota, move the cache to project space first, as in the first line:

    export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/path/to/project_space/conda_pkgs
snakemake --sdm conda --conda-prefix /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs \
    --conda-create-envs-only --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

  3. Fetch everything FunFlux downloads itself, and nothing else. Add -n first to see the plan.

    snakemake download_all --sdm conda --conda-prefix /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs \
    --cores 4 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

  4. Check. The dry run must print Nothing to be done (all requested files are present and up to date).

    snakemake download_all -n --sdm conda --conda-prefix /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs \
    --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

    Two more lines can follow it, 1 jobs have missing provenance/metadata ... and Rules with missing metadata: funannotate_db. Both are harmless: the funannotate database was already in its folder, downloaded by hand or by a run from another launch folder, so Snakemake holds no record of downloading it.

Four points about these commands, each with its reason:

Point Why Write download_all right after snakemake. --configfile and --sdm take one or more values. At the end of the line download_all is read as a second configuration file, and Snakemake stops with No such file or directory: 'download_all'. Run steps 2 to 4 and the real run from the same folder, with the same configuration and the same --conda-prefix. Relative paths in the configuration are read from the launch folder, and Snakemake keeps its records in .snakemake/ there. Without --conda-prefix the environments are in that .snakemake/conda/ too, and Medaka keeps the model weights the check downloads inside its environment. From another folder, the real run builds the environments again, without the weights. With another prefix it also runs every download step again: Snakemake records where each step's environment was (reason Software environment definition has changed since last execution), and step 4 plans the downloads instead of printing Nothing to be done. Run steps 2 to 4 again after any change to the configuration or to the input folders. A new sample, another Medaka model, the AMR screen switched on or a lineage named each add a download. Run step 4 even when step 3 went well. FunFlux checks parameters.prediction.busco_db against the funannotate database only once the database is on disk. A set the newly downloaded database lacks stops step 4 with the command that adds it, and that command needs internet too (Troubleshooting).

download_all covers every download of the run except BUSCO with lineage: auto, and with that setting it prints a note that every BUSCO job will need internet. What it fetches depends on the configuration:

Download Rule When Where it lands PhiX genome download_phix illumina, hybrid 00.resources/phix/ funannotate database, then the repair of the paths stored in it funannotate_db, normalize_funannotate_db the download only while directories.funannotate_db holds no database directories.funannotate_db UNITE reference unite_db unless directories.unite_db names your copy 00.resources/unite/ telomere repeat database telomere_db always 00.resources/telomeres/ Tiberius fungi model tiberius_model Tiberius on, the default 00.resources/tiberius/ ChroQueTas and its FungAMR database chroquetas_db AMR screen on 00.resources/chroquetas/ antiSMASH databases (9.4 GB) antismash_db unless directories.antismash_db names your copy 00.resources/antismash/ BUSCO lineage data busco_data parameters.busco.lineage names a lineage 00.resources/busco/ Medaka model weights check_medaka_model, which reads the first reads of each sample, so the reads must be in place ONT samples polished with Medaka inside the medaka environment, or ~/.medaka/data when that cannot be written

The large databases and the licensed tools stay yours to install. You provide them yourself and name them by path, as described on Reference databases and Licensed and external tools:

What Key Needed NCBI core_nt and its taxonomy files directories.blast_db with the screen on eggNOG-mapper data directories.eggnog_db always InterProScan files.iprscan always GeneMark-ES and its key directories.genemark_dir, ~/.gm_key GeneMark-ES on SignalP 6 archive files.signalp6_archive SignalP 6 on

docs.title: Run A: Snakemake sends each step to Slurm
docs.text:
Install the Slurm executor plugin once into the launcher environment, Snakemake's own conda environment:

conda activate snakemake
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm

Then, on the login node, start Snakemake inside tmux or screen, so that it keeps running when you log out:

snakemake --executor slurm --jobs 20 --latency-wait 60 --sdm conda \
    --conda-prefix /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs \
    --default-resources slurm_account=<account> slurm_partition=<partition> mem_mb=8000 runtime=240 \
    --configfile config/config_custom.yaml
Option What it does --executor slurm submits every step to Slurm with sbatch, except the local ones: the download steps and augustus_model_check run on the login node --jobs 20 the most jobs Snakemake keeps queued or running at once; it refuses to start without --jobs --latency-wait 60 after a job ends, Snakemake waits up to 60 seconds for its files to appear on the login node. Shared storage can show a file written on a compute node only some seconds later, and the default wait, 5 seconds, is often too short --default-resources the values for every job that does not set its own: the account and partition for every job (leave them out if your cluster needs none), memory (MB) and time (minutes) for the light steps. A rule's own value wins over it

--cores is not needed, because resources.threads already caps the CPUs of each job. Given together with --executor, it lowers the threads of every job to at most that number, and so what each job asks Slurm for.

Each Slurm job writes a log of its own, <Slurm job id>.log, under .snakemake/slurm_logs/rule_<rule>/ in the launch folder. For the steps that run per sample, the log is one folder further down, in a folder named after the sample. When a job fails, the Error in rule block names that file. The plugin deletes the logs of jobs that succeeded, and any log older than 10 days. The messages of the tool itself are in logs/ of the output folder, as on a single computer.

docs.title: How the settings reach Slurm
docs.text:
What each job asks Slurm for comes from three settings of the configuration and from --default-resources:

Setting Each job asks Slurm for Must not exceed Shown by resources.threads --cpus-per-task: the threads of its step, at most this number (CPU cores and threads) the CPUs of one compute node sinfo -o "%n %c" resources.ram_gb --mem: ram_gb × 1024 MB for every heavy step (table below) the memory Slurm offers one compute node sinfo -o "%n %m", in MB: divide by 1024 and round down; it is often a little less than the size the node is sold with resources.runtime_hours -t: runtime_hours × 60 minutes for every heavy and every long step the time limit of the partition sinfo -o "%P %l" --default-resources mem_mb=... runtime=... --mem and -t for the light steps the same limits the same commands

The memory and time a step asks for depend on the kind of step:

Steps Memory asked for Time asked for the heavy steps: SPAdes (illumina_assembly), hifiasm or Flye (long_read_assembly), Medaka (long_read_consensus), Polypolish (short_read_correction), the read mappings with BAM sorting (map_contigs, map_guide_contigs), BLAST (blast_contigs, blast_guide_contigs), BUSCO (completeness), repeat_masking, Tiberius (tiberius_prediction), funannotate predict and annotate, InterProScan, eggNOG-mapper, antiSMASH, SignalP 6, and in hybrid Filtlong (filter_long_reads), guided or not ram_gb runtime_hours Qualimap (map_evaluation, map_guide_evaluation) its Java heap (ram_gb, at most 64 GB) plus 4 GB, never more than ram_gb runtime_hours the long steps that hold little in memory: the PhiX filter (map_phix), the read selection of hybrid (map_sel_contigs), Filtlong in longread (filter_long_reads) nothing runtime_hours every other step (seconds to minutes, a few GB at most) nothing nothing

Set threads, ram_gb and runtime_hours so that one job fits one node and one partition. The largest memory peaks measured on the 42.6 Mb genome of B05.10 were 17 GB for hifiasm, about 16 GB for Tiberius, about 15 GB for SPAdes and 11 GB for Flye. The other heavy steps were not measured. A ram_gb well below the node's memory lets several heavy jobs share a node.

  • A step that asks for nothing gets Slurm's defaults, often a GB or two per CPU and the partition's default time. The Slurm plugin then warns No wall time information given and No job memory information ('mem_mb' or 'mem_mb_per_cpu') is given - submitting without. If the defaults are smaller than a few GB or an hour, give --default-resources mem_mb=8000 runtime=240 as above.
  • Changing threads, ram_gb or runtime_hours re-runs nothing.

docs.title: Run B: the whole run in one batch job
docs.text:
Run B treats the allocated node like a single computer:

Step What to do Request one node with N cores and enough memory: about 16 GB for Tiberius, resources.ram_gb (default 128) for SPAdes in illumina and hybrid mode, and up to 64 GB for Qualimap in the read-based modes (Memory) Configure resources.threads: N, the number of cores you request Prepare when the node has no internet: the preparation above, on the login node, with the folder and --conda-prefix of the batch script Launch inside the job, from the same folder, the usual command with --cores N (script below) Time limit allow for the run times above, 6.6 to 11.5 hours from reads, plus the building of the environments and the downloads when they were not prepared. After a job is stopped at its time limit, submit the same script again (Resuming after an interruption); if Snakemake asks for --unlock, run the command once with it first

On one node, Snakemake counts only threads, so resources.ram_gb is only the memory cap of SPAdes and the heap of Qualimap, and runtime_hours is ignored.

docs.title: A batch script
docs.text:
The script below is for Slurm, and other schedulers take the same commands with their own resource lines. Save it as funflux.sbatch and submit it with sbatch funflux.sbatch.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=funflux
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=24      # N: the same number as resources.threads
#SBATCH --mem=160G              # more than resources.ram_gb (Request row above)
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00         # Time limit row above

# Make "conda activate" work inside a batch job, then activate Snakemake.
eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"
conda activate snakemake

cd /path/to/FunFlux
snakemake --sdm conda --conda-prefix /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs \
    --cores "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK holds the number of cores Slurm gave the job, so --cores always matches the request.

docs.title: Shared storage
docs.text:
Both runs need shared storage, which on most clusters means project space plus the home folder:

Must be on storage every compute node sees, under the same path Why the FunFlux folder and the launch folder, with its .snakemake/ every job reads the workflow and Snakemake's records the conda installation, with the launcher environment (Snakemake's conda environment) in it in A, each job starts Snakemake again with the same Python, and Snakemake switches to each step's environment with that installation's activate script; in B, the batch script activates it the --conda-prefix folder every step runs in its environment from there the output folder every step reads and writes it every path in the configuration: the input folders, the annotation table and its protein files, the BLAST, eggNOG, funannotate, antiSMASH and UNITE folders, the InterProScan installation, the GeneMark-ES folder, the SignalP 6 archive the steps read them your home folder: ~/.gm_key with GeneMark-ES on, and ~/.medaka/data when Medaka could not write into its environment GeneMark-ES and Medaka look there, in the home folder of the account the job runs under
  • Put the environments on project space with one --conda-prefix, not on a home folder with a small quota. A contigs run needs 20 to 25 GB, and the read-based modes more (Sharing environments). export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/path/to/project_space/conda_pkgs moves conda's package cache there too.
  • With SignalP 6 on, a prefix that other people use also gives them the SignalP 6 installation, which is licensed to you (SignalP 6).
  • A compute node can have other base commands than the login node, so run the check under Commands outside the conda environments inside a job on a compute node.

docs.title: BUSCO on compute nodes without internet
docs.text:
BUSCO is the one step that can need internet on the compute nodes. Where its lineage data come from depends on parameters.busco.lineage:

parameters.busco.lineage Where the lineage data come from Needs internet auto, the default downloaded inside every BUSCO job, on the compute node, because BUSCO picks the lineage only after it has looked at the genome on the compute nodes a lineage, for example hypocreales_odb12 downloaded once per output folder by busco_data into 00.resources/busco/, where Snakemake runs; every BUSCO job reads it with --offline only where Snakemake runs

Name a BUSCO lineage when the compute nodes have no internet

Choose one that holds every sample of the batch. The report then shows one BUSCO row per sample, without the generic eukaryota row (see Assembly QC).

busco --list-datasets lists the names. Run it on the login node, in FunFlux's busco environment, after step 2 of the preparation:

# Print the folder of each environment; the busco one is on the line workflow/envs/busco.yaml.
snakemake --sdm conda --conda-prefix /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs --list-conda-envs \
    --configfile config/config_custom.yaml
conda activate /path/to/project_space/funflux_envs/<the folder on that line>
busco --list-datasets     # needs internet; leaves a small busco_downloads/ folder here
rm -r busco_downloads
conda activate snakemake

The list prints each name with its version after a dot, for example hypocreales_odb12.2. Write the name without the dot and the number after it, as in lineage: hypocreales_odb12. BUSCO then downloads the newest version.

docs.title: The GeneMark-ES key
docs.text: GeneMark-ES reads its licence key from ~/.gm_key in the home folder of the account the job runs under, so the key must be there on every compute node. FunFlux checks that the file exists before any job starts. In run A every job reads the workflow again, so a compute node that does not see the key stops that job with [FunFlux] GeneMark is enabled but there is no licence key at <home>/.gm_key. On clusters whose home folder is shared, copying the key once is enough (see GeneMark-ES).

docs.title: Cleaning up
docs.text:
During the run, FunFlux removes the temporary files and the scratch folders of the rules. As the last step of each sample, rule cleanup also removes the clean_* folders, *.log files and genome.fixedproducts left in 04.annotation/{sample}/, and lists them in logs/cleanup_{sample}.log. The full list of what FunFlux removes is on Output files.

Before you share or archive an output folder, see Disk use for its largest items. Deleting a final result makes the next run on that folder rebuild it, with every step after it.

Remove the SignalP 6 package from a copy you share

00.resources/signalp6/package/ (1.6 GB) holds DTU's licensed SignalP 6 model weights, and FunFlux does not remove it. In a folder you keep running, a missing package stops the next SignalP job with SignalP installation manifest points to a missing model directory.

The environments are in .snakemake/conda/ or in the --conda-prefix folder. After deleting that folder, they are built again on the next run, and SignalP 6 needs a new installation (see Conda environments).
